Passing from an algebraic $k\subset\C$ to $\Qb$ preserves the identity component of the motivated group on the given Betti realization, and hence $g,b,l,u$. In bases carried by $j_{\B}$ and $j_{\dR}$, the matrix of $\alpha_c$ is $\overline\alpha$.

Use $t_0$ only to identify geometric groups and flags over $\C$. Let $\mu$ be the Hodge cocharacter of $M$, $w$ the central weight cocharacter, and write \[ B=P_G(\mu),\quad B^-=P_G(w\mu^{-1}),\quad L=Z_G(\mu),\quad U=R_u(B). \] The joint Hodge cocharacter is $\lambda=(\mu,w\mu^{-1})\in J_{\C}$. Put \[ n=\dim N_2,\quad n_B=\dim(N_2\cap B^-),\qquad v=n-n_B. \tag{A.2.2a} \] Then $0\leq v\leq u$. On the component containing $t_0$, the dimensions of the closures of the images in (A.2.1c) are \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{c c c c c c} \toprule $\alpha$&$\beta$&$\gamma$&$\phi$&$\psi$&$(\alpha,\beta)$\rule{0pt}{2.4ex}\\ \midrule $g$&$u$&$b+v$&$u$&$u+v$&$g+v$\\ \bottomrule \end{tabular} \end{center} More precisely, under the algebraic coordinate change \[ P\times Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\times P'',\qquad (a,s)\longmapsto(s,(sa)^{-1}), \tag{A.2.2b} \] the closure of the joint image is $Q\times\Gamma$, where $\Gamma$ is the closure of the $\gamma$-image and $\dim\Gamma=b+v$.

Suppose $M$ is obtained from a motive over an algebraic $k_0\subset\R$. Let $f_\infty$ be its rational cohomological real Frobenius. Then, as equations of flags, \[ \overline\phi=f_\infty\phi,\qquad F_D^{\mathrm{opp}}=\alpha f_\infty\alpha^{-1}F_D. \] Consequently \[ \Q(\psi)=\Q(\phi),\qquad K=k(\alpha). \tag{A.2.5a} \] Over $\Qb$ one has $v=0$, and the corrected conjectural tuple is \[ (\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\phi,\psi,K;K/\alpha,K/\beta,K/\gamma) =(g,u,b,u,u,g;0,b,u), \tag{A.2.5b} \] where entries denote the degrees with the bases in A.2.4 and $\mathrm{PG}_{\mathrm{mot}}(M)$ suffices for these values.

Let $k=\Q$, use its real embedding, and put \[ E:y^2=x^3-x+1,\qquad M=h^1(E). \] Its discriminant is $-368$ and $j(E)=-6912/23$. A CM elliptic $j$-invariant is an algebraic integer, so this curve is non-CM. Thus $G=\GL_2$, $g=4$, $b=3$, $l=2$, $u=1$, and $v=0$. For this completely specified motive, the five excessive original values described above are false independently of any period conjecture. In particular conjugate periods add zero new transcendentals to $k(\alpha)$, whereas $u=1$.

For every specific motive $M$ for which $\mathrm{PG}_{\mathrm{mot}}(M\oplus c^*M)$ is established, all nine equalities in A.2.4 hold unconditionally. This is a theorem about every such case, since its proof is the application of the six fixed rational maps, not a new transcendence hypothesis.

Writing $H^{0,1}=\C(\xi+h\omega)$, one has \begin{align} h&=\frac{\eta_1\overline{\omega_2}-\eta_2\overline{\omega_1}} {\omega_1\overline{\omega_2}-\omega_2\overline{\omega_1}}\label{ell:hperiod}\\ &=\frac{\eta_1}{\omega_1}-\frac{\pi}{\omega_1^2\operatorname{Im}\tau} =\frac{\pi^2}{3\omega_1^2}E_2^*(\tau).\label{ell:he2} \end{align} For an algebraic adapted change of basis $\omega'=r\omega$, $\xi'=s\xi+t\omega$, with $r,s\in\Qb^\times$, $t\in\Qb$, the parameter is $h'=(sh-t)/r$. In particular, the property $h\in\Qb$ is independent of the adapted algebraic basis.

In the rational Betti basis dual to the cycles used above, \[ F^1=\C(1,\tau),\qquad H^{0,1}=\C(1,\overline\tau), \qquad \Q(\varphi)=\Q(\tau),\quad \Q(\psi)=\Q(\tau,\overline\tau). \] For $E/\Qb$, the filtration field has transcendence degree zero in the CM case and one in the non-CM case. The bigrading field has transcendence degree zero in the CM case; in the non-CM case its transcendence degree lies between one and two.

If $E/\Qb$ is isogenous to $\overline E$, then $\overline\tau\in\Q(\tau)$, so $\Q(\psi)=\Q(\varphi)$. In the non-CM case their common transcendence degree over $\Q$ is one. Moreover \[ h\in\Qb(\omega_1,\omega_2,\eta_1,\eta_2). \] This applies to every curve with a real model and also to curves isogenous to their conjugates without having a real model.
The curve \[ E_7/\Q(i):\quad Y^2=X^3+2X^2+(\tfrac12+i)X \] is non-CM, has no real model, and is isogenous to its conjugate. Its bigrading field has transcendence degree one.
Let $j_0=1/(2+i)$, $c=j_0/(j_0-1728)$, and \[ E_8/\Q(i):\quad y^2=4x^3-3cx-c. \] Then $j(E_8)=j_0$. This curve is non-CM, has no real model, and is not isogenous to $\overline E_8$.
For a CM elliptic curve $E/k$ in the stated Weierstrass normalization, $h\in k$. In particular its Hodge splitting is defined over $k$.

For a CM elliptic curve over $\Qb$, let \[ L=\Qb(\omega_1,\omega_2,\eta_1,\eta_2). \] Then \[ L=\Qb(\omega_1,\pi/\omega_1)=\Qb(\omega_1,\pi), \qquad \trdeg_{\Qb}L=2. \] For the degree-one motive, the CM motivic torus has dimension two; this proves the period-conjecture dimension in this case. The same transcendence degree holds after adjoining the periods of the conjugate curve.
For $E:y^2=4x^3-30x-28$ one has $j=8000$, CM by $\Q(\sqrt{-2})$, and $h=1/2$ in the basis $(dx/y,x\,dx/y)$.

For imaginary-quadratic $\tau$ with $j=j(\tau)\ne0,1728$, define $\Psi=3E_4E_2^*/(2E_6)$. Then \[ h=(g_3/g_2)\Psi,\qquad \Psi=9j\gamma+\frac{3(7j-6912)}{2(j-1728)}, \] where $\gamma\in\Q(j)$ is the modular-polynomial expression specified below. At $j=0,1728$, one has $h=0$.
For any complex elliptic curve in the short-Weierstrass normalization fixed above, \[ h=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad j(E)\in\{0,1728\}. \]

Let $f:E\to E'$ be a degree-$n$ isogeny over $\Qb$ between short-Weierstrass models, and write \[ f^*\omega'=\lambda\omega,\qquad f^*\xi'=a\omega+b\xi. \] Then $\lambda,a,b\in\Qb$, $\lambda b=n$, and \[ h_{E'}=\frac{n}{\lambda^2}h_E-\frac a\lambda. \] Hence algebraicity of the splitting is constant on an algebraic isogeny class.

For $j\ne0,1728$, define \[ \chi^*(\tau)=\frac{1728E_2^*(\tau)E_4(\tau)E_6(\tau)} {E_4(\tau)^3-E_6(\tau)^2}. \] Then \[ \chi^*=\tfrac23(j-1728)\Psi,\qquad h=\frac{3g_3}{2g_2(j-1728)}\chi^*. \] For algebraic $g_2,g_3\ne0$, algebraicity of $h$ is equivalent to algebraicity of $\chi^*(\tau)$.

Use the period normalization of the optimal modular elliptic curve $E/\Q$ in \cite{EllAGOR2015}. Write its normalized newform and Eichler integral as \[ F_E(q)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nq^n,\quad a_1=1, \qquad \mathcal E_E(q)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{a_n}{n}q^n. \] For the short-Weierstrass basis $\omega=dz$, $\xi=\wp(z)dz$, their regularized lattice sum $S(\Lambda)$ equals $h$. Their holomorphic Weierstrass mock modular form satisfies \[ \widehat{\mathfrak Z}_E^+(q) =\zeta_\Lambda(\mathcal E_E(q))-h\mathcal E_E(q), \qquad [q]\widehat{\mathfrak Z}_E^+ =\frac{a_2^2}{4}-\frac{a_3}{3}-h. \] Thus $h\in\Qb$ is equivalent to algebraicity of this one coefficient, and to algebraicity of all the coefficients of $\widehat{\mathfrak Z}_E^+$.

Let $e$ be projection onto $H^{0,1}$ along $H^{1,0}$. Its de Rham and Betti matrices are \[ e_{\dR}=\begin{pmatrix}0&h\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad e_B=\frac1{\bar\tau-\tau} \begin{pmatrix}-\tau&1\\-\tau\bar\tau&\bar\tau\end{pmatrix}. \] In particular, \[ \Qb(\text{entries of }e_B)=\Qb(\tau,\bar\tau), \] and $e_B$ has algebraic entries exactly when $E$ has CM. For a real model with real Frobenius $F=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, put $P_c=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}x&p\\y&q\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $D=\det P_c$. The inverse comparison image of the rational Betti vector $F\in\operatorname{End}^0(H_B)$ is \[ S=P_c^{-1}FP_c =\frac1D\begin{pmatrix}xq+yp&2pq\\-2xy&-xq-yp\end{pmatrix}. \] For $a\in\Qb$ and the algebraic functional $\ell_a(T)=T_{11}-aT_{21}$, \[ h=a\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \ell_a(S)=\frac{xq+yp+2axy}{D}=0. \] This is a period relation on $\operatorname{End}^0(H)\simeq\operatorname{Sym}^2H(1)$.

For $a\in\Qb$, the variety \[ V_a=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}x&p\\y&q\end{pmatrix}\in\mathrm{GL}_2: xq+yp+2axy=0\right\} \] is irreducible of dimension three. The smallest algebraic subtorsor of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ containing $V_a$ is $\mathrm{GL}_2$.

In the Legendre family \[ E_t:Y^2=4X(X-1)(X-t),\qquad t\in S=\A^1\setminus\{0,1\}, \] use $x=X-(1+t)/3$, $\omega=dx/Y$, and $\xi=x\,dx/Y$. Choose period cycles near a real $t_0\in(0,1)$ with first-row periods real and second-row periods purely imaginary along the real interval. For any fixed $a\in\Qb$, the relation $h(t_0)=a$ gives an isolated intersection of the horizontal period leaf with \[ W_a=\{R_a(P)=0\}\subset\Omega,\qquad R_a\begin{pmatrix}x&p\\y&q\end{pmatrix}=xq+yp+2axy. \] Here $\dim\Omega=4$, $\dim W_a=3$, and the algebraic monodromy group has dimension three. Thus this isolated intersection has codimension equal to the monodromy dimension, and does not satisfy the strict inequality in Bakker--Tsimerman Theorem~1.3. Adding $t=t_0$ to $W_a$ makes the strict inequality hold, but its conclusion is satisfied by every point $t_0$, without requiring CM.

Let $c=\pi/A$. The universal vector extension has the uniformization \[ E^\dagger(\C)=\C^2/\Lambda^\dagger,\qquad \Lambda^\dagger=\Z(\omega_1,\eta_1)+\Z(\omega_2,\eta_2). \] On its algebraic chart above $E\setminus\{O\}$, the coordinates and invariant differentials are \[ (u,s)\longmapsto(\wp(u),\wp'(u),t=\zeta(u)-s),\qquad du=dx/y,\quad ds=-dt-x\,dx/y. \] The canonical real Lie-group section $\kappa:E(\C)\to E^\dagger(\C)$, with image the maximal compact subgroup, is \[ \kappa([u])=[(u,hu+c\bar u)]. \] For every $P=[u]\in E(\Qb)\setminus\{O\}$, \[ t(\kappa(P))=\zeta(u)-hu-c\bar u\in\Qb \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad P\text{ is torsion}. \] The complex-linear part of $d\kappa$ has image $L_h=\{s=hu\}\subset\operatorname{Lie}E^\dagger$. This line is defined over $\Qb$ exactly when $h$ is algebraic. Its annihilator $ds-hdu$ represents $-(\xi+h\omega)$ in de Rham cohomology.

For every $a\in\Qb$, the line $L_a=\{s=au\}$ in $\operatorname{Lie}E^\dagger$ is not the Lie algebra of an algebraic subgroup. Its reductions therefore fail to be closed under $p$-th powers at infinitely many good primes of every number field of definition. In the preceding algebraic chart, put \[ D_a=y\partial_x+(6x^2-g_2/2)\partial_y-(x+a)\partial_t, \qquad V=-\partial_t. \] The derivation $D_a$ generates $L_a$. In characteristic five, \[ D_a^5=2g_2D_a+(3g_3-2g_2a)V. \] In particular, the actual CM example of A.4.4, with $(g_2,g_3,h)=(30,28,1/2)$, has good reduction at five and satisfies $D_h^5=4V$, which is not in the line generated by $D_h$.

Write $Z(P)=\zeta(u)-hu-c\bar u$ for $P=[u]\ne O$. The addition and multiplication formulas are \[ Z(P+Q)=Z(P)+Z(Q)+\frac{y(P)-y(Q)}{2(x(P)-x(Q))}, \qquad Z(mP)=mZ(P)+R_m(P), \] where $R_m\in\Q(g_2,g_3)(E)$ is independent of $h$ and $c$, and the formulas hold wherever defined. For $P$ of exact order $n\ge2$, \[ Z(P)=-R_{n-1}(P)/n. \] In particular, $Z(P)=0$ at nonzero two-torsion, and \[ Z(P)=-\frac{12x(P)^2-g_2}{12y(P)} \] at nonzero three-torsion. For every algebraic $a$ and every nonzero algebraic point $P=[u]$, however, \[ \exp(L_a)\cap E^\dagger(\Qb)=\{O\},\qquad \zeta(u)-au\notin\Qb. \]

Take $E_*:y^2=4x^3-4x-1$. Let $r\in(1,2)$ be the unique root there of $3r^4-6r^2-3r-1=0$, and put $s=\sqrt{4r^3-4r-1}>0$. Then \[ P=(r,s),\qquad \kappa(P)=\left(r,s,-\frac{3r^2-1}{3s}\right) \] are algebraic points, $P$ has exact order three, and $E_*$ is non-CM.

Define \[ \mathcal D_E=\{T\in\operatorname{End}_{\Qb}H^1_{\dR}(E/\Qb): T_\C H^{1,0}\subset H^{1,0},\quad T_\C H^{0,1}\subset H^{0,1}\}. \] Writing $e=e_{\dR}$ as in A.4.11 gives the exact formula \[ \mathcal D_E =\{aI+(d-a)e:a,d\in\Qb,\ (d-a)h\in\Qb\}. \] Consequently $\mathcal D_E=\Qb I\oplus\Qb e\simeq\Qb\times\Qb$ when $h\in\Qb$, and $\mathcal D_E=\Qb I$ otherwise. The injective pullback map \[ \iota:\operatorname{End}_{\Qb}(E)\otimes_{\Z}\Qb \longrightarrow\mathcal D_E \] has precisely the image \[ \iota\bigl(\operatorname{End}_{\Qb}(E)\otimes\Qb\bigr) =\{T\in\mathcal D_E:T_B\in M_2(\Qb)\}. \] For CM curves this map is surjective. For a non-CM curve its image is $\Qb I$, so its cokernel has dimension one exactly when $h$ is algebraic. The Hodge projector $e_B$ itself is never rational over $\Q$, including in the CM case.

Let $E$ and a rank-one projector $e\in\operatorname{End}_L H^1_{\dR}(E/L)$ be defined over a number field $L$. Its crystalline-Frobenius fixity set cannot have lower weighted density greater than $3/4$, where the density is \[ \underline\delta(e)=\liminf_{X\to\infty} \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{\substack{v:\,p_v\le X\\\varphi_v(e)=e}} [L_v:\Q_{p_v}]\,\frac{\log p_v}{p_v-1}} {[L:\Q]\displaystyle\sum_{p\le X}\frac{\log p}{p-1}}. \] Finitely many ramified or bad-reduction places are omitted. In particular such a projector is never a $1$-absolute-Tate endomorphism. At an unramified good place, write $\varphi_v=F_v\sigma_v$, where $\sigma_v$ acts on the coefficients and $F_v=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. For $e=e_h=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&h\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ defined over $L$, the exact fixity test is \[ \varphi_v(e_h)=e_h \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C=0\quad\hbox{and}\quad A\sigma_v(h)+B=hD. \] For the CM curve $E:y^2=4x^3-30x-28$ and its $\Q$-defined projector $e_{1/2}$, this test fails at $p=5$.

Let $E/L$ be a non-CM elliptic curve over a number field. At every unramified good-reduction place $v$ of residue characteristic $p>2$, absolute crystalline Frobenius does not preserve \[ \operatorname{Fil}^1 H^1_{\dR}(E/L_v). \] Consequently no rank-one de Rham projector whose kernel is this Hodge line can be fixed by that Frobenius. This applies to the projector of A.4.11 whenever its coefficients belong to $L$.

For $E_*:y^2=4x^3-4x-1$, let \[ G=\mathcal E_*[5^\infty]\otimes_{\Z_5}\mathcal O_{\C_5}. \] Then $G$ has CM in the sense of one-dimensional $p$-divisible groups, and its Hodge--Tate period field is $\Q_5$. The elliptic curve $E_*\otimes\C_5$ has no CM.

Let $f(q)=\sum_{n\ge1}b(n)q^n$ be a normalized rational weight-two newform, let \[ \varepsilon(q)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{b(n)}n q^n, \qquad Z_a(q)=\zeta(\Lambda_f,\varepsilon(q))-a\varepsilon(q), \] and use the elliptic period lattice $\Lambda_f$ of Guerzhoy's construction. For every good ordinary prime outside its finite exceptional set there is $\lambda_p\in\Z_p$ such that, for every $a\in\C_p$, \[ \inf_n v_p([q^n]Z_a)>-\infty \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a=\lambda_p. \] Algebraic coefficients do not, even in an actual CM splitting example, ensure bounded denominators. On \[ E_0:y^2=4x^3-4x,\qquad h(E_0)=0, \] put $t=-2x/y$ and let $u(t)$ be the formal logarithm with $du=dx/y$. Then \[ \zeta(u(t))=\frac1t-\frac12\sum_{n\ge1} \frac{(-1)^n\binom{2n}{n}}{4n-1}t^{4n-1}\in\Q((t)), \] and its coefficients have unbounded denominators at three. More precisely, for $n_r=(3^{2r+1}+1)/4$, the coefficient of $t^{3^{2r+1}}$ has valuation $-r-1$.

Let $\pi:X_0(N)\to E$ be a modular parametrization over $\Q$, of degree $d$, with \[ \pi^*\omega=m\omega_f,\qquad \omega_f=f(q)\frac{dq}{q},\qquad m\in\Q^\times, \] for a normalized rational newform $f$. In its two-dimensional de Rham component choose \[ \eta_f^{\rm alg}=\frac m d\pi^*\xi. \] This class is cup-dual to $\omega_f$. The complex number $a$ defined by Candelori's decomposition \[ \eta_f^{\rm alg}=a\omega_f+b\overline{\omega_f} \] satisfies the exact identity \[ a=-\frac{m^2}{d}h(E). \] For the weight-zero harmonic Maass form constructed from this class, with algebraic constant term, all of its holomorphic coefficients are algebraic exactly when $h(E)$ is algebraic. With a rational constant term, their field is precisely $\Q(h(E))$.

Let $f$ be the rational weight-two newform of an elliptic curve $E/\Q$, and let $p\ge5$ be a good ordinary prime. Write \[ T^2-b(p)T+p=(T-\beta)(T-\beta'),\qquad v_p(\beta)=0,\quad v_p(\beta')=1, \] and let $V(f)(q)=f(q^p)$ and $\theta=q\,d/dq$. Under the identification of the $f$-component with $H^1_{\dR}(E/\Q_p)$, the following three conditions are equivalent: \[ E\text{ has CM};\qquad f-\beta V(f)\in\operatorname{im}\theta;\qquad \Phi(\operatorname{Fil}^1)=\operatorname{Fil}^1. \] Here the image of $\theta$ is taken in the overconvergent spaces on the wide-open ordinary locus used in \cite[Theorem 3.3]{EllCandeloriCastella2017}, and $\Phi$ is crystalline Frobenius. For a non-CM $E$, let $r$ be a weakly holomorphic weight-two form with zero residues whose class $\delta$ belongs to the $f$-component. Let $B(q)$ be its formal primitive, $\theta B=r$, and put $\varepsilon=\sum b(n)q^n/n$. There is a unique $\alpha\in\C_p$ for which \[ (B-\alpha\varepsilon)\bigm|\left(1-\frac{\beta'}pV\right) \] is overconvergent. It is characterized exactly by \[ (1-\Phi/\beta)(\delta-\alpha[f])=0. \] In particular, $\alpha=0$ precisely when $\delta$ belongs to the unit-root Frobenius line.

On a fine modular curve, work locally with an algebraic symplectic frame $(\omega,\xi)$ of the universal elliptic de Rham bundle, with $\omega$ spanning the Hodge line and $\langle\omega,\xi\rangle=1$. Write \[ \nabla\omega=\omega\otimes A+\xi\otimes B, \qquad \operatorname{KS}(\omega^{\otimes2})=B. \] Here $B$ is a local generator of the cotangent bundle. Projection along the complement $L_a=\langle\xi+a\omega\rangle$, followed by Kodaira--Spencer, defines the weight-raising operator \[ D_a(f\omega^{\otimes k}) =\left(\frac{df}{B}+k\left(\frac AB-a\right)f\right) \omega^{\otimes(k+2)}. \] For any two complements, \[ (D_a-D_b)(f\omega^{\otimes k}) =k(b-a)f\omega^{\otimes(k+2)}. \] At a good ordinary point, let $L_{u_p}$ be the unit-root complement. For a specified embedding into $\C_p$ of a number field containing an algebraic $h$, agreement of the two operators on one section of nonzero weight and nonzero value is exactly $\iota_p(h)=u_p$.

Let $k=\Q(g_2,g_3)$ for the fixed short Weierstrass equation, let $\sigma(u)$ be normalized by $\sigma'(0)=1$, and let $h$ be the actual Hodge splitting coefficient. The normalized reduced theta function and the associated Kronecker theta function are \[ \theta_h(u)=e^{-hu^2/2}\sigma(u),\qquad \Theta_h(u,v)=e^{-huv}\frac{\sigma(u+v)}{\sigma(u)\sigma(v)}. \] Their Taylor or Laurent coefficient fields over $k$ are exactly $k(h)$. Under the principal polarization, $\Theta_h$ represents the canonical meromorphic section of \[ m^*\mathcal O_E([0])\otimes p_1^*\mathcal O_E([0])^{-1}\otimes p_2^*\mathcal O_E([0])^{-1} \quad\hbox{on }E\times E. \] For every nonzero torsion point represented by $u_0\in\Lambda\otimes\Q$, the reduced translation \[ T_{u_0}(u)= e^{-c\bar u_0(u+u_0/2)}\theta_h(u+u_0), \qquad c=\frac{\pi}{\operatorname{Area}(\Lambda)}, \] has coefficient field over $\Qb$ exactly $\Qb(h)$.

Let $K$ be a number field, let $E:y^2=P(x)=4x^3-g_2x-g_3$ be smooth over $K$, and let $Q=(x_0,y_0)\in E(K)$ satisfy $y_0\ne0$. For every $a\in K$, the germ \[ F_a(t)=-\int_0^t\frac{x_0+s+a}{\sqrt{P(x_0+s)}}\,ds, \qquad \sqrt{P(x_0)}=y_0, \] is a $G$-function over $K$. In the coordinate $x=x_0+t$ it satisfies \[ 2P(x)(x+a)F_a''+ \bigl(P'(x)(x+a)-2P(x)\bigr)F_a'=0. \] For some integer $C\ge1$, the first $n$ Taylor coefficients have a common denominator dividing \[ (4C)^{n+1}\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,n). \] If $x=\wp(u)$ and $x_0=\wp(u_0)$, the exact analytic expression is \[ F_a(x-x_0)=\zeta(u)-au-\zeta(u_0)+au_0. \] At $a=h$, its additive monodromy along an elliptic loop of period $\lambda$ is $c\bar\lambda$, and is nonzero whenever $\lambda\ne0$.

In the Legendre family \[ E_t:y^2=4x(x-1)(x-t),\qquad \omega=dx/y,\quad \eta=x\,dx/y, \] the Gauss--Manin connection matrix, with columns giving the derivatives of the basis, is \[ C(t)=\begin{pmatrix}A&A\\ B&-A\end{pmatrix},\qquad A=\frac1{2(1-t)},\qquad B=-\frac1{2t(1-t)}. \] At $t_0=1/2$, the antiholomorphic class is $\eta-\omega/2$, and the short Weierstrass equation has $g_2=1$, $g_3=0$, and $h=0$. Its horizontal extension $F(s)\omega+G(s)\eta$, with $s=t-1/2$, is \[ G(s)=\sum_{m\ge0} \frac{\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}(4j+1)^2}{(2m)!}s^{2m}, \qquad F(s)=\left(\frac12-2s^2\right)G'(s) -\left(\frac12+s\right)G(s). \] For every prime $p\equiv3\pmod4$, the coefficient $[s^{p+1}]G$ has $p$-adic valuation $-1$. Thus this actual algebraic CM Hodge splitting has horizontal Taylor coefficients with infinitely many denominator primes, and fails the $\omega(p)$-integrality condition of Lam--Litt. More generally, at every algebraic nonsingular Legendre parameter and every nonzero algebraic initial vector in a positive symmetric power of its de Rham cohomology, the horizontal extension fails both integrality conditions of \cite[Theorem 4.1.1, p.21]{EllLamLitt2025}.

For any $a\in\C$, put $\theta_a(u)=e^{-au^2/2}\sigma(u)$ and $\eta^{(a)}_\lambda=\eta_\lambda-a\lambda$. The normalized division polynomial $F_n$ satisfies \[ F_n(\wp(u),\wp'(u)) =\frac{\sigma(nu)}{\sigma(u)^{n^2}} =\frac{\theta_a(nu)}{\theta_a(u)^{n^2}}. \] For every $u_0\in\Lambda\otimes\Q$, the normalized torsion constant likewise satisfies \[ e^{-\eta^{(a)}_{u_0}u_0/2}\theta_a(u_0) =e^{-\eta_{u_0}u_0/2}\sigma(u_0). \] Thus the map from the parameter $a$ to all division-polynomial quotients and these torsion constants is constant. The same quotient identities hold as formal series over every characteristic-zero coefficient field, including a $p$-adic field.

Let $c=\pi/\operatorname{area}(\Lambda)>0$ and, for $a\in\C$, put \[ \theta_a(u)=e^{-au^2/2}\sigma(u),\qquad M_a(r)=\max_{|u|\le r}|\theta_a(u)|. \] Then \[ \log M_a(r)=\frac{c+|h-a|}{2}\,r^2+O(r) \qquad(r\longrightarrow+\infty). \] In particular, every $\theta_a$ has order two, its quadratic type is $(c+|h-a|)/2$, and $a=h$ is the unique parameter of minimal type. This gives an exact analytic property specific to the actual Hodge parameter, in addition to the coefficient-field identity in A.4.26.

Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>3$, and let \[ E/k:\quad y^2=P(x)=4x^3-g_2x-g_3 \] be smooth. Define the two explicit coefficients \[ H_p=[x^{p-1}]P(x)^{(p-1)/2},\qquad K_p=[x^{p-2}]P(x)^{(p-1)/2}. \] In the rational universal-extension chart of A.4.14, for $a\in k$ put \[ D_a=y\partial_x+ \left(6x^2-\frac{g_2}{2}\right)\partial_y -(x+a)\partial_t,\qquad V=-\partial_t. \] The restricted $p$-th power, defined by the $p$-fold iterate of a derivation, is \[ \boxed{\quad D_a^p=H_pD_a-(K_p+aH_p)V.\quad} \] Consequently the line $kD_a$ is stable under restricted $p$-th power exactly when $K_p+aH_p=0$. In ordinary reduction this determines the unique value $a=-K_p/H_p$. In supersingular reduction no line $kD_a$ is stable under restricted $p$-th power.

Let $K$ contain $g_2,g_3,a$, where $a$ is algebraic and $E:y^2=4x^3-g_2x-g_3$ is smooth, and put $d=[K:\Q]$. Omit finitely many primes so that all data have good integral reduction and their residue characteristics exceed three. For a prime $v$ of $K$ above the rational prime $p$, put \[ w_v=[K_v:\Q_p]\frac{\log p}{p-1},\qquad \beta_K(a)=\liminf_{R\to\infty} \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{\substack{v\mid p,\ p\le R\\ K_p+aH_p=0\ {\rm in}\ k(v)}}w_v} {\displaystyle\sum_{v\mid p,\ p\le R}w_v}. \] Here $H_p,K_p$ are the reductions of the coefficients in A.4.31. Then \[ \boxed{\qquad \beta_K(a)\le 1-\frac1{4d}.\qquad} \] In particular, the bound over $\Q$ is $3/4$. Equivalently, the complementary weighted upper density is at least $1/(4d)$. The analytic input is uniform in the correction parameter: the curve $\Theta_a(u)=\exp(u,au)$ has an order-two uniformization in an explicit projective compactification. For the ample bundle constructed below, the least quadratic type of a nonzero holomorphic growth section is $Nc/2$ for every $a$, where $c=\pi/\operatorname{area}(\Lambda)$.

Let $E/\Qb$, $h$, and $c=\pi/\operatorname{area}(\Lambda)>0$ have the preceding normalizations. The algebraic conjugate curve $\overline E$ has differential-normalized lattice $\bar\Lambda$. There is a surjective analytic group homomorphism \[ \Phi_h:E^\dagger(\C)\longrightarrow\overline E(\C), \qquad [(u,s)]\longmapsto[(s-hu)/c]\pmod{\bar\Lambda}. \] Its kernel is $\exp(L_h)$, and $u\mapsto[(u,hu)]$ is an injective uniformization of that kernel. On the maximal compact subgroup, it satisfies $\Phi_h(\kappa([u]))=[\bar u]$. The homomorphism $\Phi_h$ is never algebraic over $\C$. Writing $v$ for the holomorphic uniformizing coordinate of $\overline E$, its differential is \[ \Phi_h^*(dv)=c^{-1}(ds-h\,du), \qquad d\Phi_h=(-h/c,\ 1/c) \] in the algebraic coordinates of A.4.14. The pair $(h,c)$ cannot belong to $\Qb^2$. In particular, whenever $h$ is algebraic, $c$ is transcendental. For the actual CM example $(g_2,g_3,h)=(30,28,1/2)$, $\Phi_h$ is consequently an explicit nonalgebraic analytic homomorphism between algebraic groups whose differential has algebraic projective class $[-1/2:1]$.

Let $E/\Qb$, $\omega_i,\eta_i,h,c,A$ have the conventions of A.4.1, and put \[ \mu_i(a)=\eta_i-a\omega_i,\qquad \Lambda_a=\Z\mu_1(a)+\Z\mu_2(a). \] For $a\in\C$, this is a full lattice in $\C$ exactly when $|h-a|\ne c$. Off that circle its basis ratio satisfies \[ r_a=\frac{\eta_2-a\omega_2}{\eta_1-a\omega_1}, \qquad \operatorname{Im}r_a =\frac{A\bigl(|h-a|^2-c^2\bigr)} {|\eta_1-a\omega_1|^2}. \] There is a holomorphic map \[ F_a:E(\C)\setminus\{O\}\longrightarrow \C/\Lambda_a, \qquad [u]\longmapsto[\zeta(u)-au], \qquad F_a^*(dz)=-(x+a)\omega. \] It has no holomorphic extension at $O$ and is not algebraic. For algebraic $a$ and a full lattice $\Lambda_a$, the complex elliptic curve $\C/\Lambda_a$ has CM if and only if $E$ has CM and $a=h$.

Let $E/\Qb$ and $\Lambda_a$ have the conventions of A.4.34. For every $a\in\Qb$ for which $\Lambda_a$ is a full lattice, its two raw Weierstrass invariants $g_2(\Lambda_a),g_3(\Lambda_a)$ cannot both be algebraic. Consequently, every $d\in\C^\times$ for which $d^{-1}\Lambda_a$ has both Weierstrass invariants algebraic is transcendental.

For a real algebraic short model with three real roots, choose $\omega_1=w>0$ and $\omega_2=\tau w\in i\mathbf R_{>0}$. Put \[ T_a=\begin{pmatrix}2a&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad P=\begin{pmatrix}w&-(h+c)w\\ \tau w&-(h-c)\tau w\end{pmatrix}. \] The actual K\"unneth class \[ \theta_a=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\omega\wedge\operatorname{pr}_2^*\xi +\operatorname{pr}_1^*\xi\wedge\operatorname{pr}_2^*\omega +2a\operatorname{pr}_1^*\omega\wedge\operatorname{pr}_2^*\omega \] has product-cycle period matrix $PT_aP^{\mathsf T}$, and \[ \frac{PT_aP^{\mathsf T}}{2\pi i} =\begin{pmatrix} (a-h-c)/(c\tau)&(a-h)/c\\ (a-h)/c&(a-h+c)\tau/c \end{pmatrix}. \] At $a=h$ this matrix is $\operatorname{diag}(-\tau^{-1},\tau)$. For a non-CM curve no nonzero complex scalar multiple of this Betti vector has all coordinates algebraic. The determinant-twisted symmetric-square comparison identifies this class with the earlier Hodge projector by an explicit isomorphism. For every algebraic short model, without the reality restriction, the unique complex-linear map carrying its universal-extension period basis to the conjugate period basis is \[ M=\begin{pmatrix} -h/c&1/c\\ c-h\bar h/c&\bar h/c \end{pmatrix}. \] It descends to a holomorphic group isomorphism $(E^\dagger)^{\mathrm{an}}\to(\bar E^\dagger)^{\mathrm{an}}$, with $\det M=-1$ and $\bar M M=I$. This map is not algebraic; its entries cannot all be algebraic.

At a place of good ordinary reduction of residue characteristic $p>3$, the inverse-Verschiebung construction gives an integral line in $\operatorname{Lie}E^\dagger$ projecting isomorphically to $\operatorname{Lie}E$. Write its slope as $\upsilon_p(E)$ in the algebraic coframe $(du,ds)$ of A.4.14 and a good short N\'eron frame. It is functorial under actual isogenies. For a finite subgroup $C$ of order $N$, put $S_C=\sum_{P\in C\setminus\{0\}}x(P)$, and let $f:E\to E'$ be its quotient, with $f^*\omega'=\lambda\omega$. In short frames, \[ \lambda^2h(E')=Nh(E)+S_C,\qquad \lambda^2\upsilon_p(E')=N\upsilon_p(E)+S_C. \] For $h\in\Qb$, fix an embedding of a number field containing $h$ and the isogeny data into $\mathbf C_p$. In that field, \begin{equation}\label{ell:ordinary-isogeny-difference} \lambda^2\bigl(h(E')-\upsilon_p(E')\bigr) =N\bigl(h(E)-\upsilon_p(E)\bigr). \end{equation} For every number field $K$ containing $g_2,g_3,h$, the actual Hodge coefficients in differential-preserving quotient frames satisfy $\sigma(h(E_C))=h(E_{\sigma C})$ for $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\Qb/K)$. Normalize $v_p(p)=1$. Suppose $h$ is integral at the chosen place and $h\ne\upsilon_p(E)$, and put $b=v_p(h-\upsilon_p(E))\ge0$. Among cyclic subgroups of order $p^n$, let $m$ be the logarithm to base $p$ of the order of the intersection with multiplicative torsion. Then, in good N\'eron frames on their targets, \[ v_p(\lambda_C)=m,\qquad d_p(C):=\max\{0,-v_p(h(E_C))\}=\max\{0,2m-n-b\}. \] There are respectively \[ p^n\ (m=0),\qquad (p-1)p^{n-m-1}\ (1\le m<n),\qquad 1\ (m=n) \] such subgroups; their total is $D_n=(p+1)p^{n-1}$. The sum of $d_p(C)$ is at most $S_n$, where \[ S_{2r}=\frac{2(p^r-1)}{p-1},\qquad S_{2r+1}=\frac{(p+1)p^r-2}{p-1}. \] For non-CM $E$, every actual $\operatorname{Gal}(\Qb/K)$-orbit $\mathcal O$ of these subgroups satisfies \[ \frac1{|\mathcal O|}\sum_{C\in\mathcal O}d_p(C) \le I_p\frac{S_n}{D_n}=O_{E,K,p}(p^{-n/2}), \] where $I_p=[\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbf Z_p):\rho_p(\operatorname{Gal}(\Qb/K))]$.

Suppose the actual coefficient $h$ of $E/\Qb$ is algebraic, and retain the actual scale $c$ in A.4.33. The abelian group \[ S_h=\operatorname{graph}(\Phi_h)\cap (E^\dagger\times\bar E)(\Qb),\qquad \Phi_h[(u,s)]=[(s-hu)/c], \] has torsion-free rank at most two. The two universal-extension periods alone satisfy the numerical conclusion of the subgroup theorem used here and give no contradiction to this hypothesis.

Let an algebraic real short model have three distinct real roots $e_1>e_2>e_3$, and put \[ \delta=e_1-e_3,\qquad m_0=\frac{e_2-e_3}{\delta}\in(0,1), \qquad F(m)=K(m)K(1-m), \] where $K$ is the complete elliptic integral in the parameter convention. At $m=m_0$ the actual coefficients satisfy \[ h=\delta\left(m(1-m)\frac{F'}F-\frac{2m-1}{3}\right), \qquad c=\frac{\delta\pi}{4F}. \] The two numbers $F'(m_0)/F(m_0)$ and $F''(m_0)/F(m_0)$ are never both algebraic. Consequently no nonzero constant normalization of the actual germ $F(m_0+z)$ has all Taylor coefficients algebraic. In particular it is not an ordinary $G$-function germ over $\Qb$. This applies to the fixed non-CM $E_*$ and to the CM case $m_0=1/2$. For comparison, there are explicit transcendental $G$-functions in rational Fuchsian systems whose logarithmic derivative is algebraic at an ordinary nonzero algebraic point.

Let $E/K$ be an elliptic curve in the algebraic normalization of A.4.14, let $a\in K$, and write $d=[K:\Q]$. In its universal vector extension $G=E^\dagger$, let $\widehat C_a$ be the formal leaf at the identity of the invariant line $L_a=\{s=au\}$. Choose, once over $K$, \'etale parameters $X,Y$ at the identity such that \[ X(e)=Y(e)=0,\qquad D_aX(e)=1,\qquad D_aY(e)=0. \tag{A.4.40a} \] Write the actual formal graph as $Y=\phi_a(X)=\sum_{n\ge2}b_nX^n\in K[[X]]$. Outside a finite set of places, put \[ \mathcal B_a=\{v:K_{p_v}+aH_{p_v}\ne0\pmod v\},\qquad d_v=[K_v:\Q_{p_v}]. \] For the absolute value normalized by $\|p\|_v=p^{-d_v}$, the geometric size of this precise embedded formal curve satisfies \[ S_v(\widehat C_a)=\|p\|_v^{1/(p-1)}\quad(v\in\mathcal B_a), \qquad S_v(\widehat C_a)\ge\|p\|_v^{1/(p(p-1))} \quad(v\notin\mathcal B_a). \tag{A.4.40b} \] Consequently its adelic size product is zero. In particular this formal leaf fails the A-analyticity condition in Bost--Chambert-Loir's Definition~3.7. For Andr\'e's normalization $|p|_v=p^{-d_v/d}$ and his arithmetic coefficient invariant $\tau$, the same fixed graph satisfies \[ \tau(\phi_a)\ \ge\ \limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac1T \sum_{\substack{v\in\mathcal B_a\\p_v\le T}} \frac{d_v}{d}\log p_v \ \ge\ \frac1{4d}>0. \tag{A.4.40c} \] Thus the zero-$\tau$ hypothesis of Andr\'e's Theorem~5.4.3 fails for this actual graph. These statements hold for every algebraic $a$, including the established CM Hodge coefficients. They do not decide whether the actual non-CM coefficient $h$ can be algebraic.

For a non-CM elliptic curve $E/\Qb$, \[ \bar\tau\in\Q(\tau)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad E\sim\bar E. \] For $E\not\sim\bar E$, every algebraic dependence of $\tau,\bar\tau$ is generated by an irreducible polynomial \[ P(X,Y)\in\Q[X,Y],\qquad P(Y,X)=P(X,Y),\qquad \deg_XP=\deg_YP=d\ge2. \] Writing $F=\Q(\tau,\bar\tau)$, its conjugation-fixed field is \[ F^{\langle c\rangle}=\Q(\tau+\bar\tau,\tau\bar\tau), \qquad [F:F^{\langle c\rangle}]=2. \]

Let $E/\Qb$ be nonisogenous to $\bar E$, and put $A=E\times\bar E$. In the absolute-Hodge abelian category, its period torsor has group \[ \Delta_2=\{(g_1,g_2)\in\GL_2^2:\det g_1=\det g_2\},\qquad \dim\Delta_2=7. \] It has a surjective algebraic flag map \[ q:P_A\longrightarrow\mathbf P^1\times\mathbf P^1, \qquad p\longmapsto(p^{-1}F^1_{E,\mathrm{dR}},p^{-1}F^1_{\bar E,\mathrm{dR}}), \] with fibres of dimension five and \[ q(p_{\mathrm{an}})=([1:\tau],[1:-\bar\tau]). \] Thus the named instance of Bost--Charles's period conjecture for $h^1(E_8)\oplus h^1(\bar E_8)$ implies the unresolved degree-two assertion for A.3.4 through this map. The exact residual assertion is injectivity of \[ \Qb[X,Y]\longrightarrow\C,\qquad X\longmapsto\tau,\quad Y\longmapsto-\bar\tau. \] A proposed polynomial relation $P=\sum c_{ij}X^iY^j$ of bidegree $(m,n)$ is equivalently the period relation \[ \sum_{i,j}c_{ij}\omega_1^{m-i}\omega_2^i \bar\omega_1^{\,n-j}\bar\omega_2^{\,j}=0 \tag{A.3.6} \] in $\operatorname{Sym}^m H^1(E)\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^n H^1(\bar E)$, with the unaltered conjugate coordinate in this last formula.
For every elliptic curve over $\Qb$, the smallest algebraic subgroup containing a translated period locus is the full motivic group, in the category specified below.
The actual automorphism-cocycle image is Zariski dense exactly when the comparison point is generic over the same base field.
Passing from the actual cocycle image to its generated subgroup can change its Zariski closure.
Inversion converts the displayed right cocycle to a left cocycle; its graph is a homomorphism into the explicitly defined semidirect product.

There are genuine elliptic period comparisons over a transcendental field for which the actual image is not dense but its generated subgroup is dense. An augmented degree-one example has minimum field transcendence degree one and still has strictly different closures.

There are equivalences \[ \operatorname{BT}(K)\simeq \Rep_{\Z_p}^{\mathrm{free,cont}}(G_K),\qquad \operatorname{BT}(K)_{\Q}\simeq \Rep_{\Q_p}^{\mathrm{fd,cont}}(G_K). \] Thus all continuous representations occur on the generic fibre, including ones that never become Hodge--Tate after finite extension.

The functor \[ \operatorname{BT}(\mathcal O_K)\longrightarrow \Rep_{\Z_p}^{\mathrm{free,cont}}(G_K) \] is fully faithful. Its essential image consists of every free stable lattice in a crystalline representation with Hodge--Tate exponents in $\{0,1\}$. After inverting isogenies its image is exactly that class of crystalline representations. The potentially good generic-fibre category has image exactly the representations becoming crystalline with these exponents over a finite extension.

For $\ell=p$, description $5'$ is the functor in B.1.1--B.1.2. For $\ell\ne p$, the Tate functor of a $p$-divisible group is zero, has essential image only zero, and is not faithful. In equal characteristic $p$, even the $p$-adic geometric Tate functor is not faithful on all $p$-divisible groups.

For a Hodge--Tate representation set \[ D_{\mathrm{HT},r}(V)=(V\otimes_{\Q_p}C(-r))^{G_K},\qquad \bigoplus_rD_{\mathrm{HT},r}(V)\otimes_K C(r) \xrightarrow{\sim}V\otimes_{\Q_p}C. \tag{B.1.4a} \] The map is evaluation. If the continuous $G_K$-action is retained, adjoining this canonical grading gives a fully faithful functor on $\operatorname{BT}(\mathcal O_K)_\Q$, with essential image the crystalline exponent-$\{0,1\}$ representations equipped with (B.1.4a). If only the underlying $\Q_p$-space and its $C$-grading are retained, the functor is faithful but not full, even with good reduction. The analogous statements hold with ``potentially crystalline'' on the potentially good domain.

Let $\operatorname{MF}_K^\varphi$ consist of finite-dimensional $K_0$-spaces $D$ with bijective $\sigma$-semilinear $\varphi$, and an exhaustive separated decreasing filtration on $D_K=D\otimes_{K_0}K$. Morphisms commute with $\varphi$ and preserve the filtration. Put \[ t_H(D)=\sum_i i\dim_K\operatorname{gr}^iD_K,\qquad t_N(D)=v_p(\det\varphi). \] Weak admissibility means $t_H(D)=t_N(D)$ and $t_H(D')\leq t_N(D')$ for every $\varphi$-stable subspace $D'$ with its induced filtration. There is an anti-equivalence \[ \operatorname{BT}(\mathcal O_K)_\Q^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq \{D\in\operatorname{MF}_K^{\varphi,\mathrm{wa}}: \Fil^0D_K=D_K,\ \Fil^2D_K=0\}, \quad G\longmapsto D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V_pG^\vee). \tag{B.1.5a} \] The $K_0$-space and its scalar extension to $K$ are essential parts of this statement; a Frobenius lift on $K$ need not exist.

Put $A_{\inf}=W(\mathcal O_C^\flat)$, with $\theta:A_{\inf}\to\mathcal O_C$; $B_{\dR}^+$ is the $\ker\theta$-adic completion of $A_{\inf}[1/p]$, and $B_{\dR}=B_{\dR}^+[1/t]$. Here $t=\log[\epsilon]$ for compatible roots of unity, $g(t)=\chi(g)t$ and $\Fil^iB_{\dR}=t^iB_{\dR}^+$. Let $A_{\mathrm{cris}}$ be the $p$-completed divided-power envelope of $\ker\theta$, compatible with the standard divided powers of $p$, and set $B_{\mathrm{cris}}=A_{\mathrm{cris}}[1/p,1/t]$. The ring $B_{\mathrm{st}}$ also has monodromy $N$ satisfying $N\varphi=p\varphi N$; its embedding into $B_{\dR}$ uses the chosen logarithm/uniformizer convention. For $B=B_{\dR},B_{\mathrm{cris}},B_{\mathrm{st}}$, put $D_B(V)=(B\otimes_{\Q_p}V)^{G_K}$, over $K$ in the de Rham case and $K_0$ in the other two. On the $B$-admissible category, defined by equality of this dimension with $\dim_{\Q_p}V$, evaluation is the comparison isomorphism \[ B\otimes D_B(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}B\otimes_{\Q_p}V. \tag{B.2.1a} \] It respects the filtration, Frobenius and monodromy whenever those structures occur. The inverse for an admissible filtered $(\varphi,N)$-module is \[ V_{\mathrm{st}}(D)= (B_{\mathrm{st}}\otimes_{K_0}D)^{\varphi=1,N=0} \cap\Fil^0(B_{\dR}\otimes_KD_K), \tag{B.2.1b} \] inside their common $B_{\dR}$ extension; use $B_{\mathrm{cris}}$ and omit $N$ for the crystalline inverse.

For $X/K$ proper smooth, all $p$, all finite $e$, perfect $\kappa$ and no reduction assumption, there is a filtered $G_K$-equivariant comparison \[ H^i_{\mathrm{et}}(X_{\overline K},\Q_p)\otimes_{\Q_p}B_{\dR} \simeq H^i_{\dR}(X/K)\otimes_KB_{\dR}. \tag{B.2.2a} \] A proper smooth $\mathcal O_K$-model upgrades it to the $B_{\mathrm{cris}}$ comparison with the special fibre's rational crystalline cohomology. A proper flat regular semistable model with reduced normal-crossing special fibre gives the $B_{\mathrm{st}}$ comparison with Hyodo--Kato cohomology, Frobenius and monodromy. Potential semistability is obtained after a finite extension; descent information must still be kept. For the relative form let $f:X\to Y$ be proper smooth between smooth rigid-analytic varieties over $K$, and let $\mathbb L$ be a de Rham lisse $\Z_p$-sheaf on $X$ with associated filtered connection $(\mathcal E,\nabla,\Fil)$. Assume $R^if_*\mathbb L$ is lisse, as holds for the analytification of the algebraic situation. It is de Rham, with associated filtered connection \[ R^if_{\dR*}(\mathcal E,\nabla,\Fil). \tag{B.2.2b} \] For the constant sheaf this is the Gauss--Manin connection and Hodge filtration on relative de Rham cohomology.

For a proper smooth formal $\mathfrak X/\mathcal O_C$, integral comparison is carried by the perfect Frobenius complex $R\Gamma_{A_{\inf}}(\mathfrak X)$. Its derived specializations recover crystalline cohomology over $W(\kappa_C)$, de Rham cohomology over $\mathcal O_C$, crystalline cohomology over $A_{\mathrm{cris}}$, and the generic fibre's $\Z_p$-\emph{\'etale} cohomology after inverting $\mu=[\epsilon]-1$. If the special fibre's crystalline cohomology in degrees $i$ and $i+1$ is $p$-torsion-free, integral crystalline $H^i$, with Frobenius, is reconstructed from the \emph{\'etale} lattice and its $B_{\dR}^+$-lattice furnished by the comparison. For the base $\operatorname{Spf}(\mathcal O_K)$, prismatic $F$-crystals in finite locally free modules classify exactly free $\Z_p$-lattices in crystalline representations, for all $p$, arbitrary finite $e$ and perfect $\kappa$.

For $k\hookrightarrow\C$, the complex comparison is \[ H^i_{\dR}(X/k)\otimes_k\C \simeq H^i_{\B}(X(\C),\Q)\otimes_{\Q}\C. \] If ``r\'eseaux'' means the two field forms in this common space, their position is precisely the period point of A. If it means integral lattices, the de Rham lattice needs an integral model, and even the standard model of $\mathbf P^1$ does not give unscaled equality: in the conventions of A and F, \[ \alpha(e_{\B})=(2\pi i)^{-1}e_{\dR}. \] Thus the transported Betti lattice is $(2\pi i)^{-1}\Z e_{\dR}$. Tensor powers give the corresponding Tate factors in every degree.

For a real model, with a rational Betti basis and real de Rham basis, the rational cohomological involution $f_\infty$ satisfies \[ \kappa_D\alpha=\alpha f_\infty\kappa_V, \qquad \overline\alpha=\alpha f_\infty. \] Consequently the de Rham real subspace is \[ D_{\R}=\alpha\bigl((V^+\otimes\R)\oplus i(V^-\otimes\R)\bigr), \] whereas transport of the Betti real form is $\alpha(V\otimes\R)$. The Hodge splitting is obtained from $F_D$ and $\alpha f_\infty\alpha^{-1}F_D$ by the opposed-filtration construction of A.2.

For proper smooth $X/K$, reading ``$p$-adic cohomology'' as $H^i_{\mathrm{et}}(X_{\overline K},\Q_p)$ gives (B.2.2a). Reading it as special-fibre crystalline cohomology requires a good-reduction model and gives the $B_{\mathrm{cris}}$ comparison. A semistable model replaces that special-fibre object by log crystalline/Hyodo--Kato cohomology, adds $N$, and uses $B_{\mathrm{st}}$.
Over perfect $\kappa$, with $K_0=W(\kappa)[1/p]$, the following table supplies the characteristic-$p$ replacements. Every Frobenius is semilinear for the indicated base Frobenius.

Let $1\to H\to E\to\pi\to1$ be a topological group extension, with $H=G'(C)$ and continuous sections $\sigma_1,\sigma_2$. Use the stated comparison $\alpha$ to transport $u:\pi\to G(\Q_p)$ into $H$, and write $j:\Q_p^\times\to H$ for $j_2$ and $\chi:\pi\to\Q_p^\times$ for the character. The page's centralizations imply that $\sigma_1u$ and $\sigma_2j\chi$ are sections. Their equality is an additional compatibility. Under that compatibility, \[ \varphi(\gamma)=\sigma_1(\gamma)^{-1}\sigma_2(\gamma) =u(\gamma)j(\chi(\gamma)^{-1}), \tag{B.4.1a} \] and the exact right-cocycle law is \[ \varphi(\gamma\delta)= \sigma_1(\delta)^{-1}\varphi(\gamma)\sigma_1(\delta) \varphi(\delta). \tag{B.4.1b} \] Its identity fibre is the equalizer of the sections, a subgroup that need not be normal.

Under (B.4.1a), the unconditional kernel identity is \[ \ker\chi\cap\ker\varphi=\ker\chi\cap\ker u. \] It equals $\ker u$ exactly when $\ker u\subset\ker\chi$. The character $\chi$ descends to $\Pi_1=\pi/\ker u$ exactly under that same condition. A sufficient typed motivic condition is a character $\varepsilon:G\to\Gm$ with $\chi=\varepsilon\circ u$.

If $\pi$ is profinite, $u$ continuous, and $G$ a finite-dimensional linear algebraic $\Q_p$-group, then $\Pi_1=\pi/\ker u$, with its quotient topology, is a $p$-adic analytic group for every $p$. A Hodge--Tate grading gives $h:\mathbb G_{m,C}\to\GL(V_C)$ and its differential $\Theta=dh(1)$, acting by the exponent on each graded summand. The group identities above do not by themselves prove Sen's minimal-algebraic-group assertion.

The unrestricted proalgebraic version of the analyticity assertion in I.P33 is false, even for an inverse system of good-reduction Artin--Tate realizations over $\Q_p$. It remains false after imposing all the compatibility and character-descent identities of B.4.1--B.4.2.

Let $\mathcal C_{\R}^{\mathrm{ab}}$ be the rational tensor category of motives for absolute Hodge cycles over $\R$ generated by abelian varieties and Artin motives. Its realization \[ M\longmapsto (H_{\B}(M),f_{\infty,M}) \] is fully faithful into polarizable rational Hodge structures with a rational involution satisfying $f(H^{p,q})=H^{q,p}$. The essential image of the subcategory consisting of $h^1$ of abelian varieties, up to isogeny, consists exactly of such pairs of Hodge type $\{(1,0),(0,1)\}$. The essential image of $\mathcal C_{\R}^{\mathrm{ab}}$ is the rigid, additive, idempotent-complete tensor subcategory generated by these pairs and the sign Artin line.

Assume the Hodge conjecture for all products and Tate twists used to form the homological motives under consideration over $\R$. Their realization into Hodge pairs is fully faithful. This proves the fullness assertion of 18:34 in that scope; it supplies no characterization of the geometric essential image among all polarizable Hodge pairs.

In $\mathcal C_{\R}^{\mathrm{ab}}$, and in the homological category of C.1.2 under its hypothesis, the group attached to any tensor generator is generated by its identity component and $f_\infty$. Its component group is trivial or of order two. A nontrivial component is a translate of the identity component as a $\Q$-scheme.

Let $\mathcal C$ be any neutral rational Tannakian category with fibre functor $V$ and a tensor involution $f\in G(\Q)$, $G=\Aut^\otimes(V)$. Write $V(X)=V(X)^+\oplus V(X)^-$ and define \[ W(X)=V(X)^+\oplus iV(X)^-\subset V(X)\otimes_\Q\Q(i). \] Multiplication in $\Q(i)$ gives a tensor structure on $W$, making it a rational fibre functor. Its comparison torsor is the twist of $G$ by \[ a_\sigma=f^{\epsilon(\sigma)},\qquad \sigma(i)=(-1)^{\epsilon(\sigma)}i, \quad \sigma\in\Gal(\Qb/\Q). \] For a field $F$ of characteristic zero containing $\Q$, its $F$-points are, using the inverse matrix of the ambient map $V_{F(i)}\to W_{F(i)}\hookrightarrow V_{F(i)}$, \[ \Isom^\otimes(V,W)(F)= \{b\in G(F(i)):b^{-1}\bar b=f\}\quad(i\notin F). \] For $i\in F$, the torsor is trivial. This specifies its class in $H^1(\Q,G)$ and exactly tests triviality over $\Q$, $\R$ and $\C$.

For the sign Artin motive $A$ of $\C/\R$, the twisted Betti functor has no tensor isomorphism to Betti over $\Q$ or $\R$, and has one over $\C$. For the Tate category, whose group is $\Gm$, it is tensor-isomorphic over $\Q$. For the category generated by $h^1(E)$ of a real elliptic curve, it is tensor-isomorphic over $\Q$ in the non-CM case and is not tensor-isomorphic over $\R$ in the CM case. It is tensor-isomorphic over $\C$ in both cases.

In $\mathcal C_{\R}^{\mathrm{ab}}$, put $L=A\otimes\Q(-1)$. The full subcategory on which $f_\infty$ acts trivially consists exactly of finite direct sums of $L^{\otimes p}$, $p\in\Z$. The same conclusion holds for homological motives under the Hodge hypothesis of C.1.2. In particular, the assertion on 18:38 that these are sums of tensor powers of $\Q(2)$ is false.

For a motive over $\R$ in the preceding categories, use the right action on $P=\Isom^\otimes(T_{\B}\otimes\R,T_{\dR})$. Then \[ \bar\alpha=\alpha f_\infty, \qquad \alpha\in P(\R)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ f_\infty=1. \] The class of $P$ in $H^1(\R,G)$ is represented by $f_\infty$. If $\Q(-1)$ belongs to the generated category, $\R(\alpha)=\C$. Existence of some real point of $P$ does not imply that the distinguished $\alpha$ is real.

For a tensor generator $M$ in C.1.1, or under the hypothesis of C.1.2, the following conditions are equivalent: $f_\infty$ is central in $G_M$; every Hodge summand of $M$ has type $(p,p)$; $M$ belongs to the real Artin--Tate category generated by $A$ and $T=\Q(-1)$; $G_M$ is commutative.

For a topological field $K$ isomorphic to $\C$, the splitting of algebraic de Rham cohomology of a smooth projective $K$-variety obtained by Hodge theory is independent of the choice of topological isomorphism $K\simeq\C$, with coefficient conjugation included. For a field $k$ admitting a complex embedding and an archimedean place $v$, put $R_v=\{a\in k:v(a)\in\R\}$. The intersections defined on 18:41 are $k$-vector spaces for the Hodge summands and $R_v$-vector spaces for their Betti-real parts. Moreover \[ \bigcap_vR_v=\{a\in k:a\text{ is algebraic and totally real over }\Q\}. \] The intersection over all places equals the largest totally real subfield when $k$ is a number field.

Let $M$ have pure weight $n$ and let $q:M\otimes M\to\Q(-n)$ be a polarization morphism over $\R$. Use the convention of \cite[(5.4)--(5.5)]{MilneShimura}, so $C=h(i)$ and \[ B(x,y)=(2\pi i)^n q(x,Cy) \] is symmetric positive definite on $H_\B(M)\otimes\R$. Then $fCf^{-1}=C^{-1}$ and $B(fx,fy)=B(x,y)$.
For a pure motive over $\R$ in the stated realization category, the de Rham Hodge splitting $\beta$ is $\R$-rational, and $\R(\gamma)=\R(\alpha)$. This is the coefficient-field assertion on 18:38.

Put $a=\sqrt[3]{2}>0$, $V=\Q e_1\oplus\Q e_2$, and \[ V^{3,0}=\C(e_1+ia e_2),\qquad V^{0,3}=\C(e_1-ia e_2),\qquad f=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1). \] This is a polarizable rational Hodge structure with a rational anti-Hodge involution. The pair $(V,f)$ is outside the essential image of the abelian-motive category in C.1.1.

Fix the following effective enumeration $(T_n)_{n\geq1}$ of deterministic Turing machines. The tape alphabet is $\{0,1,\#,\square\}$ in that order. For each $r\geq1$ use states $0,\ldots,r$, with initial state $0$ and halt state $r$; list the tables for the $4r$ nonhalting state/symbol pairs in lexicographic order, each instruction being an output symbol, a next state, and a move from the ordered list left, stay, right. Order first by $r$. Input $n$ is the binary expansion of $n$ between two $\#$ symbols on an otherwise blank two-sided tape, with the head at the first binary digit. This specifies a single enumeration of all machines of this model. Let \[ H=\{n:T_n\text{ halts on input }n\},\qquad a_H=1+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\mathbf1_H(n)}{4^n}. \] Replace $a$ in C.1.4 by $a_H$. The resulting polarized rational Hodge pair is not the realization of a pure motive defined by algebraic correspondences over $\C$, and consequently is not the realization of such a motive over $\R$. This is an exclusion from the geometric essential image; a description of every pair in that image remains an obligation.
The integral product, restricted adelic ring and full product have the distinct maps and topologies described below. Betti comparison gives a dense integral submodule of the completed realization.
The relative tensor-comparison scheme has dimension $(n-1)\dim G$. This proves the stated componentwise bound; its joint product-ring interpretation requires the coordinate algebra specified below.

The local pages 18:42--49 do not define the $K$ used in 18:45 or explicitly identify it with the earlier comparison field $K$ on 18:11. The flag-fibre dimensions are five and four after fixing determinant; a concrete two-place example refutes automatic filtration-preserving linear commensurability.
Every compact open adelic coset contains a full-measure set of points generic over $\Q$ in every local component, including the joint version for any fixed finite tuple.
For geometrically pairwise nonisogenous non-CM elliptic curves over a number field, Galois changes of the places attain the full bound at every prime.

The connected affine groups having rational approximation in the finite adeles are characterized below. The determinant quotient proves that the full elliptic motivic groups do not have this property.
All-frame commensurability is equivalent to openness under rational approximation. Componentwise genericity has a different reverse implication, as the explicit group and motivic examples show.
The cocycle is the automorphism restriction of the fpqc descent datum of the comparison torsor. The change-of-place identity follows by typed composition.
Two conjugate CM elliptic curves can have rational and locally integral comparisons but no integral comparison compatible with their endomorphisms.
The Tate motive $\Q(-2)$ refutes universal openness of the total-image closure. For a non-CM elliptic degree-one motive over a number field, that openness is equivalent to full period genericity.

The Tate quotient forces transcendence of $\pi$ for a generic comparison point. That condition alone does not imply genericity, even at minimum field transcendence degree in the stated degree-one category.
The recovery question requires a specified category, coefficient ring and equivalence relation on places; the resolved cases are given in Part E.

Let $k\subset\C$ have characteristic zero, and let $k_0$ be its algebraic part over $\Q$. Let $v,w:k\hookrightarrow\C$ agree on $k_0$. Every finite diagram of smooth projective varieties over $k$ and algebraic correspondences has an integral Betti comparison between $v$ and $w$, compatible with cup products, K\"unneth maps, duality and those correspondences. If $k/k_0$ is finitely generated, one comparison exists simultaneously for all such varieties and correspondences. It extends to the induced rational tensor category and to the real scalar extensions of the integral realizations.

There is a countable algebraically closed field $k$ of transcendence degree one over $\Qb$, and two distinct complex places agreeing on $\Qb$, for which the integral Betti functors are not naturally isomorphic even on the abelian-variety and isogeny diagram. Each finite subdiagram admits an isomorphism. Thus the unrestricted inference on 15:221 from countability to a global integral isomorphism is false in this explicit interpretation.

Nonempty path sets in the tower on 15:221 need not have a nonempty inverse limit. The completed path torsors do admit compatible points, but those points act on profinite lattices; they need not preserve an integral lattice as E.1.2 demonstrates.

There are uncountable fields with distinct complex places inducing isomorphic integral Betti functors on all smooth projective varieties and algebraic correspondences. There are also uncountable fields with two places agreeing on $\Qb$ for which such an isomorphism does not exist.

Let $k$ be any characteristic-zero field admitting complex embeddings. On the diagram of elliptic curves over $k$, the integral Hodge realizations distinguish all \emph{chosen embeddings} $k\hookrightarrow\C$. For a number field, one labelled elliptic object suffices; for a finitely generated field, a finite labelled direct sum suffices. Complex places, defined modulo conjugation, are recovered after making the same quotient of the enriched data.

For $k=\overline{\Qb(t)}$, no motive defined by finitely many algebraic equations, projectors and correspondences distinguishes all chosen complex embeddings through its realization alone. Nevertheless the entire labelled integral Hodge diagram distinguishes them by E.3.1.

There is a countable algebraically closed field $k$ of transcendence degree one over $\Q$, and two chosen embeddings $v,w:k\hookrightarrow\C$ that define different complex places, for which the entire integral Betti correspondence diagrams are tensor-isomorphic. The comparison extends to their real spans and their finite-coefficient comparisons. Thus no single motive, and no collection of plain integral Betti tests on this diagram, separates this pair. This refutes the extension of the injectivity expectation to all fields of finite transcendence degree. The literal 15:223 paragraph assumes a number field; that narrower assertion remains a separate obligation.

Let $\mathcal C$ be the category of pure motivated motives over $\Q$, with its rational Betti fibre functor. On the geometric integral Betti diagram there exists a tensor-compatible assignment of polarizable integral Hodge structures that preserves the usual weight grading, every specified motivic tensor, Tate objects, polarizations, the real Frobenius and the unchanged finite realizations, but does not arise from a complex place of $\Q$. The same construction on the absolute-Hodge abelian subcategory has geometrically realizable real abelian Hodge objects in degree one. Thus the proposed surjectivity fails for the target consisting of these data and the usual Riemann--Hodge relations.

The deformation of E.3.3 can be constructed on the entire pure motivated category over $\C$, or its absolute-Hodge abelian subcategory, with the same rationally defined elliptic test. It is not induced by any field embedding $\C\hookrightarrow\C$. The construction accommodates the uncountable category without an inverse-limit assumption on integral isomorphisms.

Let $E/\overline\Q$ have complex multiplication by an order $\mathcal O$ in an imaginary quadratic field $K$, and put $k=K(j(E))$. Choose an elliptic model of that $j$-invariant over $k$. The integral Betti diagram consisting of this elliptic curve and its labelled endomorphisms distinguishes all complex places of $k$. In fact, one nonrational endomorphism suffices. Thus the injectivity proposed in the number-field paragraph of 15:223 holds for every elliptic ring class field with this particular finite test.

Let $k'/k$ be a finite extension of number fields. A finite integral Betti correspondence diagram over $k'$ that distinguishes all complex places of $k'$ gives a finite such diagram over $k$ that distinguishes all complex places of $k$. Its objects lie in the tensor diagram generated by one finite labelled direct sum. In particular, every subfield of an elliptic ring class field has a finite separating test. For the entire integral correspondence diagram, there is also an exact description. Fix the usual Betti functor $\omega_{\Q,\Z}$ over $\Q$. For a number field $k$, let $A_k=h^0(\operatorname{Spec}k)$, and denote by $e_u$ the primitive idempotent of $\omega_{\Q,\Z}(A_k)=\Z^{\operatorname{Hom}(k,\C)}$ indexed by $u$. For embeddings $v,w:k\hookrightarrow\C$, restriction from $k$ to the base-changed $\Q$-diagram gives the bijection \[ \Isom^\otimes(\omega_{v,\Z},\omega_{w,\Z}) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \bigl\{g\in\Aut^\otimes(\omega_{\Q,\Z}): g_{A_k}(e_v)=e_w\bigr\}. \tag{E.2.3a} \] Here, as throughout this section, the integral source is the concrete graded cohomology diagram with integral algebraic correspondences and the displayed tensor operations. The statement does not assign a free integral fibre functor to a $\Q$-linear category.

Let $L/\Q$ be a finite Galois extension containing an imaginary quadratic field $K$, and suppose $B=\Gal(L/K)$ is abelian. Let $c$ be actual complex conjugation on $L$. If $cbc^{-1}=b^{-1}$ for every $b\in B$, then every subfield of $L$ has a finite integral Betti diagram distinguishing its complex places. This includes every cubic field of negative discriminant. The ring-class-field construction has an exact restriction: a totally real Galois subfield of any elliptic ring class field has elementary abelian $2$-group as its Galois group. In particular, a totally real number field with nonabelian-dihedral normal closure is not a subfield of an elliptic ring class field. This latter assertion identifies the limit of the particular CM construction, and makes no negative claim about other motivic tests for those fields.

Every totally real number field has a finite labelled algebraic-correspondence diagram whose Betti realizations at its distinct embeddings are not isomorphic, even over $\R$. Every CM number field has such a finite test for its complex places. In particular, together with E.2.4, every cubic number field has a finite integral test distinguishing its complex places. The totally real cubic generated by a root of $x^3-4x+1$ has the explicit CM threefold construction below.

Let $k=\Q(\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is a real root of $x^4-x-1$. Its two real embeddings are distinct complex places, but their integral Betti functors are isomorphic on the following entire diagram: CM abelian varieties over $k$, finite \'etale $k$-schemes, their cohomology, products, Tate twists, tensor constructions and duals, algebraic correspondences, and compatible direct summands with their assigned intersection lattices. The comparison preserves every labelled polarization and is induced by actual algebraic isomorphisms on the CM abelian generators. Thus this CM diagram, including all its isogenies and twists, does not separate those two places. The comparison respects ordinary Hodge structures and extension of scalars to $\R$. It does not intertwine the additional geometric real-Frobenius involutions at the two real places, as the explicit Artin witness in E.2.7 shows. No isomorphism on the diagram of all pure motives is asserted.

Let $k$ be a number field. Distinct real embeddings of $k$ are separated by a finite Artin diagram equipped with the geometric real-Frobenius involutions. If $k$ has $r_1\ge2$ real embeddings, $r_1-1$ explicitly chosen quadratic Artin objects suffice. In the quartic example of E.2.6, the single object $\operatorname{Spec}k(\sqrt{\alpha})$ separates the two real embeddings by Frobenius traces $0$ and $2$.

Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a number field $k$, and let $\mathcal I_k(A)$ be the category of abelian varieties over $k$ that are $k$-isogenous to $A$, with $k$-homomorphisms. For embeddings $v,w:k\hookrightarrow\C$, there is a finite labelled diagram $\mathcal D\subset\mathcal I_k(A)$ such that restriction gives a bijection between natural integral $H_1$ comparisons on $\mathcal I_k(A)$ and comparisons on $\mathcal D$.

Let $A/k$ be an abelian variety of dimension $g>0$, and let $\eta$ be a tensor comparison between the full graded integral Betti correspondence diagrams at embeddings $v,w:k\hookrightarrow\C$. Let $\sigma\in\Gal(\Qb/\Q)$ be the Artin permutation selected by the exact transporter E.2.3, so $\sigma\circ v=w$, and put \[ \Lambda_u=H_1(A_u,\Z),\qquad T_A=(\eta_A^{-1})^\vee:\Lambda_v\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_w. \] For every $n\ge2$, define \[ \kappa_{u,n}:\Lambda_u/n\Lambda_u\xrightarrow{\sim}A_u[n](\C), \qquad x\bmod n\Lambda_u\longmapsto x/n\bmod\Lambda_u \] through exponential uniformization. Torsion points are algebraic, so Galois transport gives the isomorphism \[ \rho_{A,n}(\sigma) =\kappa_{w,n}^{-1}\circ\sigma\circ\kappa_{v,n}: \Lambda_v/n\Lambda_v\longrightarrow\Lambda_w/n\Lambda_w. \] These maps are compatible under reduction, and their inverse limit is $\rho_A(\sigma):\Lambda_v\otimes\widehat\Z \to\Lambda_w\otimes\widehat\Z$. There is a unique $\lambda_A\in\widehat\Z^\times$ such that \[ T_A\otimes\widehat\Z=\rho_A(\sigma)\,\lambda_A. \tag{E.2.9a} \] In particular, the projective Tate transport of the selected $\sigma$ must be represented by one integral unimodular Betti matrix.
There are nested compact open cosets in $\mathrm{SL}_2(\widehat\Z)$, each containing an element of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z)$, whose common intersection contains no element of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\Q)$.

Let $F_{\rm CM}\subset\Qb$ be the compositum of $K^{\rm ab}$ for all finite CM fields $K$, and take $\sigma\in\Gal(\Qb/F_{\rm CM})$. Let $\mathrm{AV}(\Q)$ be the category of pure abelian motives with absolute Hodge correspondences, including Artin motives and Tate objects. Write \[ \pi:G_{\mathrm{AV},B}\longrightarrow G_{\mathrm{CM},B}, \qquad D=\ker\pi \] for restriction of its rational Betti group to the CM/Artin subcategory. The prescribed CM comparison $g_\sigma$ of E.2.6 defines a point of $G_{\mathrm{CM},B}(\Q)$. Its fibre \[ X_\sigma=\pi^{-1}(g_\sigma) \tag{E.2.11a} \] has both a real point and a rational point. The real point can be chosen to preserve Hodge structures and labelled polarizations. The rational point is a tensor comparison in the absolute-Hodge abelian category. This assertion supplies neither integrality of that rational point nor its equality with the chosen real Hodge point. The full pure integral question (E.2.3d) remains open at this step.

Let $R$ be noetherian, let $\mathcal C$ be a small rigid symmetric $R$-linear exact tensor category, and let \[ \omega_1,\omega_2:\mathcal C\longrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}_f(R) \] be faithful exact tensor functors. Assume every object is obtained, up to isomorphism, from one object $M$ by finite sums, tensor products, duals, and admissible subobjects and quotients, and that $\omega_1(M),\omega_2(M)$ are finite free of the same rank. Then $\Isom^\otimes(\omega_1,\omega_2)$ is represented by a closed subscheme of $\Isom_R(\omega_1(M),\omega_2(M))$. A finite diagram of original objects, maps and admissible sequences determines each comparison uniquely. For $R=\Z$, consider such a category of abelian motives over the quartic field of E.2.6 with its two integral Betti realizations. Require that the generator's lattices are given by a specified admissible expression from the actual Betti lattices of finitely many abelian and Artin generators. Then these two realizations are integrally tensor isomorphic on $\mathcal C$. In this specified integral model, a single admissible tensor generator does not distinguish those quartic places.

Let \[ E:\ y^2=x(x-1)(x-3),\qquad B:\ Y^2=X^3+8X^2+4X . \] Let \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{adm}}(E)\) be the full rigid exact tensor category generated by the actual integral Hodge structure \(H_1(E(\C),\Z)\), using finite sums, tensor products, duals, saturated Hodge subobjects and free Hodge quotients. Its morphisms are all integral Hodge morphisms between the objects so obtained; direct sums of pure weights carry their weight grading. The actual \(H_1(B(\C),\Z)\) has no admissible presentation in this category. An explicit integral tensor automorphism on \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{adm}}(E)\) fails to extend naturally across the \(\Q\)-defined isogeny \(q:E\to B\).

For a full geometric abelian integral comparison as in E.2.9, the units \(\lambda_A\) are one common \(\lambda\in\widehat\Z^\times\), over all positive-dimensional abelian varieties and all Artin-selected embedding blocks. Fix \(\sigma\in\Gal(\Qb/F_{\mathrm{cm}})\) and prescribe its particular CM comparison \(\alpha\) from E.2.6. There is at most one extension of this prescribed comparison to the full geometric abelian integral diagram. Every such extension satisfies \[ T_A\otimes\widehat\Z=\rho_A(\sigma) \qquad\hbox{for every positive-dimensional abelian variety }A. \tag{E.2.14a} \]

There is an exact central extension of abstract groups \[ 1\longrightarrow\{1,w\}\longrightarrow \mathcal G_{\mathrm{ab},\Z}\longrightarrow I_{\mathrm{ab}} \longrightarrow1, \tag{E.2.15a} \] where \(w\) acts by \((-1)^m\) on every pure weight-\(m\) summand. Thus every Artin fibre has at most two elements. Let \(\Q^{\mathrm{tr}}\subset\R\) be the compositum of all finite totally real fields. Then \[ \Q^{\mathrm{cm}}=\Q^{\mathrm{tr}}(i),\qquad I_{\mathrm{ab}}\subset\Gal(\Qb/\Q^{\mathrm{tr}}). \tag{E.2.15b} \] Consequently each element of \(I_{\mathrm{ab}}\) restricts to either the identity or actual complex conjugation on the entire field \(\Q^{\mathrm{cm}}\), with one choice for all CM fields.

Let \(F_{\mathrm{cm}}\) be the field of E.2.6 and \(\Gamma_{F_{\mathrm{cm}}}=\Gal(\Qb/F_{\mathrm{cm}})\). For an abelian variety \(A/\Qb\), put \(\Lambda_A=H_1(A(\C),\Z)\), included in its profinite completion. Using the torsion comparison \(\kappa_{A,n}\) of E.2.9, define \[ \rho_A(\sigma): \Lambda_A\otimes\widehat\Z \longrightarrow\Lambda_{\sigma A}\otimes\widehat\Z . \] Then \[ I_{\mathrm{ab}}\cap\Gamma_{F_{\mathrm{cm}}} = \left\{\sigma\in\Gamma_{F_{\mathrm{cm}}}: \rho_A(\sigma)(\Lambda_A)=\Lambda_{\sigma A} \text{ for every }A/\Qb\right\}. \tag{E.2.16a} \] Inclusion of lattices in place of equality gives the same set. For each element of this set there are exactly two integral abelian lifts, differing by \(w\); the one whose CM restriction is the canonical comparison of E.2.6 is uniquely determined.

There is a specified \(\sigma\in\Gamma_{F_{\mathrm{cm}}}\) whose action on the quartic splitting field of E.2.6 is \((12)(34)\), and which is outside \(I_{\mathrm{ab}}\). For the explicit curve \[ E:y^2=x(x-1)(x-3) \] and a fixed integral Betti basis it satisfies \[ \rho_{E,5}(\sigma)= U(a):=\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\0&1\end{pmatrix}, \qquad a=\sum_{n\ge1}5^{n!}\in\Z_5\setminus\Q . \tag{E.2.17a} \] In particular this element is also excluded from the Artin image of the full pure integral diagram.

Put \[ D=\mu_2(\widehat\Z) =\{\lambda\in\widehat\Z^\times:\lambda^2=1\} =\prod_\ell\{1,-1\}, \] and define \[ \Sigma=\left\{\sigma\in\Gamma_{\Q^{\mathrm{cm}}}: \begin{array}{l} \text{there exists }\lambda\in D\text{ such that}\\ \lambda\rho_A(\sigma)(\Lambda_A)=\Lambda_{\sigma A} \text{ for every abelian variety }A/\Qb \end{array}\right\}. \tag{E.2.18a} \] For the concrete full geometric integral abelian diagram, \[ I_{\mathrm{ab}}=\Sigma\ \sqcup\ c\Sigma, \tag{E.2.18b} \] where \(c\) is actual complex conjugation. Inclusion of lattices in (E.2.18a) gives the same set. The sign pattern \(\lambda\) is unique modulo the one global sign \(\{1,-1\}\), and its class defines an abstract group homomorphism \[ \delta:\Sigma\longrightarrow \mu_2(\widehat\Z)/\{1,-1\}. \tag{E.2.18c} \] There are precisely two integral abelian lifts of each element of \(I_{\mathrm{ab}}\). On \(\Sigma\cap\Gamma_{F_{\mathrm{cm}}}\), the class \(\delta\) is trivial and the criterion is exactly E.2.16.

Every \(\sigma\in\Sigma\) of E.2.18 fixes every imaginary-quadratic ring class field pointwise. There nevertheless exists an actual \(\sigma\in\Gamma_{\Q^{\mathrm{cm}}}\), nontrivial on \(\Q(i)^{\mathrm{ab}}\), with an integral tensor comparison on the following precise diagram: all CM elliptic curves over \(\Qb\) with geometric endomorphism algebra \(\Q(i)\), all actual abelian variety lattices isogenous to products of those curves, their tensor constructions and specified summands, algebraic correspondences, and all Artin objects with every finite-model module map. The same construction respects labelled absolute-Hodge tensors in the abelian version. Its common scalar is \[ \lambda_5=-1,\qquad \lambda_\ell=1\quad(\ell\ne5), \tag{E.2.19a} \] which is not one global sign. No membership of this \(\sigma\) in the all-abelian group \(\Sigma\) is asserted.

The homomorphism \(\delta\) in E.2.18 is trivial. More precisely, an actual comparison on the full geometric CM/Artin diagram with Artin restriction in \(\Gamma_{\Q^{\mathrm{cm}}}\) and common scalar \(\lambda\in\prod_\ell\{1,-1\}\) forces \(\lambda\) to be one global \(1\) or \(-1\). Consequently E.2.18 becomes the exact criterion \[ \begin{split} \Sigma &=\{\sigma\in\Gamma_{\Q^{\mathrm{cm}}}: \rho_A(\sigma)(\Lambda_A)=\Lambda_{\sigma A} \text{ for every abelian variety }A/\Qb\},\\ I_{\mathrm{ab}}&=\Sigma\sqcup c\Sigma. \end{split} \tag{E.2.20a} \] The sign in E.2.19 is already excluded by two CM types of the explicit degree-eight field \[ L_{15}=\Q(\zeta_{15}+\zeta_{15}^{-1},i). \tag{E.2.20b} \]

Let \(I_{\mathrm{CM}}\) be the Artin image for the concrete geometric integral diagram generated by all CM abelian varieties over \(\Qb\), their actual isogeny lattices, specified tensor and summand lattices, labelled algebraic correspondences and all finite-model Artin algebra/module maps. The same assertion holds with the labelled absolute-Hodge tensors of the abelian version. Then \[ I_{\mathrm{CM}} =\Gamma_{F_{\mathrm{cm}}}\sqcup c\Gamma_{F_{\mathrm{cm}}}, \qquad F_{\mathrm{cm}}=\prod_{K\ {\rm CM}}K^{\mathrm{ab}}, \tag{E.2.21a} \] where the product denotes the compositum in \(\Qb\). Its Artin kernel consists of the identity and the global weight sign; each displayed fibre has exactly two elements. In particular every \(\sigma\in\Sigma\) fixes the full abelian extension of every imaginary-quadratic field, including all its ray class fields. Put \(X=\mathbf P^1_{\Q}\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}\), and retain the actual Betti lattices and comparison maps of E.2.21. For \(k=\Q(\alpha_1)\), they give a comparison between its two real embeddings sending \(\alpha_1\) to \(\alpha_1\) and \(\alpha_2\), on this entire diagram. Let \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{ell}}\) consist of all abelian varieties over \(\Qb\) geometrically isogenous to products of arbitrary elliptic curves and arbitrary CM abelian varieties. Let \(\mathcal A_{\leq3,\mathrm{CM}}\) consist of all abelian varieties over \(\Qb\) geometrically isogenous to products of simple factors of dimension at most three and arbitrary CM abelian varieties. Let \(X=\mathbf P^1(\C)\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}\), with basepoint \(1/2\), and let \(F=\pi_1^{\mathrm{top}}(X,1/2)=\langle x,y\rangle\), where \(x,y\) are the usual positive loops around \(0,1\). Put \(G=\widehat F\), identified with the geometric \'{e}tale fundamental group by the actual finite-cover comparison.
