Then there is a weak equivalence of based spaces \[ P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(S^3)\simeq \Omega\bigl(\mathrm{TOP}(4)/\mathrm O(4)\bigr), \tag{A.132.1} \] where $\mathrm{TOP}(4)=\operatorname{Homeo}(\mathbb R^4;0)$ is the actual group of global homeomorphisms, and the quotient on the right denotes $\operatorname{hofib}(B\mathrm O(4)\to B\mathrm{TOP}(4))$. In particular, \[ \pi_2 P_{\mathrm{PL}}(S^3)=0, \qquad \pi_2 P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(S^3)=\mathbb Z/2. \tag{A.132.2} \] Thus the natural real PL-to-TOP comparison is not a weak equivalence in unrestricted dimension. Both groups have trivial $\pi_0$ and $\pi_1$ in this example, so this discrepancy is genuinely a higher-parameter discrepancy.

Let $\mathcal M\preccurlyeq\mathcal N$ be an elementary extension of o-minimal structures in the same language, both expanding real closed fields. Let $B$ be a closed bounded definable manifold over $\mathcal M$. Then extension of definitions induces a weak equivalence of simplicial groups \[ P_{\mathrm{def},\mathcal M}(B) \longrightarrow P_{\mathrm{def},\mathcal N}(B_{\mathcal N}). \] The groups use homeomorphisms of the total product with a parameter simplex; they preserve that parameter, fix the bottom pointwise and preserve the free top. All defining parameters in the relevant structure are permitted. More generally, extension gives the same weak equivalence for the simplicial automorphism group of any closed bounded definable set with finitely many marked definable subsets, each required to be preserved setwise or fixed pointwise. If $B$ is given by a finite rational PL model, the square with the PL coefficient-extension map commutes. Hence the comparison from PL is a weak equivalence over $\mathcal M$ if and only if it is a weak equivalence over $\mathcal N$. Corresponding injectivity, surjectivity, or isomorphism assertions in each homotopy degree are equivalent as well.

Let $B$ be a compact real PL manifold without boundary, all of whose components have dimension at most two. The natural map from the simplicial group of jointly PL concordances to the singular complex of the compact-open topological concordance group is a weak equivalence: \[ P_{\mathrm{PL}}(B)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Sing}P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B). \tag{A.134.1} \] Both groups fix $B\times\{0\}$ pointwise and leave the top free. For components of dimension zero or one these spaces are weakly contractible. For every closed PL surface $F$, the natural comparison $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{PL}}(F)\to \operatorname{Sing}\operatorname{Homeo}(F)$ is a weak equivalence as well. Together with A.131, this gives the explicit recursive whole-space TOP model and recursive homotopy-group presentations in these base dimensions. The empty base has the one-element simplicial group. No statement about base dimension four, or about higher PL--semialgebraic comparison, is included here.

Let $B$ be a closed compact real PL four-manifold. All PL families below are jointly PL and preserve the parameter projection; all TOP spaces are replaced by their singular complexes. Set \[ \begin{aligned} A_C&=\operatorname{Aut}_C(B),\\ P_C&=\operatorname{Aut}_C(B\times I\text{ rel }B\times\{0\}),\\ H_C&=\operatorname{Aut}_C(B\times I\text{ rel }B\times\partial I), \qquad C\in\{\mathrm{PL},\mathrm{TOP}\}, \end{aligned} \] and let $F_A,F_P,F_H$ be the based homotopy fibres of the respective natural maps from PL to TOP, taken over the identity. Top restriction induces a map $F_P\to F_A$ with homotopy fibre \[ F_H\simeq \operatorname{Map}(B,K(\mathbb Z/2,1)). \tag{A.135.1} \] Here the mapping space is unbased, pointed by the constant map. Consequently there is a based homotopy-fibre sequence \[ \operatorname{Map}(B,K(\mathbb Z/2,1)) \longrightarrow F_P\longrightarrow F_A. \tag{A.135.2} \] In particular $\pi_jF_P\to\pi_jF_A$ is an isomorphism for $j\ge3$, and there is the exact segment \[ \begin{aligned} 0&\longrightarrow\pi_2F_P\longrightarrow\pi_2F_A \longrightarrow H^0(B;\mathbb Z/2)\\ &\longrightarrow\pi_1F_P\longrightarrow\pi_1F_A \longrightarrow H^1(B;\mathbb Z/2)\\ &\longrightarrow\pi_0F_P\longrightarrow\pi_0F_A. \end{aligned} \tag{A.135.3} \] The last line is understood with its usual pointed-set exactness. This identifies the fully boundary-fixed comparison fibre and reduces the free-top comparison to the ordinary four-manifold automorphism comparison. It does not assert that $F_A$ or $F_P$ is contractible, that the original comparison is surjective on components, or that all relative PL structures have the original PL isomorphism type. The connecting maps and any resulting extension data in (A.135.3) remain unevaluated; the abstract homotopy type of $F_A$ alone does not determine $F_P$.

For a closed compact real PL four-manifold $B$, use the based comparison fibres $F_A$ and $F_P$ of A.135. There is a specified map of based homotopy types \[ \beta_B:F_A\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}(B,K(\mathbb Z/2,2)) \tag{A.136.1} \] obtained by looping product with a line on sliced PL structures and then applying the open five-dimensional classification with its standard PL lift. It satisfies \[ F_P\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_0(\beta_B). \tag{A.136.2} \] In particular the last line of (A.135.3) extends to the exact pointed-set sequence \[ H^1(B;\mathbb Z/2)\longrightarrow\pi_0F_P \longrightarrow\pi_0F_A \xrightarrow{\pi_0\beta_B}H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2). \tag{A.136.3} \] The image of $\pi_0F_P$ consists exactly of the classes with zero obstruction $\pi_0\beta_B$. A class of $F_A$ represented by a PL automorphism $a$ and a TOP isotopy $\gamma$ from the identity to $a$ has obstruction equal to the relative PL-structure class of the cylinder homeomorphism $(x,u)\mapsto(\gamma_u(x),u)$, in $H^3(B\times I,B\times\partial I;\mathbb Z/2) =H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2)$, using the standard PL structure as origin. This describes all components and all higher homotopy groups of the \emph{based comparison fibre} in terms of the actual map $\beta_B$. It does not evaluate that map in general, determine the abstract four-manifold automorphism comparison, or determine the cokernel of $\pi_0P_{\mathrm{PL}}(B)\to\pi_0P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B)$. In particular it does not supply a model for TOP concordance components that have no PL representative. The homotopy type of $F_A$ alone is insufficient without $\beta_B$.

Let $B$ be a closed compact real PL four-manifold. Write $c_A:A_{\mathrm{PL}}\to A_{\mathrm{TOP}}$ and $c_P:P_{\mathrm{PL}}\to P_{\mathrm{TOP}}$ for the ordinary-family comparisons of A.135, and $e$ for top restriction. Define the subgroup \[ I_B=(\pi_0e)^{-1} \bigl(\operatorname{im}(\pi_0c_A)\bigr) \subseteq\pi_0P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B), \qquad J_B=\operatorname{im}(\pi_0\beta_B) \subseteq H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2), \tag{A.137.1} \] where $\beta_B$ is the map specified in A.136. There is a well-defined homomorphism \[ \lambda_B:I_B\longrightarrow H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2)/J_B \quad\hbox{such that}\quad \ker\lambda_B=\operatorname{im}(\pi_0c_P). \tag{A.137.2} \] No surjectivity of $\lambda_B$ is asserted. In particular $\operatorname{im}(\pi_0c_P)$ is normal in $I_B$ and \[ I_B/\operatorname{im}(\pi_0c_P) \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2)/J_B. \tag{A.137.2a} \] Thus this quotient is a finite elementary abelian $2$-group, of order at most $2^{\dim_{\mathbb Z/2}H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2)}$. Here is an explicit definition. Given $h\in P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B)$ whose component belongs to $I_B$, choose a TOP isotopy $\gamma$ from its top map $f=e(h)$ to a PL map $a$. Lift this endpoint change to a bottom-fixed isotopy of the cylinder and let $h_\gamma$ be its final composite with $h$, so that $e(h_\gamma)=a$. Put \[ \kappa(h_\gamma) =[\,(h_\gamma)_*\alpha_N\,]-[\,\alpha_N\,] \in H^3(N,\partial N;\mathbb Z/2) \cong H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2),\qquad N=B\times I, \tag{A.137.3} \] using the relative PL-structure classification with the standard structure $\alpha_N$ as origin. Then $\lambda_B([h])$ is the class of (A.137.3) modulo $J_B$. Product collars are imposed before taking the relative class. Consequently $h$ is TOP-isotopic, through bottom-fixed ordinary concordances with free top, to a PL concordance if and only if its top is TOP-isotopic to a PL map and the class (A.137.3) is zero modulo $J_B$. If $H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2)=0$, the endpoint condition is the only condition. The empty-base case has trivial groups throughout. This is a criterion for the complete image on components. It leaves both the ordinary four-dimensional endpoint-image predicate and $J_B$ unevaluated in general. It does not claim that vanishing of a stable boundary obstruction makes a four-dimensional homeomorphism isotopic to PL, or that every TOP concordance component is represented by a PL concordance.

Let $K$ be a closed bounded definable set in an o-minimal expansion of a real closed field $R$. Fix finitely many graph-formula formats and retain exactly the parameters defining homeomorphisms of $K$ with any prescribed finite list of definable marked-set or boundary conditions. Let $\mathcal H$ be the definable quotient by equality of the whole maps. For nonempty $K$ put \[ d(h,g)=\max_{x\in K}\|h(x)-g(x)\| +\max_{x\in K}\|h^{-1}(x)-g^{-1}(x)\|. \tag{A.138.1} \] Then $(\mathcal H,d)$ is definably homeomorphic to a definable subset of Euclidean space. For every $h_0\in\mathcal H$ and $\epsilon>0$, there are a definable $d$-open neighbourhood $U$ of $h_0$, a $\delta>0$ with $B_d(h_0,\delta)\subseteq U$, and a definable contraction $C:U\times I\to U$ such that \[ C(h,0)=h,\qquad C(h,1)=h_0,\qquad C(h_0,s)=h_0, \qquad U\subseteq B_d(h_0,\epsilon). \tag{A.138.2} \] Evaluation and inverse evaluation throughout this contraction are jointly definable and continuous. Thus it is a contraction through actual homeomorphisms satisfying the same marked conditions. The empty-set case is trivial. In contrast, if $p:[0,1]\to R$ is continuous and affine on at most $m$ intervals, where $m\ge1$ is an ordinary finite integer, then \[ \max_{x\in[0,1]}|x^2-p(x)|\ge\frac1{8m^2}. \tag{A.138.3} \] Over a non-Archimedean real closed field, a positive infinitesimal $\epsilon$ therefore admits no finite PL $\epsilon$-approximation of the semialgebraic homeomorphism $x\mapsto x^2$. Nevertheless this homeomorphism is semialgebraically isotopic to the identity relative to the two endpoints. The contraction neighbourhood in (A.138.2) depends on the fixed formula formats. The statement supplies neither a uniform contraction over the union of all formats nor a higher PL-to-semialgebraic concordance comparison.

For $n\ge2$, let \[ Y_n=\operatorname{hofib}\bigl(B\mathrm O(n)\longrightarrow B\mathrm{TOP}(n)\bigr), \qquad \mathrm{TOP}(n)=\operatorname{Homeo}(\mathbb R^n;0), \tag{A.139.1} \] where the homeomorphism group has its actual compact-open topology. For the ordinary bottom-fixed, free-top concordance space there is an equivalence \[ P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(S^n) \simeq\operatorname{hofib}_*\bigl(Y_n\longrightarrow Y_{n+1}\bigr), \tag{A.139.2} \] where the map is product with a line and all basepoints are standard. In particular \[ \pi_i P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(S^4)= \pi_i P_{\mathrm{PL}}(S^4)=0\qquad(0\le i\le3). \tag{A.139.3} \] For $i=0$ this means that the component set is a singleton. No assertion about $\pi_4$ is made. The model retains the finite-rank TOP groups; it is a sphere result and does not compute the general remaining low-dimensional concordance spaces.

Let $B$ be a connected closed oriented real PL four-manifold, and retain $I_B,J_B,\lambda_B$ and $c_P$ from A.137. Put $\pi=\pi_1(B)$ and let $\mathbb Z_{(2)}$ denote the integers localized at the prime $2$. Define \[ \begin{split} \delta_* &: H_2(B;\mathbb Z/2)\longrightarrow H_1(B;\mathbb Z_{(2)}),\\ L_B&=\mathrm{PD}_B^{-1}(\ker\delta_*) \subseteq H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2), \end{split} \tag{A.140.1} \] where $\delta_*$ is the Bockstein for $0\to\mathbb Z_{(2)}\xrightarrow{2}\mathbb Z_{(2)} \to\mathbb Z/2\to0$, and $\mathrm{PD}_B$ is mod-$2$ Poincar\'e duality. Suppose that the assembly summand of Orson--Powell--Randal-Williams, Definition~5.8, is zero: \[ I_2:H_2(\pi;\mathbb Z_{(2)}) \longrightarrow L^q_6(\mathbb Z[\pi])_{(2)}, \qquad I_2=0. \tag{A.140.2} \] Then \[ \operatorname{im}\lambda_B \supseteq (L_B+J_B)/J_B. \tag{A.140.3} \] In particular, if $H_1(B;\mathbb Z_{(2)})$ has no $2$-torsion, $\lambda_B$ is surjective and A.137 becomes the isomorphism \[ I_B/\operatorname{im}(\pi_0c_P) \cong H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2)/J_B. \tag{A.140.4} \] This does not evaluate the endpoint-image condition defining $I_B$ or the subgroup $J_B$ in general. If $B$ is simply connected, both of those restrictions disappear on the TOP concordance component group, and \[ \pi_0P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B)=1, \qquad J_B=H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2). \tag{A.140.5} \] There is the stronger ordinary-loop assertion. If $\gamma$ is a based TOP loop of automorphisms of $B$, let $T_\gamma(x,t)=(\gamma_t(x),t)$ and define \[ \eta_B:\pi_1 A_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B)\longrightarrow H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2), \qquad \eta_B[\gamma]=\kappa(T_\gamma). \tag{A.140.6} \] For simply connected $B$ this homomorphism is surjective and vanishes on the image of $\pi_1A_{\mathrm{PL}}(B)$. Consequently the ordinary automorphism comparison $A_{\mathrm{PL}}(B)\to A_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B)$ is not surjective on $\pi_1$ whenever $H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2)\ne0$. In particular this holds for the finite PL manifold $S^2\times S^2$. This last statement concerns automorphisms of the base; it is not an additional conclusion about the homotopy groups of $P_{\mathrm{PL}}(B)\to P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B)$. No computation of $\pi_0P_{\mathrm{PL}}(B)$, no smooth isotopy conclusion in dimension four, and no full higher TOP concordance computation is asserted.

Let $B$ be a connected closed oriented real PL four-manifold. Let $j:W\hookrightarrow B$ be a compact connected simply connected codimension-zero PL submanifold, with collared boundary. The boundary may be empty, in which case $W=B$. Write \[ j_!:H^2(W,\partial W;\mathbb Z/2) \longrightarrow H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2) \] for extension by zero, and write $\mathrm{PD}_W$ for relative Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality. For an ordinary based TOP loop $\gamma$ of automorphisms of $B$, define \[ \eta_B:\pi_1 A_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B)\longrightarrow H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2), \qquad \eta_B[\gamma]=\kappa_B(T_\gamma), \qquad T_\gamma(x,t)=(\gamma_t(x),t). \] This is the A.136 trace homomorphism, also displayed in (A.140.6); its definition does not require an assembly hypothesis. Retain $I_B,J_B,c_P$ from A.137. Then \[ \operatorname{im}\eta_B\supseteq\operatorname{im}j_! =\mathrm{PD}_B^{-1}\!\left( \operatorname{im}\bigl(j_*:H_2(W;\mathbb Z/2) \to H_2(B;\mathbb Z/2)\bigr)\right). \tag{A.141.1} \] Every class in the displayed subgroup is realized by an ordinary TOP loop on $B$ that is the identity outside $\operatorname{int}W$ and on one common collar of $\partial W$ throughout the loop. No assembly hypothesis on $\pi_1(B)$ is imposed. If $j_*$ on $H_2(-;\mathbb Z/2)$ is onto, then \[ \operatorname{im}\eta_B=J_B=H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2), \qquad \operatorname{im}(\pi_0c_P)=I_B. \tag{A.141.2} \] In that case the automorphism comparison $A_{\mathrm{PL}}(B)\to A_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B)$ fails to be surjective on $\pi_1$ whenever $H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2)\ne0$. In particular (A.141.2) holds for \[ B=C\mathbin{\#}D, \] where $C$ is a closed connected simply connected oriented PL four-manifold and $D$ is a closed connected oriented PL four-manifold with $H_2(D;\mathbb Z/2)=0$. It therefore holds for $C\mathbin{\#}\,k(S^1\times S^3)$ for every ordinary finite integer $k\ge0$. The equality $\operatorname{im}(\pi_0c_P)=I_B$ retains the endpoint condition: a TOP concordance component is in the PL image exactly when its top is TOP-isotopic to a PL automorphism. We do not assert that this endpoint condition is automatic for these nonsimply connected $B$, and do not compute either whole concordance space or $\pi_0P_{\mathrm{PL}}(B)$.

Let $B$ be a closed, connected, oriented real PL three-manifold whose fundamental group is finite cyclic of even order. There is a topological homeomorphism \[ F:B\times I\longrightarrow B\times I,\qquad F|_{B\times\{0,1\}}=1, \tag{G.1} \] whose component in the ordinary free-top concordance group $P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B)$ contains no PL concordance. In particular, \[ \pi_0P_{\mathrm{PL}}(\mathbb {RP}^3)\longrightarrow \pi_0P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(\mathbb {RP}^3) \quad\hbox{is not surjective}. \tag{G.2} \] For every fixed o-minimal expansion of the real field, the natural map $\pi_0P_{\mathrm{def}}(B)\to\pi_0P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B)$ is likewise not surjective. This includes the semialgebraic category. Here PL families are jointly PL, TOP families are jointly continuous, and every concordance fixes the bottom pointwise. The obstruction is a nonzero element of \[ H^3(B\times I,B\times\{0,1\};\mathbb Z/2) \cong H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2). \tag{G.3} \] No assertion that vanishing of this obstruction suffices for an unstabilized PL isotopy is made.

For every closed, connected real PL three-manifold $B$ there is a natural group homomorphism \[ c_B:\pi_0P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B)\longrightarrow H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2). \tag{C3.1} \] It vanishes on the image of $\pi_0P_{\mathrm{PL}}(B)$ and on the image of $\pi_0P_{\mathrm{def}}(B)$ for every fixed o-minimal expansion of $\mathbb R$. For a PL homeomorphism $f:B\to B'$, naturality is the typed identity \[ c_{B'}([(f\times1)H(f^{-1}\times1)]) =(f^{-1})^*c_B([H]). \tag{C3.1a} \] If $B$ is oriented and $\pi_1B$ is finite cyclic, then $c_B$ is surjective. In particular, when that cyclic group has even order, \[ \pi_0P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B)/\ker c_B\cong\mathbb Z/2, \qquad \operatorname{im}\bigl(\pi_0P_{\mathrm{def}}(B)\bigr) \subseteq\ker c_B. \tag{C3.2} \] Only this containment is asserted. The kernel is not identified with the PL or definable image, and no normality of that image in the whole TOP component group is claimed.

Let $B$ be a closed, connected, oriented real PL three-manifold with finite fundamental group. The homomorphism of A.143 is surjective: \[ c_B:\pi_0P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B)\longrightarrow H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2). \tag{144.1} \] Every class on the right is represented by a TOP concordance that is the identity on both ends. The image of the PL component map, and the image of the definable component map for every fixed real o-minimal expansion, lie in its kernel. No equality of either image with this kernel is asserted.

Let $B$ be a closed, connected real PL three-manifold; it need not be orientable. Let $W_1,\ldots,W_s\subset B$ be disjoint compact codimension-zero PL submanifolds. Suppose each $W_i$ is PL homeomorphic to $C_i\setminus\operatorname{int}D^3$, where $C_i$ is a closed, connected, oriented PL three-manifold with finite fundamental group. Write $j_i:W_i\hookrightarrow B$. Then \[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{im}c_B &\supset\sum_i(j_i)_!H^2(W_i,\partial W_i;\mathbb Z/2)\\ &=\operatorname{PD}_B^{-1} \left(\sum_i(j_i)_*H_1(W_i;\mathbb Z/2)\right). \end{aligned} \tag{145.1} \] Every term on the right is represented by a concordance supported in $W_i\times I$, equal to the identity in a neighborhood of its entire spatial and time boundary. In particular, for $B=C_1\#\cdots\#C_s\#D$, with these $C_i$ and any closed connected PL three-manifold $D$, the composite \[ \pi_0P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B)\xrightarrow{\,c_B\,}H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2) \xrightarrow{\,\operatorname{PD}_B\,}H_1(B;\mathbb Z/2) \longrightarrow\bigoplus_i H_1(C_i;\mathbb Z/2) \tag{145.2} \] is onto. Its kernel contains the PL and every real definable image. This specifies a quotient by that homomorphism's kernel; it does not identify the quotient by the PL image or all TOP components.

For the standard real PL torus $T^3$ the homomorphism of A.143 is zero: \[ c_{T^3}:\pi_0P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(T^3) \longrightarrow H^2(T^3;\mathbb Z/2), \qquad c_{T^3}=0. \tag{146.1} \] This is a computation of the obstruction homomorphism. It does not assert that every TOP concordance is PL-isotopic, or TOP-isotopic, to a PL concordance.

Fix an o-minimal expansion of the real field. Let \(B\) be a compact closed PL manifold, put \(N=B\times I\), and let \(k\geq1\). A class in \(\pi_kP_{\mathrm{def}}(B)\) belongs to the image of \[ \pi_kP_{\mathrm{PL}}(B)\longrightarrow\pi_kP_{\mathrm{def}}(B) \tag{147.1} \] if and only if it has a based definable representative \(U:N\times P\to N\), \(P=[0,1]^k\), for which a constant \(L<\infty\) satisfies \[ \|U_p(x)-U_q(x)\|_\infty\leq L\|p-q\|_\infty \quad(x\in N,\ p,q\in P). \tag{147.2} \] Here \(U_p\) fixes \(B\times\{0\}\) pointwise, preserves the top end, and \(U_p=\operatorname{id}\) for \(p\in\partial P\). Only the forward parameter estimate is assumed. In particular, real semialgebraic \(\pi_2P_{\mathrm{PL}}(T^6)\to\pi_2P_{\mathrm{SA}}(T^6)\) is surjective exactly when each based semialgebraic two-cube is based semialgebraically homotopic to one satisfying (147.2). This criterion does not itself assert existence of such representatives.

Keep the real-field and fixed o-minimal structure conventions of A.147. Let \(B\) be a compact closed PL manifold, and put \(N=B\times I\), \(A_j=B\times\{j\}\), \(P=I^k\), \(k\ge1\). Suppose \(r,s:N\times P\to N\) are continuous definable families of homeomorphisms, each preserving \(A_0,A_1\) setwise and each uniformly Lipschitz in the forward parameter variable. Suppose \[ r_p|_{A_0}=s_p|_{A_0}\quad(p\in P),\qquad r_p=s_p\quad(p\in\partial P). \tag{148.1} \] Then \(U_p=s_pr_p^{-1}\) is a based bottom-fixed cube and is based definably homotopic, through bottom-fixed homeomorphisms, to a jointly PL cube. Consequently the comparison image consists exactly of classes admitting a representative with such a relative factorization. Real semialgebraic \(T^6,\pi_2\) surjectivity is equivalent to every based semialgebraic two-cube being based semialgebraically homotopic to one admitting such a factorization with both forward parameter bounds.

Work in any fixed o-minimal expansion of the real field. Let $Z\subset\mathbb R^n$ be compact and definable, and let $F:[0,1]\times Z\to\mathbb R$ be continuous and definable. Suppose that for one $L\ge0$, \[ |F(t,z)-F(t,z')|\le L\|z-z'\|_2 \quad(t\in[0,1],\ z,z'\in Z). \tag{150.1} \] Given any finite set of prescribed times in $[0,1]$, there is an increasing definable homeomorphism $h:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ fixing those times, and a finite $K\ge0$, such that \[ |F(h(s),z)-F(h(s'),z')| \le K|s-s'|+L\|z-z'\|_2. \tag{150.2} \] In particular the reparameterized family is uniformly Lipschitz in its scalar parameter. Consequently, if $A_t$ is a Hausdorff-continuous definable family of nonempty compact sets contained in one fixed compact box in $\mathbb R^n$, then such an $h$, fixing the same prescribed finite times, makes \[ d_H(A_{h(s)},A_{h(s')})\le K|s-s'|. \tag{150.3} \] This consequence concerns the Hausdorff distance of the sets. It does not construct homeomorphic point matching between them.

Work over the real field. Put \[ C=\partial[-1,1]^2,\quad B=C^d\ (d\ge1),\quad X=B\times[-1,1],\quad P=[-1,1]^2. \] There is an explicit jointly continuous semialgebraic family $U_p:X\to X$ with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item Every $U_p$ and its inverse are spatially Lipschitz with one uniform Euclidean constant strictly less than $2$. They are the identity on both outer half-interval collars in the last coordinate. \item The family is the identity at $p=0$ and on $\partial P$, and has an explicit semialgebraic nullhomotopy relative to those parameters and the spatial boundary. \item No homeomorphism $h:P\to P$, even a nondefinable TOP homeomorphism, makes $p\mapsto\Gamma U_{h(p)}$ Lipschitz in the Euclidean Hausdorff metric. \item For no such $h$ can one write $U_{h(p)}=s_pr_p^{-1}$ with two families of homeomorphisms of $X$ that are both uniformly forward parameter-Lipschitz. This impossibility does not require the factors to be definable or to preserve any marks. \item There is a noninjective Lipschitz semialgebraic $g:P\to P$, equal to the identity on $\partial P$ and at $0$, such that $U\circ g$ is uniformly forward parameter-Lipschitz. The straight homotopy from the identity to $g$ gives the allowed based homotopy from $U$ to this representative. \end{enumerate} In particular the example is available on the literal PL six-torus $B=C^6$. It obstructs a homeomorphic reparameterization or an exact factorization of the given representative; it is not an obstruction to the homotopy regularization established later.

Work over the real field in any one fixed o-minimal expansion. All compact-set families below have bounded definable incidence sets, nonempty compact fibres, and are continuous in Hausdorff distance. Use maximum norms on finite-dimensional coordinate spaces. For a based PL sphere \(\Sigma^k=\partial[-1,1]^{k+1}\), \(k\ge1\), and such a family \(C_p\), there is a definable Lipschitz map \(g:\Sigma^k\to\Sigma^k\), based definably homotopic to the identity, such that \(C_{g(p)}\) is Hausdorff-Lipschitz. For \(P=[-1,1]^k\), if \(C|_{\partial P}\) is Hausdorff-Lipschitz, there is a definable Lipschitz \(g:P\to P\), equal to the identity on \(\partial P\), such that \(C_g\) is Hausdorff-Lipschitz. The convex homotopy \((1-t)\operatorname{id}+tg\) is relative to \(\partial P\). Consequently any based jointly definable homeomorphism cube \(U\) on a compact definable \(F\) has a based definable homotopy to \(V_p=U_{g(p)}\) with Hausdorff-Lipschitz graphs, preserving all spatial conditions of the original family. No injectivity or cell-likeness of \(g\), and no homeomorphic graph matching, is asserted.

For a compact closed PL manifold \(B\) over the real field, put \(N=B\times I\), \(A_j=B\times\{j\}\), and let \(k\ge1\). The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item \(\pi_kP_{\rm PL}(B)\to\pi_kP_{\mathcal R}(B)\) is surjective. \item Every based definable bottom-fixed cube \(V\) whose graphs are Hausdorff-Lipschitz is based definably homotopic to \(W_p=s_pr_p^{-1}\), where \(r,s\) are jointly definable continuous homeomorphism families preserving \(A_0,A_1\) setwise, both uniformly forward parameter-Lipschitz, equal on \(A_0\times I^k\), and equal on \(N\times\partial I^k\). \end{enumerate}

Let \(M\) be a fixed o-minimal expansion of a real closed field whose complete theory has a real model, and let \(B\) be a closed compact PL manifold over \(M\). Write \(N=B\times I\) and \(P=I^k\), \(k\geq1\). The following sufficient conditions place a based definable concordance class in the image of \(\pi_kP_{\rm PL}(B)\to\pi_kP_{\rm def}(B)\). \begin{enumerate} \item It has a representative \(V\) with a uniform forward parameter Lipschitz bound: \[ \|V_p(x)-V_q(x)\|_\infty\leq L\|p-q\|_\infty \quad(x\in N,\ p,q\in P) \] for an element \(L\) of the field. \item It has a representative \(s_pr_p^{-1}\), where \(r,s\) are joint definable families of homeomorphisms of \(N\), preserve both ends setwise, agree on the bottom and on the parameter boundary, and have uniform forward parameter Lipschitz bounds. \end{enumerate} Conversely, every class in the PL image has representatives satisfying both conditions. No bound on either inverse is required.

Under the hypotheses on \(M,B,N,P\) in A.149, every based definable concordance family \(U\) is definably homotopic, through based concordance families, to a family \(V\) whose compact graphs are uniformly Lipschitz in the Hausdorff metric. Thus there is an \(L\in M\) such that \[ d_H(\Gamma V_p,\Gamma V_q)\leq L\|p-q\|_\infty \quad(p,q\in P). \]

Let $M$ be an o-minimal real closed field, let $X$ be a compact finite PL polyhedron, and fix finitely many marked subpolyhedra. Let $P=[0,1]^k$ and let $U_p:X\to X$ be a jointly continuous definable family of homeomorphisms preserving the marks and equal to the identity for $p\in\partial P$. There are jointly continuous definable families of homeomorphisms $r_p,s_p$, preserving the marks and equal to the identity on $\partial P$, such that \[ U_p=s_pr_p^{-1}, \tag{154.1} \] and both families have one common uniform spatial Lipschitz bound. If $U$ fixes a marked subpolyhedron pointwise, the two factors agree there. The construction uses any fixed finite target dimension. If $M$ is an o-minimal expansion of the real field and $B$ is a closed compact PL manifold, then \[ \pi_kP_{\rm PL}(B)\longrightarrow\pi_kP_{\rm def}(B) \quad\hbox{is surjective for every }k\ge1. \tag{154.2} \] No injectivity assertion follows from this theorem alone.

Over any fixed o-minimal expansion of the real field, let \(B\) be a compact closed PL manifold of dimension at most \(2\), or of dimension at least \(5\). Then both maps in \[ P_{\mathrm{PL}}(B)\longrightarrow P_{\mathrm{def}}(B) \longrightarrow P_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B) \tag{155.1} \] are weak homotopy equivalences. More generally, let \(M\) be an o-minimal expansion of a real closed field whose complete theory has an o-minimal model expanding the real field. For every compact closed PL manifold \(B\) over \(M\), the map \[ \pi_kP_{\mathrm{PL}}(B)\longrightarrow\pi_kP_{\mathrm{def}}(B) \tag{155.2} \] is surjective for every \(k\geq1\), and it is bijective for \(k=0\). In particular this surjectivity statement applies to the semialgebraic category over every real closed field. The transfer assertion here is a surjectivity assertion; no transfer of positive-degree injectivity is inferred from a path of PL coefficient data.

Fix an o-minimal expansion of $\mathbb R$, a closed compact PL manifold $B$, and $N=B\times I$. Let $P=[0,1]^m$, $m\ge1$, and let $U_p:N\to N$ be a jointly continuous definable family of homeomorphisms fixing $A_0=B\times\{0\}$ pointwise and preserving $A_1=B\times\{1\}$ setwise. If its restriction to $N\times\partial P$ is jointly PL, there is a jointly PL family $W$ with the same spatial constraints and \[ W_p=U_p\quad(p\in\partial P). \tag{156.1} \] Consequently $P_{\rm PL}(B)\to P_{\rm def}(B)$ is a weak equivalence for every such real $B$, including dimensions three and four. This does not identify its comparison with the whole ordinary TOP concordance space.

Let \(M\) be any o-minimal expansion of a real closed field. All sets, maps, homotopies, compactness assertions, and products below are definable over \(M\). Here compact means definably compact. Let \(f:K\to Y\) be a continuous surjection between compact definable sets. If \(Y\ne\varnothing\) and \(d=\dim Y\), there are a compact definable set \(R\), a continuous surjection \(q:R\to Y\), an integer \(1\le m\le d+1\), and a continuous map \[ \ell:R\longrightarrow J_m(f),\qquad \pi\ell=q, \tag{157.1} \] where \(J_m(f)\) is the labelled \(m\)-fold fibrewise join of \(f\). The map \(q\) is universally a definable homotopy equivalence: for every continuous map \(T\to Y\) from a compact definable set, \(R\times_YT\to T\) is a definable homotopy equivalence. If \(Z\subset Y\) is closed and \(b:Z\to J_a(f)\) is a continuous section of its join projection, the resolution can be enlarged to a compact \(R'\) containing \(Z\) as a closed subspace, with \(q'|_Z=\operatorname{id}_Z\), a universal homotopy equivalence \(q':R'\to Y\), and a map \[ \ell':R'\longrightarrow J_{m+a}(f),\qquad \pi\ell'=q',\qquad \ell'|_Z=b \tag{157.2} \] (the last equality uses the last \(a\) slots). In particular, for \(Y=P=[0,1]^k\), \(Z=\partial P\), there is a continuous definable \(w:P\to J_{m+a}(f)\) with \(w|_{\partial P}=b\), and \(\pi w\) is definably homotopic to \(\operatorname{id}_P\) relative to \(\partial P\). For the following metric consequence impose an additional hypothesis, which is not supplied by the topological assertion. Suppose \(C_p\), \(p\in P\), is a bounded Hausdorff-continuous definable family of nonempty compact subsets of a fixed \(M^n\). Suppose there is a compact definable \(K\) and a Lipschitz surjection \(\phi:K\to P\) such that \(s\mapsto C_{\phi(s)}\) is Hausdorff-Lipschitz. If the boundary family \(C|_{\partial P}\) is Hausdorff-Lipschitz, there is a definable Lipschitz map \(g:P\to P\), equal to the identity on \(\partial P\), such that \(p\mapsto C_{g(p)}\) is Hausdorff-Lipschitz. The convex homotopy from \(\operatorname{id}_P\) to \(g\) fixes \(\partial P\). This consequence holds over every \(M\) as above, conditional on the displayed Lipschitz-resolution hypothesis; it does not silently extend the real-field theorem of Kocel--Cynk, Pawlucki, and Valette.

Let \(M\) be an arbitrary o-minimal expansion of a real closed field, let \(P\subset[0,1]^k\) be a nonempty compact definable set, and let \[ F:P\times[0,1]^n\longrightarrow[0,1]^r \] be continuous and definable. Use maximum norms. Suppose \[ \|F(p,x)-F(p,x')\|_\infty\le K_0\|x-x'\|_\infty \quad(p\in P,\ x,x'\in[0,1]^n) \tag{158.1} \] for some \(K_0\in M_{\ge0}\). There are standard integers \(J,D,C_\phi,C\), a compact set \[ K=\{1,\ldots,J\}\times[0,1]^D, \] and a continuous definable surjection \(\phi:K\to P\), such that \(\phi\) is \(C_\phi\)-Lipschitz and \[ (z,x)\longmapsto F(\phi(z),x) \quad\hbox{is }C(1+K_0)\hbox{-Lipschitz}. \tag{158.2} \] The standard integers may depend on the given definable family; no uniformity across all formulas or all parameter values of an additional unfixed family is claimed. Consequently every Hausdorff-continuous definable family of nonempty compact subsets \(C_p\subset[0,1]^n\), with compact definable parameter set \(P\subset[0,1]^k\), has a compact Lipschitz resolution with standard integer projection and Hausdorff constants. Combined with A.157, this gives relative Hausdorff-Lipschitz regularization on a parameter cube over every o-minimal real closed field: if the boundary family is Hausdorff-Lipschitz, there is a definable Lipschitz \(g:[0,1]^k\to[0,1]^k\), equal to the identity on the boundary, such that \(C_{g(p)}\) is Hausdorff-Lipschitz. The convex homotopy from the identity to \(g\) fixes the boundary.

Let $M$ be any fixed o-minimal expansion of a real closed field, let $B$ be a closed compact PL manifold over $M$, and put $N=B\times I$. Then \[ \pi_k P_{\mathrm{PL}}(B)\longrightarrow \pi_k P_{\mathrm{def}}(B) \quad\hbox{is surjective for every }k\geq1. \tag{159.1} \] Together with A.113 this gives the component bijection and surjectivity in every positive degree. This statement does not assert injectivity in positive degrees over an arbitrary nonreal model. The sufficient regularity criteria of A.147 and A.148 are valid over $M$ when applied on a fixed standard PL model and the forward parameter Lipschitz bounds are bounded by ordinary finite integers. In the pair criterion, the factors preserve both spatial ends setwise and agree on the bottom and on the parameter boundary. Their quotient is then definably homotopic, through based bottom-fixed concordance families, to a jointly PL family. No metric bound on either inverse is required.

Let $M$ be any fixed o-minimal expansion of a real closed field, and let $B$ be a closed compact PL manifold over $M$. Then \[ P_{\mathrm{PL}}(B)\longrightarrow P_{\mathrm{def}}(B) \tag{160.1} \] is a weak equivalence. The statement compares finite jointly PL parameter families with finite jointly definable parameter families. It does not identify either space with the whole ordinary TOP concordance space in exceptional dimensions, nor does it by itself compute their homotopy type.

Let \(M\) be any fixed o-minimal expansion of a real closed field, let \(B\) be a closed definably compact definable manifold, and choose a definable triangulation \(\tau:|K|_M\to B\) with \(K\) a finite abstract PL manifold. Let \(G=G^{\rm PL}(K)\) be the explicitly coded simplicial group of A.131. Then there is a specified weak equivalence \[ G\longrightarrow P_{\rm def,M}(B). \tag{161.1} \] It is the composite of real-algebraic coefficient extension, PL inclusion, and conjugation by \(\tau\times\operatorname{id}_I\). In particular, for every \(r\geq0\) the complete recursive presentation \(\Pi_r^{\rm PL}(K)\) of A.131 presents \(\pi_rP_{\rm def,M}(B)\). For \(r=0\) this computes the full component group. For positive \(r\) it is based at the identity, with the other components obtained by translation. For the real realization \(|K|_{\mathbb R}\), the same effective model also computes TOP concordances whenever every component has dimension outside three and four. The algorithm takes only the finite complex \(K\), not a decision procedure or an oracle for the elementary theory of \(M\). The output is the complete countable simplicial model and complete recursively enumerable group presentations. It does not assert a terminating word problem or a finite invariant-factor decomposition.

Let $D=D^4$ be the closed unit ball, $S=\partial D=S^3$, and let $\iota(x)=-x$. Put \[ H=\operatorname{Homeo}_{\iota}(D),\qquad A=\operatorname{Homeo}_{\iota}(S), \] with their compact-open topologies. Every member of $H$ fixes the unique fixed point $0$ of $\iota$. All groups below include every orientation component. Define a simplicial group $\mathcal G_{\iota}$ of \emph{joint germs} as follows. A $q$-simplex is the germ along $\Delta^q\times\{0\}$ of a continuous fibre-preserving homeomorphism between neighborhoods of that zero section in $\Delta^q\times\mathbb R^4$, fixing the zero section pointwise and commuting with $\iota$ in each fibre. Two representatives are equivalent only when they agree on a neighborhood of the \emph{entire} zero section. By compactness a representative and its inverse can be restricted to uniform balls on the relevant side. The face and degeneracy maps are parameter pullbacks. In particular, equality of two simplices is stronger than pointwise equality of all their individual germs. \textbf{Fibre model.}\quad The restriction map \[ q:\operatorname{Sing}H\longrightarrow\mathcal G_{\iota} \tag{A.162.1} \] is a Kan fibration and is onto vertices. Its strict fibre over the identity is weakly equivalent to $\operatorname{Sing}P_{\rm TOP}(\mathbb {RP}^3)$. Boundary restriction and radial coning give $H\simeq A$. Consequently, with the cone-germ map on the right, there is a natural weak equivalence \[ P_{\rm TOP}(\mathbb {RP}^3) \simeq_w\operatorname{hofib}\bigl(A\longrightarrow|\mathcal G_{\iota}|\bigr). \tag{A.162.2} \] Using the ordinary three-dimensional comparison and the generalized Smale conjecture for $\mathbb {RP}^3$, this becomes \[ P_{\rm TOP}(\mathbb {RP}^3) \simeq_w\operatorname{hofib}\bigl(O(4)\longrightarrow|\mathcal G_{\iota}|\bigr) \simeq_w\Omega|\mathcal G_{\iota}/\operatorname{Sing}O(4)|. \tag{A.162.3} \] No topology on a set of individual germs is being substituted for the specified simplicial model. In particular, no unproved comparison between that model and a naive direct-limit topology is used. Let $\mathcal G_4$ denote the same joint-germ construction without the oddness condition. The linear subgroup splits the forgetting map on based fundamental groups, and there is a natural group isomorphism \[ \pi_0P_{\rm TOP}(\mathbb {RP}^3) \cong \ker\!\left(\pi_1|\mathcal G_\iota| \longrightarrow\pi_1|\mathcal G_4|\right). \] In particular, the full component group is abelian. The kernel on the right is not evaluated here. The statement does not identify the PL image in it or prove zero-Casson--Sullivan sufficiency.

Let $B$ be a closed connected oriented real PL four-manifold which is aspherical, and put $\pi=\pi_1B$ and $N=B\times I$. Write \[ H_C=\operatorname{Aut}_C(N\operatorname{ rel}\partial N), \qquad C\in\{\mathrm{PL},\mathrm{TOP}\}. \] PL families are jointly PL and preserve their parameter projection. TOP groups have their compact-open topology and are replaced by their singular complexes when taking comparison fibres. All homotopy groups below are based at the identity. Assume $\operatorname{Wh}(\pi)=0$. Let \[ A_j:H_j(B;\mathbb L\langle1\rangle) \longrightarrow L_j(\mathbb Z[\pi]) \tag{A.163.1} \] be the quadratic surgery assembly maps, with the orientation character trivial and the decoration used by the geometric surgery sequence. The Whitehead-group hypothesis removes the simple versus homotopy decoration distinction needed here. No assembly isomorphism is assumed without being stated. If $A_7$ is injective, then \[ \ker\{\pi_0H_{\mathrm{PL}}\longrightarrow\pi_0H_{\mathrm{TOP}}\} \cong H^1(B;\mathbb Z/2). \tag{A.163.2} \] This is an isomorphism of groups, using the natural relative structure boundary map. If also $A_8$ is injective, there is an exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow H^0(B;\mathbb Z/2) \longrightarrow\pi_1H_{\mathrm{PL}} \longrightarrow\pi_1H_{\mathrm{TOP}}\longrightarrow0, \tag{A.163.3} \] and the comparison is an isomorphism on $\pi_j$ for every $j\ge2$. No splitting of (A.163.3) is asserted. Suppose in addition that $A_6$ is injective and every element of $Z(\pi)$ is the evaluation class of a based jointly PL loop of automorphisms of $B$. Then the comparison on $\pi_0H$ is onto, so (A.163.2) extends to \[ 0\longrightarrow H^1(B;\mathbb Z/2) \longrightarrow\pi_0H_{\mathrm{PL}} \longrightarrow\pi_0H_{\mathrm{TOP}}\longrightarrow0. \tag{A.163.4} \] The central evaluation hypothesis is automatic when $Z(\pi)=0$. Under these additional assumptions the ordinary-loop contribution \[ \eta_B:\pi_1\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{TOP}}(B) \longrightarrow\pi_0F_A \xrightarrow{\pi_0\beta_B}H^2(B;\mathbb Z/2) \tag{A.163.5} \] from A.136 is zero. In fact it is enough in (A.163.5) that the evaluation class of the loop in question be represented by a jointly PL loop. For the standard $T^4$, all the stated hypotheses hold. Thus its fully boundary-fixed component comparison has kernel $(\mathbb Z/2)^4$ and is surjective; its fundamental-group comparison is surjective with kernel $\mathbb Z/2$, and its comparisons in degrees at least two are isomorphisms. Also $\eta_{T^4}=0$. More generally, the assembly and Whitehead-group hypotheses for (A.163.2)--(A.163.3) hold for every such $B$ whose fundamental group is word-hyperbolic or acts properly, cocompactly and isometrically on a finite-dimensional CAT(0) space. Thus the stated relative kernel, fundamental-group exact sequence, and higher isomorphisms hold on this entire explicitly specified class. The extra conclusion (A.163.4) still requires the stated realization of central elements by PL loops; it holds in particular when the centre is trivial. These statements concern the fully boundary-fixed cylinder and the ordinary-loop part of $\beta_B$. They do not compute the free-top comparison fibre $F_P$, the whole map $\beta_B$, or the endpoint-image condition in A.137.

There is a semialgebraic Hausdorff-continuous family of strict cone neighborhoods of the origin in a fixed square, each a PL disk, whose outer faces admit no jointly continuous local parameterization at one parameter value. Both the disks and their outer faces are Hausdorff continuous. Thus Hausdorff continuity cannot replace the joint-face hypothesis of A.117. This does not decide whether the six-torus loop can be filled in the weaker Hausdorff-only model.

Let $f:X\to K_{\ge0}$ be definable and continuous, with $X$ compact and $Y=f^{-1}(0)$. For all sufficiently small positive $\epsilon$, $V=f^{-1}([0,\epsilon])$ is a strict tubular neighborhood and has a $Y$-admissible rigidification with outer face $B=f^{-1}(\epsilon)$. More generally, any strict tubular neighborhood in the sense of 119/151, whose quotient by $Y$ is a definable rigid cone, admits a $Y$-admissible rigidification, possibly different from the initial cone rigidification. For a fixed pair $(V,B)$, the homotopy class of $\varphi:B\to Y$ is independent of the admissible rigidification.

The requirement at 119/152 \[ \dim\varphi^{-1}(y)=\dim_yX-\dim_yY-1 \tag{A.2.1} \] cannot always be met by a $Y$-admissible rigidification. It fails even for a compact semialgebraic nowhere dense $Y$ in the smooth compact three-manifold $X=S^3$, with $Y\subset\overline{X\setminus Y}$. For a locally trivial conical bundle over a pure-dimensional manifold $Y$, the equality does hold, with the dimension of the fibre link. The equality alone does not imply the categorical uniqueness asserted on the page.

The collapse functor in 119/152 from a bordant pair with a locally trivial boundary map $B\to Y$ to an equisingular pair $(X,Y)$ is not an equivalence for all definable homeomorphisms. It already fails when $Y$ is one point. There is an exact corrected equivalence if the target retains a mapping-cylinder neighborhood and its full product ruling, and morphisms preserve that ruling and the boundary bundle map. This correction holds for any specified locally trivial definable bundle $B\to Y$.

There is a compact semialgebraic subset $X\subset\R^4$ with two closed filtrations, each having regular layers of dimensions $0,1,2$, which have no common coarsening with regular layers. Thus the weak interpretation of the coarsest-filtration claim at 119/153 is false, both for embedded smooth regularity and for intrinsic PL regularity.

Let $X$ be a definable set in a fixed o-minimal expansion of a real closed field, and let $\Phi$ be a finite family of closed definable subsets of $X$. There is a unique coarsest finite partition $\mathcal P(X;\Phi)$ satisfying the following requirements: its strata are locally closed PL manifolds, each of a single dimension; each stratum closure is a union of strata; the sets in $\Phi$ are unions of strata; and for every closed union $Y$ of strata, the non-PL-manifold locus $\operatorname{Sing}_{\rm PL}(Y)$ is a union of strata. Dimension may differ between strata. One may instead require connected strata (definably connected over a general real closed field); this class also has a unique coarsest partition. Both versions are preserved by definable homeomorphisms of the marked data $(X;\Phi)$. Their dimension filtration \[ X_{\le k}=\bigcup_{\substack{S\in\mathcal P(X;\Phi)\\\dim S\le k}}S \quad(-1\le k\le\dim X) \] is closed and canonical, with pure-dimensional PL-manifold layers after empty layers are omitted. If a closed filtration $\varnothing=Y_{-1}\subset Y_0\subset\cdots\subset Y_s=X$ is given, take $\Phi=\{Y_0,\ldots,Y_s\}$ and insert, in lexicographic order, the closed sets \[ E_{j,k}=Y_{j-1}\cup(Y_j\cap X_{\le k}), \qquad 0\le j\le s,\quad -1\le k\le\dim X. \] Omitting repetitions gives a canonical regular equidimensional filtration compatible with the preassigned one. The coarseness assertion concerns the stated class of partitions; it is not the false least-fine assertion among all weak filtrations.

Replacing intrinsic PL regularity in A.205 by embedded smooth regularity gives the semialgebraic coarsest partitions of A.303--304, but does not give invariants under arbitrary definable homeomorphisms. It does give naturality under isomorphisms preserving the embedded smooth loci of every closed definable subset, for example ambient smooth diffeomorphisms.

Let $Y$ be a closed compact definable manifold, let $X=Y\times[0,2]$, and fix the strict tube $V=Y\times[0,1]$, with core $Y\times\{0\}$ and identified outer face $B=Y\times\{1\}$. The simplicial space of $Y$-admissible rigidifications of this fixed tube satisfying \[ \dim\varphi^{-1}(y)=\operatorname{codim}_y(Y,X)-1=0 \quad\text{for every }y\in Y \] is naturally isomorphic, after interval reversal, to $P_{\rm def}(Y)$. Consequently the proposed dimension condition fails to give essential uniqueness even when the tube and its outer-face identification are fixed. For $Y=(S^1)^6$ this space has the nonzero component group of A.103.

Let $V$ be a compact definable manifold with boundary, let $Y$ be a union of boundary components, and let $B$ be a compact definable set. Suppose a continuous definable map \[ q:B\times[0,1]\longrightarrow V \] has $q(b,0)=\varphi(b)\in Y$ and restricts to a homeomorphism $B\times(0,1]\to V\setminus Y$. Then $\varphi$ is onto, and every fibre $\varphi^{-1}(y)$ is definably contractible. Over $\mathbb R$, the same neighborhood argument without definability shows that all fibres are cell-like when $B$ is a compact ANR. Thus all unrestricted attachment maps for the product tube in A.207 are cell-like, and their definable fibres are actual contractible compact polyhedra up to definable homeomorphism.

Let $Y=(S^1)^6$, let $V=Y\times[0,1]$, and fix its core $Y\times\{0\}$ and outer face $B=Y\times\{1\}$. Let $\mathcal R$ be the space of all continuous maps $q:Y\times[0,1]\to V$ satisfying \[ q(y,1)=(y,1),\qquad q(Y\times\{0\})\subset Y\times\{0\}, \qquad q|_{Y\times(0,1]}:Y\times(0,1]\xrightarrow{\sim} V\setminus(Y\times\{0\}). \] Give it the compact-open topology. Its homeomorphic-attachment subspace is $G=\Homeo(V\ \mathrm{rel}\ B)$, the top-fixed concordance space. There is a locally constant map \[ \lambda:\mathcal R\longrightarrow\pi_0G \quad\text{with}\quad\lambda(g)=[g]\quad(g\in G), \] where $\pi_0G$ is discrete. In particular $\pi_0G\to\pi_0\mathcal R$ is injective, so $\mathcal R$ is not contractible and not even path connected. The same counterexample applies to jointly continuous definable families in any o-minimal expansion of $\mathbb R$. It also applies to semialgebraic families over every real closed field, with a fixed finite PL representative of the two distinct rigidifications. Thus essential uniqueness in the full fixed-tube sense fails; no fibre-dimension restriction is needed for this failure. The tube is a strict tube in $X=Y\times[0,2]$.

If the symbol $R$ denotes an ordered real closed field with its order topology, the simultaneous requirements M0 and M9 of cote 120 are inconsistent. Consequently M0--M11 with unary finiteness cannot, as one simultaneous axiom system, characterize compact definable sets of structures with o-minimal open core.

Let $K$ be a real closed field, $X$ a set, $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal P(X)$, and $j:X\hookrightarrow K^m$ an injection. Form the smallest all-arity family $\mathcal D=(\mathcal D_n)$ containing all semialgebraic sets over $K$ and the predicates $j(A)$ for every $A\in\mathcal F$, and closed under finite Boolean operations, products, coordinate permutations and coordinate projections. There is an o-minimal expansion of the ordered field $K$ in which $j(X)$ is definable and its definable subsets are exactly $j(\mathcal F)$ if and only if \[ \begin{gathered} X\in\mathcal F,\qquad \mathcal D_1=\{\text{finite unions of points and intervals in }K\}, \\ \{D\cap j(X):D\in\mathcal D_m\}=j(\mathcal F). \end{gathered} \] Here parameters from $K$ are allowed. If one-space topology is part of the data, $j$ must in addition be a homeomorphism onto its image. The criterion applies whether or not the one-space finite-dimension axiom $(e_n)$ is initially imposed. It neither derives the missing coordinates from $(e_n)$ nor substitutes that bound for the all-arity and trace tests.

A definable realization of dimension $d$ satisfies the one-space axiom $(e_d)$ when ``rare'' means nowhere dense. Over a real closed field which is not Dedekind complete, ordinary connected-component finiteness instead of definable connected-component finiteness forces every definable realization in a finite Cartesian power of the field to be finite.

Let $X\subset\R^N$ be semialgebraic and let $\Phi$ be a finite family of semialgebraic subsets. Assume the standard semialgebraic facts that finite families admit finite smooth frontier partitions and that the nonsmooth locus of a closed semialgebraic set is a closed semialgebraic subset of smaller dimension. Then there is a unique coarsest finite cellular $F$-regular partition of $X$ adapted to $\Phi$. Its strata are smooth. No connectedness or equisingularity assertion is included in this result.

In A.303 one may require all strata to be connected, or all strata to have a single dimension, or both. Each of the resulting classes has its own unique coarsest adapted cellular $F$-regular partition. The connected version also has pure-dimensional strata.

Let $K$ be a real closed field. For each $n\geq0$ let $\mathcal M_n\subseteq\mathcal P(K^n)$ contain $K^n$, the empty set, and every parameter point. Assume closure under finite intersections, products, coordinate permutations and coordinate images, and that the graphs of addition and multiplication belong to the appropriate families. Call a map moderate when its graph belongs to the corresponding family. Assume, as in the algebraic zero-set axiom of cote 120, that for every $Y\in\mathcal M_n$ there are finitely many moderate functions $f_i:K^n\to K$ with $Y=\bigcap_i f_i^{-1}(0)$. Then the $\mathcal M_n$ are exactly the sets definable, with parameters, in an expansion of the ordered field $K$. This expansion is o-minimal if and only if $\mathcal M_1$ consists of finite unions of points and intervals. No compactness axiom is imposed in this assertion. Conversely, the definable sets of every expansion of $K$, with all definable maps allowed, satisfy the stated zero-set axiom.

For an arbitrary expansion $\mathcal R$ of an ordered real closed field $K$, let $\mathcal C_n$ be all its definable closed bounded subsets of $K^n$, allowing parameters. The expansion of the ordered field by all the predicates in all $\mathcal C_n$ is interdefinable with the open core of $\mathcal R$. Here the open core means the expansion of the ordered field by every open $\mathcal R$-definable subset of every $K^n$. Over $\R$, closed bounded has its ordinary compact meaning. Consequently, a prescribed family $(\mathcal C_n)_n$ of closed bounded sets is exactly the family of compact sets of an expansion with o-minimal open core if and only if the minimal all-arity definable expansion $K_{\mathcal C}$ generated by those predicates is o-minimal and its closed bounded definable sets are exactly the prescribed $\mathcal C_n$. This criterion includes the requirement that all parameter singletons occur.

The last sentence of 121/065, read literally as extension of a given triangulation, is false already for compact semialgebraic pairs. It remains false when linear subdivisions of the prescribed triangulation are allowed. Therefore the compact systems of 121/054--073, if they include that sentence, cannot characterize all compact definable sets of any o-minimal expansion of a real closed field. The true replacement is existence of a triangulation compatible with any finite family of definable subsets. A prescribed triangulation of a closed subset can be extended, up to subdivision, if its transition to the restriction of an ambient triangulation is PL.

Let $I=[-1,1]\subset\R$ and let $\mathcal C_n$ be the family of all closed subsets of $I^n$. Let $\mathcal C$ be the category of compact spaces admitting an embedding in a finite cube, with all continuous maps as morphisms. This model satisfies the compact axioms of 121/054--064, including finite intersections, all the specified direct and inverse images, the field operations on their compact domains, interval injectivity, and the zero-set condition. It also satisfies the compact-neighbourhood and gluing conditions of 121/070--073, using all compact subsets of $\R^n$ there. Amalgams along two closed embeddings exist, have the asserted intersection, and are preserved by the functor to compact spaces. More generally a pushout along one closed embedding and an arbitrary morphism exists in this category. Nevertheless this model contains the Cantor set, is not a system of compact definable sets with o-minimal open core, and fails finite triangulability. Thus these axioms, with intersections and the corrected interval, do not imply the proposed characterization. The extra triangulation claims of 121/065 must be separated: finite triangulability is independent of these axioms, while its arbitrary-prescribed-extension clause is false even for compact semialgebraic sets by A.307. The exact additional completion criterion is A.306.

The reconstruction in 120/008, even with a faithful, conservative, transportable, finite-limit-preserving functor to sets, does not imply M1. The same failure occurs for the proposed compact-space converse in 120/018. There is a three-element example, with every object finite, whose relation families are closed under unique existential quantification but not under ordinary existential quantification.

Let $U:\mathcal E\to\mathrm{Set}$ be faithful, conservative, transportable, and finite-limit-preserving. Let $R\in\mathcal E$ and suppose every object embeds in some $R^n$. Identify subobjects with their underlying subsets. Then the families $\mathcal M_n=U(\operatorname{Sub}_{\mathcal E}(R^n))$ are closed under unique existential quantification. They satisfy all coordinate-image instances of M1 if and only if every morphism has a factorization \[ X\xrightarrow{e} I\xrightarrow{m}Y, \qquad U(e)\text{ surjective},\quad m\text{ monic},\quad U(m)(U(I))=U(f)(U(X)). \] Under this additional image condition, $\mathcal E$ is equivalent over sets to the category of allowed subsets with allowed functional graphs. It is regular and $U$ preserves regular images. Conversely regularity with $U$ preserving images supplies exactly this condition. Thus Lead L3 is correct with this explicit repair; the hypotheses alone are insufficient.
For locally finite-dimensional topological spaces, Proposition A of 121/027 is false, already for a compact metrizable zero-dimensional space.

The proposed recursion does not always produce a privileged partition, even for a proper map of finite compact PL spaces that is a semialgebraic map. Therefore it cannot in general produce the coarsest privileged partition.

For compact PL spaces $K,L$, suspension is cancellative: $\Sigma K\simeq_{\rm PL}\Sigma L$ implies $K\simeq_{\rm PL}L$. If $M$ is a PL manifold of dimension $d$, then \[ \nu_{M\times X}(m,x)=d+\nu_X(x),\qquad Y_j(M\times X)=M\times Y_{j-d}(X). \] The convention is $Y_a(X)=\varnothing$ for $a<0$.

Each $Y_i(X)$ is a PL manifold of pure dimension $i$, and $X$ is PL equisingular along it. Its transverse pointed PL germ is immobile and unique up to pointed PL isomorphism, and its type is constant on each connected component of $Y_i(X)$. For $x\in Y_i(X)$, the germ $(Y_i(X),x)$ is the largest manifold germ along which $X$ is equisingular. The other such germs are exactly the locally flat PL submanifold germs of $(Y_i(X),x)$.

Conjecture 1 of 121/034 holds for locally finite PL spaces and for definable sets in any fixed o-minimal expansion of the real field, with isomorphisms in the respective category and with connected leaves, as in the component definition at 121/031. The leaves are the connected components of $Y_i(X)$. They form a locally finite PL partition, respectively a finite definable partition. The partition is privileged, is coarser than every other privileged partition, and restricts to opens by taking the connected components of its intersections with those opens. In the definable statement, opens are definable when a finite globally definable partition is required.

In the category of complex algebraic varieties with globally locally closed algebraic leaves, the assertion of 121/049 is false when ``locally finite'' refers to the classical topology. It fails at the existence stage. A locally finite closed family likewise need not admit a finite globally definable adapted partition.

Read ``strictly admissible'' as 121/051: the leaves are connected and locally connected, the partition is locally finite and satisfies the frontier condition, and for every open $W\subset X$, the connected components of all $F\cap W$ again give a locally finite frontier partition of $W$. Every locally finite PL or locally definable conically equisingular manifold partition is strict. A finite family of closed PL subspaces, respectively closed definable subspaces, therefore has a strict adapted partition. For any strict adapted partition the set \[ U_0=X\setminus\bigcup_\alpha\partial_XT_\alpha \] is saturated and open, and its connected components cannot be crossed by a leaf. The same statement holds locally for a locally finite family. The draft expression $\bigcup_\alpha\operatorname{int}_X(T_\alpha)$ in 121/049 is not the required first open set.

For every continuous definable map $f:X\to Y$, there is a dense definable open subset $U_0\subset Y$ which is a manifold, possibly with components of different dimensions, and over which $f$ is definably locally trivial. Consequently the maximal such open $U$ exists and has nowhere dense complement. If $\dim Y\leq1$, then $U$ is definable. More generally, $U$ is definable if $f$ admits a finite definable triangulation as a simplicial map; this includes proper finite PL maps. Properness is not needed for the first assertion.

The claim of 121/049 is false in the PL and semialgebraic contexts, even for one closed marked subspace of a compact finite polyhedron. Here ``strict'' has exactly the connectedness, local connectedness, and universal open-restriction meaning of 121/051, conditions (C), not the additional manifold or equisingularity conditions listed separately on that page.

There is a reduced affine complex algebraic space $X$ of pure complex dimension three, with one closed algebraic subspace $T\subset X$, having two strict adapted partitions and no strict common adapted coarsening. The failure occurs on a Zariski open subset. Consequently the assertion of 121/049 fails in both $\mathrm{Alg}_{\mathbb C}$ and $\mathrm{An}_{\mathbb C}$, as well as in the PL and semialgebraic contexts of A5.009.

The uniqueness bracket of Proposition B, 121/027, fails even when $X$ itself is a locally finite polyhedron, the maximal mobility stratum is a line, and both competing transverse spaces are locally compact, finite-dimensional ENRs with exactly one nonmanifold point. More precisely, let \[ L=S^5/C_{23},\qquad \zeta\cdot(z_1,z_2,z_3)=(\zeta z_1,\zeta z_2,\zeta z_3), \quad \zeta=e^{2\pi i/23}. \] There is an open smooth six-manifold $W$ with two ends and an end compactification $C=W\cup\{v\}$ at its positive end such that \[ F:(\mathbb R\times C,\mathbb R\times\{v\}) \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ } (\mathbb R\times cL,\mathbb R\times\{o\}), \qquad F(x,v)=(x,o), \tag{A5.11.1} \] but $(C,v)$ and $(cL,o)$ are not homeomorphic as germs. Their vertices are immobile, and every point of the distinguished axis in (A5.11.1) has mobility exactly one.

Fix an o-minimal expansion of an arbitrary real closed field $K$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous definable map of definable subsets of finite-dimensional $K$-spaces, and assume it is \emph{definably proper}: inverse images of definably compact sets are definably compact. Suppose every fibre is finite. Then the maximal open \emph{definable-manifold} locus $U\subset Y$ over which $f$ is definably locally trivial is definable, and $Y\setminus U$ is nowhere dense. Manifolds here have no boundary; no triangulation of the map is required.

Let $M$ be an o-minimal expansion of a real closed field and let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous definably proper definable map. Suppose $\dim Y\leq2$. Then the largest open subset of $Y$ which is a definable manifold without boundary and over which $f$ is definably locally trivial is definable. Thus the remaining maximal-locus question requires a target of dimension at least three and positive-dimensional fibres.

Let $M$ be an o-minimal expansion of a real closed field, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous definably proper definable map whose fibres have dimension at most one. Then its maximal open definable-manifold-without-boundary local-triviality locus is definable, with no restriction on $\dim Y$. For an arbitrary continuous definably proper map, the part of its maximal locus over which the fibres have dimension at most one is also definable. Combined with A5.013, the remaining question requires fibre dimension at least two and target dimension at least three.

Let $R$ be any real closed field, equipped with any o-minimal expansion. Put \[ M=S^2_R=\{x=(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in R^3: x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2=1\},\qquad h(x)=x_1, \] and let $X=R^2\times M\times R$, with coordinates $(a,b,x,u)$. The polynomial map \[ f:X\longrightarrow R^3,\qquad f(a,b,x,u)=(a,b,u^3-bh(x)) \tag{A5.15.1} \] is definably proper and globally semialgebraically trivial, with closed fibre $S^2_R$. Its source is a smooth algebraic $5$-manifold. Nevertheless, for every $a_0\in R$, no open neighbourhood of $(a_0,0,0)$ admits a finite definable ambient $C^1$ Thom $a_f$ stratification for $f$. This is a method obstruction, not a counterexample to A.5: the maximal open manifold-and-bundle locus of this map is all of $R^3$.

Fix an o-minimal expansion of $\mathbb R$. Let $F\subset\mathbb R^m$ and $G\subset\mathbb R^n$ be compact definable closed topological surfaces, and let $q:F\to G$ be a continuous definable surjection whose point inverses are cell-like in the classical topological sense. Then there are $\epsilon>0$ and a jointly definable continuous map \[ k:(0,\epsilon]\times G\longrightarrow F \] such that each $k_s$ is a homeomorphism and \[ \lim_{s\downarrow0}\sup_{y\in G}\|q(k_s(y))-y\|=0. \tag{A5.16.4} \] Equivalently, $q$ is the endpoint of a definable continuous family $h_s:F\to G$ with $h_0=q$ and $h_s$ a homeomorphism for every $s>0$. Consequently the associated double mapping-cylinder projection is definably locally trivial at its central parameter.

There is a single definable map \[ \psi:A\times(0,1]\times F\longrightarrow G \tag{A5.17.1} \] such that, for every $(a,\eta)$, the slice $\psi_{a,\eta}:F\to G$ is a homeomorphism and \[ \sup_{x\in F}\|\psi_{a,\eta}(x)-q_a(x)\|<\eta. \tag{A5.17.2} \] The map $\psi$ need not be jointly continuous in $a$ or $\eta$. Its graph is nevertheless defined by one formula with finitely many fixed parameters. The claim is consequently a genuine finite-format existence assertion, stronger than independent existence of an approximant for each $(a,\eta)$.

Let $R$ be a real closed field with an o-minimal expansion. Let $A,F,G$ be closed bounded definable sets, and let $q:A\times F\to G$ be jointly continuous and definable. Suppose there is one definable family \[ \psi:A\times(0,1]\times F\to G \] whose slices $\psi_{a,s}:F\to G$ are homeomorphisms and satisfy \[ \|\psi_{a,s}-q_a\|_\infty<s. \tag{A5.18.1} \] No joint continuity of $\psi$ is assumed. Then there exist $s_0>0$ and a jointly continuous definable map \[ h:A\times[0,s_0]\times F\to G \] such that $h_{a,0}=q_a$, every $h_{a,s}$ with $s>0$ is a homeomorphism, and $h_{a,s}\to q_a$ uniformly in $(a,x)$ as $s\downarrow0$. The empty parameter case and the case $F=G=\varnothing$ are immediate. If $A$ is nonempty and exactly one of $F,G$ is empty, the assumed family of homeomorphisms does not exist. Assume henceforth all three are nonempty.

Fix one continuous definably proper map $f:X\to Y$ in an o-minimal expansion of a real closed field. Name its finitely many coefficients. On the definable manifold locus of $Y$, its exact local definable bundle locus, with any prescribed finite fibre-manifold filter, admits the following reduction. There are finitely many definable scalar-certificate families. On each admissible family the source is a fixed product $L\times[-1,1]^m$ and the unresolved condition is the existence of homeomorphisms of $L\times\partial[-1,1]^m$ satisfying one exact angular equation and tending to the identity in the $L$ coordinate. In particular, all varying PL attachment maps can be replaced by the standard projection to $L$. For the fixed named-coefficient complete theory, the all-model definability assertion for this exact locus is equivalent to a finite pool of the explicit angular formula certificates described below. This is a strict normalization of the remaining geometry, not a proof that such a finite pool exists. It does not close original A5 or establish the separate rarity and privileged-recursion assertions.

For $m\in\mathbb R$, put $Y=x^2+y^2-1$, $A=xY-2yz$ and $B_m=(x+my)Y-2(y-mx)z$, and define \[ f_m:\mathbb R^3\longrightarrow\mathbb R^3, \qquad f_m(x,y,z)=(A^2B_m^2,Y,z). \] Every $f_m$ is proper and has degree twelve. The maps $f_m$ and $f_{-m}$ are polynomially right-left equivalent, whereas the subfamily $m>0$ is pairwise topologically right-left inequivalent. In particular the subfamily $m>1$ already has infinitely many topological map types. This corrects the all-distinct-real-parameters wording attached to the displayed family in Jelonek's original introduction. Its exceptional circle fibre has nearby finite fibres, so this is neither a constant-fibre counterexample nor a counterexample to original A5.

Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories and let $T:\mathcal B\longrightarrow\mathcal A$ be an additive left exact functor. Write $\mathcal C_T$ for the category of triples $(F,G,u)$ with $F\in\mathcal A$, $G\in\mathcal B$, and $u:F\to TG$. A morphism $(a,b)$ satisfies $T(b)u=u'a$. Then $\mathcal C_T$ is abelian and has the recollement functors \[ \begin{array}{lll} i^*(F,G,u)=F,&i_*F=(F,0,0),&i^!(F,G,u)=\ker u,\\ j_!G=(0,G,0),&j^*(F,G,u)=G,&j_*G=(TG,G,1). \end{array} \] Their adjunctions are $i^*\dashv i_*\dashv i^!$ and $j_!\dashv j^*\dashv j_*$. Both $i_*$ and $j_!,j_*$ are fully faithful, and $\ker j^*=\operatorname{im}i_*$. The functors $i^*,i_*,j_!,j^*$ are exact; $i^!,j_*$ are left exact. There are natural exact sequences \[ 0\to j_!j^*C\to C\to i_*i^*C\to0, \qquad 0\to i_*i^!C\to C\to j_*j^*C \to i_*\operatorname{coker}u\to0. \] For the displayed triples on 121/039, take $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sh}_\Lambda(Y)$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Sh}_\Lambda(X)$, and $T=p_*i^{-1}$. The adjunction $p^{-1}\dashv p_*$ identifies $u$ with the manuscript's $\alpha:p^{-1}F\to i^{-1}G$. Here $i^{-1}$ means ordinary sheaf restriction; it is not the extraordinary restriction $i^!$.

Let $i:Y\hookrightarrow Z$ be a closed embedding and $j:U=Z\setminus Y\hookrightarrow Z$ its open complement. For sheaves of modules over any fixed ring $\Lambda$, restriction induces an equivalence \[ \operatorname{Sh}_\Lambda(Z)\simeq \mathcal C_{i^{-1}j_*}. \] It identifies all six functors with A6.001. In particular the right adjoint to restriction to the open part is $j_*$, and the right adjoint to extension from the closed part is the kernel of the specialization arrow. For a boundary pushout $Z=Y\cup_pX$ with $p:\partial X\to Y$, the unrestricted triples of page 039, with $G$ an arbitrary sheaf on the whole resolved $X$, are in general a larger category than $\operatorname{Sh}_\Lambda(Z)$. They become the usual gluing formula when $G$ denotes a sheaf on $U=X\setminus\partial X$ and the gluing functor is $i^{-1}j_*$. If a compatible mapping-cylinder collar is chosen and $G$ is pulled back from a sheaf $H$ on the link in that collar, this functor is $p_*H$ when the radial interval is the ordinary real interval. This last radial simplification is not asserted for all ordinary topological sheaves on a non-Archimedean order topology. The open--closed formula and the six abstract adjoints above remain valid for ordinary sheaves on every topological space.

For stable categories $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ and an exact functor $T:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$, let $\mathcal C_T$ be the homotopy gluing category of arrows $F\to TG$. Its six functors have the same formulas as A6.001, with $\ker u$ replaced by $\operatorname{fib}u$. The exact sequences become the distinguished triangles \[ j_!j^*C\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow i_*i^*C\longrightarrow, \qquad i_*i^!C\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow j_*j^*C\longrightarrow. \] For derived sheaves in the preceding open--closed situation the gluing functor is $T=i^{-1}Rj_*$, so the extraordinary restriction is the homotopy fiber of $F\to i^{-1}Rj_*G$.

The following is a precise form of the data on 121/041--047. Fix a finite partially ordered set $I$. For each $i$ give a compact manifold with embedded corners $M_i$ of dimension $d_i$. For each $j<i$ give a possibly empty collective boundary hypersurface $H_{ij}\subset M_i$ and a locally trivial fibration $p_{ij}:H_{ij}\to M_j$ of manifolds with corners, whenever $H_{ij}\ne\varnothing$. A collective hypersurface is a disjoint union of boundary hypersurfaces with a specified common base. Require the following conditions. \begin{enumerate} \item Every boundary hypersurface occurs in exactly one $H_{ij}$. An intersection of several nonempty $H_{ij}$ can occur only when their lower labels form a chain. The intersection is a corner of the expected codimension. \item For $j<k<i$ one has \[ H_{ij}\cap H_{ik}=p_{ik}^{-1}(H_{kj}),\qquad p_{ij}=p_{kj}p_{ik}\quad\hbox{on }H_{ij}\cap H_{ik}. \] Restrictions of the fibrations to these corners are locally trivial. Their entire finite diagram over a sufficiently small open set in $M_j$ has a simultaneous local trivialization. This last condition specifies compatibility as a family, and not merely the separate local triviality of each arrow. \item Compatible collars are part of the datum. They commute on corners and preserve all the displayed maps: a collar for a lower face $H_{ij}$, restricted to $H_{ik}$ with $j<k$, projects by $p_{ik}$ to the corresponding collar of $H_{kj}$ in $M_k$; a collar for $H_{ik}$, restricted to $H_{ij}$, is vertical for $p_{ij}$. Their products give corner charts with independent nonnegative radius coordinates. \end{enumerate} Here and below an empty face contributes no condition. The fiber of $p_{ij}$ has dimension $d_i-d_j-1$. Its boundary consists exactly of the corners with labels $j<k<i$; the part of $\partial H_{ij}$ over $\partial M_j$ consists of the labels $k<j$. Thus \[ \partial H_{ij}= \bigcup_{k<j}p_{ij}^{-1}(H_{jk}) \ \cup\ \bigcup_{j<k<i}(H_{ij}\cap H_{ik}). \] In particular a fiber has empty boundary when $j$ is an immediate predecessor of $i$. For a chain $i>j_1>\cdots>j_r$ the total corner $H_{ij_1}\cap\cdots\cap H_{ij_r}$ has dimension $d_i-r$. The subscripts in the dimension formula refer to $i$, not to $j_1$.

A resolution datum as in A6.004 reconstructs the compact stratified space \[ X=\left(\coprod_{i\in I}M_i\right)\big/ \bigl(x\sim p_{ij}(x),\ x\in H_{ij}\bigr). \] Its strata are exactly the images of the interiors $M_i^\circ$. It has compatible conical control neighborhoods, with retraction $\pi_j$ and radius $\rho_j$ induced by the boundary fibration and its collar. Conversely, a compact finitely stratified space with such conical control data has a resolution datum, obtained by successively replacing cones on links by cylinders on the links, starting at the closed strata. These operations are mutually inverse when the collective faces, their common bases, and the collar data are retained. More precisely, the control data used in this statement include locally trivial charts $V\times C(L)$ over each stratum, compact links with the same structure recursively, and compatible radial trivializations on overlapping tubes. Transition maps preserve the cone rays and the radius, with the induced maps on links compatible recursively. This is the conical-atlas condition in Definition 1(v) of Albin--Leichtnam--Mazzeo--Piazza~\cite{ALMP2012}, \emph{The signature package on Witt spaces}, pp.249--250. No Witt condition or orientability is needed in this topological statement. The finite family formulation permits nonpure dimensions and codimension-one strata. The same constructions work in the PL category, and for finite definable conical control atlases and compatible definable collars in a fixed o-minimal expansion of a real closed field. In that version compact means definably compact and the quotients carry their definable-space topology. All chart and transition maps in the construction stay in the given structure.

For fixed resolutions, a stratum-preserving homeomorphism smooth on each stratum and commuting with the scalar control functions $\pi,\rho$ need not lift even continuously. This failure already occurs for the compact semialgebraic suspension of a circle. Thus an equivalence of categories requires a specified regularity condition on the angular maps. One valid convention is that they extend smoothly to the resolved corners, preserve the boundary fibrations, and have radius components of the prescribed corner-map class. With these morphisms and the complete data of A6.004--005, resolution and blowdown are inverse functors. In the stricter category preserving the chosen product trivializations, both sides must use that same stricter condition. Forgetting the common-base labels can even lose the homeomorphism type of the reconstructed space.

For a compact surface $M$, the ordinary fundamental-groupoid functor \[ \Pi_1(\partial M)\longrightarrow\Pi_1(M), \] with its decomposition into connected components, determines the unmarked homeomorphism type of every component of $M$, including orientability, genus and number of boundary circles. For a connected component with nonempty boundary, let $b$ be the number of boundary circles and let $r$ be the rank of the abelianization of its fundamental group. It is orientable precisely when \[ \ker\bigl(\mathbb Z^b=H_1(\partial M;\mathbb Z) \longrightarrow H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\bigr)\ne0. \] In the orientable case its genus is $(r-b+1)/2$; in the nonorientable case its crosscap number is $r-b+1$. For a closed component, $H_1=\mathbb Z^{2g}$ determines the orientable genus $g$, whereas $H_1=\mathbb Z^{h-1}\oplus\mathbb Z/2$ determines the nonorientable crosscap number $h$. Thus the sphere and the projective plane are also distinguished. This is the precise useful surface interpretation of the ``1-special'' and ``2-special'' ordinary groupoids on 121/043. It does not assert that the manuscript defines those words: the page contains a sketch and no definition of ``admissible functor''. Corner flags and their attaching maps must still be kept when several surface pieces are glued.

Keeping only the peripheral groupoids of surface pieces, the fundamental groupoid of the lower graph, and their attaching functors does not determine a compact two-dimensional stratified space up to stratified homeomorphism. The following two finite polygonal gluings give an explicit counterexample: \[ w_1=aa^{-1}bb^{-1}cc^{-1},\qquad w_2=abb^{-1}a^{-1}cc^{-1}. \] In each case attach a closed hexagonal disk to the rose of three circles by mapping each side linearly once around the edge named by its signed letter. Use the rose vertex, its three open edges, and the disk interior as strata. The aggregate groupoid diagrams are equivalent, but the stratified spaces are not homeomorphic. The finite program \texttt{code/check\_A6\_finite.py} checks both words, their complete vertex links, and all signed edge relabelings and polygon dihedral actions; its actual output is in \texttt{logs/check\_A6\_finite.txt}.

An ordinary fundamental groupoid, up to equivalence, determines exactly the homotopy $1$-type: connected components and their fundamental groups. A diagram of ordinary groupoids retains the corresponding diagram of $1$-types, including its specified functors and natural transformations. It cannot in general recover higher homotopy within any piece, nor the homeomorphism type of a stratified space. This remains false for compact one-stratum smooth semialgebraic manifolds of fixed dimension: $S^4$ and $\mathbb{CP}^2$ have identical fundamental groupoids. In dimension two compactness and peripheral data are essential to A6.007. The once-punctured torus and the thrice-punctured sphere have equivalent fundamental groupoids and no manifold boundary, but are not homeomorphic. There is a precise positive homotopy statement. If a resolution diagram consists of aspherical pieces, all attaching maps and their coherence are retained, and its geometric realization is the homotopy colimit of the diagram, then the groupoid diagram determines that full homotopy type: take the homotopy colimit of the classifying spaces of the groupoids. Taking a colimit inside ordinary groupoids instead need not do so, even for a sphere with one marked point.
