For compact finite PL resolution systems of dimension at most two, the following finite and groupoid data classify the blown-down stratified spaces up to a homeomorphism preserving the resolution labels: \begin{enumerate} \item the components of every resolved stratum, their dimensions, and the finite corner flags, including the cyclic incidence of arcs around each boundary circle and their common-base labels; \item for each compact surface component, its peripheral functor $\Pi_1(\partial M)\to\Pi_1(M)$, with the boundary components identified with those in the flag datum; \item for each one-dimensional boundary fibration over a resolved one-dimensional stratum, its finite covering monodromy, with its endpoint maps to the flags. \end{enumerate} Isomorphisms of these data must preserve the coherent diagrams, including the boundary-loop maps in item 2. The one-dimensional pieces themselves are compact intervals or circles, with their finite endpoints; zero-dimensional pieces are finite sets. For a trivial covering over an interval the covering datum is just the set of sheets and the two endpoint maps. For a circle it is a finite set with a permutation, up to simultaneous conjugacy and, when the base orientation is reversed, inversion. Thus ordinary peripheral groupoids determine the compact surface pieces, and a complete flag/covering diagram supplies exactly the remaining boundary assembly in dimension two. A6.008 proves that one cannot discard the flag incidence and retain only aggregate attaching groupoids. This statement does not classify mapping spaces or replace the angular condition of A6.006.

Interpret $\mathcal C'$ in 119/146 as triples $(X,\mathcal T,p)$, where $\mathcal T$ is an \emph{\'etendue} and $p:\operatorname{Sh}(X)\to\mathcal T$ is open, connected and locally connected. Sending such a triple to its local kernel does not give an equivalence with local equivalence relations. This remains false for the circle with its single-leaf relation, with every fibre a connected one-dimensional manifold. The manuscript's third condition is indeed ``et connexes'', as checked on the original scan, not simple connectivity.

For two triples $(X,\mathcal T,p)$ and $(Y,\mathcal U,q)$ as above, define a morphism to be $(f,g,\alpha)$, where $f:X\to Y$ is continuous, $g:\mathcal T\to\mathcal U$ is a geometric morphism, and $\alpha:q\operatorname{Sh}(f)\Rightarrow gp$ is an invertible $2$-cell. A $2$-cell between such morphisms with the same $f$ is a $2$-cell $\theta:g\Rightarrow g'$ compatible with their displayed triangles. There are no $2$-cells between different $f$'s. If $p$ is connected, each such Hom category is equivalent to a discrete category. It need not be literally discrete before taking isomorphism classes. Omitting the triangle changes this conclusion.

Let $r$ be a locally connected local equivalence relation on $X$ for which $\mathcal M_r=\operatorname{Sh}(X,r)$ is a Grothendieck topos and the inclusion is the inverse image of $\pi_r:\operatorname{Sh}(X)\to\mathcal M_r$. For a connected $p:\operatorname{Sh}(X)\to\mathcal T$, there is an equivalence $\mathcal T\simeq\mathcal M_r$ over $\operatorname{Sh}(X)$ if and only if \[ \operatorname{EssIm}(p^*)=\operatorname{Sh}(X,r). \tag{A.7.1} \] This is the exact additional descent condition; connected fibres alone do not imply it. The following geometric condition suffices. Suppose $\mathcal T$ is an \emph{\'etendue}, $p$ is connected and locally connected, $r=\operatorname{Lker}(p)$, and there is an epimorphic \emph{\'etale} localic atlas $\operatorname{Sh}(A)\to\mathcal T$ whose pullback is $\operatorname{Sh}(B)\to\operatorname{Sh}(X)$, such that the resulting map of locales $b:B\to A$ is simply connected in the following explicit sense: $b^*$ is fully faithful, and any sheaf on $B$ locally isomorphic to pullbacks by $b^*$ is globally such a pullback. Then (A.7.1) holds. In particular $\mathcal M_r$ is an \emph{\'etendue} in this situation.

Restrict objects on the quotient side to presentations $(X,r,\mathcal T,p)$ remembering the recognized relation and satisfying (A.7.1), and on the relation side to relations whose invariant-sheaf category is an \emph{\'etendue} with its connected quotient map. Define a morphism $f:(X,r)\to(Y,s)$ to be a continuous map for which $f^{-1}$ takes $s$-invariant sheaves to $r$-invariant sheaves. Then the quotient construction is an equivalence from this category to the $2$-category of such presentations after replacing its Hom groupoids by their isomorphism classes. These are explicitly \emph{sheaf-detected} morphisms; a theorem for a different notion of foliated map is not being asserted without a comparison. The relation decoration can be omitted in the subclass with $r=\operatorname{Lker}(p)$. On the relation side it suffices to require locally simply connected effective charts: each chart relation is the kernel pair of its quotient map. Then the local kernel of the canonical quotient is the original relation, by \cite[Remark 6.5]{KockMoerdijk1992}. Without effectivity one must not assert that equality merely from equality of the invariant-sheaf categories. The same recognition criterion and equivalence hold relative to a Grothendieck topos $\mathcal E$, for internal locales, internal local relations and relative topoi, with the foregoing descent and simple-connectivity hypotheses imposed internally and stably under base change. The unrestricted suggestion ``[ou topos ?]'' is false, since its instance over $\mathrm{Set}$ is A.701.

Let $A$ be a unital $k$-algebra containing $L$ by $s:L\longrightarrow A$. Put $D=A\otimes_k A$ and let $J$ be the right ideal generated by $s(\lambda)\otimes1-1\otimes s(\lambda)$, for $\lambda\in L$. The quotient $D/J$ is the tensor product of the two left $L$-modules $A$. The image of the left idealizer $\widetilde J=\{d:dJ\subset J\}$ is \[ A\mathbin{\times_L}A= \left\{\sum_i a_i\otimes_L b_i: \sum_i a_i s(\lambda)\otimes_L b_i =\sum_i a_i\otimes_L b_i s(\lambda) \text{ for every }\lambda\in L\right\}. \] Multiplication is induced by factorwise multiplication in $D$. Thus $\widetilde J/J\simeq A\times_L A$ as algebras. The same statement holds for the completed products of 155/002.

Even for $L=k=\mathbb F_2$ and finite-dimensional $U$, the data 1), 2), (i), and (ii) on 155/002 do not imply the asserted tensor-category reconstruction. The missing constraint is the character identity for the coalgebra counit. In the neutral case it says that this counit is an algebra homomorphism. Consequently R7 and L6 require this correction.

In the manuscript data, assume that $A$ is a pseudocompact $k$-algebra and that the multiplication is continuous. Write $e:A\longrightarrow L$ for the transpose of $1_U$. Add \begin{equation}\label{eq:B-character} e(1)=1,\qquad e(ab)=e\bigl(a\,s(e(b))\bigr)\quad(a,b\in A). \end{equation} The first equality already follows if the stated augmentation of $U$ is unital. With this addition, the displayed data are exactly the data of a continuous cocommutative left $L$-bialgebroid with equal source and target $s$. They give a symmetric abelian tensor category of continuous $A$-modules finite-dimensional over $L$, with exact faithful forgetful functor to $\operatorname{Modf}(L)$. Conversely every essentially small abelian $k$-linear symmetric tensor category with such a fibre functor reconstructs these data. Both reconstructions are inverse up to an equivalence respecting the fibre functors and the induced isomorphism of the pro-algebras.

Assume that the category in B.003 is rigid and that $k\simeq\operatorname{End}(1)$. Its scalar extension to $L$ has an exact faithful fibre functor induced by $F$. In the module description this is the restricted diagonal functor on finite $(A\widehat\otimes_k L)$-modules written on 155/004. It is exact and faithful for every finite field extension $L/k$, including inseparable ones. By contrast, the diagonal functor on all $(L\otimes_k L)$-modules need not be exact, and is not generally faithful even for a nontrivial separable extension.

Choose a nonzero $k$-linear functional $\ell:L\longrightarrow k$ and write $U=\operatorname{Hom}^{\mathrm{cont}}_L(A,L)$, where $A$ is a left $L$-module by $s$. Give $U$ the left $A$-action $(a u)(b)=u(ba)$. Then \[ \operatorname{Hom}_A(M,U)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_L(M,L), \qquad \phi\longmapsto\bigl(m\longmapsto\phi(m)(1)\bigr), \qquad \operatorname{End}_A(U)\simeq A^{\mathrm{op}}. \] The last isomorphism uses $\ell$ when $L\ne k$. A rigid tensor structure supplies a continuous anti-isomorphism $a_\ell:A\longrightarrow A^{\mathrm{op}}$, fixing $s(L)$, and hence a second, commuting $A$-action on $U$. Evaluation and coevaluation are \[ \operatorname{ev}_M(m\otimes\phi)=\phi(m)(1),\qquad \operatorname{coev}_M(1)=\sum_i m_i\otimes\phi_i, \] where $(m_i), (\phi_i)$ are dual $L$-bases under the first isomorphism. Conversely a continuous anti-isomorphism fixing $s(L)$ gives rigidity exactly when these two maps are $A$-linear for every finite continuous $A$-module $M$. Their two triangle identities always hold as linear maps, and therefore hold in the module category when the maps are $A$-linear. For pro-$A$, the manuscript's instruction to test only $M=A$ must be replaced by tests on finite modules; $A$ need not itself be an object of the category.

Let \[ \Omega_{\mathrm{DP}}=\bigoplus_{n\ge1}\mathbb Z\gamma_n, \qquad \gamma_n=T^n/n!\in\mathbb Q[T]. \] With ordinary polynomial addition, multiplication, and composition, this is a nonunital analyser satisfying 153/006, axioms 1) and 2), with composition unit $T=\gamma_1$ and constant subring zero. Its natural domain of action is any divided-power ideal $I$ in a commutative unital ring, by $\left(\sum a_n\gamma_n\right)(x)=\sum a_n\gamma_n^I(x)$. It does not satisfy the optional axiom 3a) literally printed on 153/006. The correct nonunital coaddition has its target in the augmentation ideal of $\mathbb Z[\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\ldots]\otimes \mathbb Z[\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\ldots]$, not in $\Omega_{\mathrm{DP}}\otimes\Omega_{\mathrm{DP}}$ alone.

Let $P$ be a unital analyser and let $k$ be a specified unital subring of its constant ring. A compatible $k$-plethory structure is exactly the following additional data and conditions: a $k$--$k$ biring structure on the $k$-algebra $P$, with coaddition and comultiplication realizing the finite decompositions in 3a) and 3b), with $\beta(c)(F)=F\circ c$; and the requirement that the induced map $P\odot_k P\longrightarrow P$, $F\odot G\longmapsto F\circ G$, and $k[T]\longrightarrow P$, $T\longmapsto T$, are biring morphisms. Here a biring includes additive and multiplicative counits, additive coinverse, coassociativity, cocommutativity, codistributivity, and the scalar map $\beta:k\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(P,k)$. None of these coalgebra identities is encoded by unspecified existence of decompositions alone. There is a useful sufficient criterion with no choice of additional operations: if the constant ring is a field $k$, $P$ acts faithfully on $k$, and 1)--3) hold with the unitality convention of 153/006, then there is a unique compatible $k$-plethory structure.

After the manuscript replaces a fraction-field inclusion by an arbitrary inclusion $R\subset S$ of commutative rings, the marginal claim ``OK if $\Omega$ is free'' does not ensure well-determined coaddition or comultiplication tensors. It fails even when $R,S$ are fields. The correction ``$R$ is a domain'' in the earlier study does not suffice either.

For an inclusion $R\subset S$, let $\Omega=\{F\in S[T]:F(R)\subset R\}$ and let \[ \theta_2:\Omega\otimes_R\Omega\longrightarrow S[X,Y], \qquad G\otimes H\longmapsto G(X)H(Y). \] The polynomial identities on 153/004 determine one and only one tensor for every $F$ if and only if $\theta_2$ is injective and both $F(X+Y)$ and $F(XY)$ belong to its image for every $F\in\Omega$. For a domain $R$ with fraction field $S$, freeness of $\Omega$ over $R$ implies these conditions and, more strongly, gives isomorphisms \[ \theta_n:\Omega^{\otimes_R n}\xrightarrow{\sim} \{P\in S[T_1,\ldots,T_n]:P(R^n)\subset R\} \quad(n\ge1). \] In this case the coaddition, comultiplication, and ordinary composition give a unique compatible $R$-plethory structure.

For any analyser $\Omega$, evaluation on its constant subring $\Omega_0$ is injective exactly when the constants separate elements of $\Omega$ under composition. For the polynomial analyser of an inclusion $R\subset S$, this has the following explicit coefficient criterion: \[ \bigcap_{r\in R}\ker\bigl(S^{d+1}\longrightarrow S, (a_0,\ldots,a_d)\longmapsto\sum_{i=0}^d a_i r^i\bigr)=0 \quad\hbox{for every }d\ge0. \] In particular, if $S$ is a domain it is injective exactly when $R$ is infinite. More generally it is injective if for every $d$ there are $r_0,\ldots,r_d\in R$ such that $\prod_{i<j}(r_j-r_i)$ is a non-zero-divisor in $S$. The unqualified desirability statement on 153/008 is not a theorem: $\mathbb F_q[T]$ and the divided-power analyser B.006 both give nonfaithful examples.

The $64$-element algebra \[ P=\mathbb F_2[T]/\bigl((T^2-T)^3\bigr) \] with ordinary polynomial substitution is a unital analyser satisfying 153/006, 1)--3), including both optional decomposition axioms. It has no compatible plethory structure. Thus the missing biring data in B.007 cannot be inferred from those axioms.

After adding B.003's unit constraint, the algebra on 155/002 is a cocommutative equal-source-and-target instance of Takeuchi's $\times_L$-bialgebra, presented as a pro-dual. Without that constraint, it is not a bialgebroid, by B.002. The manuscript's reconstruction is a special case of the general reconstruction theorems below, with a separate completion step; its rigid case has the non-neutral groupoid interpretation of Deligne. Thus L6 is valid as a qualified structural comparison, and is false if it asserts that the literal displayed data already satisfy the modern definition. No priority claim or claim of independence follows from these comparisons.

Let $R\ne0$ be a finite commutative ring and let $R\subset S$ be a unital inclusion. For the module $\Omega$ and map $\theta_2$ of B.009, the following are equivalent: $\theta_2$ is injective; the identities on 153/004 determine unique coaddition and comultiplication tensors; and $S=R$. In the last case $\Omega=R[T]$ with its usual plethory structure. This classifies arbitrary extensions of a finite base, including extensions that are infinite or have zero divisors.

Let $R$ be an infinite domain, $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, and let $R\subset S$ with $S$ torsion-free as an $R$-module. Inside $K\otimes_R S$ define the overring \[ S_{\mathrm{rat}}=S\cap(K\cdot1). \] Then \[ \Omega(R,S)=\{F\in S_{\mathrm{rat}}[T]:F(R)\subset R\}. \] Moreover $\ker\theta_2$ is exactly the $R$-torsion submodule of $\Omega\otimes_R\Omega$. In particular, for an infinite field base $R$, every unital extension $R\subset S$ gives $\Omega=R[T]$ and unique standard co-operations. Together with B.013, this is a complete classification for every field base: an infinite field allows every extension; a finite field allows unique polynomial tensor expansions exactly for the identity extension.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a local domain with fraction field $K$. Suppose $u_n\in R$ have the following property: for every finite set $\mathcal H\subset\operatorname{Int}(R)$ there is an $n$ with $h(u_n)-h(0)\in\mathfrak m$ for every $h\in\mathcal H$. If $g\in\operatorname{Int}(R)$ satisfies $g(0)=0$ and $g(u_n^2)\notin\mathfrak m^2$ for every $n$, then \[ g(XY)\notin\operatorname{im}\bigl( \operatorname{Int}(R)\otimes_R\operatorname{Int}(R) \longrightarrow K[X,Y]\bigr). \] Consequently no compatible biring, and hence no compatible plethory, can have its polynomial inclusion $R[T]\to\operatorname{Int}(R)$ as a biring morphism.

For every finite field $k=\mathbb F_q$, put \[ T=k[t]_{\{h:h(0)h(1)\ne0\}},\qquad m=t(t-1),\qquad R=k+mT\subset K=k(t). \] Then $R$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain, but $\operatorname{Int}(R)$ has no compatible comultiplication tensor for a specific polynomial of degree $q^2$. In particular the fraction-field hypothesis alone does not repair the unrestricted claim on 153/004; freeness or another genuine tensor condition is needed. The case $q=2$ was found in the opened primary preprint \cite[Theorem 3.4, pp.7--8]{JiangEtAl2026}; the argument here treats all finite fields and proves the final biring obstruction directly.

For a nonzero commutative ring $R$, the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item every residue field $R/\mathfrak m$ at a maximal ideal is infinite; \item for every unital inclusion $R\subset S$, every polynomial in $S[T]$ preserving $R$ already belongs to $R[T]$; \item for every such inclusion, the identities of 153/004 determine unique coaddition and comultiplication tensors. \end{enumerate} Thus no structural classification gate remains for bases all of whose residue fields are infinite. This includes every ring containing an infinite field. If $R$ has even one finite residue field, the square-zero extension constructed below already violates uniqueness.

Let $R$ be an infinite domain and $R\subset S$ a unital inclusion with $S$ torsion-free over $R$. If $\Omega=\{F\in S[T]:F(R)\subset R\}$ is free over $R$, then for every $n\ge1$ the natural map is an isomorphism \[ \Omega^{\otimes_R n}\xrightarrow{\sim} \{P\in S[T_1,\ldots,T_n]:P(R^n)\subset R\}. \] Consequently the two requested tensors and the compatible plethory structure exist uniquely. This extends B.009 from a fraction field to every torsion-free overring of an infinite domain; B.008 shows why the word infinite cannot simply be omitted.

In the infinite-domain, torsion-free-extension setting of B.014, assume the following condition on the $R$-module $\Omega$: for every finite subset $E\subset\Omega$ there are finitely many $b_i\in\Omega$ and $R$-linear maps $\lambda_i:\Omega\to R$ such that \[ x=\sum_i b_i\lambda_i(x)\qquad(x\in E). \] Then every multivariable tensor map in B.018 is an isomorphism, and $\Omega$ has the unique compatible plethory structure. In particular this holds if $\Omega$ is projective over $R$; freeness is unnecessary.

Let $R$ be an infinite Noetherian normal domain and $R\subset S$ an arbitrary $R$-torsion-free unital extension. Then $\Omega$ is a projective $R$-module, all the multivariable tensor maps are isomorphisms, and the unique co-operations and compatible plethory exist. More explicitly, put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and $L=S_{\mathrm{rat}}\subset K$. For $n\ge0$ put \[ w_q(n)=\sum_{a\ge1}\left\lfloor\frac{n}{q^a}\right\rfloor, \qquad I_n=\prod_{\substack{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1\\ |R/\mathfrak p|=q<\infty}} \mathfrak p^{-w_q(n)}. \] Only finitely many factors are nontrivial. There are monic $P_n\in R[T]$ of degree $n$ such that \[ \operatorname{Int}(R)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I_nP_n, \qquad \Omega=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}(I_n\cap L)P_n. \] Each fractional ideal $I_n\cap L$ is invertible. These formulas include nonprincipal ideals and therefore do not assume a regular free polynomial basis.

Let $V\to D$ be a surjective ring homomorphism, let $k\to D$ be a second homomorphism, and put $R=V\times_D k$. Fix a set $I$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:D^{(I)}\to D^{(I)}$. Define \[ M_\alpha=\{(b,c)\in V^{(I)}\oplus k^{(I)}: \bar b=\alpha(\bar c)\}. \] Then $M_\alpha$ is projective over $R$, even for infinite $I$. More precisely $M_\alpha\oplus M_{\alpha^{-1}}$ is free over $R$.

Let $k=\mathbb F_q$, let $m\ge1$, put \[ V=k[[t]],\qquad K=k((t)),\qquad R=k+t^mV. \] Then $R$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with fraction field $K$, and $A=\operatorname{Int}(R)$ is a projective $R$-module. Consequently all its multivariable tensor maps are isomorphisms and it has the unique compatible plethory structure. In particular $R=\mathbb F_2[[t^2,t^3]]$ satisfies these assertions. The conjectured nonflatness for this example recorded in the opened Elliott paper \cite[introduction, p.2]{ElliottPresentations2011} is false: projectivity implies flatness.

Let $k\subset l$ be finite fields of cardinalities $q$ and $Q=q^f$, let $m\ge1$, and put \[ V=l[[t]],\qquad K=l((t)),\qquad R=k+t^mV. \] Then $R$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain and $\operatorname{Int}(R)$ is projective over $R$. All multivariable tensor maps are isomorphisms, so its unique compatible plethory exists. In particular this proves flatness also for $\mathbb F_2+t\mathbb F_4[[t]]$, the second conjectured nonflat example recorded in \cite[introduction, p.2]{ElliottPresentations2011}. Neither example is the two-branch local domain of B.016.

Let $V$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, uniformizer $\pi$, and finite residue field of cardinality $Q$. Let $R\subset V$ be a unital subring containing $\pi^mV$ for some $m\ge1$. Then $R$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain, $V$ is its finite normalization, and $A=\operatorname{Int}(R)$ is projective over $R$. Consequently all multivariable tensor maps are isomorphisms and $A$ has the unique compatible plethory. This includes incomplete and mixed characteristic rings, and arbitrary conductor gaps rather than only the pure gaps of B.023.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with finite residue field, fraction field $K$, and finite normalization $T\subset K$. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $T$ is local; \item every map $\operatorname{Int}(R)^{\otimes_R n} \to\operatorname{Int}(R^n)$ is an isomorphism; \item the polynomial identities of 153/004 give unique coaddition and comultiplication tensors; \item $F(XY)$ is a sum of terms $G(X)H(Y)$ with $G,H\in\operatorname{Int}(R)$ for every $F\in\operatorname{Int}(R)$. \end{enumerate} If $T$ is not local, the proof gives an explicit higher-variable polynomial obstruction, which rules out condition 4 by finite iteration. Thus the criterion does not merely assert failure of projectivity or of a sufficient condition.

Let $R\subset V$ satisfy B.024, with fraction field $K$, and let $R\subset S$ be any $R$-torsion-free unital extension. Put $L=S_{\mathrm{rat}}\subset K$ as in B.014. Then the identities on 153/004 determine unique coaddition and comultiplication tensors if and only if \[ L=R\quad\hbox{or}\quad L=K. \] In both cases the compatible plethory exists. A proper intermediate coefficient overring $R\subsetneq L\subset K$ has a noninjective tensor map. Thus even in this one-branch class the answer depends on the specified coefficient ring, and does not grow monotonically with that ring.

Let $R$ be a one-dimensional Noetherian domain, $K$ its fraction field, and $R\subset L\subset K$ an arbitrary overring. For $n\ge1$ put \[ \Omega_n(R,L)=\{F\in L[X_1,\ldots,X_n]:F(R^n)\subset R\}. \] For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ one has, as submodules of $K[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$, \[ \Omega_n(R,L)_{\mathfrak m} =\Omega_n(R_{\mathfrak m},L_{\mathfrak m}). \] In particular the tensor maps in B.009 localize to the corresponding maps for $(R_{\mathfrak m},L_{\mathfrak m})$. No polynomial localization property is assumed in this statement.

Let $R$ be a one-dimensional Noetherian domain with fraction field $K$ and finite normalization $T$ in $K$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ with finite residue field, $T_{R\setminus\mathfrak m}$ is local, equivalently exactly one maximal ideal of $T$ lies above $\mathfrak m$; \item all maps $\operatorname{Int}(R)^{\otimes_R n} \to\operatorname{Int}(R^n)$ are isomorphisms; \item the polynomial coaddition and comultiplication of 153/004 have unique tensor representatives; \item $F(XY)$ has a finite expansion $\sum_iG_i(X)H_i(Y)$ with $G_i,H_i\in\operatorname{Int}(R)$ for every $F\in\operatorname{Int}(R)$. \end{enumerate} When these hold, $\operatorname{Int}(R)$ has its unique compatible plethory. Thus, for fraction-field coefficients, B.2(c) is completely settled in dimension one with finite normalization. Only the maximal ideals with finite residue field enter the criterion.

Let $R$ and $T$ satisfy B.028, and suppose the equivalent conditions of that result hold. For any $R$-torsion-free unital extension $R\subset S$, put $L=S_{\mathrm{rat}}\subset K$ as in B.014. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $\Omega(R,S)$ has uniquely determined polynomial coaddition and comultiplication tensors; \item all its multivariable tensor maps are isomorphisms; \item for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ with finite residue field, one has $L_{\mathfrak m}=R_{\mathfrak m}$ or $L_{\mathfrak m}=K$. \end{enumerate} Whenever these hold the compatible plethory exists. The choices $R_{\mathfrak m}$ and $K$ may differ at different maximal ideals.

Let $R\subset S$ be an injective unital extension of nonzero commutative rings, with $R$ local and $S$ finite as an $R$-module. Suppose its conductor \[ J=\{r\in R:rS\subset R\} \] has finite quotient $R/J$. Then the second polynomial tensor map for $\Omega(R,S)$ is injective if and only if $S=R$. Consequently unique polynomial coaddition and comultiplication occur exactly in that case.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with finite residue field, fraction field $K$, and finite normalization $T$. Let $R\subset S$ be any $R$-torsion-free unital extension, and put $L=S_{\mathrm{rat}}$. Then the polynomial coaddition and comultiplication tensors for $\Omega(R,S)$ are uniquely determined if and only if \[ L=R\quad\hbox{or}\quad (T\hbox{ is local and }L=K). \] In these cases every multivariable tensor map is an isomorphism and the unique compatible plethory exists. If $T$ has more than one maximal ideal and $L\not\subset T$, even the existence of multiplicative tensors fails.

Let $R$ be a one-dimensional Noetherian domain, let $K$ be its fraction field, and suppose its normalization $T$ in $K$ is a finite $R$-module. For any $R$-torsion-free unital extension $R\subset S$, put $L=S_{\mathrm{rat}}\subset K$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item the polynomial identities on 153/004 determine unique coaddition and comultiplication tensors for $\Omega(R,S)$; \item every multivariable tensor map for $\Omega(R,S)$ is an isomorphism onto the corresponding integer-valued polynomials; \item for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ with finite residue field, either \[ L_{\mathfrak m}=R_{\mathfrak m}, \quad\hbox{or}\quad L_{\mathfrak m}=K\ \hbox{ and }\ T_{R\setminus\mathfrak m} \hbox{ is local}. \] \end{enumerate} These conditions also give the unique compatible plethory. There is no restriction at a maximal ideal with infinite residue field. The criterion includes all coefficient overrings and all normalization branch counts in the stated class.

The conclusion of B.027 holds for every Noetherian domain $R$, without a dimension restriction, and for localization at any multiplicatively closed subset $U\subset R\setminus\{0\}$: \[ U^{-1}\Omega_n(R,L)=\Omega_n(U^{-1}R,U^{-1}L). \] The inclusion from left to right holds for every domain, without Noetherianity.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonfield Noetherian local domain with fraction field $K$. Define the explicitly specified overring \[ R^\sharp=\{x\in K:\mathfrak m^Nx\subset R \text{ for some }N\ge0\}. \] Then \[ R^\sharp=\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\ne\mathfrak m}R_{\mathfrak p} \quad\hbox{inside }K, \qquad R^\sharp=R\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \operatorname{depth}R\ge2. \] If the residue field is finite, and $R\subset L\subset K$ is an overring, put $E=L\cap R^\sharp$. Then \[ \Omega_n(R,L)=\Omega_n(R,E)\quad(n\ge1), \qquad \Omega_1(R,L)=R[X]\ \Longleftrightarrow\ E=R. \] Thus the ring controlling whether nonpolynomial operations can occur is determined without referring to tensor maps.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local domain of dimension at least two with finite residue field, fraction field $K$, and finite normalization $T$. Let $R\subset L\subset K$ and set $E=L\cap R^\sharp$ as in B.034. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item the polynomial coaddition and comultiplication tensors for $\Omega(R,L)$ are uniquely determined; \item $\Omega(R,L)=R[X]$; \item $E=R$. \end{enumerate} When $E\ne R$ and $E\subset T$, the second tensor map fails injectivity. When $E\not\subset T$, multiplicative tensors fail to exist for all elements. In particular, for $L=K$ the answer is exactly $\operatorname{depth}R\ge2$.

Let $R$ be a nonfield Noetherian domain whose normalization $T$ in its fraction field $K$ is finite. Let $R\subset S$ be any $R$-torsion-free unital extension and put $L=S_{\mathrm{rat}}$. For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, write $R_m=R_{\mathfrak m}$, $L_m=L_{\mathfrak m}$ and $T_m=T_{R\setminus\mathfrak m}$. The polynomial identities of 153/004 give unique coaddition and comultiplication tensors if and only if the following holds at every maximal ideal with finite residue field: \begin{enumerate} \item if $\dim R_m=1$, then $L_m=R_m$, or $L_m=K$ and $T_m$ is local; \item if $\dim R_m\ge2$, then \[ L_m\cap R_m^\sharp=R_m, \qquad R_m^\sharp=\{x\in K:(\mathfrak mR_m)^Nx\subset R_m \text{ for some }N\ge0\}. \] \end{enumerate} In every positive case all multivariable tensor maps are isomorphisms and the unique compatible plethory exists. For fraction-field coefficients $S=K$, this criterion is: \begin{enumerate} \item a single normalization branch at each finite-residue maximal ideal of height one; \item depth at least two at every finite-residue maximal ideal of height at least two. \end{enumerate} No hypothesis or restriction is imposed at maximal ideals with infinite residue field.

Put \[ T=\mathbb F_2[x,y]_{(x,y)},\qquad I=(x,y)^2T,\qquad R=\mathbb F_2+I,\qquad K=\mathbb F_2(x,y). \] Then $R$ is a two-dimensional Noetherian local domain with residue field $\mathbb F_2$ and finite normalization $T$. With $q(X)=X^2-X$, \[ \operatorname{Int}(R)=R\oplus RX\oplus q(X)T[X]. \] The nonzero tensor \[ z=(xq)\otimes q-q\otimes(xq) \] has zero polynomial image. Thus even fraction-field coefficients do not give uniquely determined polynomial tensors in this explicit higher-dimensional case, essentially of finite type over $\mathbb F_2$.

Let $R$ be a domain with fraction field $K$, let $V\subset K$ be a discrete valuation overring of $R$, and let $D:K\to K$ be a derivation satisfying $D(R)\subset V$. Suppose there are $u_n\in R$ with $v(u_n)\to\infty$ and $D(u_n)=1$. For $A=\operatorname{Int}(R)$ the map \[ \lambda:A\longrightarrow V,\qquad F\longmapsto F'(0) \] is well-defined. There is an $R$-balanced bilinear map \[ \beta:A\times A\longrightarrow K/V, \qquad \beta(F,G)=D(F'(0))G'(0)+V. \] If $P\in R[X]$, $c\in K$, $cP\in A$ and $D(c)P'(0)^2\notin V$, then \[ (cP)\otimes P-P\otimes(cP) \] is a nonzero tensor with zero polynomial image.

Let $k=\mathbb F_2$, $A_0=k[t]_{(t)}$, $n_0=0$ and $n_i=(i+1)!$ for $i\ge1$. In $k[[t]]$ set \[ z=\sum_{i\ge0}t^{n_i},\qquad z_i=\frac{z-\sum_{j<i}t^{n_j}}{t^{n_i}},\qquad u=t(z-1),\qquad s_i=(z_i-1)^2. \] Define \[ C=A_0[u,s_0,s_1,\ldots],\qquad M=(t,u)C,\qquad R=C_M. \] Then $R$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with residue field $k$, fraction field $K=k(t,z)$ and normalization a discrete valuation ring $V$ with parameter $t$ and residue field $k$. Its normalization is not a finite $R$-module. Nevertheless, unlike the finite-conductor one-branch cases, $\operatorname{Int}(R)$ has a noninjective tensor map. Explicitly, with $q(X)=X^2-X$ and $c=z-1$, \[ cq\in\operatorname{Int}(R),\qquad (cq)\otimes q-q\otimes(cq)\ne0, \] while its polynomial image is zero.

Let $A_0$ be any discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $t$ and finite residue field of cardinality $q$. Choose units $a_i\in A_0$ and exponents $n_0=0$, $n_{i+1}\ge2n_i+2$, such that $z=\sum_i a_it^{n_i}\in\widehat A_0$ is transcendental over $\operatorname{Frac}(A_0)$. Define $z_i,C,M,R$ by Reid's construction: \[ z_i=\frac{z-\sum_{j<i}a_jt^{n_j}}{t^{n_i}},\qquad C=A_0[t(z-a_0),(z_i-a_i)^2:i\ge0]. \] Put \[ M=(t,t(z-a_0))C,\qquad R=C_M. \] Then $R$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with nonfinite discrete valuation normalization $V$, as in Reid's opened theorem. With $c=z-a_0$ and $P=X^q-X$, one has $cP\in\operatorname{Int}(R)$ and \[ (cP)\otimes P-P\otimes(cP)\ne0, \] although its polynomial image is zero. This includes mixed characteristic; it is not restricted to characteristic two.

Let $V$ be an infinite valuation domain with fraction field $K$, and let $V\subset S$ be any $V$-torsion-free unital extension. Then every polynomial tensor map for $\Omega(V,S)$ is an isomorphism, and the unique compatible plethory exists. More precisely, put $L=S_{\mathrm{rat}}$. If the residue field of $V$ is infinite or its maximal ideal is nonprincipal, then $\Omega(V,S)=V[X]$. If its nonzero maximal ideal is principal, with finite residue field, then \[ \Omega(V,S)= \begin{cases} V[X],&L=V,\\ \operatorname{Int}(V),&L\ne V, \end{cases} \] and $\operatorname{Int}(V)$ has an explicit free Newton basis. This covers valuation domains of arbitrary rank and does not assume Noetherianity. A finite valuation domain is a finite field and is governed instead by B.013.

Let $R$ be an infinite Krull domain with fraction field $K$, and let $R\subset S$ be an $R$-torsion-free unital extension. Then $\Omega(R,S)$ is a projective $R$-module, every multivariable tensor map is an isomorphism, and the unique compatible plethory exists. No Noetherian hypothesis is needed. Here the Krull hypotheses used are precisely $R=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}R_{\mathfrak p}$, each $R_{\mathfrak p}$ a discrete valuation ring, and every nonzero element of $R$ lying in only finitely many such primes.

Let $k=\mathbb F_q$ be finite, let $l\supset k$ be any infinite field, and put \[ V=l[[t]],\qquad R=k+t^aV\quad(a\ge1),\qquad K=l((t)). \] For every $R$-torsion-free unital extension $R\subset S$, put $L=S_{\mathrm{rat}}$. Then the polynomial coaddition and comultiplication tensors are uniquely determined if and only if $L=R$. In particular fraction-field coefficients fail. For $A=\operatorname{Int}(R)$, $s\in l\setminus k$, $Q(X)=X^q-X$ and $F(X)=Q(X)^2/t^a$, an explicit kernel is \[ (sF)\otimes F-F\otimes(sF)\ne0. \] The ring $R$ is a non-Noetherian local domain with maximal ideal $t^aV$, residue field $k$, and fraction field $K$.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with finite residue field, let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, and put $A=\widehat R$ and $Q=K\otimes_R A$. For every number of variables $n$ there is a canonical isomorphism \[ \operatorname{Int}(R^n,R)\otimes_R A \simeq \operatorname{Int}(A^n,A)\subset Q[X_1,\ldots,X_n]. \] It identifies the tensor maps after faithfully flat base change. In particular a noninjective second tensor map for $A\subset Q$ implies a noninjective second tensor map for $R\subset K$.

Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a one-dimensional complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field. Assume that $A$ is Cohen--Macaulay and that either $A$ has characteristic $p>0$, or $A$ has characteristic zero and $p$ is a nonzerodivisor, where $p$ is its residue characteristic. If $A$ is not reduced, then \[ \operatorname{Int}(A)\otimes_A\operatorname{Int}(A) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Int}(A^2) \] is not injective. Here coefficients belong to the total quotient ring of $A$. The proof constructs a nonzero tensor and an explicit balanced linear functional detecting it.

Let $R$ be an infinite one-dimensional Noetherian domain, and put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. The compatible coaddition and comultiplication tensors for $\operatorname{Int}(R)$ are uniquely determined if and only if, at each maximal ideal with finite residue field, the completion $\widehat{R_{\mathfrak m}}$ is a domain. Equivalently, at each such ideal the normalization of $R_{\mathfrak m}$ is finite and local. In every positive case all multivariable tensor maps are isomorphisms and the compatible plethory is unique.

In the setting of B.044, let $R\subset L\subset K$ be any overring and put $B=L\otimes_R A\subset Q$. For every $n$ there is a natural isomorphism \[ \Omega_n(R,L)\otimes_R A\simeq\Omega_n(A,B). \] Here $\Omega_n(A,B)$ denotes the polynomials in $B[X_1, \ldots,X_n]$ taking $A^n$ into $A$. The tensor maps correspond, and existence of the coaddition and comultiplication expressions passes to this base change.

Let $V$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $t$ and fraction field $F$. Let $W$ be a finite-dimensional $F$-vector space, and let $M\subset W$ be a $V$-submodule containing a full $V$-lattice. There is an $F$-vector subspace $D=\bigcap_{j\ge0}t^jM$ such that $M/D$ is a finite free $V$-module. More precisely, after a choice of $F$-basis, $M$ is a direct sum of finitely many fractional ideals $t^aV$ and finitely many copies of $F$.

Let $V$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field, let $A$ be a local commutative $V$-algebra finite and torsion-free over $V$, and put $Q=A\otimes_V\operatorname{Frac}(V)$. For any overring $A\subset B\subset Q$, the multiplication map $B\otimes_A B\to B$ is an isomorphism if and only if \[ B=A+eQ \] for an idempotent $e\in Q$. Moreover injectivity of the second polynomial tensor map for $\Omega(A,B)$ forces this ring-epimorphism condition.

Let $R$ be an infinite one-dimensional Noetherian domain, let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, and let $R\subset S$ be an $R$-torsion-free unital extension. Put $L=S_{\mathrm{rat}}\subset K$ as in B.014. The coaddition and comultiplication tensors are uniquely determined if and only if at each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ with finite residue field either \[ \begin{gathered} L_{\mathfrak m}=R_{\mathfrak m},\qquad\hbox{or}\\ L_{\mathfrak m}=K\quad\hbox{and}\quad \widehat{R_{\mathfrak m}}\hbox{ is a domain}. \end{gathered} \tag{B50.1} \] Equivalently, in the second alternative the local normalization is finite and local. In every positive case all tensor maps are isomorphisms and the compatible plethory is unique. There is no finite-normalization assumption on $R$.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local domain with fraction field $K$, let $A=\widehat R$, $Q=K\otimes_R A$, and let $R\subset L\subset K$ be any overring. Put $B=L\otimes_R A\subset Q$. For every $n$, \[ \Omega_n(R,L)\otimes_R A \simeq\Omega_n(A,B). \tag{B51.1} \] The tensor maps and existence of the two polynomial co-operations pass through this identification. There is no dimension or finite-normalization hypothesis.

Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete Noetherian local ring, containing a complete discrete valuation ring $V$ with uniformizer $t$, with $t\in\mathfrak m$ a nonzerodivisor on $A$. Assume the residue field of $V$ maps isomorphically to $A/\mathfrak m$. Let $W\subset A$ be a multiplicative set of nonzerodivisors containing $t$, and put $Q=W^{-1}A$. Suppose \[ A\subset B\subset Q,\qquad \text{every element of }B/A\text{ is killed by a power of }\mathfrak m. \] Then there is a finite-dimensional $F=\operatorname{Frac}(V)$ vector space $D\subset B$ which is an ideal of $Q$, such that $B/D$ is a finite $A$-module and $A\cap D$ is a finite $V$-module. If $A\to B$ is a ring epimorphism, then \[ B=A+eQ,\qquad D=eQ \tag{B52.1} \] for an idempotent $e\in Q$, and $eQ$ is finite-dimensional over $F$. If the common residue field is finite, injectivity of the polynomial tensor map for $\Omega(A,B)$ implies this epimorphism condition.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local domain of dimension at least two with finite residue field, let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and $R\subset L\subset K$. Put \[ R^\sharp=\{x\in K:\mathfrak m^jx\subset R \text{ for some }j\},\qquad E=L\cap R^\sharp. \] The polynomial coaddition and comultiplication tensors are uniquely determined if and only if $E=R$, equivalently $\Omega(R,L)=R[X]$. No assumption on normalization is needed.

Let $R$ be a nonfield Noetherian domain with fraction field $K$, and let $R\subset S$ be an $R$-torsion-free unital extension. Put $L=S_{\mathrm{rat}}$. The polynomial coaddition and comultiplication tensors are uniquely determined exactly under the following conditions, imposed only at maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$ with finite residue field: \[ \begin{gathered} \dim R_{\mathfrak m}=1:\quad L_{\mathfrak m}=R_{\mathfrak m}\quad\hbox{or}\\ \bigl(L_{\mathfrak m}=K\text{ and } \widehat{R_{\mathfrak m}}\text{ is a domain}\bigr);\\[2mm] \dim R_{\mathfrak m}\ge2:\quad L_{\mathfrak m}\cap R_{\mathfrak m}^{\sharp}=R_{\mathfrak m}. \end{gathered} \tag{B54.1} \] There is no finite-normalization or finite bound on Krull dimension. In every positive case all multivariable tensor maps are isomorphisms and the compatible plethory is unique. For $S=K$, the first condition says finite local normalization with one branch, and the second is exactly $\operatorname{depth}R_{\mathfrak m}\ge2$.

Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring and $R\subset S$ an arbitrary unital inclusion. No torsion-free hypothesis is imposed. For every multiplicative subset $U\subset R$ and every $n$, \[ U^{-1}\Omega_n(R,S) =\Omega_n(U^{-1}R,U^{-1}S). \tag{B55.1} \] If $(R,\mathfrak m)$ is local, set $A=\widehat R$ and $S_A=S\otimes_R A$. Then \[ \Omega_n(R,S)\otimes_R A=\Omega_n(A,S_A). \tag{B55.2} \] When the residue field is finite, every coefficient of an integer-valued polynomial lies in the ring \[ \begin{gathered} C(R,S)=\bigcup_{j\ge0}(R:_S\mathfrak m^j),\\ (R:_S\mathfrak m^j)=\{s\in S:\mathfrak m^js\subset R\}. \end{gathered} \tag{B55.3} \] These rings commute with completion, and $C(R,S)/R$ is elementwise killed by powers of $\mathfrak m$. All tensor maps and the existence conditions commute with the identifications above.

Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field. Let $A\subset C$ be a unital ring epimorphism, and suppose every element of $C/A$ is killed by a power of $\mathfrak m$. Define \[ D=\bigcap_{j\ge0}\mathfrak m^j C,\qquad I=A\cap D. \] Then \[ C=A+D,\qquad D=\mathfrak mD=D^2=eC \tag{B56.1} \] for an idempotent $e\in C$, and there is an isomorphism of $A$-algebras \[ C\simeq D\times A/I,\qquad a\longmapsto(ea,a+I). \tag{B56.2} \] The ideal $D$ is finitely generated over $C$. No finiteness assumption on $C$ itself is needed.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ be a nonfield Noetherian local domain with finite residue field, let $K$ be its fraction field, and put $A=\widehat R$, $Q=K\otimes_R A$. Let $A\subset C$ be any unital extension such that $C/A$ is elementwise killed by powers of the maximal ideal of $A$. The polynomial coaddition and comultiplication tensors for $\Omega(A,C)$ are uniquely determined if and only if \[ C=A\quad\text{or}\quad \bigl(\dim R=1,\ A\text{ is a domain},\ C=Q\bigr), \tag{B57.1} \] where the second identification is as $A$-algebras. In both positive cases all multivariable tensor maps are isomorphisms. In particular no nonzero effective base torsion survives the uniqueness and existence requirements.

Let $R$ be a nonfield Noetherian domain with fraction field $K$, and let $R\subset S$ be an arbitrary unital inclusion, allowing base torsion in $S$. For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ with finite residue field define the actual coefficient subring of $S_{\mathfrak m}$ \[ C_{\mathfrak m} =\{s\in S_{\mathfrak m}:\mathfrak m^jR_{\mathfrak m}s \subset R_{\mathfrak m}\text{ for some }j\}. \] The polynomial coaddition and comultiplication tensors are uniquely determined if and only if, for every such $\mathfrak m$, \[ \begin{gathered} C_{\mathfrak m}=R_{\mathfrak m},\quad\text{or}\\ \dim R_{\mathfrak m}=1,\qquad \widehat{R_{\mathfrak m}}\text{ is a domain},\qquad C_{\mathfrak m}=K. \tag{B58.1} \end{gathered} \] The last equality means the canonical copy of $K$ extending $R_{\mathfrak m}$ inside $S_{\mathfrak m}$. No torsion-free or finite-normalization hypothesis is imposed. In every positive case all multivariable tensor maps are isomorphisms and the compatible plethory is unique. Together with B.013--B.014, this settles every Noetherian domain base and every commutative coefficient extension.

Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete one-dimensional Noetherian Cohen--Macaulay local ring with finite residue field, in arbitrary characteristic. Write $Q=Q(A)$ for its total quotient ring. If $A$ is nonreduced, the polynomial tensor map for $\operatorname{Int}(A)\subset Q[X]$ is not injective. This includes generic local factors of characteristic $p^a$ for $a>1$ and mixed-characteristic rings in which $p$ is a zero divisor. The same detector applies to a selected nonreduced local Artinian ring $Q_0$ as an idempotent factor of a coefficient extension of an ambient complete local ring, provided its image order $A_0$ is a complete one-dimensional Cohen--Macaulay quotient and a finite order in $Q_0$ has a nonzero conductor into the ambient ring.

Under the hypotheses of B.056, suppose $D\ne0$, and let $A_0=eA\subset D$ be the image order. Then $A_0$ is a complete one-dimensional Cohen--Macaulay local ring, and \[ D=Q(A_0). \tag{B60.1} \] The ideal $I=A\cap D$ maps injectively into $A_0$ as an ideal containing a nonzerodivisor of $A_0$. If $I$ is proper in $A$, it is also proper in $A_0$. This conclusion has no characteristic restriction.

Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be any complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field, and let $A\subset C$ be a unital extension with $C/A$ elementwise killed by powers of $\mathfrak m$. The polynomial coaddition and comultiplication tensors are uniquely determined if and only if \[ C=A\quad\text{or}\quad \bigl(A\text{ is a one-dimensional domain}, C=\operatorname{Frac}(A)\bigr). \tag{B61.1} \] Every positive case has all multivariable tensor isomorphisms. Thus an actual zero-divisor local base has only the ordinary-polynomial positive case.

Let $R$ be any nonzero Noetherian commutative ring and let $R\subset S$ be any unital commutative extension. For each finite-residue maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ form \[ C_{\mathfrak m} =\{s\in S_{\mathfrak m}:\mathfrak m^jR_{\mathfrak m}s \subset R_{\mathfrak m}\text{ for some }j\}. \] The polynomial coaddition and comultiplication tensors are uniquely determined exactly when, at every such maximal ideal, \[ \begin{gathered} C_{\mathfrak m}=R_{\mathfrak m},\quad\text{or}\\ R_{\mathfrak m}\text{ is a one-dimensional domain},\\ \widehat{R_{\mathfrak m}}\text{ is a domain},\qquad C_{\mathfrak m}=\operatorname{Frac}(R_{\mathfrak m}). \tag{B62.1} \end{gathered} \] The fraction field is required as the canonical subring extending $R_{\mathfrak m}$ inside $S_{\mathfrak m}$. No reducedness, domain, torsion-free, or finite-normalization assumption is imposed on the original inclusion. In every positive case all multivariable tensor maps are isomorphisms and the compatible plethory is unique.

Let $(V,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonfield valuation domain, of arbitrary rank, and let $V\subset S$ be any unital commutative extension. If the residue field is infinite, every such extension has the unique standard polynomial co-operations. If the residue field is finite, the polynomial coaddition and comultiplication tensors are uniquely determined if and only if \[ \operatorname{Ann}_S(\mathfrak m)=0. \tag{B63.1} \] Every positive case has all multivariable tensor isomorphisms. This removes the torsion-free restriction from B.041; base torsion away from the maximal-ideal socle is permitted.

For any unital inclusion $R\subset S$ and $d\ge1$, let $D_d(R)$ be the ideal generated by all Vandermonde determinants on $d+1$ elements of $R$, and put \[ C_d=(R:_S D_d(R)),\qquad C=\bigcup_{d\ge1}C_d. \tag{B64.1} \] Then $C$ is a subring of $S$. It is exactly the set of coefficients that occur in integer-valued polynomials, and also exactly the set of their possible leading coefficients, with zero included. Every multivariable integer-valued polynomial has its coefficients in $C$. If the second polynomial tensor map is injective, the inclusion $R\to C$ is a ring epimorphism. If $C=R$, all tensor maps are the ordinary polynomial isomorphisms.

Let $R$ be an absolutely flat commutative ring, meaning that every $R$-module is flat, and let $R\subset S$ be any unital commutative extension. With the explicit Vandermonde ideals of B.064, the following are equivalent: \[ \begin{gathered} \text{the polynomial co-operations are uniquely determined};\\ \theta_2\text{ is injective};\qquad (R:_S D_d(R))=R\text{ for every }d;\\ \operatorname{Ann}_{S/R}(D_d(R))=0\text{ for every }d;\qquad \Omega(R,S)=R[X]. \tag{B65.1} \end{gathered} \] Every positive case has all polynomial tensor isomorphisms. In particular, for any Boolean ring, finite or infinite, the positive extensions are exactly $S=R$.

For every unital inclusion $R\subset S$, let $D_d(R)$ be the explicit Vandermonde ideal of B.064. Evaluation \[ \Omega(R,S)\longrightarrow\operatorname{App}(R,R) \] is injective if and only if \[ \operatorname{Ann}_S(D_d(R))=0 \quad\text{for every }d\ge1. \tag{B66.1} \] There are no finiteness, reducedness, domain or torsion-free hypotheses. Thus B.2(d), for the polynomial analyser of any ring inclusion, has an explicit ring-ideal criterion rather than only a degreewise evaluation-matrix restatement.

There is an explicit proper inclusion $R\subset S$ of zero-dimensional local $\mathbb F_2$-algebras such that every nilpotent squares to zero, $R$ is non-Noetherian, and every map \[ \Omega(R,S)^{\otimes_R n}\longrightarrow\Omega_n(R,S) \] is an isomorphism. Nevertheless $\Omega(R,S)$ is not flat over $R$, and the coefficient ring of B.064 is the proper ring $S$. Thus flatness of the analyser or of its coefficient ring cannot be imposed as a necessary condition in the remaining non-Noetherian classification.

Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring, let $Q$ be its total quotient ring, and let $D_d(R)$ be the Vandermonde ideals of B.064. Suppose that, for every $d\ge1$, the ideal $D_d(R)$ contains a nonzerodivisor of $R$, and \[ (R:_Q D_d(R))=R. \tag{B68.1} \] Then for every unital inclusion $R\subset S$ the following are equivalent: \[ \begin{gathered} \text{the polynomial co-operations exist uniquely};\\ \theta_2\text{ is injective};\\ \Omega(R,S)\longrightarrow\operatorname{App}(R,R) \text{ is injective};\\ \operatorname{Ann}_S(D_d(R))=0\quad\text{for every }d;\\ \Omega(R,S)=R[X]. \tag{B68.2} \end{gathered} \] Every positive case has all multivariable polynomial tensor isomorphisms. The hypotheses hold for every infinite domain with $\operatorname{Int}(R,\operatorname{Frac}R)=R[X]$. They also hold for $R=A[Z,W]$ over every nonzero commutative ring $A$, without finiteness or reducedness assumptions. More generally they hold for $R=A[Z]$ whenever each $D_d(A)$ contains a nonzerodivisor; in particular, this includes every infinite domain $A$.

Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring. Suppose that, at each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ with finite residue field, the local maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mR_{\mathfrak m}$ satisfies \[ \mathfrak n=(a^N:a\in\mathfrak n) \quad\text{for every integer }N\ge1. \tag{B69.1} \] Then for every unital inclusion $R\subset S$ the following conditions are equivalent: \[ \begin{gathered} \text{the polynomial co-operations exist uniquely};\\ \theta_2\text{ is injective};\qquad C=R;\\ (R:_S D_d(R))=R\quad\text{for every }d\ge1;\\ \operatorname{Ann}_{S/R}(D_d(R))=0\quad\text{for every }d\ge1;\\ \Omega(R,S)=R[X], \tag{B69.2} \end{gathered} \] where $C$ is the actual coefficient ring of B.064. Every positive case has all multivariable polynomial tensor isomorphisms. In particular this class includes every commutative $\mathbb F_p$-algebra with surjective Frobenius, with arbitrary nilpotents and without Noetherian assumptions. Surjectivity, rather than injectivity, of Frobenius is what this assertion requires.

Let $R$ be a nonzero binomial ring: its additive group is $\mathbb Z$-torsion-free, and $\binom r n\in R$ for every $r\in R$ and $n\ge0$, with the fraction interpreted in $\mathbb Q\otimes R$. For every unital commutative inclusion $R\subset S$, the polynomial coaddition and comultiplication tensors are uniquely determined if and only if the additive group of $S$ is $\mathbb Z$-torsion-free. In every positive case all multivariable polynomial tensor maps are isomorphisms. No Noetherian, domain or reducedness hypothesis is required on $R$, and $S$ may have torsion as an $R$-module. This includes $R=\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb Z)$, and also the nonreduced non-Noetherian binomial ring $R=\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Q\epsilon$ with $\epsilon^2=0$.

Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be any nonzero local commutative ring with finite residue field and $\mathfrak m=\pi A$, and let $A\subset S$ be a unital commutative inclusion. Put \[ C=\{s\in S:\pi^Ns\in A \text{ for some }N\ge0\}. \] Then the polynomial coaddition and comultiplication tensors are uniquely determined precisely in the following cases: \[ C=A,\quad\text{or}\quad \pi\text{ is regular in }A\text{ and }C=A[1/\pi] \text{ as a canonical subring of }S. \tag{B71.1} \] Every positive case has all polynomial tensor isomorphisms. If $\pi$ is regular in $A$, the criterion is equivalently $\operatorname{Ann}_S(\pi)=0$. If $\pi$ is nilpotent, the criterion reduces to $S=A$. Neither Noetherianity nor reducedness is assumed.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero local $\mathbb F_p$-algebra with finite residue field $\mathbb F_q$. Suppose that $x^p=0$ for every $x\in\mathfrak m$; the ideal $\mathfrak m$ need not be nilpotent or finitely generated. For every unital inclusion $R\subset S$, the following are equivalent: \[ \begin{gathered} \text{the polynomial co-operations exist uniquely};\\ \theta_2\text{ is injective};\\ R\longrightarrow S\text{ is a ring epimorphism and } (R:_S\mathfrak m)=R. \tag{B72.1} \end{gathered} \] Every positive case has all multivariable polynomial tensor isomorphisms. Thus the nonflat example B.067 lies in a fully classified class of possibly infinite, non-Noetherian bases. If $\mathfrak m$ is nilpotent as an ideal, these conditions force $S=R$.

Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring with nilradical $N$. Suppose $R/N$ is absolutely flat and $N$ is T-nilpotent: for every sequence $n_1,n_2,\ldots$ in $N$, some finite product $n_1\cdots n_j$ is zero. Then every injective ring epimorphism out of $R$ is an isomorphism. Consequently, for every unital inclusion $R\subset S$, the following are equivalent: \[ \begin{gathered} \text{the polynomial co-operations exist uniquely};\\ \theta_2\text{ is injective};\qquad C=R;\\ (R:_S D_d(R))=R\quad\text{for every }d\ge1;\\ \operatorname{Ann}_{S/R}(D_d(R))=0\quad\text{for every }d\ge1;\\ \Omega(R,S)=R[X]. \tag{B73.1} \end{gathered} \] All positive cases have every multivariable polynomial tensor isomorphism. In particular the theorem applies to every zero-dimensional ring with T-nilpotent nilradical; the nilradical need not be nilpotent.

Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring such that, for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ with finite residue field, the maximal ideal of $R_{\mathfrak m}$ contains a regular sequence of length two. For every unital extension $R\subset S$, the polynomial co-operations exist uniquely exactly when \[ (R:_S D_d(R))=R\quad\text{for every }d\ge1, \quad\text{equivalently}\quad \operatorname{Ann}_{S/R}(D_d(R))=0\quad\text{for every }d. \tag{B74.1} \] This is also equivalent to tensor injectivity, to $C=R$, and to $\Omega(R,S)=R[X]$. All positive cases have all tensor isomorphisms. There is no Noetherian, reducedness or coefficient-torsion hypothesis. The proof does not presume localization of $\Omega$.

Let $k=\mathbb F_q\subset l$ with $l$ an infinite field, let $a\ge1$, and put \[ V=l[[t]],\qquad K=l((t)),\qquad R=k+t^aV,\qquad \mathfrak m=t^aV. \] For every unital commutative inclusion $R\subset S$, with arbitrary $R$-torsion in $S$, the following are equivalent: \[ \begin{gathered} \text{the polynomial co-operations exist uniquely};\\ \theta_2\text{ is injective};\qquad (R:_S\mathfrak m)=R;\\ \operatorname{Ann}_{S/R}(\mathfrak m)=0;\qquad \Omega(R,S)=R[X]. \tag{B75.1} \end{gathered} \] Every positive case has all multivariable tensor isomorphisms. This removes the torsion-free restriction from the entire family B.043, including the explicit base $\mathbb F_2+t\mathbb F_2(u)[[t]]$.

Let $V$ be a valuation domain of characteristic $p$ with infinite residue field $l$, containing a finite subfield $k=\mathbb F_q$. Let $0\ne x\in\mathfrak m_V$, and put \[ R=k+xV,\qquad\mathfrak m=xV. \] For every unital commutative inclusion $R\subset S$, the polynomial coaddition and comultiplication tensors exist uniquely if and only if \[ (R:_S\mathfrak m)=R. \tag{B76.1} \] This is equivalent to tensor injectivity, to the absence of a $\mathfrak m$-annihilator in $S/R$, and to $\Omega(R,S)=R[X]$. All positive cases have every multivariable tensor isomorphism. No discreteness, rank, completeness, or coefficient-torsion condition is imposed. The conductor $xV$ is principal as a $V$-ideal; it need not be principal as an $R$-ideal.

Let $V$ be a characteristic-$p$ valuation domain with infinite residue field $l$ and a nontrivial valuation $v:K^\times\to\Gamma\subset\mathbb R$, where $K=\operatorname{Frac}(V)$. Suppose $V$ contains $k=\mathbb F_q$. Let $J$ be any nonzero proper ideal of $V$ and put $R=k+J$. For every unital commutative inclusion $R\subset S$, with arbitrary base torsion, the following are equivalent: \[ \begin{gathered} \text{the polynomial co-operations exist uniquely};\\ \theta_2\text{ is injective};\qquad (R:_S J)=R;\\ \operatorname{Ann}_{S/R}(J)=0;\qquad \Omega(R,S)=R[X]. \tag{B77.1} \end{gathered} \] All positive cases have every multivariable polynomial tensor isomorphism. The ideal $J$ may be an open or irrational valuation cut; it need not have a generator or a least element of its value set. In particular this settles the previously listed Hahn example with residue $\mathbb F_2(u)$, value group $\mathbb Q$, and $J=\{v>\sqrt2\}$.

Let $V$ be a valuation domain with fraction field $K$ and infinite residue field $l$. Let $R\subset V$ be a unital subring containing a nonzero proper $V$-ideal $J$, and suppose $R/J=k$ is a finite field of cardinality $q$. No coefficient-field section or characteristic assumption is imposed. For every unital commutative extension $R\subset S$, the following are equivalent: \[ \begin{gathered} \text{the standard polynomial co-operations exist uniquely};\\ \theta_2\text{ is injective};\qquad (R:_S J)=R;\\ \operatorname{Ann}_{S/R}(J)=0;\qquad \Omega(R,S)=R[X]. \tag{B78.1} \end{gathered} \] Every positive case has all multivariable polynomial tensor isomorphisms. The valuation may have arbitrary rank and arbitrary cardinality; the ideal may be nonprincipal and need not have a value-group infimum.

For an arbitrary unital inclusion $R\subset S$, let $C=\bigcup_d(R:_S D_d(R))$ be the effective coefficient ring of B.064, and put $Q=C/R$. Define the $R$-module directly by finite coefficient relations \[ N(R,Q)=\left\{(q_0,q_1,\ldots)\in\bigoplus_{i\ge0}Q: \sum_i r^i q_i=0\text{ for every }r\in R\right\}. \tag{B79.1} \] If the polynomial tensor map $\theta_2$ is injective, then $R\to C$ is epic and \[ C\otimes_R\Omega(R,S)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } C[X], \qquad C\otimes_RN(R,Q)=0. \tag{B79.2} \] The two assertions in (B79.2) are equivalent, without assuming injectivity of $\theta_2$. They are necessary conditions, not a universal sufficient criterion. Even when $C$ is a flat localization of a domain $R$, they do not imply injectivity of $\theta_2$ or injectivity of multiplication by monic polynomials on its source.

Let $R\subset S$ be any unital commutative inclusion. Form the explicit coefficient ring $C=\bigcup_d(R:_S D_d(R))$ of B.064, and assume that $R\to C$ is flat and epic. Put $Q=C/R$ and define the $R$-module \[ E=\left\{\left(r\longmapsto\sum_{i=0}^d c_i r^i+R\right): d\ge0,\ c_i\in C\right\} \subset\operatorname{App}(R,Q). \tag{B80.1} \] Thus $E$ is specified by coefficient and value relations in $R\subset C$, without choosing tensor presentations of integer-valued polynomials. For $A=\Omega(R,S)$ there is a canonical exact sequence \[ \begin{gathered} 0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tor}_2^R(E,E) \longrightarrow A\otimes_R A\\ \xrightarrow{\theta_2} C[X,Y] \xrightarrow{\partial}\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(E,E) \longrightarrow0. \end{gathered} \tag{B80.2} \] The map $\partial$ is given explicitly below, with all connecting maps fixed by the evaluation sequence. In particular the two tensors on 153/004 exist uniquely exactly when \[ \begin{gathered} \operatorname{Tor}_2^R(E,E)=0,\\ \partial\!\left(\sum_{i,j\ge0}\binom{i+j}{i} a_{i+j}X^iY^j\right)=0,\\ \partial\!\left(\sum_{i\ge0}a_iX^iY^i\right)=0 \tag{B80.3} \end{gathered} \] for every finite vector $(a_i)$ in $C$ satisfying $\sum_i a_i r^i\in R$ for all $r\in R$; missing coefficients are zero. If only flatness of $C$ is initially assumed, epicness is an additional necessary condition, and epicness together with (B80.3) is sufficient. This is an exact obstruction calculation for the flat-coefficient scope, not a classification of arbitrary nonflat coefficient extensions.

Every injective ring epimorphism $R\to C$ is an isomorphism in either of the following situations: \begin{enumerate} \item $R$ is a directed union of unital self-injective subrings, where self-injective means injective as a module over itself. \item $R$ is local with nil maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and it has an ideal $I$ such that $\mathfrak m^N I=0$ for some finite $N$, while every injective ring epimorphism out of $R/I$ is an isomorphism. \end{enumerate} For any such base and any unital inclusion $R\subset S$, the polynomial co-operations exist uniquely exactly when \[ (R:_S D_d(R))=R\quad\text{for all }d\ge1, \quad\text{equivalently}\quad \Omega(R,S)=R[X]. \tag{B81.1} \] Every positive case has all multivariable tensor isomorphisms. In particular this completely decides all coefficient extensions of the previously specified test base \[ R=\mathbb F_2[z,x_1,x_2,\ldots]/ (z^2,\ zx_i\ (i\ge1),\ x_i^{2^{i+1}}\ (i\ge1)). \tag{B81.2} \] This base is local of dimension zero and non-Noetherian; its maximal ideal is not T-nilpotent and its elementwise nilpotence has no uniform bound. Thus the conclusion does not follow from those earlier bounded-nilpotence cases.

Let $R\subset S$ be any unital inclusion of commutative rings. The following construction uses only ideals, coefficient functions and finite linear relations associated with this inclusion. It imposes no finiteness, reducedness, flatness or domain hypothesis. First form \[ \begin{gathered} C=\bigcup_{d\ge1}(R:_S D_d(R)),\qquad \mathcal F=C[X],\\ E=\operatorname{im}\left(\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\varepsilon} \operatorname{App}(R,C/R)\right),\\ \varepsilon\left(\sum c_iX^i\right)(r)=\sum c_ir^i+R. \end{gathered} \tag{B82.1} \] The first arithmetic test is that every $c\in C$ have a finite matrix presentation \[ \begin{gathered} c=Y M Z,\qquad M\in\operatorname{Mat}_{n}(R),\\ Y\in C^{1\times n},\quad Z\in C^{n\times1},\quad YM\in R^{1\times n},\quad MZ\in R^{n\times1}. \end{gathered} \tag{B82.2} \] This test is equivalent to epicness of $R\to C$. If it fails, the requested tensors are not uniquely determined. When it holds, define the following finite-depth syzygy invariants. Set \[ \begin{aligned} U_q&=\operatorname{Tor}_q^R(\mathcal F,\mathcal F),\\ V_q&=\operatorname{Tor}_q^R(\mathcal F,E) \oplus\operatorname{Tor}_q^R(E,\mathcal F),\\ W_q&=\operatorname{Tor}_q^R(E,E),\qquad U_q\xrightarrow{a_q}V_q\xrightarrow{b_q}W_q, \end{aligned} \tag{B82.3} \] where \[ \begin{aligned} a_q&=(\operatorname{Tor}_q(1,\varepsilon), \operatorname{Tor}_q(\varepsilon,1)),\\ b_q&=\operatorname{Tor}_q(\varepsilon,1) -\operatorname{Tor}_q(1,\varepsilon). \end{aligned} \tag{B82.4} \] The two terms of $b_q$ act on the respective summands of $V_q$; thus $b_qa_q=0$. Put \[ Z_q=\ker a_q,\quad T_q=\operatorname{coker}b_q,\quad K_1=\ker b_1/\operatorname{im}a_1. \tag{B82.5} \] There are canonical maps, explicitly constructed in the proof, \[ \begin{gathered} \delta_0:C[X,Y]=Z_0\longrightarrow T_1, \qquad \delta_1:Z_1\longrightarrow T_2,\\ K_2=T_2/\operatorname{im}\delta_1. \end{gathered} \tag{B82.6} \] The two polynomial tensors on 153/004 exist uniquely if and only if (B82.2) holds and \[ \begin{gathered} K_1=K_2=0,\\ \delta_0\left(\sum_{i,j\ge0}\binom{i+j}{i} a_{i+j}X^iY^j\right)=0,\\ \delta_0\left(\sum_{i\ge0}a_iX^iY^i\right)=0 \tag{B82.7} \end{gathered} \] for every finite coefficient vector $(a_i)$ in $C$ satisfying $\sum_i a_ir^i\in R$ for every $r\in R$. Missing coefficients are zero. All quantities in this test are defined before forming any tensor power of $\Omega(R,S)$; in particular it is not a test that presupposes the image or kernel of that tensor map. Its free-module implementation below uses only finite coefficient relations in homological degrees at most three. The criterion does not assert a uniformly terminating algorithm for arbitrary presentations of infinite rings, and it does not replace the separate higher-coherence conditions for a plethory by a binary test.

Let $R\xrightarrow{u}K\xrightarrow{\rho}L\xrightarrow{\delta}R[1]$ be a distinguished triangle in $D(\Lambda[t,t^{-1}])$, and suppose that $t-1=0$ as an endomorphism of $L$ in that category. Then there is a morphism $V:K\to R$ with $uV=t-1$. For any one such $V_0$, the entire set of choices is \[ V_0+\operatorname{im}\bigl( \operatorname{Hom}(K,L[-1])\xrightarrow{\delta[-1]\circ-} \operatorname{Hom}(K,R)\bigr). \] In particular, existence does not imply uniqueness. This applies to the triangle of cote 122, scan 022, with $R=D_\Lambda K[-2n]$, once its boundary action is trivial as an object of the derived category.

The hypotheses of C.001, including perfectness, Poincare--Lefschetz duality, and a trivial boundary action, do not force $V$ to be unique. There is a geometric counterexample in every integer $n\geq2$: \[ M=S^n\times D^n,\qquad \partial M=S^n\times S^{n-1}, \qquad h=\operatorname{id}_M, \] with coefficients in any field $\Lambda$. The actual variation of this identity monodromy is zero, whereas the factorization equation admits nonzero solutions.

Let $(M,B)$ be a compact triangulable manifold with boundary $B$, and let $h:M\to M$ be a homeomorphism that is the identity on $B$. Let $t$ act on singular chains by $h_\#$ and on cochains by pullback $h^*$ (this choice fixes the generator convention). There is an equivariant cochain map \[ V:C^*(M;\Lambda)\longrightarrow C^*(M,B;\Lambda), \qquad (Vc)([z])=c(h_\#z-z). \] If $u:C^*(M,B)\to C^*(M)$ is the usual inclusion, then $uV=h^*-1$ and $Vu=h^*_{\mathrm{rel}}-1$ as actual cochain maps. The induced derived map agrees with classical variation in SGA~7~II, XIV, 3.1.9--3.1.10, after matching its transport-of-structure convention.

Orient a compact smooth $2n$-manifold $M$ and its boundary $B$ by the outward-normal-first convention. Write $r:H^i(M)\to H^i(B)$ for restriction and $\delta:H^{2n-i-1}(B)\to H^{2n-i}(M,B)$ for the connecting map. With ordinary cohomology in the first slot of each duality pairing, \[ \langle b,\delta a\rangle_M =(-1)^i\langle rb,a\rangle_B. \tag{C.7.1} \] Thus the degree-$n$ arrows $\rho$ and $\rho'$ in scan 022 are transposes with sign $(-1)^n$. For the whole graded triangle the sign is $(-1)^i$, not one scalar independent of degree. Using the relative class in the first slot instead gives the sign-free identity $\langle\delta a,b\rangle_M=\langle a,rb\rangle_B$. For an isolated hypersurface Milnor page let $H=H_n(M;\mathbb Z)$, $Q=H_n(M,B;\mathbb Z)$, $v:Q\to H$ be homological variation for positive monodromy, and $\epsilon=(-1)^n$. The pairing $(q,x)$ between $Q$ and $H$ is the oriented intersection number. In the Seifert convention \[ L(x,y)=-\epsilon\,(v^{-1}y,x), \tag{C.7.2} \] the intersection pairing $I$ represented by the middle map $u$ satisfies \[ I=L+\epsilon L^{\mathsf t},\qquad L(x,Ty)=-\epsilon L(y,x). \tag{C.7.3} \] In column-vector bases dual for $(q,x)$, these are $V=-\epsilon L^{-1}$ and $T=-\epsilon L^{-1}L^{\mathsf t}$. These conventions specify the signs completely.

Let $S$ be an excellent strictly henselian trait of residue characteristic $p$, let $f:X\to S$ be separated of finite type, and let $x$ be a geometric closed point of the special fibre. Suppose that near $x$ the generic fibre is smooth and pure of dimension $n$, and that $f$ is smooth on the special fibre away from $x$. Take $\Lambda=\mathbb Z/\ell^a$ with $\ell\ne p$, or a finite field of characteristic $\ell$. Let $I$ be inertia, $P_w$ its wild pro-$p$ subgroup, and $I_t=I/P_w$. On the strict localization at $x$ put \[ K=(R\Psi\Lambda)_x,\quad R=R\Gamma_{\{x\}}(X_s,R\Psi\Lambda),\quad L=R\Gamma(X_s\setminus\{x\},\Lambda). \] There is an $I$-equivariant triangle \[ R\xrightarrow{u}K\longrightarrow L^{\rm triv}\longrightarrow R[1], \qquad R\simeq D_\Lambda K(-n)[-2n]. \tag{C.8.1} \] Consequently $K_t=K^{P_w}$ has the triangle in the continuous derived category of $\Lambda[I_t]$-modules \[ D_\Lambda K_t(-n)[-2n]\xrightarrow{u_t}K_t \longrightarrow L^{\rm triv}\longrightarrow. \tag{C.8.2} \] For a chosen $\sigma\in I_t$, canonical nearby/vanishing-cycle variation gives $V_\sigma:K_t\to D_\Lambda K_t(-n)[-2n]$ with $u_tV_\sigma=\sigma-1$. This choice is geometric; it is not the unique abstract lift furnished by the triangle. If wild inertia acts trivially, $K_t=K$ and (C.8.2) is the requested tame version for the whole fibre. For a bounded perfect tame complex, continuous group duality gives \[ R\Gamma(I_t,D_\Lambda K_t) \simeq D_\Lambda R\Gamma(I_t,K_t)(-1)[-1]. \tag{C.8.3} \] Hence the left term after derived tame invariants in (C.8.2) is $D_\Lambda R\Gamma(I_t,K_t)(-n-1)[-2n-1]$. For trivial $L$ the right term is $L\oplus L(-1)[-1]$. The shifts and twists $(-n)$ and $(-n-1)$ are therefore forced, rather than interchangeable conventions.

Smooth total space and an isolated non-smooth point do not in themselves make nearby cycles tame. Consequently the assertion that the whole $K$ carries a tame-inertia action requires a tameness hypothesis; without it, (C.8.2) applies to $K^{P_w}$.

Let $M$ be a connected compact oriented $2n$-manifold with nonempty boundary $B$, where $n\geq2$. Suppose that an open book with page $M$, binding $B$, and monodromy fixed on $B$ has total space $W=S^{2n+1}$. Assume that $B$ is $(n-2)$-connected and that $H^j(M;\Lambda)=0$ for $j>n$, where $\Lambda$ is a field. Then $H^{n-1}(M;\Lambda)=0$. These hypotheses hold for the compact Milnor page of an isolated critical point of a holomorphic function on a smooth complex $(n+1)$-fold.
The statement $H^{n-1}(M;\Lambda)=0$ in C.1(d) and Lead L5 is false if $n=1$ is included literally. The correct uniform assertion is $\widetilde H^{n-1}(M;\Lambda)=0$.

For an isolated complex hypersurface critical point with smooth total space and complex fibre dimension $n\geq1$, $\widetilde H^j(M;A)=0$ for $j<n$ and every abelian coefficient group $A$. In particular the unreduced assertion requested in C.1(d) holds when $n\geq2$, and must be reduced when $n=1$. The boundary duality triangle, its six-term middle sequence, the upper cohomological bound, and $(n-2)$-connectedness of the boundary, taken by themselves, do not imply $H^{n-1}(M)=0$.

The following assertions, if read literally in scans 003, 007, 022, 030, 032 and 034, are false. Each has the correction specified below. \begin{enumerate} \item For a merely paracompact manifold with boundary, compactly supported interior cohomology cannot replace relative cohomology in the ordinary boundary triangle. On a compact finite-type manifold it can. Without finite-type hypotheses, duality must also retain its correct dual direction rather than identify a vector space with its double dual. \item In scan 007 the complementary manifold is $Q=W\setminus\mathring P$, not the written $P\setminus\mathring P$. \item In scan 022 an equivariant map $D_\Lambda K[-2n]\to K$ is classified by $H^{2n}(R\Gamma(\pi,K\otimes^L K))$, not in general by $H^{2n}(K\otimes^L K)$. \item For a Milnor open-book complement $P=W\setminus B$, the upper bound is $H^i(P)=0$ for $i>n+1$. The stronger bound $i>n$ in one reading of scan 030 fails. The upper bound $H^i(M)=0$ for $i>n$ for the fibre is true independently. \item The arrow $H^{n-1}(B)\to H^n(M)^\vee$ in scan 032 need not be surjective. In scan 034 the list of possible nonzero degrees of $B=V_s$ must include its top degree $2n-1$. \end{enumerate}

Let $M$ be a compact oriented $2n$-manifold with nonempty boundary $B$, where $n\geq1$, let $h:M\to M$ preserve orientation and fix a collar of $B$, and set \[ P=(M\times[0,1])/((x,1)\sim(hx,0)),\quad Q=B\times D^2,\quad W=P\cup_{B\times S^1}Q. \] The gluing uses the identity on $B$ and the positive angular coordinate. It gives a closed oriented $(2n+1)$-manifold. With coefficients in a field, all the boundary, support, Mayer--Vietoris, duality and residue statements on scans 003--034 hold with the corrections in C.017 and the conventions below. The same derived triangles hold over any commutative ring when the finite complexes and orientation twists are retained. In particular, if $W$ is a cohomology sphere, then \[ H^i(P)\xrightarrow{\ \beta\ }H^{i-1}(B) \quad\hbox{is an isomorphism for }i\notin\{0,2n\}, \tag{C.10.1} \] and \[ H^0(P)=\Lambda,\qquad 0\longrightarrow H^{2n}(P)\longrightarrow H^{2n-1}(B) \xrightarrow{\int_B}\Lambda\longrightarrow0. \tag{C.10.2} \] Thus $H^{2n}(P)=0$ exactly when $B$ is connected. No unqualified assertion about degree zero of a one-dimensional Milnor fibre is implicit here.
Let $A$ be a commutative noetherian ring, let $E$ be a finite $A$-module with $\operatorname{Supp}_A(E)=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, and let $N$ be any $A$-module. Then $E\otimes_A N=0$ implies $N=0$.

Let $X$ be a projective scheme over a field $k$, let $\mathcal O_X(1)$ be a very ample line bundle, let $Y\subseteq X$ be closed, and put $U=X\setminus Y$. Let $E$ be a coherent sheaf with support all of $X$, and let $m\geq1$. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $H^p(U,F)=0$ for every coherent sheaf $F$ on $U$ and every $p\geq m$; \item $H^p(U,E(-N)|_U)=0$ for all $p\geq m$ and all sufficiently large integers $N$. \end{enumerate} There is no local-freeness assumption on $E$.

Let $X$ be a projective Cohen--Macaulay $k$-scheme, pure of dimension $r$, let $\omega_X$ denote its dualizing sheaf, let $Y$ be closed, and let $\widehat X$ be the completion along $Y$. For every coherent $F$ and every integer $p$ there are natural identifications \[ H^p(X,F)^\vee\cong\operatorname{Ext}^{r-p}_X(F,\omega_X), \qquad H_Y^p(X,F)^\vee\cong \operatorname{Ext}^{r-p}_{\widehat X}(\widehat F,\widehat\omega_X). \tag{C.13.1} \] Here $(-)^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(-,k)$ is the full algebraic dual, and the formal Ext is hyper-Ext of coherent modules on the formal scheme. The dual of $H_Y^p(X,F)\to H^p(X,F)$ is the completion map on the right. Moreover \[ R\mathcal Hom_X(\omega_X,\omega_X)\simeq\mathcal O_X, \qquad R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat X}(\widehat\omega_X,\widehat\omega_X) \simeq\mathcal O_{\widehat X}. \tag{C.13.2} \]

Assume the hypotheses of C.013, choose a very ample $\mathcal O_X(1)$, and fix $0<m<r$. Put $d=r-m>0$ and $U=X\setminus Y$. The following seven conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $H^p(U,F)=0$ for every coherent $F$ on $U$ and every $p\geq m$. \item $H^p(U,\mathcal O_X(-N)|_U)=0$ for $p\geq m$, $N\gg0$. \item For every coherent $F$ on $X$, $H_Y^p(X,F)\to H^p(X,F)$ is bijective for $p>m$ and surjective for $p=m$. \item Condition (3) holds for $F=\mathcal O_X(-N)$, $N\gg0$. \item For every coherent $F$ on $X$, the completion map \[ \operatorname{Ext}^q_X(F,\omega_X)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Ext}^q_{\widehat X}(\widehat F,\widehat\omega_X) \] is bijective for $q<d$ and injective for $q=d$. \item For $N\gg0$, $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(N))\to H^0(\widehat X,\mathcal O_{\widehat X}(N))$ is bijective and $H^q(\widehat X,\mathcal O_{\widehat X}(N))=0$ for $0<q<d$. \item For every finite locally free $E$ on $X$, the completion map $H^q(X,E)\to H^q(\widehat X,\widehat E)$ is bijective for $q<d$ and injective for $q=d$. \end{enumerate} The same assertions include $Y=\varnothing$ and $Y=X$; no nonemptiness hypothesis has been suppressed. In (4), the surjectivity requirement at $p=m$ is automatic for $N\gg0$.

The seven-condition chain with one global dimension $r$ is false for a projective Cohen--Macaulay scheme of dimension $r$ unless pure dimension is required or the comparison thresholds are made componentwise. A counterexample to conditions (1) and (6) of C.014 being equivalent under the literal mixed-dimensional hypothesis is \[ X=\mathbb P_k^2\amalg\operatorname{Spec}k,\qquad Y=\mathbb P_k^2,\qquad r=2,\quad m=1. \tag{C.23.1} \] Here is the full corrected chain without a purity assumption. Let $X$ be projective and Cohen--Macaulay over $k$, let $Y\subset X$ be closed, let $\mathcal O_X(1)$ be very ample, and let $m>0$. Write the finite decomposition into open and closed subschemes \[ X=\coprod_sX_s,\quad \dim X_s=s\ \hbox{purely},\qquad Y_s=Y\cap X_s,\quad U_s=X_s\setminus Y_s,\quad d_s=s-m. \tag{C.23.2} \] Omit the empty $X_s$, and let $\omega_s$ be the dualizing sheaf of $X_s$. Write $\widehat X_s$ for its completion along $Y_s$. The following seven conditions are equivalent. Negative sheaf cohomology and negative Ext groups are understood to be zero. \begin{enumerate} \item $H^p(X\setminus Y,F)=0$ for every coherent $F$ on $X\setminus Y$ and every $p\ge m$. \item $H^p(X\setminus Y,\mathcal O_X(-N)|_{X\setminus Y})=0$ for every $p\ge m$ and all sufficiently large $N$. \item For every coherent $F$ on $X$, the natural map $H_Y^p(X,F)\to H^p(X,F)$ is bijective for $p>m$ and surjective for $p=m$. \item Condition (3) holds for $F=\mathcal O_X(-N)$ for all sufficiently large $N$. \item For every $s$ and every coherent $F_s$ on $X_s$, the completion map \[ \operatorname{Ext}_{X_s}^q(F_s,\omega_s)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Ext}_{\widehat X_s}^q(\widehat F_s,\widehat\omega_s) \] is bijective for $q<d_s$ and injective for $q=d_s$. \item For every $s>m$ and all sufficiently large $N$, the map \[ H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s}(N))\longrightarrow H^0(\widehat X_s,\mathcal O_{\widehat X_s}(N)) \] is bijective and $H^q(\widehat X_s,\mathcal O_{\widehat X_s}(N))=0$ for $0<q<d_s$. For $s=m$, the same map on $H^0$ is required only to be injective for all sufficiently large $N$. There is no condition for $s<m$. \item For every $s$ and every finite locally free $E_s$ on $X_s$, the map \[ H^q(X_s,E_s)\longrightarrow H^q(\widehat X_s,\widehat E_s) \] is bijective for $q<d_s$ and injective for $q=d_s$. \end{enumerate} Thus C.014 is exactly the special case $X=X_r$ and $0<m<r$. In the mixed-dimensional case the surjectivity clause of (4) is automatic for large $N$ if no component has dimension $m$; it cannot in general be deleted when such a component is present.

Replacing $\mathcal O_X(-N)$ by $\mathcal O_X(N)$ in C.014(2) is false, even for smooth projective $X$, nonempty $Y$, and $0<m<\dim X$. Likewise $\Omega^r_{X/k}$ cannot be used as a synonym for $\omega_X$ for a general Cohen--Macaulay scheme.

Let $X$ be projective over a field, let $\mathcal I$ be a coherent ideal, and let $F,G$ be coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Put $F_a=F/\mathcal I^aF$ and let hats denote completion along $V(\mathcal I)$. Then for every $q\geq0$ the canonical map is an isomorphism \[ \operatorname{Ext}^q_{\widehat X}(\widehat G,\widehat F) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \varprojlim_a\operatorname{Ext}^q_X(G,F_a). \tag{C.16.1} \] No Cohen--Macaulay or local-freeness hypothesis is needed for this comparison itself. Such hypotheses enter only when these groups are identified with dual cohomology groups.

Let $X$ be projective Cohen--Macaulay and pure of dimension $r$.
