The bordered capping functor is an equivalence with pointed spheres equipped with an admissible three-disc system, when admissible has its definition from 67/065--066 and arrows retain those discs.

\label{A1-retained-discs} Fix a stable graph. Enlarge the target by retaining admissible pointed caps at every branch of every node, as well as at the external markings, and a toric boundary identification at every node. Require the two hyperbolic boundary lengths at a node to be equal. Then geodesic cutting and canonical capping give an equivalence of groupoids with hyperbolic bordered surfaces cut along that graph. The nodal tensor alone is a forgetful invariant of this equivalence.

\label{A1-first-order} For an ordinary node with branches $a,b$ on a smooth normalization $Y$, the one-dimensional space of local first-order smoothings is canonically $T_aY\otimes T_bY$. Given analytic coordinates $x,y$ at the branches, the family $xy=t$ represents this identification by $t\,\partial_x\otimes\partial_y$. Coordinate choices enter at higher order. For a fixed stable complex curve, sufficiently small such parameters together with deformation parameters for the normalized pointed components give local analytic plumbing charts, modulo its finite automorphism group.

\label{A1-nontoric-cut} If the cut circles in 67/074 are interpreted as arbitrary embedded smooth, or even analytic, circles, cutting and canonical capping does not always give the asserted antiisomorphisms of pointed caps. This failure already occurs on a four-punctured sphere with one separating circle. The geodesic-cut model used in Theorems~\ref{A1-graph-range} and~\ref{A1-bordered-shadow-range} therefore requires geodesic representatives, or toric compatibility together with equality of the paired hyperbolic boundary lengths. Smoothness alone does not supply these conditions. Toric compatibility without length equality defines the larger, noninjective model of Theorem~\ref{A1-toric-domain}.

\label{A1-graph-range} For the fixed normalization, the unbordered canonical surgery map, with actual toric seam identifications as its phase variables, is a real-analytic diffeomorphism onto \[ \mathcal U_\Gamma(Y)= \left\{(q_e)\in\prod_{e\in E}(T_{a_e}Y\otimes T_{b_e}Y)^\times: \sum_e p_e\log|q_e|<K_\Gamma(p) \quad\text{for all }0\ne p\in[0,\infty)^E\right\}. \] Its logarithmic radial image is open, convex, and downward closed. If $E\ne\varnothing$, this is a proper subset of the unrestricted nonzero-tensor fiber. The tangent map of surgery is an isomorphism. As the normalization varies on its fixed graph stratum, these images form an open real-analytic subbundle of the nonzero-tensor bundle. Its inclusion is an equivariant homotopy equivalence, and consequently induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups, including orbifold fundamental groups when finite automorphisms are retained. These conclusions allow loop edges as well as edges between different components.

\label{A1-small-ranges} For the separating one-node $(0,4)$ curve, normalize each rational component by putting its node at $0$ and its two external markings at $1,\infty$. In the resulting tensor frame the exact range is \[ 0<|q|<16. \] For the irreducible one-node $(1,1)$ curve, put its two branches at $0,1$ and its marking at $\infty$ on its rational normalization. In the frame $\partial_z|_0\otimes\partial_z|_1$ the exact range is \[ 0<|q|<1. \] In both cases every phase occurs and the length is uniquely determined by $|q|$.

\label{A1-bordered-landing} Canonical cutting and capping need not produce an admissible system of external discs on the normalization when the node caps are forgotten and their centers are left as punctures. This already fails for a four-holed sphere with one separating cut, all five geodesic lengths---the four external boundaries and the cut---equal to $2\pi$. Thus, with the componentwise admissibility just specified, the displayed arrow $MDB\longrightarrow M_{\mathrm{st}}ND$ of 67/076 is not a well-defined map on all objects.

\label{A1-bordered-shadow-range} On the fixed graph and normalization, record the nonzero node tensors $q_e$ and the external cap shadows, of radii $r_l>0$. Canonical cutting and capping gives a real-analytic diffeomorphism from bordered cut surfaces, with actual toric seam phases, onto \begin{align*} \mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)=\biggl\{(q,r):\quad& \sum_{e\in E}p_e\log|q_e|+ \sum_{l\in L}p_l\log r_l<K_{\Gamma,L}(p)\\ &\text{for every }0\ne p\in[0,\infty)^P\biggr\}. \end{align*} The logarithmic radial image is open, convex, and downward closed. The source length at every edge or external leg is $2\pi\sqrt{t_j}$, where $t$ is the unique solution \[ \nabla\Psi_{\Gamma,L}(t) =\bigl((\log|q_e|)_{e\in E},(\log r_l)_{l\in L}\bigr). \] Thus the node tensors and the external shadows determine all node and external cap domains, all boundary lengths, and the cut surface. The statement includes self-nodes and fixed cusp markings. Its tangent map is an isomorphism; as the normalization varies, the range forms an open real-analytic subbundle. The inclusion into the full nonzero-tensor and positive-shadow bundle is an equivariant homotopy equivalence.

\label{A1-bordered-shape-image} Replace the manuscript's external-only admissibility requirement by arbitrary embedded pointed external discs with disjoint analytic closures avoiding every other special point. The exact image of canonical surgery in this target consists of the tuples $(Y,(q_e),(D_l))$ satisfying both of the following conditions: \begin{enumerate} \item The tensors and the shadows $r_l=r(D_l)$ satisfy all support inequalities of Theorem~\ref{A1-bordered-shadow-range}. \item Let $t$ be the unique gradient inverse furnished by that theorem. On every component, the given external discs $D_l$ are exactly the external members of the canonical full cap system with squared length parameters $B_vt$. \end{enumerate} These conditions determine a real-analytic graph over $\mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)$. They give a complete reconstruction criterion, and do not require the retained external subsystem to be admissible after the node caps have been discarded.

\label{A1-toric-domain} The tensor and external-shadow map from $\mathcal R_{\Gamma,L}(Y)$ has exactly the same image $\mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)$ as the equal-length geodesic map of Theorem~\ref{A1-bordered-shadow-range}; for $L=\varnothing$ this is $\mathcal U_\Gamma(Y)$ of Theorem~\ref{A1-graph-range}. In particular \[ P_*(D_Y)=\left\{y:\ p\cdot y<K_{\Gamma,L}(p) \text{ for all }0\ne p\in[0,\infty)^P\right\}. \] This is a proper subset of the unrestricted tensor/shadow fiber whenever $P\ne\varnothing$; when $P=\varnothing$ it is the entire one-point fiber. Before finite automorphism quotients, the fiber over a fixed tensor and shadow tuple is an open convex set of dimension $|E|$ in its full cap logarithms. More strongly, after orienting each edge, the quantities \[ d_e=s_{h_e^+}-s_{h_e^-}\in\R \] give a global real-analytic identification \[ \mathcal R_{\Gamma,L}(Y) \simeq\mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)\times\R^E, \] under which the surgery map is projection and the geodesic submodel is $d=0$. Thus its tangent map is surjective with kernel dimension $|E|$; it is an isomorphism precisely when $E=\varnothing$. If the normalization varies and the graph has total genus $g$ and $n$ external markings, the broader toric source has real dimension $6g-6+2n+|L|+|E|$, whereas the tensor/shadow target has dimension $6g-6+2n+|L|$. Thus the dimension count in 67/077 applies to the geodesic model, not to actual toric cuts of independent lengths. The identification is intrinsic if $\R^E$ is regarded as the real space of antisymmetric functions on the two branches of each edge. Branch interchange changes the corresponding $d_e$ to $-d_e$, and graph automorphisms also permute edges. The construction varies real-analytically with the normalization and is equivariant. Consequently it defines a real vector orbibundle over the geodesic image when finite automorphisms are retained. Scaling $d$ to zero is a fiber-preserving equivariant strong deformation retraction. The broader toric surgery map therefore induces the same fundamental-group isomorphism to the unrestricted tensor/shadow target, although its tangent map has a nonzero kernel whenever there is a cut.

\label{A1-toric-noninjective} Even for the unbordered four-labelled sphere with one separating analytic cut, the torically compatible surgery map is not injective. There are distinct such cut objects with fixed normalization and tensor $q=\partial_z|_0\otimes\partial_w|_0$.

\label{A1-toric-full-discs} For the broader toric interpretation, retain arbitrary pointed external discs with disjoint analytic closures, in addition to the tensors. Such a tuple $(Y,q,(D_l))$ is a surgery output if and only if its external shadows $r_l=r(D_l)$ and tensors belong to $\mathcal V_{\Gamma,L}(Y)$ and there exists $d\in\R^E$ for which the unique canonical cap system constructed in Theorem~\ref{A1-toric-domain} has external members exactly $D_l$. Its fiber is precisely this set of $d$'s, with the prescribed finite automorphism identifications. In particular the $\R^E$-fiber assertion concerns the tensor/shadow target; it must not be transferred to a target retaining full external disc shapes. The geodesic criterion of Corollary~\ref{A1-bordered-shape-image} is the special case $d=0$.

\label{A1-pant-third-jet} Let the hyperbolic pant have one boundary of length $2\pi\lambda$, $\lambda>0$, and two cusps. Normalize its capped sphere by placing the cap centre at $0$ and the ordered cusps at $1,\infty$. Let $r(\lambda)$ be the cap's conformal radius, and normalize its unit-disc coordinate $u_\lambda$ to have positive derivative at zero. Then \[ g_\lambda(z):=r(\lambda)u_\lambda(z) =z+\frac12z^2+\beta(\lambda)z^3+O(z^4), \qquad \beta(\lambda)=\frac5{16} +\frac1{16(\lambda^2+4)}. \] Moreover $r:(0,\infty)\to(0,4)$ is a strictly increasing real-analytic bijection.

\label{A1-four-point-plumbing-jet} On two spheres with node $0$ and external markings $1,\infty$, take node-coordinate germs \[ g_i(z)=z+\frac12z^2+\beta_i z^3+O(z^4),\qquad i=1,2. \] Plumb by $g_1(z)g_2(w)=t$. On the resulting four-pointed sphere, normalize the global coordinate so that the first component's $\infty$ is $\infty$, its $1$ is $1$, and the second component's $\infty$ is $0$. Let $\Lambda(t)$ be the coordinate of the second component's $1$. Then \[ \Lambda(t)=t-\frac12t^2+ \left(\frac9{16}-\frac54(\beta_1+\beta_2) +4\beta_1\beta_2\right)t^3+O(t^4). \] In particular, for the germs of Lemma~\ref{A1-pant-third-jet}, the cubic coefficient is \[ C(\lambda_1,\lambda_2) =\frac{11}{64} +\frac1{64(\lambda_1^2+4)(\lambda_2^2+4)}. \]

\label{A1-toric-nondescent} There is a four-labelled punctured sphere $X$ with two isotopic essential analytic cuts $C,C_{\mathrm{geo}}$ such that both cuts are canonically torically compatible, $C_{\mathrm{geo}}$ is the unique hyperbolic geodesic in their isotopy class, and raw canonical cutting and capping produces different nodal tensors. Thus raw toric surgery does not descend to a functor on cut isotopy classes. Replacing a representative by its geodesic before applying surgery defines the different, well-defined functor already studied.

\label{A1-cut-not-algebraic} Let $\mathcal D$ be a connected component of the moduli space of four-labelled punctured spheres equipped with one essential unoriented cut isotopy class, represented by its hyperbolic geodesic. Give $\mathcal D$ its natural complex structure: forgetting the locally constant cut class is a local biholomorphism to $M_{0,4}^{\mathrm{an}}$. Then \[ \mathcal D\simeq \mathbb H/\langle\tau\mapsto\tau+2\rangle \simeq\{q\in\C:0<|q|<1\}. \] In particular $\mathcal D$ is not the analytification of a smooth connected finite-type algebraic curve over $\C$. Thus the natural geodesic-cut source cannot be treated as a finite-type algebraic moduli curve, and it cannot be algebraically isomorphic to the corresponding unrestricted nodal-tensor stratum $\C^\times$. This is a limitation of that specified algebraic interpretation; it does not infer nonholomorphicity of the surgery map from its real-analytic description.

\label{A1-welding-plumbing} For the corrected surgery data of Proposition~\ref{A1-retained-discs}, every seam is an ordinary analytic plumbing, using the coordinate germs supplied by its two pointed caps. This assertion identifies the welded surface itself. It does not identify the finite plumbing parameter, in a fixed independent choice of germs, with an arbitrary element of the whole normal tensor line.

\label{A1-kra-comparison} Fix a maximal pants graph of type $(g,n)$ and put $d=3g-3+n>0$. Kra's horocyclic plumbing parameters range in a domain $D$ satisfying \[ \mathbb D_{e^{-2\pi}}^{d}\subset D \subset\mathbb D_{e^{-\pi/2}}^{d}. \] They cover the moduli of surfaces of that type, generally many times. On marked Teichm\"uller space the logarithmic coordinates $\tau_j$ are global holomorphic coordinates on their image; the corresponding Dehn twist sends $\tau_j$ to $\tau_j+2$. After quotienting these twists, $t_j=e^{\pi i\tau_j}$ are the plumbing coordinates on $D\cap(\C^\times)^d$. They are not coordinates on an unrestricted normal-tensor bundle.

\label{A1-wolpert-comparison} The local family $xy=t$, $0<|t|<1$, is the annulus $|t|<|x|<1$. Its complete curvature-minus-one metric and core length are \[ ds_t^2=\left[ \frac{\pi}{|\log|t||} \csc\!\left(\frac{\pi\log|x|}{\log|t|}\right) \left|\frac{dx}{x}\right|\right]^2, \qquad L_t=\frac{2\pi^2}{-\log|t|}. \] On compact subsets of either punctured limiting branch the metric tends to the cusp metric. For a degenerating family of compact stable curves, Wolpert's Expansion~4.2 compares the global hyperbolic metric with the interpolated cusp/annulus metric; its constants are local in the normalization parameters and coordinate germs. This supplies a metric comparison for plumbing, not a global inverse on normal tensors.

\label{A1-hinich-counterexample} Even for $(g,n)=(0,4)$, disjoint coordinate discs and the equation $xy=t$ do not ensure that the plumbing map is locally invertible at every nonzero parameter. An instance of Hinich's counterexample is obtained by \[ R=\tfrac32,\quad B=\tfrac34,\quad C=10,\quad A=\tfrac{420}{569},\quad \varepsilon=\tfrac1{10}, \qquad \phi(z)=(z-R)^2. \] The critical plumbing parameter is $t=9/11$.

\label{A1-Earle-Sipe-comparison} Let $z,w$ be disjoint local unit-disc coordinates on the two branches to be joined. For $0<r_1,r_2<1$ and $t=r_1r_2e^{i\theta}$, plumbing by $zw=t$ is precisely the analytic boundary welding which removes $|z|<r_1$ and $|w|<r_2$ and identifies \[ z=r_1e^{i\varphi},\qquad w=r_2e^{i(\theta-\varphi)}. \] Its normal tensor is $t\,\partial_z\otimes\partial_w$. This is the same coordinate-level comparison as the original Earle--Sipe construction, with the full local coordinates retained.

\label{A1-Earle-Marden-original} The joint manuscript of Earle and Marden, \emph{Holomorphic Plumbing Coordinates on Teichm\"uller and Compactified Moduli Space}, dated \emph{Draft 8/24/11}, gives the following identification. It is an original author manuscript, recovered from the public archive of Marden's Minnesota papers directory, rather than the distinct published 2012 chapter. The relevant locators are \S4.1.1--4.1.2, pp.~39--40; \S4.5, p.~50; and \S4.8.1--4.8.2, equations~(4.8.1)--(4.8.2), p.~57 \cite{EarleMarden2011DraftA567}. Normalize the peripheral translation to $A(\zeta)=\zeta+1$. Suppose the two disjoint puncture neighborhoods are the quotients of $\operatorname{Im}\zeta>h$ and $\operatorname{Im}\eta<-h$, where $h>0$. For $\tau=a+2si$, $s>h$, the identification $\zeta=\eta+\tau$ becomes classical plumbing \[ z=e^{2\pi i\zeta},\qquad w=e^{-2\pi i\eta},\qquad zw=t,\qquad t=e^{2\pi i\tau}. \] Writing $\rho=e^{-2\pi h}$ and $r=e^{-2\pi s}$ gives the exact bounds \[ 0<r<\rho<1,\qquad |t|=r^2<\rho^2=e^{-4\pi h}. \] The sewn collar is the annulus \[ \frac{|t|}{\rho}<|z|<\rho,\qquad \operatorname{mod}=\frac{1}{2\pi}\log\frac{\rho^2}{|t|} =\operatorname{Im}\tau-2h. \] On its middle circle the sewing is $re^{i\theta}\mapsto re^{i(\phi-\theta)}$, where $t=|t|e^{i\phi}$. More generally, after rescaling by positive $0<r_+,r_-<\rho$ satisfying $r_+r_-=|t|$, put $u=z/r_+$ and $v=w/r_-$. Then the same sewing is \[ uv=e^{i\phi},\qquad t\,\partial_z\otimes\partial_w =e^{i\phi}\,\partial_u\otimes\partial_v. \] Thus the toric boundary welding in Proposition~\ref{A1-welding-plumbing} is exactly this plumbing operation when its full coordinate germs are retained. The normal tensor is its first-order invariant.

\label{A2-schwarzian} Let a hyperbolic pant have boundary lengths $\ell_0,\ell_1,\ell_\infty>0$, and canonically cap it at the three boundaries. Normalize the resulting sphere by placing the cap centres at $0,1,\infty$. Set \[ a_j=\frac12\left(1+\frac{\ell_j^2}{4\pi^2}\right). \] The hyperbolic developing map extends as a complex projective structure to the punctured capped sphere, whose Schwarzian in the coordinate $z$ is \[ T(z)=\frac{a_0}{z^2}+\frac{a_1}{(z-1)^2} +\frac{a_\infty-a_0-a_1}{z(z-1)}. \] If $u$ is any centred unit-disc coordinate on the cap at $0$, write $u(z)=c z(1+bz+O(z^2))$. Then \[ b=\frac{a_0+a_1-a_\infty}{2a_0}. \]

\label{A2-independence} In a canonically capped pant the cap at $0$ need not depend only on $\ell_0$. In particular, the pants with length triples $(2\pi,2\pi,2\pi)$ and $(2\pi,4\pi,2\pi)$ have different caps at $0$ in the common normalization $0,1,\infty$.

\label{A2-cusp-norm} For a compact pointed complex curve $(Y,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ with $2g-2+n>0$, the complete hyperbolic metric on $Y\setminus\{p_i\}$ defines canonical Hermitian norms on $T_{p_i}Y$. If $q_i$ is its cusp coordinate, then \[ ds^2=\frac{|dq_i|^2}{|q_i|^2\log^2|q_i|},\qquad \|v\|_{p_i}=|dq_i(v)|. \] The coordinate is unique up to a constant of modulus one. A horocycle of circumference $h_i$ has coordinate radius $\exp(-2\pi/h_i)$ wherever embedded. Penner's unrestricted decorations, understood as horocycles in the cusp cover and allowing their immersed images, form a principal $(\R_{>0})^n$-bundle. The map which assigns to $X$ the capped curve and decorations of circumferences $\ell_i(X)$ identifies its positive-length bundle with the one in Theorem \ref{A4-grafting}.

\label{A2-collar} Let $(M,g)$ be a compact hyperbolic surface with geodesic boundary and negative Euler characteristic. Remove pairwise disjoint normal collars of widths $d_i>0$ from selected boundary components, without changing the topological type, and call the remaining surface $M'$. Let $g'$ be its conformally compatible hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary. Then $g'=e^{2u}g$ on $M'$ with $u>0$. More precisely $u$ is the unique smooth solution of \[ \Delta_g u=e^{2u}-1\quad\hbox{on }M',\qquad \partial_{n}u=\begin{cases}\tanh d_i&\hbox{on a new boundary},\\0&\hbox{on a retained boundary},\end{cases} \] where $\Delta=\operatorname{div}\operatorname{grad}$ and $n$ is the outward unit normal of $M'$. The new boundary corresponding to a former boundary of length $L_i$ has length strictly greater than $L_i\cosh d_i$ in $g'$.

\label{A2b-regularity} Locally in $(0,\infty)^I$, the canonical seams and their conformal cap maps depend real-analytically on $s$. After local trivialization of each moving piece, the hyperbolic and flat metrics depend real-analytically on $s$. The logarithm of the metric density is $C^{1,1}$ across each seam and is smooth on either side. Its first parameter variation is continuous across the seam and has the one-sided normal derivatives used below.

\label{A2b-energy} The Jacobian $dF/ds$ is symmetric positive definite everywhere. Consequently $F$ is the gradient of a strictly convex real-analytic function $S$ on $(0,\infty)^I$, and is injective. In particular an admissible canonical cap system is determined by its conformal radii.

\label{A2b-recession} There are constants $B_i<\infty$, depending only on the marked $Y$ and the chosen tangent coordinates, such that every embedded pointed disc avoiding the other marked points has conformal radius at most $B_i$. For a canonical cap one has \begin{equation}\label{A2b-collar-bound} r_i(s)\leq B_i\exp\left( -\frac{\arctan(\operatorname{csch}(\pi\sqrt{s_i}))}{\sqrt{s_i}} \right). \end{equation} Moreover, for every $s_0>0$ and $p\geq0$, \begin{equation}\label{A2b-recession-formula} \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{S(s_0+tp)-S(s_0)}t=K(p). \end{equation}

\label{A2b-image} The canonical cap radius map is a real-analytic diffeomorphism \[ (0,\infty)^I\longrightarrow\exp\mathcal L_Y, \qquad \mathcal L_Y= \left\{x\in\R^I:\ p\cdot x<K(p) \text{ for every }p\in[0,\infty)^I\setminus\{0\}\right\}. \] In particular its logarithmic image is open, convex, and downward closed. It is precisely the set of conformal-radius vectors realized by systems of pointed discs with pairwise disjoint analytic closures avoiding all the other marked points. The boundary support values are the weighted Strebel extrema \eqref{A2b-support}.

\label{A2-strebel-deficit} Put $c=2g-2+n>0$. For every $s\in(0,\infty)^I$ and every pairwise disjoint system of pointed conformal discs $E_i$ avoiding the other marked points, \[ \sum_{i\in I}s_i\bigl(\log r_i(E_i)-F_i(s)\bigr)\leq c. \] Consequently \[ 0\leq K(s)-s\cdot F(s)\leq c. \] The constants do not depend on the boundary lengths. Fixed cusp ends are allowed.

\label{A2-cap-limit} Fix $Y$ and its marked points as above. Let $s^{(m)}>0$ and $t_m\to\infty$ satisfy $s^{(m)}/t_m\to p\in[0,\infty)^I\setminus\{0\}$. For every $i$ with $p_i>0$, the pointed caps $D_i(s^{(m)})$ converge in the Carath\'eodory kernel sense to the Jenkins--Strebel disc $U_i(p)$ with circumference weights $2\pi\sqrt{p_i}$. Their normalized conformal maps converge locally uniformly, and \[ r_i(s^{(m)})\longrightarrow R_i(p). \] For $p_i=0$, the radii tend to zero. In particular the limit depends on the relative growth of the lengths and on $Y$; it is not universally a Koebe slit domain. No assertion of a fixed limit is made when the marked compactification itself is allowed to diverge.

\label{A2-explicit-limits} Normalize a capped pant by placing its centres at $0,1,\infty$. If $L_0\to\infty$ and $L_1/L_0,L_\infty/L_0\to0$, then the cap at $0$ tends to $\C\setminus[1,\infty)$, its conformal radius tends to $4$, and its normalized conformal map tends to \[ k(u)=\frac{4u}{(1+u)^2},\qquad |u|<1. \] If instead $L_0/L_1,L_0/L_\infty\to1$ and the lengths tend to infinity, the cap at $0$ tends to \[ Q_0^\circ=\{|z|<1,\ \operatorname{Re}z<1/2\}, \qquad r(Q_0,0)=\frac4{3\sqrt3}. \] The other two limits follow by the permutations of $0,1,\infty$. This is the precise limiting sense in which the orange slices are valid.

\label{A2-nonbox} For the pants normalization $0,1,\infty$, every genuine admissible cap system satisfies $r_0r_1<1$. Nevertheless the individual supremum of each of $r_0,r_1,r_\infty$ over such systems is $4$. The set of admissible radii is therefore not a Cartesian product of intervals.

\label{A2-collar-general} Let $(M,g)$ be a compact connected hyperbolic surface with geodesic boundary and $\chi(M)<0$. Let $M'\subset M$ be obtained by removing finitely many disjoint smooth open boundary collars, with $M'$ diffeomorphic to $M$. Write $k_g=g(\nabla_TT,n)$ on $\partial M'$, where $T$ is a unit tangent and $n$ is the outward unit normal. The unique conformally compatible hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary is $g'=e^{2u}g$, where $u\in C^\infty(M')$ is the unique solution \[ \Delta_g u=e^{2u}-1,\qquad \partial_nu=k_g. \] Its area and boundary lengths are exactly \[ \int_{M'}e^{2u}\,dA_g=-2\pi\chi(M),\qquad L_{g'}(B)=\int_B e^u\,ds_g\quad(B\subset\partial M'). \] If $k_g\ge0$ everywhere and is positive somewhere, then $u>0$ everywhere. In general the sign of $u$ is not determined by the fact that a collar was removed.

\label{A2-collar-shape} Let the boundary components of $(M,g)$ have arclength coordinates $s$, and choose smooth functions $a_i(s)>0$. In inward Fermi coordinates remove the collars $0\le r<\varepsilon a_i(s)$, for sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, and let $u_\varepsilon$ be as in Theorem~\ref{A2-collar-general}. After any smooth identification with $M$ which is the identity at $\varepsilon=0$, \[ u_\varepsilon=\varepsilon h+O(\varepsilon^2)\quad\hbox{in }C^2, \qquad (\Delta_g-2)h=0,\quad \partial_nh=a_i-a_i''. \] Here the prime is differentiation in boundary arclength. In particular, take the unique hyperbolic pant all of whose boundary lengths are $2\pi$. On one boundary set \[ a_1(s)=1+\tfrac12\cos(ns), \] and on the other two set $a_2=a_3=1$. For every sufficiently large integer $n$, and then every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the resulting $u_\varepsilon$ takes a negative value at a point of the new first boundary. Thus even smooth analytic, everywhere inward collar removal need not increase the hyperbolic metric pointwise. The same metric takes a positive value somewhere.

\label{A2-collar-explicit} Let $M$ be the hyperbolic pant with all three geodesic boundary lengths equal to $2\pi$. Label the boundaries $B_1,B_2,B_3$, and take an arclength coordinate $s\in\R/(2\pi\Z)$ on $B_1$, with origin at its shortest perpendicular to $B_2$. Set \[ n=10^4,\qquad \varepsilon=10^{-14},\qquad a_1(s)=1+\tfrac12\cos(ns),\qquad a_2=a_3=1. \] In inward Fermi coordinates remove the three collars $0\le r<\varepsilon a_i(s)$. They are disjoint, everywhere inward, and have analytic boundaries. On the retained pant let $g'=e^{2u}g$ be its conformally compatible hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary. At the point of its first boundary with $s=\pi/n$ one has \[ u\le-\frac{9991}{20}\,10^{-14}<0. \] The same function $u$ is positive somewhere. Thus the general-shape counterexample of Proposition~\ref{A2-collar-shape} can be given with these fixed parameters, without an unspecified perturbation threshold.

\label{A3-boundary-chart} Let $f$ be a nonconstant holomorphic germ at zero with $f(0)=0$, real values on the real axis, and $\operatorname{Im} f(z)\geq0$ for $z$ in the upper half-disc. Then $f'(0)>0$. In particular the germ is locally biholomorphic, as required by Th\'eor\`eme 1 of cote 67/055--056.

\label{A3-rectifiable} Let $U\subset\C$ be open and let $C$ be a relatively closed rectifiable curve in $U$, or locally a finite union of rectifiable arcs. Every continuous complex-valued function on $U$ which is holomorphic on $U\setminus C$ is holomorphic throughout $U$. In particular the continuous-function assertion of 67/061 is valid; this does not by itself assert existence of a welding for an arbitrary interval homeomorphism.

\label{A3-welding} Let $X_1,X_2$ be bordered Riemann surfaces with analytic boundary, and identify selected boundary circles by orientation-reversing homeomorphisms that are quasisymmetric in analytic boundary coordinates. For finitely many such identifications, the topological quotient has a conformal structure for which the inclusions of the interiors are holomorphic and the seams are locally quasiconformal images of line segments. It is unique up to the unique conformal isomorphism restricting to the identity on every original piece. More generally, whenever a welding exists, the same uniqueness conclusion holds if its seam is conformally removable.

\label{A3-graph} Theorem \ref{A3-welding} extends to finite systems of orientation-reversing boundary-arc identifications, provided that the topological quotient is an oriented surface and the identifications are quasiconformal-compatible at the vertices: in a neighborhood of each vertex there is an orientation-preserving homeomorphism to a standard finite star of sectors which is quasiconformal on each incident open sector with one common finite bound. Cutting and welding are then inverse equivalences between these marked seam surfaces and their cut surfaces with pairing data. Smooth arc identifications with compatible nonzero derivatives and finite nonzero sector angles satisfy this condition.

\label{A3-slit} Let $V$ be a Jordan domain and let $I$ be a Jordan arc joining $a\in V$ to $b\in\partial V$, with $I\setminus\{b\}\subset V$. No rectifiability is required for the conformal uniformization of the cut domain $V\setminus I$ by a disc. Its prime-end boundary consists of the outer boundary and two copies of the slit, with a single tip and two copies of its root. Specifying three positively cyclically ordered prime ends fixes the uniformizing map uniquely. For the converse in Lemma 4B and the Scholie of 67/072--073, take the three source points $1,\zeta,\bar\zeta$, $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/3}$, and the arcs $\beta=[1,\zeta]$, $\bar\beta=[1,\bar\zeta]$ in the source circle. Let $h:\beta\to\bar\beta$ identify the tip $1$ with itself and the two roots with each other. Assume the induced order-reversing involution on the combined arc $\beta\cup\bar\beta$ is quasisymmetric, with the endpoint compatibility of Proposition \ref{A3-graph}. Then there is a unique continuous map \[ f:\overline\D\to\overline\D \] which is conformal and injective on $\D$, has image $\D\setminus I$ there for a quasislit $I$ from $0$ to $1$, sends the source tip $1$ to $0$ and the source roots $\zeta,\bar\zeta$ to $1$, and realizes $h$ as its bank identification. Conversely, a quasiconformal image of the standard slit pair gives such pairing data. For an arbitrary slit whose welding exists, uniqueness holds whenever the slit is removable; one must not assert that every quasisymmetric welding produces a rectifiable slit.

\label{A3-L5} For the geodesic cutting and canonical capping operations of section 6, all boundary circle gluings are analytic diffeomorphisms. Their existence and uniqueness do not use a separate rectifiability conjecture. The same conclusion holds for smooth boundary diffeomorphisms, but mere differentiability of a homeomorphism without a nonvanishing derivative is not the same hypothesis.

\label{A4-orange-extremal} Let $Q_0=\{|z|\leq1,\ \operatorname{Re}z\leq1/2\}$ in the sphere with centres $0,1,\infty$. The canonical cap $D_0$ for a generalized pant of boundary lengths $(32,0,0)$ is not contained in $Q_0$. In particular the literal model in the letter to Bers, which permits the other two caps to degenerate to points, is false.

\label{A4-orange-jets} There are no three fixed pointed discs $Q_0,Q_1,Q_\infty$ whose independently concentric subdiscs describe all canonically capped pants. Thus the literal model in 67/019--020 is false, independently of its additional spherical description.

\label{A4-grafting} Let $S$ be a marked compact oriented surface of type $(g,n)$ with $n\geq1$ and negative Euler characteristic. Let $\mathcal T_B^{\geq0}(S)$ classify complete hyperbolic structures with each labelled end either a geodesic boundary of length $\ell_i>0$ or a cusp of length $\ell_i=0$, and with no nodes in the interior. Let $\mathcal T_{g,n}$ be its punctured Teichm\"uller space. Canonical capping gives a mapping-class-equivariant homeomorphism \[ \Phi=(\operatorname{cap},\ell):\mathcal T_B^{\geq0}(S) \longrightarrow\mathcal T_{g,n}\times[0,\infty)^n. \] Its restriction to each boundary-type stratum is a real-analytic diffeomorphism. In particular the positive-length part is a trivial principal $(\R_{>0})^n$-bundle over $\mathcal T_{g,n}$ by boundary lengths, not by all possible tangent radii.

\label{A4-action} The multiplicative monoid $[0,\infty)^n$ acts continuously and intrinsically on $\mathcal T_B^{\geq0}(S)$ by \[ \lambda\cdot X=\Phi^{-1}\bigl(\operatorname{cap}(X),(\lambda_i\ell_i(X))_i\bigr). \] It commutes with the mapping class action (and with a simultaneous permutation of end labels). On the positive-length part its group of units acts freely and transitively on each capping fibre. The zero vector gives the canonical capping retraction. The maps $X\mapsto\Phi^{-1}(\operatorname{cap}(X),(1-t)\ell(X))$ give a strong deformation retraction onto the punctured locus.

\label{A5-normalizer} Every faithful action of $V$ on $\mathbf P^1_k$ is conjugate to \[ V_0=\{z,\ -z,\ 1/z,\ -1/z\}. \] Its centralizer in $\operatorname{PGL}_2(k)$ is $V_0$, and its normalizer is isomorphic to $\mathfrak S_4$. The maps \[ V\longmapsto N(V),\qquad \Gamma\longmapsto \text{the unique normal Klein subgroup of }\Gamma \] are inverse bijections between Klein subgroups and subgroups isomorphic to $\mathfrak S_4$, in every characteristic different from $2$.

\label{A5-six-points} If $\operatorname{char}k\ne2,5$, a six-point set projectively equivalent to $S_0=\{0,\infty,\pm1,\pm i\}$ determines a unique Klein subgroup $V$ with $S(V)=S_0$, and its full projective stabilizer is $N(V)\simeq\mathfrak S_4$. In characteristic $5$, the same set is $\mathbf P^1(\mathbf F_5)$, its stabilizer has order $120$, and exactly five Klein subgroups have this fixed-point set. Retaining the antipodal pairing determined by $V$ restores the correspondence in characteristic $5$.

\label{A5-faces} A single face of the oriented octahedron has stabilizer of order $3$ in $N(V)$. An unordered pair of opposite faces has stabilizer $\mathfrak S_3$, complementary to $V$. Thus the splitting on 67/085 belongs to a pair of opposite faces.

\label{A5-groupoid} Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $\operatorname{char}k\ne2$, and fix a choice of $i^2=-1$. Let $\mathcal C_k$ be the groupoid whose objects are projective lines $X/k$ with an embedded four-element set $I$, and whose arrows are projective isomorphisms carrying the embedded set bijectively to the embedded set. For $I$, let $J(I)$ be its three partitions into two pairs and let $Z(J(I))$ be the projective line with those three labels as marked points. Then $\mathcal C_k$ is equivalent to the groupoid of pairs \[ (I,\zeta),\qquad \zeta\in Z(J(I))\setminus J(I), \] with arrows the bijections of $I$ whose induced maps of three-pointed lines carry $\zeta$ to $\zeta'$. The torsor-twist construction on 67/088--089 is an inverse. No exception at characteristic $3$ or $5$ is needed.

\label{A5-moduli} Set $R=\Z[1/2,i]$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}R[\lambda,\lambda^{-1},(\lambda-1)^{-1}]$. The family version of Theorem~\ref{A5-groupoid} gives \[ \mathcal M_{0,[4],R}\simeq[U/\mathfrak S_4], \] where the action factors through $\mathfrak S_4/V\simeq\mathfrak S_3$ and the usual six anharmonic transformations of $\lambda$. Its coarse moduli space is $\mathbf A^1_R$, with coordinate \[ J=\frac{(\lambda^2-\lambda+1)^3}{\lambda^2(\lambda-1)^2}. \] In particular the groupoid theorem does not identify the unordered moduli stack with its coarse space: generic inertia is $V$.

\label{A6-ordinary-counterexample} The ordinary arithmetic fundamental group of a stable marked curve cannot reconstruct a chosen nonzero normal tensor, even for $(g,n)=(0,4)$ over $\Q$. Moreover its geometric version does not retain nodal inertia.
\label{A6-kummer} For a field $K$ finitely generated over $\Q$, the Kummer map \[ K^\times\longrightarrow H^1(G_K,\widehat{\Z}(1)) \] is injective. Also $(\widehat{\Z}(1))^{G_K}=0$.

\label{A6-graphic} For the framed logarithmic realization above, every $G_K$-compatible outer isomorphism $\Delta_{Y,N}\simeq\Delta_{Y',N'}$ preserves the entire semi-graph of anabelioids: vertices, nodes, cusps, and incidence.

\label{A6-normal-kummer} Fix a stable marked curve $Y/K$ as above. After a finite extension splitting its nodes and branches, choose bases for their normal lines. For two propagators $N=(c_e)$ and $N'=(c'_e)$, geometric transport identifies their admissible groups, and the difference of their arithmetic outer actions is the cocycle \[ \bigl(\kappa(c'_e/c_e)\bigr)_e \ \in Z^1\!\left(G_K,\prod_e\widehat{\Z}(1)\right). \] Changing that transport changes the cocycle by a coboundary. The group of graphic automorphisms that act identically on the underlying graph and on every component anabelioid is precisely the displayed product of profinite Dehn twist groups. This statement includes loops and self-nodes.

\label{A6-anabelian} Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\Q$, and let $(Y,N)$ and $(Y',N')$ be geometrically connected stable marked curves with nonzero normal tensors as above. For the framed logarithmic fundamental groups, the natural map \[ \operatorname{Isom}_K\bigl((Y,N),(Y',N')\bigr) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Isom}^{\mathrm{out}}_{G_K} \bigl(\Delta_{Y,N},\Delta_{Y',N'}\bigr) \] is bijective. Labels, if prescribed, must be preserved on both sides. In particular, the graph, component curves, marked points, and actual normal tensors are all recovered. The use of a framed logarithmic group is a hypothesis of this theorem and is the interpretation needed for the manuscript's normal propagator.

\label{A6-procyclic} The condition of being isomorphic to $\widehat{\Z}$, with invariant conjugacy class and cyclotomic arithmetic action, does not put such subgroups in bijection with nodes and marked points. Even with all points rational, infinitely many subgroups satisfy it. The strongest reconstruction statement established here is instead the canonical recovery of the full finite graph and all its maximal node and cusp inertia groups in Lemma~\ref{A6-graphic}. It uses the arithmetic action on finite covers, not merely the proposed condition on an individual subgroup.

\label{A6-cyclotomic-detection} Let $U/k$ be a smooth affine geometrically connected hyperbolic curve over a number field, with $\Pi=\pi_1(U)$ and geometric kernel $\Delta$. For $1\ne z\in\Delta$, the element $z$ belongs to a conjugate of a cusp inertia group if and only if there is a closed subgroup $N\subset\Pi$ whose image in $G_k$ is open and such that \[ nzn^{-1}=z^{\chi(n)}\qquad(n\in N). \] Here $\chi$ is the cyclotomic character pulled back from $G_k$.

\label{A6-three-classes} For every hyperbolic type $(g,n)$ in characteristic zero, there are infinitely many conjugacy classes of injective continuous homomorphisms $\widehat{\Z}(1)\to\Delta_{g,n}$. Thus the NB cannot literally assert that there are three such classes, or two when $n=0$. For geometric simple loops there is a meaningful three-way division into peripheral, separating essential, and nonseparating loops. This is a division into kinds, not three conjugacy classes. Under the mapping class group with unordered punctures, peripheral loops have one orbit when $n>0$, nonseparating loops one orbit when $g>0$, and separating loops have orbits indexed by unordered admissible pairs \[ \{(h,r),(g-h,n-r)\},\qquad 2h+r-1>0,\quad 2(g-h)+(n-r)-1>0. \] For labelled punctures their subsets must also be specified.

\label{A6-blowup} Let $U=(\mathbf P^1_\Q\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$. The same smooth variety, and hence the same augmented arithmetic fundamental group, admits two nonisomorphic smooth proper compactifications with strict normal-crossings boundary, containing respectively six and seven irreducible boundary components.

\label{A6-SNC-existence} Every smooth separated finite-type variety over a characteristic-zero field has a smooth proper compactification with reduced strict normal-crossings boundary. Therefore every member of $\mathcal A$ has a tangential log compactification in the stated sense.

\label{A6-log-specialization} Let $k$ have characteristic zero, $R=k[[t]]$, $F=k((t))$, and let $S^{\log}$ be $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with the divisorial log structure of $t=0$. Let $\mathcal X^{\log}\to S^{\log}$ be a proper morphism of noetherian fs log schemes with $\mathcal X^{\log}$ log regular. Suppose its interior $U$ is contained in the generic fibre and is geometrically connected over $F$. Put \[ X_0^{\log}=\mathcal X^{\log}\times_{S^{\log}}s^{\log}, \] where $s^{\log}$ is the strict closed log point. Restriction gives equivalences \[ \operatorname{F\acute Et}(U) \simeq\operatorname{K\acute Et}(\mathcal X^{\log}) \simeq\operatorname{K\acute Et}(X_0^{\log}). \] Consequently there is an outer isomorphism \[ \pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U)\simeq \pi_1^{\mathrm{k\acute et}}(X_0^{\log}) \quad\hbox{over}\quad G_F\simeq\pi_1^{\mathrm{k\acute et}}(s^{\log}). \] The frame $t$ gives a section $\sigma_t:G_k\to\pi_1^{\mathrm{k\acute et}}(s^{\log}) \simeq\widehat{\Z}(1)\rtimes G_k$. Pullback along that section defines a tangential specialization extension \[ 1\longrightarrow\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U_{\overline{F}}) \longrightarrow \pi_1^{\mathrm{k\acute et}}(X_0^{\log}) \times_{\pi_1^{\mathrm{k\acute et}}(s^{\log})}G_k \longrightarrow G_k\longrightarrow1. \] In particular this applies to proper log-smooth saturated semistable pairs, with horizontal boundary included. It retains the logarithmic special fibre, rather than replacing it by the ordinary singular fibre.

\label{A6-canonical-compactification} Let $(X,D)$ and $(X',D')$ be smooth proper pairs over a characteristic-zero field $k$, with reduced strict normal-crossings boundaries. Suppose $L=\omega_X(D)$ and $L'=\omega_{X'}(D')$ are ample. Every isomorphism $U=X\setminus D\simeq X'\setminus D'=U'$ extends uniquely to an isomorphism of pairs. Consequently, on any isomorphism-anabelian class $\mathcal A$, the map \[ \operatorname{Isom}_k((X,D),(X',D')) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Isom}_{G_k} \bigl(\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U),\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U')\bigr) /\operatorname{Inn}\bigl(\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U'_{\overline{k}})\bigr) \] is bijective for these compactifications. In particular their strata, normal-torus diagrams and the associated tangential fibre functors are recovered functorially.

\label{A6-matrix-presentations} The presentations, with the involution relations made explicit, are \[ \operatorname{SL}_2(\Z) =\langle \sigma,\rho\mid \sigma^2=\rho^3,\ \rho^6=1\rangle, \] \[ \operatorname{GL}_2(\Z) =\langle r_1,r_2,r_3\mid r_1^2=r_2^2=r_3^2=1,\ (r_1r_2)^2=(r_2r_3)^3,\ (r_1r_2)^4=1\rangle. \] We may take \[ \sigma=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad \rho=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\quad r_1=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\ r_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\ r_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}. \] In particular these identify the ordinary and extended once-punctured torus groups.

\label{A6-four-punctures} For the four-punctured sphere, \[ \operatorname{PMod}(S_{0,4})\simeq F_2 \simeq \Gamma(2)/\{\pm I\}, \qquad \operatorname{Mod}(S_{0,4}) \simeq V_4\rtimes\operatorname{PSL}_2(\Z). \] The subgroup fixing one specified puncture is $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\Z)$, and the quotient of the full group by its displayed normal $V_4$ is also $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\Z)$. Thus the formula with $+!$ is false if that symbol consistently means the pure group; it is correct if the second superscript means the distinguished-point subgroup. The exact diagram intended by the main part of 051 is \[ \begin{array}{ccccccccc} 1&\longrightarrow&F_2&\longrightarrow& \operatorname{Mod}(S_{0,4})&\longrightarrow&S_4&\longrightarrow&1\\ &&\Vert&&\downarrow&&\downarrow\\ 1&\longrightarrow&\Gamma(2)/\{\pm I\}&\longrightarrow& \operatorname{PSL}_2(\Z)&\longrightarrow&S_3&\longrightarrow&1 . \end{array} \]

\label{A6-binary-S3} There is an exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow F_2\longrightarrow\operatorname{SL}_2(\Z) \longrightarrow\widetilde{S}_3\longrightarrow1, \] where $\widetilde{S}_3$ is the binary dihedral group of order $12$. It can be obtained as a quotient of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\Z/4\Z)$, as suggested by the partially erased formula on the sheet. The quotient by $\{\pm I\}$ gives the lower row of Proposition~\ref{A6-four-punctures}. This is not the ordinary reduction-modulo-$2$ sequence, whose kernel contains $-I$.

\label{A6-projective-line} With \[ B_\infty=\left\{\ \pm\begin{pmatrix}1&n\\0&1\end{pmatrix} :n\in\Z\right\}, \] there are bijections of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\Z)$-sets \[ \operatorname{SL}_2(\Z)/B_\infty \simeq\mathbf P^1(\Z)\simeq\mathbf P^1(\Q). \] Reduction gives the displayed surjection $\mathbf P^1(\Z)\to\mathbf P^1(\mathbf F_2)$. These are point sets; the quotient written on the sheet is not an identification with the entire scheme $\mathbf P^1_{\Z}$.

\label{A6-birman} Let $S=S_{g,n-1}$ be an oriented surface with $2g-2+(n-1)>0$, and let $p$ be an additional marked point. There are exact sequences \[ 1\longrightarrow\pi_1(S,p)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Mod}(S,p)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}(S) \longrightarrow1, \] and their pure and extended versions. Here the middle group fixes $p$; forgetting one point is not a map from a group that is allowed to interchange that point with all the others. The same form holds with boundary fixed pointwise. The positivity condition is essential.

\label{A6-presentation-types} The three presentation mechanisms anticipated on 050 have rigorous realizations, with different conventions. The pants and Lego mechanisms give complete mapping-class \emph{groupoid} presentations by local moves and their relations. Closed extended mapping class groups of every genus $g\ge1$ admit finite presentations on orientation-reversing involutions; generation by three such involutions is known. These assertions do not by themselves identify an arithmetic automorphism group of the full Teichm\"uller tower.

\label{A6-model-system} Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $U/k$ be smooth, geometrically connected, separated and of finite type. Define $\mathcal C_k(U)$ as follows. An object is a smooth proper integral $k$-scheme $X$, with a specified dense open immersion $j_X:U\hookrightarrow X$ whose reduced complement $D_X$ is a strict normal-crossings divisor. A morphism from $X$ to $Y$ is a $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ satisfying $f\circ j_X=j_Y$. Then: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $\mathcal C_k(U)$ is essentially small, nonempty and cofiltered. There is at most one morphism between any two objects. Every morphism is proper and satisfies $f^{-1}(j_Y(U))=j_X(U)$. \item Its inverse system, with its marked common interior, \[ \mathfrak C_k(U)=\bigl((X,D_X)\bigr)_{X\in\mathcal C_k(U)}, \qquad U\longrightarrow\mathfrak C_k(U), \] is independent, up to canonical pro-isomorphism, of the choice of a small skeleton. For any fixed model $X_0$, restricting to all models dominating $X_0$ gives the same pro-object. The same holds after fixing any finite collection of initial models. \item Every $k$-isomorphism $\varphi:U\to V$ extends uniquely to an isomorphism of these pro-systems with their marked interiors. Thus, on any class $\mathcal A$ for which the augmented arithmetic fundamental group is fully faithful on isomorphisms, that group reconstructs $\mathfrak C_k(U)$ functorially. The reconstructed object retains the schemes, boundaries and transition maps, not just the abstract indexing partially ordered set. \end{enumerate} Here an isomorphism of marked pro-systems includes the isomorphism of their interiors and commutes with the displayed maps from those interiors. The theorem makes no selection of one compactification.

\label{A6-model-specialization} Let $k$ have characteristic zero, put $R=k[[t]]$ and $F=k((t))$, and fix a smooth geometrically connected separated finite-type $F$-scheme $U$. Consider proper integral regular $R$-schemes $\mathcal X$ containing $U$ as a dense open, with reduced complement $D_{\mathcal X}$ a strict normal-crossings divisor. Give them their divisorial log structures, and give $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ the log structure of $t=0$. Their morphisms are $R$-morphisms restricting to $\operatorname{id}_U$. This category is nonempty and cofiltered. Every such model is flat over $R$, and it has a canonical morphism of log schemes to $S^{\log}$. For every model, write $\mathcal X_0^{\log}$ for its strict closed log fibre. The equivalences \[ \operatorname{F\acute Et}(U) \simeq\operatorname{K\acute Et}(\mathcal X^{\log}) \simeq\operatorname{K\acute Et}(\mathcal X_0^{\log}) \] are compatible with every transition map. In particular, if $f:\mathcal X'\to\mathcal X$ is one, then \[ f_0^*:\operatorname{K\acute Et}(\mathcal X_0^{\log}) \longrightarrow \operatorname{K\acute Et}(\mathcal X_0'{}^{\log}) \] is an equivalence. The comparisons between any two models are independent of common refinement, up to the unique natural isomorphism compatible with restriction to $U$. They preserve the maps to $G_F$ and, for the same chosen frame $t$, the tangential specialization extensions over $G_k$ of Theorem~\ref{A6-log-specialization}.

\label{A6-special-fibre-counterexample} Over $R=\Q[[t]]$, there are two proper integral regular models of the same smooth geometrically connected generic open, both with strict normal-crossings reduced boundary, whose special fibres are not isomorphic. Nevertheless their strict special log fibres have equivalent finite Kummer-\'etale cover categories over $G_{\Q((t))}$ and the same tangential arithmetic extension over $G_\Q$ for the fixed frame $t$. Thus even these augmented and framed cover data do not reconstruct a chosen special-fibre scheme. This does not contradict reconstruction of the complete marked model system.

\label{A6-tame-specialization} Let $R$ be a complete noetherian discrete valuation ring, with fraction field $F$ of characteristic zero and residue field $k$ of characteristic $p\geq0$. Give $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ the divisorial log structure of its closed point. Let $U/F$ be a smooth geometrically connected separated finite-type variety. Suppose that $\mathcal X^{\log}\to S^{\log}$ is a proper morphism of noetherian fs log schemes, that $\mathcal X^{\log}$ is integral and log regular, and that its interior is identified with $U$. Write $\mathcal X_0^{\log}$ for its strict closed log fibre. Then restriction gives equivalences \[ \operatorname{Tame}_{\mathcal X}(U) \simeq\operatorname{K\acute Et}(\mathcal X^{\log}) \simeq\operatorname{K\acute Et}(\mathcal X_0^{\log}). \] They commute with pullback from $S^{\log}$. If $\mathcal Y^{\log}$ is any other model satisfying these same hypotheses for the same $U$ and $R$, then \[ \operatorname{Tame}_{\mathcal X}(U) =\operatorname{Tame}_{\mathcal Y}(U) \quad\text{as full subcategories of }\operatorname{F\acute Et}(U). \] Consequently the special-log-fibre cover categories are canonically equivalent through this common category. The comparisons are independent of a common refinement, whose existence is not assumed. They are unique up to the natural isomorphism normalized by their restriction to $U$. For an actual log morphism of models fixing $U$, its pullback is this equivalence. Let $G_F^t$ be the quotient of $G_F$ classifying finite extensions tame over $R$, and let $\Pi^t(U)$ be the fundamental group of the common tame-cover category. There is a natural surjection $\Pi^t(U)\to G_F^t$. A uniformizer $\varpi$ supplies a section \[ \sigma_{\varpi}:G_k\longrightarrow G_F^t, \qquad G_F^t\simeq\widehat{\Z}^{(p')}(1)\rtimes G_k, \] where all primes are retained when $p=0$. If $\Delta^t=\ker(\Pi^t(U)\to G_F^t)$, the resulting tangential extension \[ 1\longrightarrow\Delta^t\longrightarrow \Pi^t(U)\times_{G_F^t}G_k \longrightarrow G_k\longrightarrow1 \] is independent of the chosen model. For $p>0$ we do not identify $\Delta^t$ with the full geometric \'etale fundamental group, nor do we replace $G_F^t$ by $G_F$.

\label{A6-frobenius-counterexample} The characteristic-zero Isom-anabelian property used in the compactification definition is not preserved unchanged under arithmetic specialization. There are two nonisomorphic hyperbolic curves over $k=\mathbf F_{16}$ whose augmented \'etale fundamental groups are isomorphic over $G_k$. Both are good reductions of hyperbolic curves over the number field $\Q(\zeta_{15})$.

\label{A6-wild-counterexample} The first equivalence of Theorem~\ref{A6-tame-specialization} is false with $\operatorname{F\acute Et}(U)$ in place of the tame subcategory, even for a smooth proper relative curve with strict normal-crossings boundary and hyperbolic generic interior.

\label{A6-node-character} Let $e$ be a geometric node of a stable curve in the framed logarithmic interpretation of Theorem~\ref{A6-anabelian}, over a characteristic-zero field $K$. On the subgroup of $G_K$ stabilizing $e$, let $\varepsilon_e$ be the character which is $1$ when the two branches are preserved and $-1$ when they are interchanged. The character on its node inertia group is \[ I_e\simeq\widehat{\Z}(1)\otimes\varepsilon_e, \qquad \gamma\longmapsto\chi_{\rm cyc}(\gamma)\varepsilon_e(\gamma). \] In particular the invariant-conjugacy-class condition does not by itself make the character cyclotomic. It becomes cyclotomic after passing to the branch-splitting field. Marked-point inertia has the ordinary cyclotomic character on its point stabilizer.

\label{A6-intrinsic-tame} Let $R$ be a complete noetherian discrete valuation ring, let $F=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ have characteristic zero, and let $U/F$ be nonempty, smooth, geometrically connected, separated and of finite type. A test trait is a discrete valuation ring $A$, not a field, with an $R$-algebra structure, together with an $R$-morphism \[ f_A:\eta_A=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}(A)\longrightarrow U. \] The ring $A$ need not be excellent, henselian, or of finite type over $R$; the structure map need not be local. In particular, tests for which a uniformizer of $R$ becomes a unit in $A$ are included. Give $T_A=\operatorname{Spec}A$ the divisorial log structure of its closed point, denoted $T_A^{\log}$. Define $\operatorname{Tame}^{\rm tr}_R(U)$ to be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{F\acute Et}(U)$ consisting of covers $V\to U$ such that, for every test trait, $f_A^*V\to\eta_A$ is the generic fibre of a \emph{finite Kummer-\'etale cover} of $T_A^{\log}$. Then the following hold. \begin{enumerate} \item With the restriction of any geometric fibre functor on $U$, $\operatorname{Tame}^{\rm tr}_R(U)$ is a Galois category. It is closed in $\operatorname{F\acute Et}(U)$ under finite limits, finite sums, subobjects and quotients. Its fundamental group $\Pi^{\rm tr}_R(U)$ is a quotient of $\pi_1(U)$. \item Pullback along an $F$-morphism $U'\to U$ between such varieties preserves these categories. Pullback of tame covers of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ gives a natural surjection $\Pi^{\rm tr}_R(U)\twoheadrightarrow G_F^t$. \item Whenever a proper integral noetherian fs log-regular model $\mathcal X^{\log}\to(\operatorname{Spec}R)^{\log}$ with interior $U$ exists, one has equality of full subcategories \[ \operatorname{Tame}^{\rm tr}_R(U) =\operatorname{Tame}_{\mathcal X}(U) \subseteq\operatorname{F\acute Et}(U). \] Consequently the equivalence with finite Kummer-\'etale covers of the strict special log fibre in Theorem~\ref{A6-tame-specialization} realizes this intrinsic category. \end{enumerate}

\label{A7-gluing-modules} Let $R$ be a ring, not necessarily commutative, and use left $R$-modules. The category of pairs $(M,\sigma)$ with $M$ an $R$-module, multiplication by $2$ injective on $M$, and $\sigma^2=1$, is equivalent to the category of triples $(P,Q,m)$, where $P,Q$ are $2$-torsion-free $R$-modules and \[ m\subset(P/2P)\oplus(Q/2Q),\qquad m\cap(P/2P)=m\cap(Q/2Q)=0. \] Morphisms of triples are pairs of module maps preserving $m$ after reduction modulo $2$. No Noetherian or finite-generation hypothesis is required. In the proof, localization at $2$ is valid because the integer $2$ is central; equivalently, $M[1/2]=M\otimes_{\Z}\Z[1/2]$.

\label{A7-domain-counterexample} The assertion following 67/091 that the two eigenspaces of a nontrivial involution on a rank-two projective module are invertible is false even over a $2$-torsion-free domain. Thus the supplied correction ``needs $\operatorname{Spec}R$ connected (e.g. a domain)'' is insufficient. A counterexample is \[ R=\Z[x,y,z]/(x^2+yz-1),\qquad M=R^2, \qquad \sigma=\begin{pmatrix}x&y\\z&-x\end{pmatrix}. \] The categorical statement in Proposition~\ref{A7-gluing-modules} remains valid. Its eigenspaces are invertible under either of the sufficient hypotheses: $R$ is a Dedekind domain and $M$ is finite projective of rank two; or $2$ is invertible in $R$, $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is connected, and $M$ is finite projective of rank two. In these two cases we require $\sigma\ne\pm1$.

\label{A7-PID-count} Suppose $R$ is a PID, $2\ne0$, and $\kappa=R/2R$ is a field. Conjugacy classes of involutions $\sigma\in\operatorname{GL}_2(R)$ with $\sigma\ne\pm1$ consist of one split class and a set of nonsplit classes canonically indexed by \[ \kappa^\times/\operatorname{im}(R^\times\to\kappa^\times). \] For $R=\Z$ there are two classes in total. For $R=\Z[(1+\sqrt{-11})/2]$ there are four classes in total, three of them nonsplit. The struck surjectivity proviso on 67/100 is therefore necessary for the assertion that there is just one nonsplit class.

\label{A7-real-classification} For $a>0$ define real elliptic curves by their complex uniformizations and the indicated conjugation: \[ E_a:\quad \C/(\Z+i\sqrt a\,\Z),\qquad E'_a:\quad \C/\bigl(\Z+\tfrac{1+i\sqrt a}{2}\Z\bigr), \qquad \sigma[z]=[\bar{z}]. \] These two disjoint families, with the parameter $a$ unique in each, are the complete list of origin-marked real elliptic curves up to real isomorphism. Their real origin-preserving automorphism groups are $\{\pm1\}$. A fixed complex elliptic curve has real forms if and only if its usual modular invariant $j$ is real, and then has exactly two real isomorphism classes. Outside the square case they are either $\{E_a,E_{1/a}\}$ or $\{E'_a,E'_{1/a}\}$ with $a>1$. For the square lattice they are $\{E_1,E'_1\}$. For the hexagonal lattice they are $\{E'_3,E'_{1/3}\}$.

\label{A7-ratio-j} With $Q$ the quadratic form used on 67/093 and 099, the hexagonal ratio is $3$, not $\sqrt3$. The usual modular invariant is \[ j(E_a)=j(i\sqrt a),\qquad j(E'_a)=j\left(\frac{1+i\sqrt a}{2}\right), \] and is unchanged by $a\mapsto1/a$ in either family. It is not $c\log a$ for either tentative nonzero constant in 67/097.

\label{A7-real-topology} The real locus and the first Galois cohomology group are \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} E & E(\R) & H^1(\R,E)\\\hline E_a & (\R/\Z)\times(\Z/2\Z) & \Z/2\Z\\ E'_a & \R/\Z & 0. \end{array} \] The quotients of the complex curves by their standard real structures are respectively an annulus and a M\"obius band. The unique nontrivial $E_a$-torsor has no real point; its antiholomorphic involution is $[z]\mapsto[\bar{z}+1/2]$, and its quotient is a Klein bottle. These torsors together with the two pointed families classify all smooth projective geometrically connected genus-one curves over $\R$.

\label{thm:B1a-betti} Let $X$ be a smooth connected projective complex variety of dimension four. Two codimension-two cycles with rational coefficients on $X$ are numerically equivalent if and only if their rational Betti classes agree.
\label{lem:B-basechange-num} Let $X/k$ be smooth projective, $K/k$ a field extension, and $z\in\mathrm{CH}^r(X)_{\Q}$. Then $z$ is numerically trivial if and only if $z_K$ is numerically trivial.

\label{thm:B1a-etale} Let $k$ be any field of characteristic zero, $X/k$ smooth projective of pure dimension four, and $\ell$ any prime. Numerical and geometric $\ell$-adic homological equivalence coincide for codimension-two cycles with rational coefficients on $X$.

\label{prop:B1b-criterion} Fix a Weil cohomology on smooth projective varieties over a field $k$. Let $X/k$ be a smooth projective fourfold and $h$ an ample divisor class. Suppose that its algebraic classes in $H^4$ admit the orthogonal decomposition \[ A^2=\Q h^2\oplus hA^1_{\mathrm{prim}}\oplus A^2_{\mathrm{prim}}, \] that the intersection form is negative definite on $hA^1_{\mathrm{prim}}$ and positive definite on $A^2_{\mathrm{prim}}$. Positivity here is on the $\Q$-vector spaces of \emph{homological} algebraic classes, before dividing by numerical equivalence. Then numerical and homological equivalence coincide in codimension two. Conversely, if the decomposition exists, numerical primitive positivity together with numerical--homological equality implies this criterion.

\label{prop:B1b-gap} The Lefschetz standard conjecture and positivity of the primitive form \emph{on numerical classes} do not, by the preceding linear-algebra argument alone, prove numerical--homological equality. Ancona's 2021 theorem supplies this numerical positivity for abelian fourfolds; its stated equality theorem covers infinitely many primes $\ell$, not every $\ell$.

\label{thm:B1b-abelian} Let $A/k$ be an abelian fourfold over any field and let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Numerical and $\ell$-adic homological equivalence coincide for all cycles on $A$ with rational coefficients, in particular for its two-dimensional cycles.

\label{prop:B1b-scope} The positivity-and-specialization argument applies to every smooth projective fourfold $X/k$ whose algebraic Lefschetz decomposition exists and which has a smooth projective specialization $X_0$ for which numerical--$\ell$-adic equality and numerical primitive positivity both hold. It also proves numerical--$\ell$-adic equality on every smooth projective fourfold dominated by a smooth projective fourfold $Y$ having that equality, by a generically finite surjective morphism $f:Y\to X$. In particular it applies to fourfolds dominated in this sense by an abelian fourfold.

\label{thm:B1c} With the classical definition of $\tau$-triviality (some nonzero integral multiple is algebraically equivalent to zero), the first assertion of question 24 is false, even for smooth complex quintic threefolds. It is also false if the doubtful glyph is read as algebraic triviality itself. The implication from $\tau$-triviality to numerical triviality remains true.

\label{lem:B2-mumford} Let $S$ be a smooth projective complex surface, let $\omega\in H^0(S,\Omega_S^2)$, and let $T$ be smooth and integral. For a morphism $f:T\to\operatorname{Sym}^d S$, write $f^*\omega^{(d)}$ for Mumford's induced two-form. If $f,g:T\to\operatorname{Sym}^d S$ are families whose cycles are rationally equivalent at the generic point after an algebraic extension of $\C(T)$, then $f^*\omega^{(d)}=g^*\omega^{(d)}$.

\label{thm:B2-square} Let $E/\overline\Q$ be the smooth elliptic curve $y^2=x^3-x$ with origin $o$, and let $S=E_\C\times E_\C$. Choose $p,q\in E(\C)$ such that the point $(p,q)$ is generic over $\overline\Q$; for example choose $x(p),x(q)$ algebraically independent over $\overline\Q$ and then choose the square roots defining their $y$-coordinates. Put \[ a=\operatorname{pr}_1^*([p]-[o]),\quad b=\operatorname{pr}_2^*([q]-[o]),\quad D=a+b\in\mathrm{CH}^1(S). \] Then $D$ is algebraically trivial, but $D^2$ is nonzero, and indeed nontorsion, in $\mathrm{CH}^2(S)$. Moreover \[ z=[(p,q)]-[(p,o)]-[(o,q)]+[(o,o)] \] is Albanese-trivial and nontorsion. Thus each question has a negative answer with integral coefficients and with rational coefficients.

\label{prop:B2-kernel} For $S=E_\C\times E_\C$, the kernel of $\operatorname{alb}:\mathrm{CH}_0(S)^0\to\operatorname{Alb}(S)(\C)$ on degree-zero classes is generated by the cycles \[ z(p,q)=([p]-[o])\times([q]-[o]),\qquad p,q\in E(\C). \] Consequently over $\Q$ this kernel is spanned by squares of algebraically trivial divisors. Products in the counterexample are Albanese-trivial, although they need not be rationally trivial.

\label{thm:B3-21} Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, and $i:Z\to X$. The following statements are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair. \item For every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $F$ on $X$, the restriction $H^0(X,F)\to H^0(Z,i^*F)$ is an isomorphism. \item For every such $F$ and every $q\ge0$, the restriction $H^q(X,F)\to H^q(Z,i^*F)$ is an isomorphism. \end{enumerate} In particular $I$-adic completeness is sufficient, without a noetherian hypothesis. The quantifier ``every sheaf'' cannot be replaced by ``one fixed sheaf'' in the degree-zero test.

\label{thm:B3-fujiwara} Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair with $I$ finitely generated, let $\widehat A$ be its $I$-adic completion, and let $U\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an open subset containing $\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$. Put $\widehat U=U\times_A\widehat A$ and let $\pi:\widehat U\to U$ be the projection. For every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $F$ on $U$ and every $q\ge0$, \[ H^q(U,F)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ H^q(\widehat U,\pi^*F). \]

\label{thm:B3-flat-crys} For any scheme $X$, let $a_X:\operatorname{Sh}((\operatorname{Sch}/X)_{\mathrm{fppf}}) \to\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{et}})$ be the comparison morphism. For every bounded below complex $K$ of abelian \'etale sheaves, \[ K\simeq Ra_{X,*}a_X^*K, \qquad R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},K) \simeq R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{fppf}},a_X^*K). \] There is no invertibility condition on the torsion in this assertion. For the crystalline addition to subject 1 and the connection addition to subject 8, let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a divided power ring with a prime $p$ nilpotent in $A$. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, let $Y\to S$ be smooth, and put $X=Y\times_A A/I$. If $\mathcal F$ is a crystal in quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X/S}$-modules, its value $\mathcal F_Y$ has a canonical integrable connection and \[ R\Gamma(\operatorname{Cris}(X/S),\mathcal F) \simeq R\Gamma(Y,\mathcal F_Y\otimes\Omega^\bullet_{Y/S}). \]

\label{thm:B3-approx} Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair with $A$ a noetherian G-ring. Given polynomials $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in A[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$, a solution $\widehat a\in\widehat A^n$ in the $I$-adic completion, and $N\ge1$, there is an exact solution $a\in A^n$ with $a\equiv\widehat a\pmod{I^N\widehat A}$. If $A=R$ is a henselian discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $t$, and the fraction field extension $\operatorname{Frac}\widehat R/ \operatorname{Frac}R$ is separable in positive characteristic, there are constants $c,b\ge1$, depending on the finite polynomial system, such that every solution modulo $t^{cn+b}$ is congruent modulo $t^n$ to an exact solution in $R$, for every $n\ge1$.
\label{thm:B3-topos} A small site with finite limits whose coverings admit finite refinements has enough points. An unrestricted Grothendieck topos need not have even one point.

\label{thm:B3-raynaud-flatness} Let $f:X\to S$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. For $g:T\to S$, write $f_T:X\times_S T\to T$ for the base-changed morphism and $F_T$ for the pullback of $F$ to $X\times_S T$. Suppose $F$ satisfies Raynaud's property $W$: there is a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $Q$ such that, for every $g:T\to S$ and every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_T$-module $M$, there are natural isomorphisms \[ (f_T)_*(F_T\otimes f_T^*M) \simeq\mathcal H\!om_{\mathcal O_T}(g^*Q,M). \] Then formation of $f_*F$ commutes with every base change if and only if $Q$ is finite locally free. In that case $f_*F\simeq Q^\vee$. If $F$ is also flat over $S$, this is cohomological flatness in dimension zero in Raynaud's terminology.

\label{thm:B3-picard} Let $S$ be the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring with perfect residue field, and let $f:C\to S$ be a proper flat relative curve. Assume $C$ is regular and $f_*\mathcal O_C=\mathcal O_S$. Let $\delta$ be the greatest common divisor of the multiplicities of the irreducible components of the geometric special fibre. Then $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/S}$ is representable if and only if it is separated, and these conditions hold if and only if $\delta=1$. When these conditions hold, it is a smooth separated group scheme, and for every base change $T\to S$ one has canonically \[ (f_T)_*\mathcal O_{C\times_S T}\simeq\mathcal O_T. \]

\label{thm:B3-descent} Affine schemes satisfy effective fpqc descent over every base scheme. An \'etale equivalence relation $R\rightrightarrows U$ of schemes has an algebraic-space quotient $U/R$, and $U\to U/R$ is \'etale surjective. Effective flat descent fails in the category of all schemes, even for descent data on a projective morphism relative to an \'etale covering.

\label{thm:B3-tannaka} Let $k$ be a field and $\mathcal T$ a rigid abelian symmetric $k$-linear tensor category with $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$. If $\omega:\mathcal T\to\operatorname{Vect}_k$ is exact, faithful, and symmetric tensor, then $G=\operatorname{Aut}^{\otimes}(\omega)$ is an affine group scheme and $\mathcal T\simeq\operatorname{Rep}_k(G)$ as tensor categories. Rigidity and the abelian tensor axioms alone do not imply this conclusion, even in characteristic zero.

\label{thm:B3-motives} For every finite type $\Z$-scheme $X$ there is a rational tensor triangulated category of Beilinson motives $\mathrm{DM}_{B}(X)$. Its constructible subcategory has the six operations, with $f_!$ attached to separated finite type morphisms, and Verdier duality for separated finite type $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\Z$. An explicit categorical construction is \[ \mathrm{DM}_{B}(X)\simeq \operatorname{Ho}(H_{B,X}\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}), \] where $H_{B,X}$ is the Beilinson motivic-cohomology spectrum, the degree-zero Adams summand of the rational $KGL$ spectrum representing homotopy invariant algebraic $K$-theory.

\label{thm:B3-flat-duality} Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic $p>0$ with finite residue field, and $N$ a finite commutative $K$-group scheme. Write $N^D=\mathcal Hom(N,\mathbf G_m)$ for its Cartier dual. For every $r$, cup product and the invariant of the Brauer group give Pontryagin dualities \[ H^r_{\mathrm{fppf}}(K,N^D)\times H^{2-r}_{\mathrm{fppf}}(K,N)\longrightarrow\Q/\Z. \] The natural locally compact topologies must be retained. If $X$ is a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over a finite field, $U\subseteq X$ is a nonempty open subscheme, and $N/U$ is a finite flat commutative group scheme, there are canonical isomorphisms \[ H^{3-r}_{c,\mathrm{fppf}}(U,N) \simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}} (H^r_{\mathrm{fppf}}(U,N^D),\Q/\Z). \] Here the group on the right is the dual of the discrete global cohomology group. Compact support is the mapping-fibre construction using the completions at $X\setminus U$.

\label{thm:B3-analytic-duality} Let $X$ be a complex analytic space, countable at infinity and of bounded dimension. There is a dualizing complex $K_X$ with coherent cohomology and a trace $H_c^0(X,K_X)\to\C$ such that, for every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$, the pairings \[ H^q(X,F)\times\operatorname{Ext}^{-q}_c(F,K_X)\to\C, \qquad H_c^q(X,F)\times\operatorname{Ext}^{-q}(F,K_X)\to\C \] are perfect topological dualities after passing to the associated Hausdorff quotients. The separatedness criteria have a one-degree shift: \[ H^q(X,F)\text{ is Hausdorff} \ \Longleftrightarrow\ \operatorname{Ext}^{1-q}_c(F,K_X)\text{ is Hausdorff}, \] \[ H_c^q(X,F)\text{ is Hausdorff} \ \Longleftrightarrow\ \operatorname{Ext}^{1-q}(F,K_X)\text{ is Hausdorff}. \] If $X$ is smooth of dimension $n$, then $K_X\simeq\omega_X[n]$. In particular, for compact smooth $X$ and a holomorphic vector bundle $E$, the first pairing is the finite dimensional perfect pairing \[ H^q(X,E)\times H^{n-q}(X,E^\vee\otimes\omega_X)\to\C. \]

\label{thm:B3-neron} Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring, $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$, and $K^{\mathrm{sh}}$ the fraction field of a strict henselization. A smooth $K$-group scheme $G$ of finite type admits a N\'eron model of finite type over $R$ if and only if $G(K^{\mathrm{sh}})$ is bounded. In particular every abelian variety over $K$ has such a model. More generally an abelian variety over the function field of a connected Dedekind scheme $S$ has a N\'eron model over $S$. In each assertion the model represents, on smooth $S$-schemes, the functor \[ Y\longmapsto\operatorname{Hom}_K(Y_K,G):\quad \operatorname{Hom}_S(Y,\mathcal G) \xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_K(Y_K,G). \] It is unique up to a unique isomorphism respecting the generic fibre.

\label{thm:B3-nonneutral} For the tensor category $\mathcal T$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:B3-tannaka}, suppose there is an exact symmetric $k$-linear tensor functor $\omega$ to vector bundles on a nonempty $k$-scheme $S$. Then \[ G=\operatorname{Isom}^{\otimes}_k (\operatorname{pr}_2^*\omega,\operatorname{pr}_1^*\omega) \longrightarrow S\times_k S \] is an affine faithfully flat groupoid and $\mathcal T\simeq\operatorname{Rep}(S:G)$. The fpqc stack of fibre functors is a gerbe, and its vector-bundle representations recover $\mathcal T$. In characteristic zero such a fibre functor exists over some nonempty $S$ if and only if every object has categorical dimension a nonnegative integer; equivalently, for every object $M$ some exterior power $\bigwedge^nM$ vanishes.

\label{thm:B3-rosenlicht} Let $S$ be any scheme and $\overline C\to S$ a flat finitely presented proper relative curve with geometrically integral fibres, locally projective over $S$. Let $T\subset\overline C$ be a relative effective Cartier divisor, flat over $S$, such that $C=\overline C\setminus T$ is smooth over $S$. There is an explicitly constructed inverse limit of smooth commutative $S$-group schemes $J^\bullet_\infty$, with a morphism $\varphi:C\to J^\bullet_\infty$, such that, for every smooth commutative $S$-group scheme $G$, composition gives a bijection \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{S\text{-}\mathrm{gp}}(J^\bullet_\infty,G) \xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_S(C,G). \] Thus no chosen section of $C/S$ is necessary; the degree components are part of the representing group.

\label{thm:B3-pprimary} Let $Y$ be a smooth projective connected curve of genus $g$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, and let $N$ be a constructible $\mathbf F_p$-sheaf whose sections have open support. There are explicitly defined nonnegative rational local indices $C_y(N)$, zero except at finitely many points, such that \[ \chi(Y,N)\ge (1-g)\operatorname{rank}N-\sum_{y\in Y}C_y(N). \] An equality determined solely by the genus, rank and multiset of local ramification representations is false for $p$-coefficients. Already over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_7$, the two degree-two covers \[ E_0:y^2=x^3-x,\qquad E_1:y^2=x^3-x+1, \qquad\beta_i:E_i\longrightarrow\mathbf P^1, \] give rank-two sheaves $N_i=\beta_{i*}\mathbf F_7$ with four identical tame local representation types and $\chi(\mathbf P^1,N_0)=1$, $\chi(\mathbf P^1,N_1)=0$. The branch points themselves occupy different positions; the assertion concerns local types and their multiplicities, not an isomorphism of sheaves with a fixed labelled branch divisor.

\label{thm:B3-trace} Let $X$ be a proper scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed field $k$, let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_kX$ be a correspondence with $C$ proper. For $F\in D^b_c(X,\Q_\ell)$ and a cohomological correspondence $u:c_{2!}c_1^*F\to F$, the Lefschetz--Verdier formula is \[ \operatorname{Tr}(R\Gamma(u)) =\sum_{\beta\in\pi_0(\operatorname{Fix}(c))}\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u). \] The local terms are canonically defined by the trace class in the dualizing complex of the fixed-point scheme. Consequently a finite \'etale map $f:Y\to X$ of constant degree $n$ satisfies \[ \chi(Y,\Q_\ell)=n\chi(X,\Q_\ell). \] No smoothness assumption on $X$ is needed. Properness is essential.

\label{thm:B3-index} Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field, and let $F$ be a constructible sheaf of vector spaces over a finite field $\Lambda$ of characteristic invertible in the base field. Its characteristic cycle $CC(F)$ is an integral conical $d$-cycle on $T^*X$, characterized by the Milnor formula for vanishing cycles, and \[ \chi(X,F)=(CC(F),T_X^*X)_{T^*X}. \] For a locally constant sheaf of rank $r$, $CC(F)=(-1)^d r[T_X^*X]$. On a curve the additional fibre coefficients are the negatives of the Artin conductors.

\label{thm:B3-operators} Let $C$ be a smooth projective connected curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p\ge0$, let $R$ be an arbitrary ring, and let $F$ be a constructible \'etale sheaf of $R$-modules finite as sets killed by a power of a prime $\ell\ne p$. In the Grothendieck group $K_0(\mathrm{FinMod}_R)$, \[ \sum_i(-1)^i[H^i(C,F)] =(2-2g)[F_{\bar\eta}]-\sum_x\epsilon_x^R(F), \] where \[ \epsilon_x^R(F)= [F_{\bar\eta}]-[F_{\bar x}] +[\operatorname{Hom}_{\Z_\ell[G_x]}(P_{G_x},F_{\bar\eta})]. \] Here $G_x$ is a finite local monodromy quotient and $P_{G_x}$ its projective Swan module. This definition is independent of the chosen quotient. It applies in particular to the constructible extension of the $\ell^m$-torsion of an abelian variety over $k(C)$, with any ring of endomorphisms acting on it.

\label{thm:B3-arithmetic-duality} Let $B$ be the spectrum of a ring of integers in a number field, $f:X\to B$ separated of finite type, and $F$ a torsion \'etale sheaf on $X$. Bloch's cycle complex $\Z_X^c$ gives a canonical duality \[ R\operatorname{Hom}_X(F,\Z_X^c) \simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{\Z} (R\Gamma_c(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}},F),\Z)[-1]. \] For constructible $F$ it induces perfect pairings of finite groups \[ \operatorname{Ext}^{2-i}_X(F,\Z_X^c) \times H_c^i(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}},F)\longrightarrow\Q/\Z. \] Compact support incorporates the modified cohomology at real places; this modification matters for $2$-primary coefficients.

\label{thm:B3-positive-cones} Let $X$ be a projective variety over an algebraically closed field. For every $k$ the pliant cone $\mathrm{PL}^k(X)\subset N^k(X)_\R$, defined as the closed cone generated by products of pullbacks of Schubert classes from Grassmannians, is full dimensional and contains no line. Complete intersections of ample divisors lie in its interior. It is contained in the nef cone, is preserved by pullbacks, and its classes and their products cap $[X]$ to pseudoeffective dimensional cycle classes. Here $N^k(X)_\R$ is the dual of the numerical group $N_k(X)_\R$; on singular $X$ the cap map to $N_{\dim X-k}(X)_\R$ need not be an isomorphism. On smooth $X$ there are functorial inclusions \[ \mathrm{PL}^k(X)\subseteq\mathrm{BPF}^k(X) \subseteq\mathrm{Upsef}^k(X)\subseteq\mathrm{Nef}^k(X), \] where $\mathrm{BPF}$ is generated by flat moving families and $\mathrm{Upsef}$ consists of classes whose pullback to every projective variety is pseudoeffective. Also the cone of pseudoeffective $k$-dimensional cycles is full dimensional and salient; degree against an ample $h^k$ is the restriction of a norm on $N_k(X)_\R$.

\label{thm:B3-abelian-duality} Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field with perfect residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, and let $A/K$ be an abelian variety with dual $A^\vee$. Regard flat cohomology as a complex of sheaves on the ind-rational pro-\'etale site of $k$, and write $C^{\mathrm{SD}}=R\mathcal Hom(C,\Z)$. Then the Poincar\'e biextension induces an isomorphism \[ R\underline{\Gamma}(K,A^\vee)^{\mathrm{SDSD}} \simeq R\underline{\Gamma}(K,A)^{\mathrm{SD}}[1]. \] In particular Grothendieck's pairing on the two N\'eron component groups is perfect, including its $p$-primary part. For the global version let $X/k$ be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$, let $A/k(X)$ be an abelian variety, and let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A^\vee_0$ denote respectively its N\'eron model and the identity component of the dual model. Put \[ V=T\mathcal H^1(X,\mathcal A^\vee_0)_{\rm div}\otimes\Q. \] Here the subscript means the maximal divisible subsheaf, and $T$ is its full Tate module. There is a canonical distinguished triangle \[ V[-1]\longrightarrow R\underline{\Gamma}(X,\mathcal A^\vee_0)^{\mathrm{SDSD}} \longrightarrow R\underline{\Gamma}(X,\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{SD}} \longrightarrow V. \] The term $V$ cannot be discarded in the theorem over arbitrary perfect $k$.
