\label{thm:B3-specialization} For a proper smooth morphism with geometrically connected fibres over a locally noetherian base, specialization between geometric fibres induces a surjection of \'etale fundamental groups. If the special residue characteristic is $p>0$, it induces an isomorphism on the maximal prime-to-$p$ quotients; in residue characteristic zero it is an isomorphism on the full groups. The assertion of full invariance in positive characteristic is false, even for smooth proper elliptic curves.

\label{thm:B3-homogeneous} Let $G$ be a connected simply connected semisimple group over an algebraically closed field, $P\subseteq G$ a parabolic subgroup, and $X_w\subseteq G/P$ a Schubert variety. For a dominant character $\lambda$ of $P$, with the convention that $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ is globally generated, one has \[ H^i(X_w,\mathcal L(\lambda)|_{X_w})=0\quad(i>0), \] and restriction $H^0(G/P,\mathcal L(\lambda))\to H^0(X_w,\mathcal L(\lambda)|_{X_w})$ is surjective. In particular every nef line bundle on the complete homogeneous space $G/P$ has vanishing higher cohomology. This holds in every characteristic.

\label{thm:B3-adeles} Let $X$ be noetherian and $F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Parshin--Beilinson ad\`eles give a functorial flasque resolution \[ 0\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow\mathbb A^0(F) \longrightarrow\mathbb A^1(F)\longrightarrow\cdots. \] Consequently the alternating flag complex of global ad\`eles computes $H^*(X,F)$. If $X$ is also reduced, excellent and pure dimensional of dimension $n$, the ad\`ele ring of a saturated length-$n$ flag is a finite product of $n$-local fields with last residue fields finite over the residue field of the final point. For the local-Jacobian part, let $A$ be noetherian, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $\mathfrak C=\operatorname{Spf}A[[T]]$, and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A((T))$. The commutative group functor \[ \mathcal J(R)=R((T))^\times \] on $A$-algebras has a canonical natural bijection \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{S\text{-}\mathrm{gp}}(\mathcal J,G) \simeq G(U) \] for every smooth separated commutative $S$-group scheme $G$. It is implemented by an Abel--Jacobi morphism $U\to\mathcal J_{\rm omb}$ and the canonical extensions of group homomorphisms to this intermediate functor. It is not implemented by a morphism $U\to\mathcal J$.

\label{thm:B3-dmodule} Let $X$ be a complex analytic manifold of dimension $d$, countable at infinity, and $\mathcal D_X$ its sheaf of holomorphic differential operators. For every bounded complex $M$ of left $\mathcal D_X$-modules with holonomic cohomology, put \[ \mathrm{DR}(M)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal D_X}(\mathcal O_X,M), \qquad \mathrm{Sol}(M)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal D_X}(M,\mathcal O_X). \] There is a canonical isomorphism \[ \mathrm{DR}(M)\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{\C_X}(\mathrm{Sol}(M),\C_X). \] Equivalently, with Verdier duality $D_X(-)=R\mathcal Hom_{\C_X}(-,\C_X[2d])$, one has \[ \mathrm{DR}(M)[d]\simeq D_X(\mathrm{Sol}(M)[d]). \] No regular-singularity assumption is required for this local duality.

\label{thm:B3-riemann-roch} For every separated finite type scheme $X$ over a field there is a Riemann--Roch transformation \[ \tau_X:G_0(X)\longrightarrow\mathrm{CH}_*(X)_\Q \] commuting with proper pushforward and satisfying $\tau_X(E\otimes F)=\operatorname{ch}(E)\cap\tau_X(F)$ for vector bundles $E$. If $X$ is smooth, then $\tau_X(F)=\operatorname{ch}(F)\operatorname{td}(T_X)\cap[X]$. Thus for a proper morphism $f:X\to Y$ of smooth schemes, \[ f_*\bigl(\operatorname{ch}(E)\operatorname{td}(T_X)\cap[X]\bigr) =\operatorname{ch}(Rf_*E)\operatorname{td}(T_Y)\cap[Y]. \] Neither $X,Y$ nor $f$ is required to be projective. For proper pseudo-coherent morphisms of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, $Rf_*$ preserves pseudo-coherent complexes. If the morphism also has finite Tor dimension, it preserves perfect complexes. This includes proper lci morphisms and nonnoetherian bases. For complex analytic spaces, coherent sheaves likewise have a natural transformation $\alpha_X:G_0^{\rm hol}(X)\to K^{\rm top}_0(X)$ to topological $K$-homology, compatible with proper direct images. On a complex manifold it sends a vector bundle to its Dolbeault $K$-homology class. This includes possibly singular and nonprojective complex spaces.

\label{thm:B3-stacks} Let $S$ be locally noetherian with G-ring local rings, and let $\mathcal X$ be a category fibred in groupoids over $S$ satisfying the usual set-size condition. Suppose its diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces, it is an \'etale stack, and it commutes with filtered limits of affine schemes. Suppose also that its deformation categories satisfy the Rim--Schlessinger fibre-product condition and have finite dimensional tangent and infinitesimal-automorphism spaces, every formal object over a complete noetherian local $S$-algebra is effective, and versality is open in finite type families. Then $\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack, locally of finite presentation over $S$.

\label{thm:B3-artinian} Let $R\rightrightarrows U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an equivalence relation of schemes with both projections finite locally free. Write $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and \[ C=\{a\in A:s^*a=t^*a\text{ in }B\}. \] Then the fppf quotient is the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}C$, $U\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is finite faithfully flat, and $R=U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}C}U$. In particular this applies to artinian $U$; its quotient is again artinian. The same conclusion of schematic representability holds for nonaffine $U$ if every equivalence class is contained in an affine open, as is the case for $U$ quasi-projective over an affine scheme.

\label{thm:B3-holomorphic-lefschetz} Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold, $E$ a holomorphic vector bundle, $f:X\to X$ holomorphic, and $u:f^*E\to E$ a holomorphic bundle map. Suppose every fixed point $x$ is nondegenerate: $\det_\C(1-df_x)\ne0$. Then the induced maps on coherent cohomology satisfy \[ \sum_q(-1)^q\operatorname{Tr}(u\circ f^*:H^q(X,E)) =\sum_{f(x)=x}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(u_x)} {\det_\C(1-df_x)}. \] More generally an elliptic complex on a compact smooth manifold, with a geometric endomorphism over a map having only nondegenerate fixed points, has local contribution $\sum_q(-1)^q\operatorname{Tr}(u_{q,x})/ |\det_\R(1-df_x)|$.

\label{thm:B3-homotopy} Every $\infty$-topos $\mathcal X$ has a shape, the pro-space corepresenting the accessible left exact functor $K\mapsto\Gamma_{\mathcal X}(\Delta K)$. A pointed object $A\in\mathcal X$ has internal homotopy sheaves $\pi_n(A)=\tau_{\leq0}\Omega^nA$; fibre sequences give the usual long exact sequence, with the group action interpretation at $\pi_0$. If $A$ is $(n-1)$-connected and $n\geq1$, then \[ \pi_n(A)^{\mathrm{ab}}\otimes M \simeq\widetilde H_n(A;M) \] for every internal abelian group $M$. For a finite type $\C$-scheme $X$, the profinite completion of its \'etale shape is the profinite completion of the singular homotopy type of $X^{\rm an}$. Infinitesimal homotopy sheaves are possible on the fppf site: in characteristic $p$, $B\alpha_p$ has $\pi_1=\alpha_p$. They are not detected by the small \emph{\'etale} site of a reduced scheme. The distinction between internal homotopy sheaves and external pro-homotopy groups of the shape is essential.

\label{thm:B3-chow-pullback} Let $Y$ be a regular separated scheme of finite type over $\Z$. For each morphism $f:X\to Y$ of separated finite type $\Z$-schemes there is a canonical rational bivariant orientation $[f]$, uniquely characterized by $[f]([Y])=[X]$. For irreducible $X,Y$ it has degree $-\dim_YX$ and gives, in the relative dimension grading, \[ f^*:\mathrm{CH}_k(Y)_\Q\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}_{k+\dim_\Z X-\dim_\Z Y}(X)_\Q. \] It is compatible with proper pushforward, flat pullback and refined Gysin maps; compositions of orientations agree whenever the intermediate target is also regular. In particular $X$ need not be regular, and $f$ need not be flat or lci. The coefficient field $\Q$ and the finite type hypotheses are retained.

\label{thm:B3-resolution} Every generically reduced noetherian quasi-excellent $\Q$-scheme admits a finite sequence of blowups with regular centres, disjoint from the inverse image of its regular locus, whose final scheme is regular. The construction is functorial for regular morphisms, up to omitting empty blowups. For a separated finite type scheme $X$ over any field $k$, a nowhere dense closed $Z\subset X$, and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, there are a finite extension $k'/k$ of degree prime to $\ell$ and a proper surjective generically finite alteration $X'\to X$ of degree prime to $\ell$, with $X'$ smooth quasi-projective over $k'$ and inverse image of $Z$ the support of a strict normal-crossings divisor. The alteration assertion does not assert a birational resolution in arbitrary characteristic and dimension.

\label{thm:B3-purity} Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of constant codimension $c$ between regular noetherian schemes, and let $\Lambda=\Z/n\Z$ with $n$ invertible on $X$. The cycle-class Gysin morphism is an isomorphism \[ Ri^!\Lambda\simeq\Lambda(-c)[-2c]. \] In particular $\mathcal H^q_Z(\Lambda)$ vanishes for $q\ne2c$; in degree $2c$ it is $i_*\Lambda(-c)$.

\label{thm:B3-regular-bc} In a Cartesian square with $f:T\to S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $g:S'\to S$ a regular morphism of noetherian schemes, let $f':T'\to S'$ and $g':T'\to T$ be the projections. For every \'etale $\Z/n\Z$-sheaf $F$ on $T$, where $n$ is invertible on $S$, the base-change map is an isomorphism \[ g^*Rf_*F\simeq Rf'_*g'^*F. \]

\label{thm:B3-local-biduality} Let $X$ be a noetherian excellent $\Z[1/n]$-scheme with a dimension function $\delta$, and put $\Lambda=\Z/n\Z$. There is a normalized potential dualizing complex $K_{X,\delta}$, unique with its normalization, belonging to $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\Lambda)$. The functor $D_K=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,K_{X,\delta})$ preserves $D^b_c$, and for every $M\in D^b_c$ the canonical map \[ M\longrightarrow D_KD_KM \] is an isomorphism. The complex has finite quasi-injective dimension if and only if $X$ has finite Krull dimension; in that case it is also a dualizing complex in the SGA~5 sense.

\label{thm:B3-finiteness} Let $X$ be noetherian quasi-excellent, $f:Y\to X$ of finite type, and $F$ a constructible \'etale $\Z/n\Z$-sheaf on $Y$, with $n$ invertible on $X$. Then every $R^qf_*F$ is constructible and $R^qf_*F=0$ for all sufficiently large $q$. Equivalently $Rf_*$ preserves bounded constructible complexes. No properness assumption on $f$ or finite Krull dimension assumption on $X$ is needed in this theorem.

\label{thm:B3-affine-cd} Let $X$ be noetherian quasi-excellent with dimension function $\delta$, let $f:Y\to X$ be affine of finite type, and let $F$ be a constructible \'etale $\Z/n\Z$-sheaf with $n$ invertible on $X$. Set $\delta_Y(y)=\delta(f(y))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(y))}\kappa(y)$ and $\delta(F)=\sup\{\delta_Y(y):F_{\bar y}\ne0\}$. Then \[ \sup\{\delta(x):(R^qf_*F)_{\bar x}\ne0\}\leq\delta(F)-q. \] For an affine variety of dimension $d$ over a separably closed field, this implies $H^q(Y,F)=0$ for $q>d$.

\label{thm:B3-grauert} For a proper holomorphic map $f:X\to Y$ of complex analytic spaces and a coherent analytic $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$, every $R^qf_*F$ is coherent. In particular cohomology of a coherent sheaf on a compact complex space is finite dimensional.

\label{thm:B3-rigid} Let $K$ be complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean valuation. On an affinoid rigid space $X=\operatorname{Sp}A$, finite $A$-modules correspond to coherent analytic sheaves and have no higher cohomology. For every proper map of rigid $K$-spaces, all higher direct images of coherent sheaves are coherent. If $R$ is the valuation ring, taking generic fibre induces an equivalence between quasi-paracompact admissible formal $R$-schemes localized at admissible formal blowups and quasi-paracompact quasi-separated rigid $K$-spaces.

\label{thm:B3-sga2} The reference is to SGA~2, and its proposed finiteness statements cannot all be recorded as affirmative theorems. In particular SGA~2, Expos\'e XIII, Conjecture 1.1 is false: a local cohomology module of a finite module over a regular noetherian ring need not have finitely generated $I$-annihilator. A precise positive local Lefschetz conclusion is that every noetherian local complete-intersection ring of dimension at least four is parafactorial. Consequently a noetherian local complete-intersection ring that is factorial at every prime of height at most three is factorial.

\label{B1b-correspondence} Let $X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_m$ be smooth projective fourfolds over $k$, and suppose $D^2_\ell(Y_i)$ holds. Suppose algebraic correspondences $a_i\in\operatorname{CH}^4(X\times Y_i)_\Q$ and $b_i\in\operatorname{CH}^4(Y_i\times X)_\Q$ satisfy \[ \sum_i(b_i)_*(a_i)_*=\operatorname{id} \quad\hbox{on }H^4(X_{\bar k},\Q_\ell(2)). \] Then $D^2_\ell(X)$ holds. In particular this applies to a generically finite surjective morphism from any $Y_i$ to $X$.

\label{B1b-blowup} Let $X$ be a smooth projective fourfold over $k$, let $Z\subset X$ be a smooth closed center of positive codimension on every component, and let $f:W=\operatorname{Bl}_ZX\to X$. Then $D^2_\ell(W)$ holds if and only if $D^2_\ell(X)$ holds.

\label{B1b-fermat} Let $\operatorname{char}k\ne3$ and let \[ F=\{z_0^3+\cdots+z_5^3=0\}\subset\mathbf P^5_k. \] For every $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, numerical and $\ell$-adic homological equivalence agree for all cycles on $F$ with rational coefficients. The same holds for any smooth projective $k$-form of $F$. Together with Ancona's numerical Hodge theorem for $F$, this places these fourfolds in the homological-positivity class of Proposition~\ref{prop:B1b-criterion}.

\label{C-exp-log} The maps \[ D\longmapsto \exp D=\sum_{j\geq0}\frac{D^j}{j!},\qquad u\longmapsto \log u=\sum_{j\geq1}\frac{(-1)^{j+1}}j(u-1)^j \] are mutually inverse bijections between nilpotent $K$-derivations of $A$ and $K$-algebra automorphisms $u$ for which $u-1$ is nilpotent in $\operatorname{End}_K(A)$. Both sums are finite. The nilpotency indices of $D$ and $\exp D-1$ coincide.

\label{C-filtered} Let $I\subset A$ be an ideal with $I^m=0$, where $m\geq1$. Exponential is a bijection from \[ \mathfrak d_I= \{D\in\operatorname{Der}_K(A):D(I^k)\subset I^{k+1} \text{ for every }k\geq0\} \] to \[ U_I=\{u\in\operatorname{Aut}_K(A):u(I)=I, \ \operatorname{gr}_I(u)=1\}. \] Its inverse is the polynomial logarithm. Here $I^0=A$ and $\operatorname{gr}_I(A)=\bigoplus_{k\geq0}I^k/I^{k+1}$. This is the valid replacement of the last corollary of 68/046.

\label{C-differential} For $u\in\operatorname{Aut}_K(A)$ let $J=(u(a)-a:a\in A)\subset A$. For every $n\geq0$, \[ u\text{ has differential order at most }n \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad J^{n+1}=0. \] Suppose more generally that $I^m=0$ and $u$ induces the identity on $A/I$. Then $u(I)=I$ and it induces an $(A/I)$-linear automorphism $\gamma:I/I^2\to I/I^2$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $u=\exp D$ for a nilpotent $K$-derivation $D$ of $A$; \item $u-1$ is nilpotent on the $K$-module $A$; \item $\gamma-1$ is nilpotent on the $(A/I)$-module $I/I^2$. \end{enumerate} If $(\gamma-1)^r=0$, then one valid bound is \[ (u-1)^{m+(r-1)m(m-1)/2}=0. \] In particular this characterizes exactly which differential automorphisms are exponentials, by taking $I=J$. The other differential automorphisms are exactly those with non-unipotent action on $J/J^2$, where unipotent here requires a uniform nilpotence bound.

\label{C-other-autos} A differential automorphism need not be an exponential of a nilpotent derivation. On $A=\Q[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$, the automorphism $u(\epsilon)=2\epsilon$ has differential order one and is not such an exponential. The assertion in 68/045 that $u$ automatically acts identically on $\operatorname{gr}_J(A)$ is also false. For any $\Q$-vector space $V$, the square-zero algebra $\Q\oplus V$ has all $\Q$-algebra automorphisms of the form $1\oplus T$, with $T\in\operatorname{GL}_{\Q}(V)$. All are differential of order at most one; precisely those for which $T-1$ is uniformly nilpotent are exponentials of nilpotent derivations. Thus no finite dimensional or semisimple description of the remaining automorphisms is available without additional hypotheses.

\label{C-intertwine} Let $M,N$ be arbitrary $K$-modules, let $u\in\operatorname{End}_K(M)$ and $v\in\operatorname{End}_K(N)$ be locally nilpotent, and let $f:M\to N$ be $K$-linear. Then \[ f\exp(u)=\exp(v)f\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad fu=vf. \] The exponentials are pointwise finite, mutually invertible linear maps.

\label{C-functor-criterion} For any $K$-module functor $\mathcal M$: \begin{enumerate} \item The ordinary exponential map \[ \{u\in\mathscr E(K):u\text{ nilpotent}\} \longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal O,\mathscr E^\times) \] is injective. Its image consists exactly of actions $\rho$ satisfying both of the following explicit conditions: there is a single integer $m$ with $(\rho_R(\lambda)-1)^m=0$ for every $R$ and $\lambda\in R$; and their polynomial logarithms define an $\mathcal O$-linear natural map $L:\mathcal O\to\mathscr E$. Thus this exponential map is bijective exactly when every action satisfies these two conditions. \item The formal exponential map \[ \mathscr E(K)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal N,\mathscr E^\times) \] has image exactly the formal actions $\rho$ for which each $\rho_R(\lambda)-1$ is nilpotent in $\mathscr E(R)$ and the natural map $L_R(\lambda)=\log\rho_R(\lambda)$ extends to an $\mathcal O$-linear natural map $\mathcal O\to\mathscr E$. Nilpotence bounds in this assertion may depend on $(R,\lambda)$. Its fibres, when nonempty, are translates of \[ H(\mathcal M)=\{w\in\mathscr E(K): \lambda w_R=0\text{ for every }R\text{ and every } \lambda\in\operatorname{Nil}(R)\}. \] Consequently formal exponential is bijective exactly when $H(\mathcal M)=0$ and every formal action meets the displayed logarithm and extension conditions. \end{enumerate} These criteria apply to every module functor; they require no quasicoherence assumption.
\label{C-functor-counter} The formal exponential need not be injective, and neither exponential map need be surjective, for arbitrary module functors.

\label{C-qcoh} Let $M$ be any $K$-module and $\mathcal M(R)=R\otimes_K M$. Formal actions of $\widehat{\mathbb G}_a=\mathcal N$ on $\mathcal M$ are uniquely the $\bar e_u$ for $u\in\operatorname{End}_K(M)$. Ordinary actions of $\mathbb G_a=\mathcal O$ are uniquely the $e_u$ for locally nilpotent endomorphisms $u$ of $M$. Consequently the ordinary map with domain only uniformly nilpotent endomorphisms is bijective exactly when every locally nilpotent endomorphism of $M$ is uniformly nilpotent. Finite generation of $M$ suffices for this last property but is not asserted to be necessary. The ordinary classification is stated in \cite[Chapter VIII, Example 2.1 and footnote 1, p.~113]{MilneAGS}.

\label{C-rearrangement} For $f,g\in\R^{(G)}_+$, \[ \sup_{f'\sim f}\sum_x f'(x)g(x)=|f,g|, \qquad \|f*g\|_\infty\leq|f,g|. \] An inner product achieves its rearrangement maximum precisely when every positive superlevel set of one factor is comparable by inclusion with every positive superlevel set of the other. Consequently $(f,g)$ is pr\'etass\'e precisely when there exists $s\in G$ such that the superlevel sets of $f$ and $\delta_s*\check g$ together form a chain. Moreover $f'\prec f$ is equivalent to $|f',h|\leq|f,h|$ for every $h\in\R^{(G)}_+$.

\label{C-chain-true} Under (a)--(d), $S=\bigcup_{a\in\widetilde G}C_a$ is convolution stable, and every pair in $S\times S$ is pr\'etass\'e. This conclusion does not require the additional kernel and torsion equivariance assumptions.

\label{C-K-counter} The axioms on 68/017 do not imply Condition $K$ on 68/021, even with all positive cardinalities represented, nonempty families, and the exact specified two-torsion kernel. This failure already occurs on $G=\Z/4\Z$.

\label{C-K-replacement} Let $S\subset\R^{(G)}_+$ be convolution stable and suppose that for every positive integer $k\leq|G|$ it contains an indicator $1_{A_k}$ with $|A_k|=k$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item Every pair in $S\times S$ is tass\'e. \item For every $n\geq2$, $f_i\in S$ and $f_i'\prec f_i$ imply $f_1'*\cdots*f_n'\prec f_1*\cdots*f_n$. \item Condition $K$ holds: under those hypotheses, $\|f_1'*\cdots*f_n'\|_\infty \leq\|f_1*\cdots*f_n\|_\infty$. \end{enumerate} For the implication from (3) to (1), it suffices to assume only the three-factor instances with third factor $1_{A_k}$. Thus the missing hypothesis in Lead L8 is a genuine convolution-majorization property; chain closure and pairwise optimal suprema alone do not supply it.

\label{C-literal-class} Interpret ${}_2G$ as the subset $T=\{t\in G:t^2=e\}$ with the multiplication inherited from $G$, and retain exactly the draft axioms just stated, without adding cardinality completeness. For a finite or arbitrary discrete group $G$, data satisfying these axioms and $i:T\simeq\ker\rho$ exist if and only if $T$ is a subgroup of $G$, equivalently if and only if every two involutions commute. The construction can have a surjective $\rho$ and at least one nonzero cone. In particular, within the abelian category every finite and every discrete group admits a system in this literal sense.

\label{C-extension} The chain, symmetry, convolution, and alignment axioms do not determine the kernel of $\rho$. Even after the additional requirement $\ker\rho\simeq{}_2G$ is imposed, they do not determine the extension up to group isomorphism, including when all possible positive set cardinalities occur.

\label{C-symmetry} For a group $G$, the pr\'etass\'e relation on all of $\R^{(G)}_+\times\R^{(G)}_+$ is symmetric if and only if $G$ is abelian. If both $f$ and $g$ are individually equal to their inversions up to a left translation, their particular pr\'etass\'e relation is symmetric on any group, as asserted on 68/021.
\label{C-packed-asymmetry} On $S_3$ the tass\'e relation also need not be symmetric. With $a=(01)$ and $b=(12)$ in Theorem~\ref{C-symmetry}, the pair $(f,g)$ is tass\'e and $(g,f)$ is not.

\label{A:tensor} \status{Proved.} Let $f_\pm:(\D,0)\to(D_\pm,p_\pm)$ be pointed conformal parametrizations. An orientation-reversing isometry between their boundary circle torsors has the form $\zeta_- = e^{i\theta}/\zeta_+$ on $|\zeta_+|=1$. The induced propagator is \[ q=e^{i\theta}df_{+,0}(1)\otimes df_{-,0}(1) \in T_{p_+}Y\otimes T_{p_-}Y, \qquad |q|_{z_+,z_-}=r_{z_+}(D_+,p_+)r_{z_-}(D_-,p_-). \] The inverse tensor, viewed as a nonzero bilinear pairing into $\C$, has reciprocal modulus.
\label{A:koebe} \status{Known theorem, applied with all normalizations specified.} If $f:\D\hookrightarrow\PP^1\setminus\{1,\infty\}$ is holomorphic, $f(0)=0$, and $r=|f'(0)|$, then $r\leq4$.

\label{A:04} \status{Refuted, with a complete geometric counterexample.} For the targets described on 67/075--078, the capping-and-forgetting maps $MD_{0,4}\to M_{\mathrm{st}}N_{0,4}$ and, whenever defined with the same unrestricted nodal tensor, $MDB_{0,4}\to M_{\mathrm{st}}ND_{0,4}$ are not surjective. In particular, they are not algebraic, complex analytic, real analytic, topological, or set-theoretic isomorphisms onto those targets. Lead L2 is false.

\label{A:alltypes} \status{Proved.} Fix any stable pointed complex curve $Y$ with at least one node. The propagators obtainable from embedded caps on its fixed normalization are bounded in each nodal tangent line, for any fixed Hermitian norms. Thus the unrestricted nonzero-tensor target over $Y$ is never the image of capping. For every stable type with $3g-3+n>0$ this gives a counterexample to a global isomorphism. The sole stable type of complexity zero is $(0,3)$; there are no nodal stable curves of that type, and capping with all three external discs retained is an equivalence.

\label{A:arbitrarycuts} \status{Proved under stated interpretation; the hypothesis matters.} If the source on 67/074 includes arbitrary smooth cut circles, the canonical hyperbolic boundary torsors need not be respected by the identification of their two banks. In that interpretation the asserted pointed-disc anti-isomorphism, and hence the asserted tensor functor, is not defined by the stated construction. Restricting to geodesic cuts in the canonical hyperbolic metric removes this problem but does not remove Theorem~\ref{A:04}.

\label{A:fullcaps} \status{Proved.} For a fixed stable graph $\Gamma$, consider the following two groupoids: (i) hyperbolic bordered surfaces with labelled disjoint essential geodesic cuts of graph $\Gamma$, with conformal isomorphisms preserving all labels; (ii) their compact normalized components with a full admissible system of pointed cap discs at every half-edge and external mark, equal hyperbolic lengths on paired half-edges, and a specified orientation-reversing toric identification on each paired boundary. Cutting and capping gives an equivalence of these groupoids, with inverse obtained by deleting the node caps and welding the paired boundaries. Cuspidal external components are allowed as zero discs.

\label{A:plumbing} \status{Known, with the comparison explicitly limited to germs.} For a stable complex curve $Y$ and a multicurve $\Gamma$ representing its nodes, choose holomorphic coordinates $z_e,w_e$ near the two branches of each node and local parameters $u$ for the pointed normalization. For sufficiently small $t_e$, the equations $z_ew_e=t_e$ yield local analytic deformation coordinates after the appropriate Dehn-twist quotient. Their normal tangent directions are canonically the lines $T_{p_e^+}Y\otimes T_{p_e^-}Y$. This does not identify an entire product of punctured tangent lines with the global cut-surface moduli.

\label{A:grafting} \status{Known, with a proved identification of the manuscript operation.} Let $S$ be a compact oriented surface with $n\geq1$ labelled boundary components and $\chi(S)=2-2g-n<0$. Let $\mathcal T^B(S)$ denote marked hyperbolic surfaces with these boundary components geodesic, and let $\mathcal T_{g,n}$ denote the Teichmuller space of the corresponding punctured surfaces. Canonical capping of 67/061--070, followed by remembering the cap centres, satisfies \[ \Psi=(\operatorname{cap},\ell):\mathcal T^B(S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathcal T_{g,n}\times(0,\infty)^n \] as a mapping-class-equivariant real analytic diffeomorphism. Allowing some boundary lengths to vanish extends this to a homeomorphism \[ \overline\Psi:\mathcal T^{B,\geq0}(S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathcal T_{g,n}\times[0,\infty)^n, \] real analytic on every fixed boundary/cusp stratum. No assertion of analyticity across all corner strata is needed here.

\label{A:cuspnorm} \status{Proved; the norm is the known Wolpert norm.} For a marked compact Riemann surface $(X,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ with $2g-2+n>0$, the complete curvature $-1$ metric on $X\setminus\{p_i\}$ defines a canonical Hermitian norm on every $T_{p_i}X$. A normalized cusp coordinate $q$ has \[ ds^2=\frac{|dq|^2}{|q|^2(\log|q|)^2},\qquad \|\partial_q\|_{\mathrm{cusp}}=1. \] In its embedded range the horocycle $|q|=\rho$ has length $h=-2\pi/\log\rho$. The unrestricted horocycle-decoration torsor is parametrized by $h>0$, with no requirement that all projected horocycles be disjoint. Via $h_i=\ell_i$, Theorem~\ref{A:grafting} identifies the positive-length capping bundle with Penner's decoration bundle. This identification does not send actual cap shadows to cusp discs.

\label{A:collar} \status{Proved.} Let $(X,h)$ be a compact hyperbolic surface with geodesic boundary. Remove smooth open boundary collars so that the remaining surface $X'$ is diffeomorphic to $X$. Let $h'$ be its canonical hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary. There is a unique smooth real function $u$ on $X'$ such that $h'=e^{2u}h$, and it is characterized by \[ \Delta_hu=e^{2u}-1\quad\text{on }X',\qquad \partial_{n}u=-k_h\quad\text{on }\partial X'. \] Here $\Delta_h=\operatorname{div}_h\nabla$, $n$ is the outward unit normal, and $k_h$ is geodesic curvature measured toward the interior of $X'$. For collars cut at constant inward distance $a_i>0$ below their embedding widths, $k_h=-\tanh a_i$ on the corresponding new boundary and $u>0$ throughout $X'$. Thus $h'>h$ pointwise there.

\label{A:welding} \status{Known existence theorem, with the category and uniqueness specified.} Let compact oriented bordered Riemann surfaces have finitely many paired boundary circles, and glue each pair by an orientation-reversing quasisymmetric homeomorphism, measured in analytic boundary coordinates. The topological quotient carries a conformal structure which restricts to the given structures on every interior, and its seams are quasicircles. It is unique under the identity on the pieces. More generally, for any given welding homeomorphisms, two realizations are conformally identical if one realization's seams are conformally removable. Rectifiable seams satisfy this uniqueness condition. Quasisymmetry is sufficient for existence and characterizes quasicircle realizations; it is not necessary for existence of arbitrary Jordan-curve weldings.

\label{A:slit} \status{Proved from the welding theorem and prime-end uniformization.} Let $V$ be a Jordan disc and let $I$ be a Jordan arc with one endpoint on $\partial V$ and its remaining points in $V$. Cutting $V$ along $I$ gives a simply connected surface with a prime-end boundary circle. Its Riemann map has the boundary identifications of 67/071--073, with the slit tip and its two access points at the attachment prescribed as the three normalization points. No rectifiability is needed for this cutting assertion. Conversely, let the two designated boundary banks be identified by $\varphi$, and form their bank-exchanging involution $H$: $H=\varphi$ on one bank and $H=\varphi^{-1}$ on the other. Require $H$ to be quasisymmetric in an analytic boundary coordinate on the \emph{union} of the banks, including their common endpoint. This condition has a slit realization which is the image of a straight radial slit under a quasiconformal homeomorphism of a disc. After putting its tip at $0$ and its attachment at $1$ in the unit disc, the normalized realization is unique. Conversely every such quasiconformal slit pair has this welding condition. The correspondence is therefore with this specified class of slit pairs; quasisymmetry on a single bank alone is insufficient at the fold. For a prescribed rectifiable slit the normalized welding is unique, but ``rectifiable graph'' does not supply an existence criterion for an arbitrary interval homeomorphism.

\label{A:L5} \status{Proved under the stated geodesic-cut convention.} On 67/074--082, geodesic cuts and the rotational capping identifications are real analytic, hence quasisymmetric and removable. No earlier assertion about arbitrary rectifiable weldings is needed for that construction. If ``differentiable cut'' is taken literally without toric compatibility, the obstruction in Proposition~\ref{A:arbitrarycuts} remains; smoothness alone does not produce the claimed nodal tensor.

\label{A:orange} \status{Refuted; the method is credited to Michel Hua's project.} The model proposed on 67/019--020, in which all admissible pants caps are concentric subdiscs of three fixed orange slices, is false. There is a hyperbolic pair of pants with two cusps and third boundary length $32$ whose canonical cap cannot lie in the proposed cell at $0$.

\label{A:action} \status{Proved from Theorem~\ref{A:grafting}.} The semigroup $[0,\infty)^I$ acts continuously on $\mathcal T^{B,\geq0}(S)$ by \[ a\cdot Y=\overline\Psi^{-1} \bigl(\operatorname{cap}(Y),(a_i\ell_i(Y))_{i\in I}\bigr). \] It is intrinsic and mapping-class equivariant; it is real analytic on each stratum on which the source and target patterns of zero lengths are fixed. The group $(0,\infty)^I$ acts freely and transitively on each positive-length fibre. The all-zero multiplier is the capping retraction. The quotient is $\mathcal T_{g,n}$. The section with all lengths equal to $1$ is canonical.

\label{A:graph-radius-domain} Let $\Gamma$ be a connected stable graph of type $(g,n)$, with edge set $E\ne\varnothing$. Fix its pointed compact normalization components $X_v$, with every branch and external marking labelled. For an ordinary fibre, retain an identification of the normalization with these fixed objects; merely labelling the special points need not remove their finite automorphisms. All constructions below are equivariant for those automorphisms and also define the corresponding groupoid maps. We first take all external ends to be cusps. At each special point choose a local coordinate, used only to measure radii and tensor moduli. Let $I_v$ be the set of node branches on $X_v$. For $a\in[0,\infty)^E$, define $(B_va)_h=a_e$ when the branch $h$ belongs to the edge $e$; both branches of a loop are included separately. Let $H_v$ be the Jenkins--Strebel support function for these active points, with all other special points kept marked, and put \[ H_\Gamma(a)=\sum_v H_v(B_va),\qquad H_v(0)=0. \] Define the explicit open convex set \[ K_\Gamma=\left\{y\in\R^E: \sum_e a_e y_e<H_\Gamma(a) \text{ for every }a\geq0,\ \sum_ea_e=1\right\}. \] The attainable nonzero node tensors are exactly those with $(\log|q_e|)_e\in K_\Gamma$. Every such tensor system has a unique labelled geodesic-cut preimage, up to the equivalence of Theorem~\ref{A:fullcaps}. More precisely, if $x_e=(\ell_e/2\pi)^2$, the logarithmic modulus map is \[ G_\Gamma(x)=\sum_v B_v^T F_v(B_vx),\qquad G_\Gamma:(0,\infty)^E\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K_\Gamma, \] where $F_v$ is the vector of logarithmic cap radii on $X_v$. It is a real analytic diffeomorphism with symmetric positive definite derivative. In the phase coordinates specified by normalized cap maps, the complete tangent map is block diagonal with blocks $DG_\Gamma$ and the identity on $\R^E$. This is the tangent map on the fixed normalization fibre. When the normalization components also vary, the differential is block triangular with the identity on the normalization-moduli base and this invertible fibre block. In particular the full real tangent map is invertible everywhere on the fixed graph stratum.

\label{A:graph-pi-one} For a fixed labelled normalization with its identification retained, the map on ordinary fundamental groups from the geodesic-cut source to the unrestricted tensor target is the identity $\Z^E\to\Z^E$ in the twist generators, although its image is the proper domain of Theorem~\ref{A:graph-radius-domain}. The analogous statement holds for orbifold fundamental groups when the normalization components vary and their finite automorphisms are retained: inclusion of the restricted tensor domain is a homotopy equivalence on each fixed graph stratum. This is compatible with the everywhere invertible real tangent map. Neither test supplies the missing properness onto the unrestricted target.

\label{A:bordered-radius-algorithm} The same finite-dimensional inversion determines the image when external caps are retained. Add one positive variable $x_i$ for each positive external boundary, and one output coordinate $\log r_i$ for its shadow. In $B_v$, copy a node variable to each of its two flags and an external variable to its single flag. Then $B^T(F_v)_v$ is a real analytic diffeomorphism onto the strict support domain with support $\sum_vH_v(B_va)$. For specified normalization components, node tensors, and actual external pointed discs, the following is a necessary and sufficient test for a geodesic-cut preimage: their tensor moduli and external shadow radii belong to that domain; the unique recovered length vector produces exactly the specified external discs. When both conditions hold, the preimage is unique. Zero external radii are handled on their corresponding face. This test states the additional disc compatibility instead of assuming that forgetting node caps preserves admissibility.

\label{A:cap-plumbing-equation} The inverse on the restricted propagator domain in Theorem~\ref{A:graph-radius-domain} is a plumbing in the canonical cap coordinates, which themselves depend on the recovered length vector. If $z_\pm$ are coordinates at the two node branches and $f_\pm:\D\to D_\pm$ are normalized so that $(z_\pm\circ f_\pm)'(0)=r_\pm>0$, put $Z_\pm=r_\pm f_\pm^{-1}$. Its seam identification is exactly \[ Z_+Z_-=q,\qquad q=r_+r_-e^{i\theta}. \] This identity does not identify the radius inverse with plumbing in one fixed pair of coordinate germs for all $q$.

\label{A:plumbing-sources} Kra's horocyclic construction and Wolpert's hyperbolic plumbing are valid comparisons after their coordinate choices and domain restrictions are retained. They do not parametrize arbitrary nonzero normal tensors by the manuscript's canonical capping map.

\label{A:EarleMarden-local} On a neighbourhood of a fixed nodal surface, the Earle--Marden Kleinian plumbing family and the Hubbard--Koch family give the same analytic marked deformation germ. This comparison follows from the proved Appendix of \citet[pp.~41--42 in the opened author version] {HubbardKoch2014}. It is a local comparison with a specified Dehn-twist quotient.

\label{A:single-cap-all-lengths} Let $(X;p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ be a fixed connected compact marked Riemann surface. Suppose two systems of pairwise disjoint embedded pointed discs $(D_j,p_j)$ and $(D'_j,p_j)$ arise by infinite grafting of hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundaries of positive lengths $\ell_j$ and $\ell'_j$, respectively. If, for one index $i$, \[ D_i=D'_i, \] then $\ell_j=\ell'_j$ for every $j$, including $j=i$. With the usual marking convention, Mondello's grafting theorem further implies that the two complete systems are equal.

\label{A:single-cap-with-cusps} The preceding uniqueness holds also when some of the other ends are complete hyperbolic cusps, assigned length zero, while the compared cap is a positive cap in both constructions. Therefore keeping one positive pointed cap unchanged cannot be compatible with replacing any other positive geodesic boundary by a complete cusp on the same marked compactification.

\label{A:MDB-forgetting-admissibility} Interpret the admissibility of the external cap system in 67/075(b) to mean that on each normalization component the node branches are complete cusps, as the point-like boundary components $s,t$ on 67/081 specify. Under this convention, the proposed capping-and-forgetting operation $MDB_{g,n}\to M_{\mathrm{st}}ND_{g,n}$ need not take values in its stated target. It already fails for two positive-boundary pairs of pants glued along one boundary, giving type $(0,4)$. More generally it fails on any normalization component that has both a forgotten positive node cap and a retained positive external cap.

\label{A:pants-cap-dependence} Normalize the capped, labelled pair of pants to $(\mathbb P^1;0,1,\infty)$. The cap at $0$ is not a function of its own boundary length alone. Specifically the length vectors \[ (2\pi,2\pi,2\pi),\qquad(2\pi,4\pi,2\pi) \] give different embedded pointed discs at $0$, although that boundary has the same length in both examples. Every positive length vector is realized by a hyperbolic pair of pants, so both examples meet all hypotheses of the question.

\label{C:A2b-regularity} The caps and their normalized conformal coordinates vary real-analytically along each finite-dimensional real-analytic family in a fixed face of the length space. In particular $F_X$ is real-analytic. After identifying the infinitely grafted surface with $X\setminus\{p_i\}$, its Thurston metric varies differentiably off the moving seams. At a seam it is $C^{1,1}$, its first variation is continuous, and the one-sided derivatives used below exist.

\label{C:A2b-injectivity} On every face of the nonnegative boundary-length space, the canonical cap system is determined by its conformal radii. On its positive coordinates the logarithmic radius map is a real-analytic diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $\mathbb R^I$, and is the gradient of a strictly convex real-analytic function of $x_i=(\ell_i/2\pi)^2$. In particular the full map of admissible canonical cap systems to their tangent-disc radii is injective. Changing the local coordinate norms translates the logarithmic radius map by a constant vector and does not change these assertions.

\label{C:A2b-support} For $a\ne0$, let $Q_a$ be the unique Jenkins--Strebel differential whose characteristic domains are exactly the punctured discs at the active punctures $\{p_i:a_i>0\}$, with circumferences $2\pi\sqrt{a_i}$; at the inactive marked points it has at most simple poles. In particular no additional characteristic annuli are permitted. Let $D_i^a$ be its characteristic pointed discs and $R_i(a)$ their conformal radii. Then \[ H_X(a)=\sum_{a_i>0}a_i\log R_i(a)<\infty. \] Among disjoint active pointed discs avoiding all the other marked points, equality in this weighted radius inequality holds exactly for the indicated Strebel discs. Their complement is the critical graph, including inactive marked points, and has empty interior. The function $H_X$ is convex, positively homogeneous, and continuous on the whole nonnegative orthant.

\label{C:A2b-support-integral} The preceding support value can be evaluated directly from $Q_a$. On an active characteristic disc choose the branch $\sqrt{Q_a}\sim i\sqrt{a_i}\,dz_i/z_i$ near $p_i$, and choose a regular point $b_i$ of its boundary. Then \[ w_i(z)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i}{\sqrt{a_i}} \int_{b_i}^{z}\sqrt{Q_a}\right) \] is its normalized disc coordinate up to rotation, and \[ \log R_i(a)=\lim_{z\to p_i} \left[\log|z_i(z)|- \operatorname{Re}\!\left(-\frac{i}{\sqrt{a_i}} \int_{b_i}^{z}\sqrt{Q_a}\right)\right]. \] Thus the image inequalities use only the unique meromorphic quadratic differential with principal parts $-a_i\,dz_i^2/z_i^2$ whose characteristic domains are precisely the punctured discs around the active marks, followed by these integrals and limits. At inactive marks at most simple poles are allowed; there are no additional characteristic annuli. No elementary expression for its coefficients in every genus is asserted.

\label{C:A2b-gap} For the canonical cap radii $F_X(x)_i=\log r_i$, with active parameters $x_i=\lambda_i^2>0$, we have \[ 0\leq H_X(x)-x\cdot F_X(x)\leq2g-2+n. \] Here inactive ends remain cusps and are included in $n$. The lower inequality is strict for every nonzero finite parameter vector.

\label{C:A2b-collar} Put \[ Y(\lambda)=\arctan\!\left(\frac{1}{2\sinh(\pi\lambda)}\right), \qquad \eta_i=Y(\lambda_i)/\lambda_i. \] The canonical cap discs can be simultaneously enlarged to disjoint pointed discs whose logarithmic radii are $F_X(x)_i+\eta_i$. Consequently \[ H_X(a)-a\cdot F_X(x)\geq\sum_{i\in I}a_i\eta_i>0 \quad(a\geq0,\ a\ne0), \] and \[ F_X(x)_i\leq H_X(e_i)-Y(\lambda_i)/\lambda_i \longrightarrow-\infty\quad\text{as }\lambda_i\to0. \] The last estimate is uniform in all other lengths.

\label{C:A2b-image} For every stable fixed pointed conformal surface and every nonempty active set $I$, the map \[ F_X:(0,\infty)^I\longrightarrow\mathcal K_{X,I} \] is a real-analytic diffeomorphism. Thus a vector of positive radii $(r_i)_{i\in I}$ is realized by a unique admissible canonical cap system, with all other ends cuspidal, if and only if \[ \prod_{i\in I}r_i^{a_i} <\prod_{a_i>0}R_i(a)^{a_i} \quad\text{for every }a\geq0,\quad\sum_{i\in I}a_i=1. \] Here $R_i(a)$ are computed from the unique Jenkins--Strebel system of circumferences $2\pi\sqrt{a_i}$. The zero radius vector corresponds to the all-cuspidal system. These statements give the whole image on all faces, and injectivity on their union.

\label{C:A2b-normal-families} For a fixed index $i$, let $f_m:\mathbb D\to X$ be injective holomorphic maps with $f_m(0)=p_i$ whose images avoid every $p_j$, $j\ne i$. Normalize their derivatives to be positive in the chosen coordinate norm. Their conformal radii have a finite upper bound. Every sequence has a subsequence converging locally uniformly to a holomorphic map; if its radii are bounded away from zero, the limit is an injective holomorphic disc avoiding the other marked points. Nonconstant limits of mutually disjoint discs are mutually disjoint. If the radii converge to a positive value, convergence of the normalized maps to a nonconstant limit is equivalent to pointed conformal kernel convergence of their image domains.

\label{C:A2b-strebel-limit} Let $x^{(m)}=(\lambda_i^{(m)})^2$ be a sequence of squared length vectors with \[ s_m=\sum_i x_i^{(m)}\longrightarrow\infty, \qquad a^{(m)}=x^{(m)}/s_m\longrightarrow a, \qquad a_i\geq0,\quad\sum_i a_i=1. \] The canonical cap at every index with $a_i>0$ converges, in the pointed conformal-kernel sense, to its unique Jenkins--Strebel disc with circumference proportional to $\sqrt{a_i}$. Every remaining cap has conformal radius tending to zero and has degenerate pointed kernel. In particular, if one boundary length tends to infinity while the others remain bounded, its cap tends to the unique one-weight Strebel slit domain. This is a domain limit on the fixed conformal surface; it does not assert Hausdorff convergence of arbitrary boundary traces.

\label{C:A2b-pants-extremes} On $X=\mathbb P^1$ with marks $0,1,\infty$, use coordinates $z,z-1,1/z$ respectively. The one-weight extremal disc at $0$ is $\mathbb C\setminus[1,\infty)$, with radius $4$. For equal weights at $0,1$ and zero weight at $\infty$, the extremal discs are the half-planes $\operatorname{Re}z<1/2$ and $\operatorname{Re}z>1/2$, both of radius $1$. Thus every finite canonical cap system satisfies $r_0r_1<1$, although the individual supremum of each of these radii is $4$. Its image is therefore not a box. The limiting disc at $0$ is the slit domain when $\lambda_0\to\infty$ with the others bounded; it is the indicated half-plane when $\lambda_0=\lambda_1\to\infty$ and $\lambda_\infty$ stays bounded.

\label{C:A2e-nonmonotonicity} Let $(X,h)$ be any compact connected hyperbolic surface with nonempty geodesic boundary and negative Euler characteristic. There are arbitrarily thin open collars of its boundary, with real-analytic inner boundaries, such that the remaining surface $X_t$ is diffeomorphic to $X$ but its canonical curvature $-1$ metric $h_t'$ with geodesic boundary is neither pointwise greater than nor pointwise less than $h|_{X_t}$. More precisely, their conformal ratio satisfies \[ h_t'=e^{2u_t}h|_{X_t}, \qquad \min_{X_t}u_t<0<\max_{X_t}u_t. \] This includes every compact hyperbolic pair of pants and every compact one-holed torus. The new boundaries can converge to the original ones in $C^m$ for every fixed $m$.

\label{A:octahedron} Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field with $\operatorname{char}k\ne2$, let $G=\operatorname{PGL}_2(k)$, and choose $i\in k$ with $i^2=-1$. Put \[ V=\{z\mapsto z,\ z\mapsto-z,\ z\mapsto1/z,\ z\mapsto-1/z\}, \qquad S=\{0,\infty,1,-1,i,-i\}. \] Every Klein four-subgroup of $G$ is conjugate to $V$. Its normalizer has order~24 and is isomorphic to $\mathfrak S_4$. The assignments $V'\mapsto N_G(V')$ and $\Gamma\mapsto$ its normal Klein four-subgroup give inverse bijections between Klein four-subgroups and subgroups isomorphic to $\mathfrak S_4$, in every characteristic different from~2. The assignment taking $V'$ to the union of the fixed points of its three nonidentity elements is a bijection onto the projective translates of $S$ if and only if $\operatorname{char}k\ne5$. In characteristic~5 it is five-to-one, and the stabilizer of $S$ has order~120.

\label{A:fourpoint-groupoid} Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic different from~2. For a four-element set $I$, let $V(I)$ be its canonical Klein group of double transpositions and let $J(I)=V(I)\setminus\{1\}$. Let $Z(J)$ be the projective line with its three labelled distinct points indexed by $J$, and write $Z(J)^*$ for the complement of those points. There is an equivalence between the groupoid of four-point curves $(X,I\hookrightarrow X)$, with bijections of $I$ allowed, and the groupoid of $(I,\zeta)$ with $\zeta\in Z(J(I))^*$. This remains true in characteristic~5. The construction retains $V(I)$ and does not attempt to recover it from a bare six-point set.

\label{A:unordered-stack} Put $R=\mathbb Z[1/2,i]$, and $U=\operatorname{Spec}R[\lambda,\lambda^{-1},(1-\lambda)^{-1}]$. The stack of genus-zero curves with an unordered finite \'etale degree-four divisor is \[ \mathcal M_{0,[4],R}\simeq[U/\mathfrak S_4], \qquad \mathfrak S_4\longrightarrow\mathfrak S_3 =\operatorname{Aut}\{0,1,\infty\}. \] The action factors through the displayed quotient and has kernel $V_4$. Its coarse quotient is \[ \operatorname{Spec}R[j],\qquad j=256\frac{(\lambda^2-\lambda+1)^3} {\lambda^2(1-\lambda)^2}. \] Consequently Lead L7 is correct as a statement about the unordered moduli stack, together with its coarse space, but a groupoid of unordered four-point curves is not represented by the scheme $\mathbb A^1_R$. The stack description in fact descends to $\mathbb Z$; adjoining $i$ and inverting~2 are needed only for the specified octahedral presentation.

\label{A:inertia-maximality} Conjugacy classes of all closed subgroups isomorphic to $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$, externally invariant under the arithmetic Galois group and acted on cyclotomically, cannot be in bijection with the finite set of nodes and marked points of a stable curve. This is false even for the smoothing fundamental group of the split stable four-pointed genus-zero curve consisting of two three-pointed lines. For a smooth hyperbolic curve over a field with non-Tate $\ell$-adic cyclotomic character, a correct cuspidal criterion uses \emph{maximal} closed procyclic cyclotomically normalized subgroups with nonzero $\ell$-primary part. It identifies the cusps, not every possible nonperipheral cutting curve.

\label{A:three-types} For an oriented surface $S_{g,n}$, the geometric kinds of nontrivial simple closed curve are peripheral, nonseparating, and separating nonperipheral. Some kinds may be absent. Within the separating kind, the mapping class orbit is specified by the genera and puncture sets on the two sides, up to exchanging the sides. Within the peripheral kind, a pure mapping class orbit specifies the puncture. These kinds are not three conjugacy classes in a fundamental group, nor three conjugacy classes of homomorphisms $\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)\to\pi_1$.

\label{A:ordinary-nodal-loss} Let $Y$ be the proper split stable four-pointed genus-zero curve in Proposition~\ref{A:inertia-maximality}. Its ordinary geometric \'etale fundamental group is trivial. Removing its four external marks gives a free profinite group of rank~2. A smooth four-punctured genus-zero fibre has free profinite group of rank~3. Thus neither ordinary group can serve as the smoothing group in 67/048.

\label{A:log-graphicity} For stable log curves over an algebraically closed standard log point, an isomorphism of their geometric pro-$\Sigma$ groups that intertwines their logarithmic inertia actions and preserves the cuspidal inertia classes induces an isomorphism of the graphs of groups. This includes recovery of the vertices, nodes, cusps, and incidence relations. For curves without cusps the cuspidal condition is empty. More generally, for the outer representations of Hoshi--Mochizuki's Definition~2.4(iii), the same conclusion holds under their NN hypothesis, nonempty cusp set, and group-theoretic cuspidality.

\label{A:tensor-log-comparison} Let $(Y,D)$ be a stable pointed curve over a characteristic-zero field $K$. At a geometric node $e$, write $e^+,e^-$ for its two normalization branches and $L_e=T_{e^+}\widetilde Y\otimes T_{e^-}\widetilde Y$. A Galois-equivariant collection $N_e\in L_e\setminus\{0\}$ defines a stable log curve $Y_N^{\log}\to S_K^{\log}$, with thickness one at every node, and hence an outer action \[ \rho_N:G_K\longrightarrow\operatorname{Out}(\Delta_N),\qquad \Delta_N=\pi_1^{\log}(Y_N^{\log}/\overline S_K^{\log}). \] Here $\rho_N$ is the restriction along $s_t$ of the logarithmic base action. Its geometric group is the profinite fundamental group of a smooth surface of the same type as $(Y,D)$. Over $\mathbb C$ it is the profinite completion of the topological surface obtained by gluing the oriented real boundary circles at the nodes using the phases of $N_e$. The construction depends only on $(Y,D,N)$, not on higher order plumbing coordinates or a choice of smoothing family. After a finite extension splitting the nodes, take two tensor systems $N,N'$ on the same $Y$, and put $\delta_e=N'_e/N_e\in K^\times$. Identify their geometric groups and graphs by choosing compatible roots $\delta_e^{1/n}$ in $\overline K$. In the Dehn-twist coordinates of Hoshi and Mochizuki (2012), Theorem~4.8, the difference of the two outer actions is \begin{equation}\label{A:node-Kummer-action} \rho_{N'}(g)=T^{\kappa(\delta)(g)}\rho_N(g),\qquad \kappa(\delta_e)(g)= \bigl(g(\delta_e^{1/n})/\delta_e^{1/n}\bigr)_n \in\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1). \end{equation} The orientation of each twist is chosen to agree with the Kummer inertia of its smoothing coordinate.

\label{A:Kummer-faithfulness} If $K$ is finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$, the Kummer map \[ K^\times\longrightarrow H^1(G_K,\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)) \] is injective, and $\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)^{G_K}=0$.

\label{A:tangential-anabelian} Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$. Let $(Y,D,N)$ and $(Y',D',N')$ be geometrically connected stable pointed curves of hyperbolic type with a nonzero tensor at every node, and use the tangential groups of Lemma~\ref{A:tensor-log-comparison}. The natural map \[ \operatorname{Isom}_K((Y,D,N),(Y',D',N')) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Isom}_{G_K}^{\mathrm{out}} ((\Delta_N,\rho_N),(\Delta_{N'},\rho_{N'})) \] is a bijection. On the right, isomorphisms are continuous and considered modulo geometric inner automorphisms. If markings are labelled, require their peripheral conjugacy classes to match their labels. In particular the arithmetic outer action recovers the curve, its node and cusp incidence, and the actual nonzero tensors, rather than only their orders or their classes modulo powers.

\label{A:compactification-obstruction} Even for a known smooth anabelian surface over $\mathbb Q$, its arithmetic fundamental group does not determine an arbitrary chosen smooth projective compactification with simple normal crossings boundary. In particular such compactifications cannot form a category on which the functor assigning only the fundamental group of the interior is fully faithful on isomorphisms.

\label{A:polystable-compactification} Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$. Consider strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods $U/K$ that admit a hyperbolic-curve tower whose stages are split and saturated in the sense of Mochizuki (1999, \emph{Extending families}), Definitions~7.2--7.3. In characteristic zero it suffices that the punctures of each stage are disjoint sections and its proper smooth curve admits a full level-$\ell$ structure for some prime $\ell\ge3$. Then $U$ has a canonical proper log-polystable compactification $X_U^{\log}$, independent of the choice of a tower. Moreover \[ \operatorname{Isom}_K(X_U^{\log},X_V^{\log}) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \operatorname{Isom}^{\mathrm{out}}_{G_K} (\pi_1(U),\pi_1(V)). \] Here the arithmetic groups retain their augmentations to $G_K$, and the outer quotient is by the geometric inner automorphisms. The statement includes $U=(\mathbb P^1_K\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^d$ for every $d\ge1$.

\label{A:polycurve-coarse-compactification} Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $U/K$ be a geometrically connected hyperbolic polycurve: $U$ admits a finite tower of hyperbolic curves, in the sense of Mochizuki (1999), Definition~4.6. No splitness or level structure is assumed. There is a canonical normal projective pair $(\overline U,U)$ over $K$, obtained by the following procedure: \begin{enumerate} \item Choose a connected finite \'etale cover $V\to U$ which, over a finite extension $K'/K$, has a split saturated hyperbolic curve tower. Let $(X_V,V)$ be its polystable compactification. \item Choose a connected finite \'etale Galois cover $W\to U$ dominating $V$, and normalize $X_V$ in $K(W)$, obtaining $Z$. \item Extend $G=\operatorname{Gal}(W/U)$ to $Z$ and set $\overline U=Z/G$. \end{enumerate} The resulting pair is independent, up to the unique isomorphism which is the identity on $U$, of all covers, towers, and field extensions in the procedure. Every $K$-isomorphism $U\simeq U'$ extends uniquely to an isomorphism of these pairs. If $U$ already has a polystable compactification, this procedure returns it. For $K$ finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$ and $U,U'$ strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods, consequently \[ \operatorname{Isom}_K\bigl((\overline U,U),(\overline {U'},U')\bigr) \simeq \operatorname{Isom}^{\mathrm{out}}_{G_K} \bigl(\pi_1(U),\pi_1(U')\bigr). \] The right side retains the augmentations to $G_K$, with geometric inner automorphisms divided out. The normal coarse boundary is not asserted to be log regular; the log-regular normalization $Z$ is retained whenever a log specialization theorem is applied.

\label{A:intrinsic-anabelian-compactification} The normal compactification of Theorem~\ref{A:polycurve-coarse-compactification} satisfies Definition~\ref{A:anabelian-compactification-definition}. For an arbitrary smooth $U/K$, a compactification satisfying that definition is unique if it exists. Every $K$-morphism between two interiors having such compactifications extends uniquely to their compactifications. In particular arithmetic isomorphism reconstruction of an interior implies arithmetic isomorphism reconstruction of this pair, without retaining any auxiliary cover.

\label{A:polycurve-four-dimensional-anabelian} Let $p$ be a prime and let $K$ be a sub-$p$-adic field: that is, $K$ embeds into a finitely generated extension of $\mathbb Q_p$. Let $U,U'$ be geometrically connected hyperbolic polycurves over $K$, and suppose that $\min\{\dim U,\dim U'\}\leq4$. Write $\Pi_U=\pi_1^{\mathrm{\acute et}}(U)$ and $\Delta_U=\ker(\Pi_U\to G_K)$, and similarly for $U'$. For their canonical normal projective compactifications from Theorem~\ref{A:polycurve-coarse-compactification}, the natural map \[ \operatorname{Isom}_K\bigl((\overline U,U), (\overline {U'},U')\bigr) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Isom}_{G_K}(\Pi_U,\Pi_{U'})/ \operatorname{Inn}(\Delta_{U'}) \] is bijective. In particular every prescribed geometric-inner class of an augmentation-preserving arithmetic group isomorphism is realized by one and only one isomorphism of compactified pairs. No chosen tower, split marking, level structure, saturation, or strongly hyperbolic Artin hypothesis is imposed on these interiors.

\label{A:canonical-log-model-product} For $U=(\mathbb P^1_K\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$, let $(Z,E)$ be any smooth projective compactification with reduced simple normal crossings boundary. The graded ring \[ R(U)=\bigoplus_{m\ge0}H^0(Z,\omega_Z^{\otimes m}(mE)) \] is independent of this choice, under the natural identification as rational pluricanonical forms on $U$, and \[ \operatorname{Proj}R(U)\simeq\mathbb P^1_K\times\mathbb P^1_K. \] Thus the arithmetic interior group recovers this canonical log model, although it does not recover an arbitrary chosen blowup.

\label{A:log-specialization-higher} Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field $F$, residue characteristic $p\ge0$, and its standard divisorial log structure. Let $\mathcal X^{\log}\to(\operatorname{Spec}R)^{\log}$ be proper and log smooth, with fine saturated log structures and geometrically connected generic fibre, and let $U$ be its trivial-log locus. Write $s^{\log}$ for the induced log special point. There is a Galois-compatible equivalence \[ \operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(U_{\bar F})^{(p')} \simeq \operatorname{KCov}_{\mathrm{geom}} (\mathcal X_s^{\log}/s^{\log})^{(p')}, \] and thus an outer isomorphism of the corresponding fundamental groups. Superscript $(p')$ means finite quotients of order prime to $p$; if $p=0$, all finite quotients are retained. The right side uses log-geometric covers, obtained after all finite Kummer extensions of the base log point, not ordinary covers of the underlying singular special fibre.

\label{A:SL-GL-presentations} The manuscript's presentations, with the involution relations made explicit, are \[ \operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z) =\langle\sigma,\rho\mid\sigma^2=\rho^3,\ \rho^6=1\rangle \] and \[ \operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb Z) =\langle r_1,r_2,r_3\mid r_1^2=r_2^2=r_3^2=1,\ (r_1r_2)^2=(r_2r_3)^3,\ (r_1r_2)^4=1\rangle. \] In the second presentation all three generators reverse orientation.

\label{A:four-puncture-MCG} Let $V=(\mathbb Z/2)^2$ and $\Gamma(2)=\ker(\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\to \operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb F_2))$. Then \[ \operatorname{Mod}_{0,4}\simeq V\rtimes\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z),\qquad \operatorname{PMod}_{0,4}\simeq \Gamma(2)/\{\pm I\}\simeq F_2. \] The quotient of $\operatorname{Mod}_{0,4}$ by $V$, and also the subgroup fixing one distinguished puncture, are each isomorphic to $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)$. The two exact rows are \[ 1\longrightarrow F_2\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}_{0,4} \longrightarrow\mathfrak S_4\longrightarrow1, \] \[ 1\longrightarrow F_2\longrightarrow\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z) \longrightarrow\mathfrak S_3\longrightarrow1. \] The map between their finite quotients is $\mathfrak S_4\to\mathfrak S_4/V\simeq\mathfrak S_3$. In particular $\operatorname{PMod}_{0,4}$ is not $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)$.

\label{A:Birman} Let $S$ be an oriented surface of finite type with $\chi(S)<0$, and let $p$ be a newly distinguished point in its interior. Then \[ 1\longrightarrow\pi_1(S,p)\stackrel{\mathrm{Push}}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Mod}(S,p)\stackrel{\mathrm{Forget}}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Mod}(S)\longrightarrow1 \] is exact. The new point must be preserved, even when the other punctures may be permuted. The unrestricted assertion without $\chi(S)<0$ is false; for the closed torus the forgetful map $\operatorname{Mod}_{1,1}\to\operatorname{Mod}_{1,0}$ is an isomorphism and the point-pushing map from $\mathbb Z^2$ is zero.

\label{A:reflection-generators} For an oriented closed surface with finitely many marked points, the extended mapping class group has a finite generating set consisting of orientation-reversing involutions. It therefore has a finite presentation on such generators. This assertion concerns marked points; it is not asserted for a group required to fix a nonempty boundary pointwise.

\label{A:arithmetic-quilts} For every stable type $2g-2+n>0$, the profinite Teichm\"uller groupoids with the above tangential objects admit the natural $G_{\mathbb Q}$ action in pants/quilt coordinates. Fusing moves are controlled by the action on $\mathcal M_{0,4}$, simple moves by the elliptic moduli problem with a nonzero tangent vector, and local Dehn twists and half-twists by the cyclotomic character. The relations are the usual topological quilt relations, with changes of base object and stabilizers retained. At a fixed quilt this gives a lift to automorphisms of the profinite pure mapping class group; at each Galois element a different quilt changes that automorphism by a specified inner factor. The factor may depend on the Galois element: the assertion is equality of the outer actions, not conjugacy of the two entire representations by one fixed inner automorphism. The resulting outer action is compatible with inclusion of quilted subsurfaces and with filling boundary circles by marked discs.

\label{A:real-Galois-obstruction} Let $U=\mathcal M_{0,4}=\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\setminus \{0,1,\infty\}$, choose the rational base point $2$, and set \[ \Delta=\pi_1(U_{\overline{\mathbb Q}},2)\simeq\widehat F_2. \] Fix an embedding $\overline{\mathbb Q}\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$, write $c$ for its complex conjugation, and let $H_c=\Delta\rtimes\langle c\rangle$, using the action supplied by the base point. This is the arithmetic fundamental group over the chosen real closure, and is the profinite completion of the corresponding extended pure four-point mapping class group. An element $\sigma\in G_{\mathbb Q}$ has its natural outer action on $\Delta$ induced by an automorphism of $H_c$ preserving $\Delta$ if and only if $\sigma\in\{1,c\}$. Thus the whole $G_{\mathbb Q}$ action cannot be extended to this single fixed real extended group with the indicated compatibility. There is instead a canonical outer action on the family $\{H_{\sigma c\sigma^{-1}}\}_{\sigma\in G_{\mathbb Q}}$ by isomorphisms between its members. With the chosen rational base point this action can be made strict inside $\Delta\rtimes G_{\mathbb Q}$.

\label{A:real-elliptic} Every elliptic curve over $\mathbb R$, with its origin, is isomorphic over $\mathbb R$ to exactly one member of the following two disjoint families, with complex conjugation as real structure: \[ E_a(\mathbb C)=\mathbb C/(\mathbb Z+i\sqrt a\,\mathbb Z), \qquad E'_a(\mathbb C)=\mathbb C/ \bigl(\mathbb Z+\tfrac{1+i\sqrt a}{2}\mathbb Z\bigr), \qquad a>0. \] For a fixed complex elliptic curve admitting a real structure, there are two real forms. Except for the square lattice, they are either $\{E_a,E_{1/a}\}$ or $\{E'_a,E'_{1/a}\}$ with $a>1$. For the square lattice they are $E_1$ and $E'_1$. For the hexagonal lattice they are $E'_3$ and $E'_{1/3}$. The corresponding modular functions are \[ j(E_a)=j(i\sqrt a),\qquad j(E'_a)=j\bigl((1+i\sqrt a)/2\bigr). \] In each family $j(a)=j(1/a)$. In particular the guess $j=c\log a$ on 67/097 is false for every constant $c$.

\label{A:pid-involutions} Let $k$ be a principal ideal domain of characteristic different from~2 such that $k_0=k/2k$ is a field. Conjugacy classes of $\sigma\in\operatorname{GL}_2(k)$ with $\sigma^2=1$ and $\sigma\ne\pm1$ consist of one split class and a collection of nonsplit classes indexed by \[ k_0^\times/\operatorname{im}(k^\times\longrightarrow k_0^\times). \] There are exactly two classes if and only if the unit map is surjective. For $k=\mathbb Z[(1+\sqrt{-11})/2]$ there are four classes in total: one split and three nonsplit. Thus the struck unit-surjectivity proviso on 67/100 is necessary.

\label{A:eigenmodule-correction} The attached correction R5, which adds connectedness of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to the rank-two projective corollary on 67/091, is insufficient. Even for a connected commutative 2-torsion-free ring, the positive and negative eigenspaces of a nontrivial involution on a free rank-two module need not be invertible modules. The corollary is valid over a PID, as in Proposition~\ref{A:pid-involutions}; it is also valid over a connected ring with $2$ invertible, provided the involution is neither $1$ nor $-1$.

\label{A:real-topology} For every $a>0$, \[ E_a(\mathbb R)\simeq (\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z, \qquad E'_a(\mathbb R)\simeq\mathbb R/\mathbb Z, \] as compact real Lie groups. Moreover \[ H^1(\mathbb R,E_a)\simeq\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z, \qquad H^1(\mathbb R,E'_a)=0. \] The quotient Klein surfaces of the two elliptic groups are respectively an annulus and a M\"obius band. The unique nonzero torsor under $E_a$ has no real points; its complex curve modulo its real structure is a Klein bottle, a surface without boundary. Thus the deletion of ``sans'' on 67/101 must be reversed.

\label{B:betti} Let $X$ be a smooth projective connected complex variety of complex dimension $4$. For every $z\in\mathrm{CH}^2(X)_{\mathbb Q}$, numerical triviality is equivalent to $\operatorname{cl}_B(z)=0$ in $H^4(X,\mathbb Q)$. Here numerical triviality is tested against every $w\in\mathrm{CH}^2(X)_{\mathbb Q}$.

\label{B:num-basechange} Let $X$ be smooth projective over a field $k$, let $K/k$ be an extension, and let $z\in\mathrm{CH}^r(X)_{\mathbb Q}$. Then $z$ is numerically trivial over $k$ if and only if its flat pullback $z_K$ is numerically trivial over $K$.

\label{B:charzero} Let $k$ be any field of characteristic $0$, $X/k$ smooth projective and geometrically connected of dimension $4$, and $\ell$ any prime. For $z\in\mathrm{CH}^2(X)_{\mathbb Q}$, \[ z\equiv_{\mathrm{num}}0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{cl}_\ell(z)=0\text{ in }H^4_{\acute et}(X_{\bar k},\mathbb Q_\ell(2)). \] For a smooth projective variety without geometric connectedness the same conclusion holds componentwise after a finite extension, and descends by trace.

\label{B:ancona-scope} Ancona's Theorem~1.3 proves positivity for primitive classes \emph{modulo numerical equivalence}. Its combination with the Lefschetz standard conjecture alone does not give the asserted all-primes homological--numerical comparison. The conclusion stated in Ancona's Theorem~1.6 is comparison for infinitely many primes. This is a correction to the proposed proof, not a counterexample to standard conjecture~$D$.

\label{B:abelian} Let $A$ be an abelian variety of dimension $4$ over any field $k$ and let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Then numerical and $\ell$-adic homological equivalence agree on rational cycles on $A$, in particular on its $2$-cycles. This conclusion uses Broe's 2026 preprint, not only the sources remembered in the prompt.

\label{B:criterion} Fix a Weil cohomology theory and let $X$ be a smooth projective fourfold. Suppose its rational algebraic cohomology in degree four admits the algebraic orthogonal Lefschetz decomposition \[ A^2(X)=\mathbb Qh^2\oplus L A^1_{\mathrm{prim}}(X)\oplus A^2_{\mathrm{prim}}(X), \] and suppose the divisor summand has the usual nondegenerate Hodge index form. Assume also that the primitive intersection form is positive semidefinite. Then numerical and homological equivalence agree in codimension two if and only if the primitive form is positive definite. In particular, the argument applies whenever the Lefschetz standard conjecture and the Hodge standard conjecture \emph{on homological algebraic classes} both hold. More explicitly, the \emph{class of applicability of the positivity argument} is the class $\mathscr C_H$ of polarized fourfolds with the displayed algebraic decomposition, nondegenerate divisor block and positive definite primitive block. Within the stated semidefinite setting, membership in $\mathscr C_H$ is necessary and sufficient for this argument to prove the comparison. This class includes all characteristic-zero fourfolds for Betti and $\ell$-adic cohomology, all abelian fourfolds using Theorem~\ref{B:abelian}, and smooth projective fourfolds admitting a finite surjective morphism from an abelian fourfold. This determines applicability of the argument; it is not a claim that varieties outside it fail standard conjecture~$D$. Independently of a positivity formulation, $\ell$-adic comparison in codimension two holds for every smooth projective fourfold $X$ admitting a dominant generically finite morphism $f:A\to X$ from an abelian fourfold, for every prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$.

\label{B:tau} The original image of cote~66, scan~4, reads $\tau$-equivalence; this is the standard relation defined in Kleiman \cite[\S1.1, p.~362]{BKleiman1968}: a nonzero integer multiple is algebraically equivalent to zero. There is a smooth projective connected complex threefold $X$ and an integral one-cycle $z$ which is homologically, hence numerically, trivial, but for which $mz$ is not algebraically trivial for any integer $m\ne0$.

\label{B:trace} Let $S$ be a smooth projective complex surface and $\omega\in H^0(S,\Omega_S^2)$. If $T$ is a smooth irreducible complex variety and $F,G:T\to\operatorname{Sym}^n S$ are morphisms whose effective zero-cycles $F(t),G(t)$ are rationally equivalent for every $t\in T(\mathbb C)$, then their induced trace forms satisfy $\omega_F=\omega_G\in H^0(T,\Omega_T^2)$.

\label{B:square} Let $E/\mathbb C$ be the elliptic curve $y^2=x^3-x$, with origin $O$ at infinity, and put $S=E\times E$. Choose $u,v\in\mathbb C$ algebraically independent over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, choose roots $a^2=u^3-u$ and $b^2=v^3-v$, and set $P=(u,a)$, $Q=(v,b)$. Then \[ z=[(P,Q)]-[(P,O)]-[(O,Q)]+[(O,O)]\in\mathrm{CH}_0(S) \] has infinite order and lies in the Albanese kernel. The divisor \[ D=\operatorname{pr}_1^*([P]-[O])+\operatorname{pr}_2^*([Q]-[O])\in\mathrm{CH}^1(S) \] is algebraically trivial, but $D^2=2z\ne0$ in $\mathrm{CH}_0(S)$.

\label{B:alb-kernel} For any complex elliptic curve $E$, the Albanese kernel $T(E\times E)$ is generated, as an abelian group, by the exterior products \[ ([P]-[O])\times([Q]-[O]) \quad (P,Q\in E(\mathbb C)). \] Equivalently, the product map from $\mathrm{CH}_0(E)^0\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathrm{CH}_0(E)^0$ onto $T(E\times E)$ is surjective. Products of algebraically trivial cycles are algebraically, and thus homologically and numerically, trivial; rational triviality is the false additional conclusion in question~25.

\label{B:henselian} Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subset A$ an ideal, with $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair; \item $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal F|_Z)$ is bijective for every sheaf of sets on $X_{\acute et}$. \end{enumerate} Under these equivalent conditions, for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ and every integer $q\ge0$, restriction is an isomorphism \[ H^q_{\acute et}(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^q_{\acute et}(Z,\mathcal F|_Z). \] No noetherian hypothesis or invertibility of the torsion orders is needed. In particular the assertion holds if $A\simeq\varprojlim_n A/I^n$, and for the henselization $A^h$ of $A$ along $I$.

\label{B:henselian-general} Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion. The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $H^0(X,\mathcal F)\to H^0(Z,i^*\mathcal F)$ is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$; \item for every finite $X$-scheme $X'$, restriction induces a bijection between the clopen subsets of $X'$ and those of $X'\times_X Z$. \end{enumerate} Condition~(2) is the geometric definition of a \emph{henselian pair} $(X,Z)$. If these conditions hold, then \[ \bigl(B,J\bigr)=\bigl(\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X), \ker[\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)]\bigr) \] is a henselian ring pair. If, additionally, $X$ is proper over a noetherian ring $A$ and $Z=X\times_A A/I$ for some ideal $I\subset A$, the comparison is an isomorphism in every degree for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf on $X$.

\label{B:H1-gate} Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be any closed immersion of schemes, and let $j:U=X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ be its complement. Assume that $H^0(X,\mathcal F)\to H^0(Z,i^*\mathcal F)$ is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$. Then restriction is fully faithful on finite \'etale covers and is injective on the nonabelian pointed sets $H^1(X,G)\to H^1(Z,i^*G)$ for every \'etale sheaf of groups $G$. Moreover the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item restriction is an isomorphism in every degree for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf on $X$; \item $H^q(X,j_!\mathcal G)=0$ for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $U$ and every $q\ge2$. \end{enumerate} The analogous vanishings in degrees zero and one already follow from the hypothesis. In particular the full torsion comparison holds whenever the torsion \'etale cohomological dimension of $X$ is at most one. None of these assertions needs quasi-compactness.

\label{C:torsion-degree-two-reduction} Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion, and let $j:U=X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ be its open complement. Assume that \[ H^0(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^0(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F) \] is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on $X$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $H^2(X,j_!\mathcal G)=0$ for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $U$. \item For every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$, restriction on $H^1$ is surjective, and hence bijective. \item For every finite morphism $f:Y\to X$, every prime $\ell$, and every integer $\nu>0$, every torsor under the constant group $\mathbb Z/\ell^\nu\mathbb Z$ on $Y\times_XZ$ is the restriction of such a torsor on $Y$. \end{enumerate} In condition~(3), it suffices to test finite morphisms of finite presentation. If these conditions hold, restriction on $H^2$ is injective for every torsion abelian sheaf on $X$.

\label{C:henselian-flat-trait-proper} Let $R$ be a henselian discrete valuation ring, with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, generic point $\eta$ and closed point $s$. Let $X$ be a flat separated scheme of finite type over $R$. Assume that restriction \[ H^0(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^0(X_s,\mathcal F|_{X_s}) \] is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on $X$. Then $X$ is proper over $R$. Neither excellence nor completeness of $R$ is required. The same conclusion holds under the weaker hypothesis that every closed point of $X$ lies in $X_s$.

\label{C:henselian-trait-comparison} Let $R$ be a henselian discrete valuation ring, let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $R$, and put $Z=X_s$. Assume the universal degree-zero comparison for $(X,Z)$. Then, for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ and every $q\ge0$, \[ H^q(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F). \] No flatness or properness hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

\label{C:henselian-proper-closed-fibre} Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian ring pair and let $X$ be separated and of finite type over $A$. Put $Z=X\times_A A/I$. If $Z$ is proper over $A/I$ and $(X,Z)$ satisfies the universal degree-zero comparison, then $X$ is proper over $A$. If $A$ is noetherian, the all-degree torsion comparison of Theorem~\ref{B:henselian-general} follows.

\label{B:henselian-local-flat-proper} Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a henselian noetherian local ring with $\dim R>0$. Let $X$ be flat, separated and of finite type over $R$. If every point closed in $X$ belongs to the closed fibre $X_k$, then $X$ is proper over $R$. In particular, universal degree-zero comparison for $(X,X_k)$ implies properness and, for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ and every $q\geq0$, \[ H^q(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim} H^q(X_k,\mathcal F|_{X_k}). \] No excellence, Nagata, reducedness, irreducibility, completeness, or dimension-one hypothesis is imposed on $R$.

\label{C:local-curve-avoidance} Let $(A,\mathfrak n)$ be a noetherian local domain and let $0\ne a\in\mathfrak n$. There is a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ such that $a\notin\mathfrak p$ and $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)=1$.

\label{C:henselian-horizontal-proper} Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian ring pair with $A$ noetherian. Let $X$ be an integral separated scheme of finite type over $A$, whose generic point lies outside $X_I=X\times_A A/I$. If every point closed in $X$ belongs to $X_I$, then $X$ is proper over $A$. Locality of $A$, flatness, catenarity, excellence, normality, and a finite normalization hypothesis are not required.

\label{C:henselian-noetherian-pair-comparison} Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian ring pair with $A$ noetherian, let $X$ be any separated scheme of finite type over $A$, and set $Z=X\times_A A/I$. Suppose every closed point of $X$ lies in $Z$.
