Then for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ and every $q\ge0$, \[ H^q(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim} H^q(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F). \] In particular this holds if $(X,Z)$ satisfies the universal degree-zero comparison for \'etale sheaves of sets. Neither flatness nor properness of $X$ is required. No locality, catenarity, excellence, completeness, or dimension hypothesis is imposed on $A$.

\label{C:henselian-noetherian-closedpoint-criterion} Let $(A,I)$ be a noetherian henselian ring pair, let $X$ be separated and of finite type over $A$, and put $Z=X\times_A A/I$. Then the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item every point closed in $X$ belongs to $Z$; \item restriction $H^0(X,\mathcal H)\to H^0(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal H)$ is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets $\mathcal H$. \end{enumerate} Either condition therefore gives the all-degree torsion comparison of Theorem~\ref{C:henselian-noetherian-pair-comparison}.

\label{C:Nagata-input} There are a normal local domain $(R,\mathfrak m)$, a nonzero $d\in\mathfrak m$, and $a,b\in\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ such that \[ R\text{ is henselian},\qquad R[1/d]=\operatorname{Frac}(R), \qquad ab=d, \qquad a,a^{-1},b,b^{-1}\notin R. \]

\label{C:Goldman-branches} For $R,d,a,b$ as in Lemma~\ref{C:Nagata-input}, there is a normal local domain $(B,\mathfrak n)$ containing $R[a,b]$ such that \[ B[1/d]=\operatorname{Frac}(B),\qquad d\in\mathfrak n, \] and two primes $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak n$ satisfy \[ b\in\mathfrak p,\quad a\notin\mathfrak p, \qquad a\in\mathfrak q,\quad b\notin\mathfrak q. \] In particular $V(d)\cap D(a+b)$ is nonempty and disconnected in $\operatorname{Spec}B$.

\label{C:subject21-torsion-counterexample} There exist a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $X$ and a principal closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ for which \[ H^0(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^0(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F) \quad\text{for every \'etale sheaf of sets }\mathcal F, \] but, for every integer $n>1$, \[ H^1(X,\underline{\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z})=0, \qquad H^1(Z,\underline{\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z})\ne0. \] In particular, degree-zero comparison for all \'etale sheaves of sets does not imply higher torsion comparison for arbitrary scheme pairs.

\label{C:henselian-affine-closed-fibre} Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be an affine closed subscheme. Suppose that \[ H^0(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^0(Z,i^{-1}\mathcal F) \] is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets on $X$. Then $X$ is affine. Consequently restriction induces an isomorphism on $H^q$ for every $q\ge0$ and every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf on $X$. No quasi-compactness, noetherianity, or finite-presentation assumption on the original pair is required beyond the stated quasi-separatedness of $X$ and affineness of $Z$.

\label{B:henselized-affine-cover} Let $X$ be qcqs, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed, and assume universal degree-zero comparison for every \'etale sheaf of sets. Choose finitely many affine open subschemes $U_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ whose union contains $Z$, and write $Z\cap U_a=\operatorname{Spec}(A_a/I_a)$. Then \[ W=\coprod_a\operatorname{Spec}(A_a)^h_{I_a}\longrightarrow X \] is an fpqc cover and a $v$-cover, with each displayed affine term a henselian pair along its inverse image of $Z$. Torsion \'etale cohomology satisfies descent along this cover. This statement does not assert that its \v Cech intersections are henselian pairs.

\label{B:henselized-Cech-obstruction} Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field and put \[ A=k[[x,t]],\qquad X=\operatorname{Spec}A,\qquad Z=V(t), \qquad B=(A[1/x])^h_{(t)}. \] The affine henselian pair $(X,Z)$ has universal degree-zero comparison. Nevertheless, with $C=B\otimes_A B$, the map \[ H^0(\operatorname{Spec}C,\{0,1\})\longrightarrow H^0(\operatorname{Spec}(C/tC),\{0,1\}) \] is not injective. Thus a \v Cech self-intersection in the henselization cover associated with $\{X,D(x)\}$ fails even the degree-zero hypothesis. Henselizing that intersection along $t$ does not produce an arc-cover of the original intersection. This refutes an automatic termwise descent argument, not torsion comparison for general henselian scheme pairs.

\label{B:constant-integer-rigidity} Set \[ f=y^2-x^2(x+1),\qquad A=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\mathbb C[x,y]/(f^n),\qquad X=\operatorname{Spec}A,\quad Z=V(f)\subset X. \] Then $(A,fA)$ is a noetherian henselian pair, $X$ is regular and integral, and restriction on $H^0$ is bijective for every \'etale sheaf of sets. Nevertheless, for the constant abelian sheaf $\underline{\mathbb Z}$, \[ H^1_{\acute et}(X,\underline{\mathbb Z})=0, \qquad H^1_{\acute et}(Z,\underline{\mathbb Z})\simeq\mathbb Z. \] Thus the unrestricted-coefficient implication in subject~21 is false even for a constant, finitely generated, torsion-free coefficient group. For this very same pair, the comparison remains an isomorphism in all degrees for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf, by Theorem~\ref{B:henselian}.

\label{B:H0-counterexample} Even for an affine smooth complex scheme, an isomorphism in degree zero for a fixed torsion \'etale sheaf does not imply isomorphisms in higher degrees. Take $X=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[t,t^{-1}]$, $Z=\{t=1\}$ and $\mathcal F=\mu_n$ for any integer $n>1$.

\label{B:nontorsion-rigidity} Let $R=\mathbb C[[t]]$ and let $B=(R[x])^h_{(t)}$ be the henselization along the ideal $(t)$. Set $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $i:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(B/tB)\hookrightarrow X$, so $Z\simeq\mathbb A^1_{\mathbb C}$. Restriction is bijective on $H^0$ for every \'etale sheaf of sets on $X$. Nevertheless, for the additive \'etale structure sheaf $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, \[ H^1_{\acute et}(X,\mathcal F)=0, \qquad H^1_{\acute et}(Z,i^*\mathcal F)\ne0. \] Here $i^*\mathcal F$ means inverse image as an abelian \'etale sheaf, not the tensor-product structure sheaf $\mathcal O_Z$. Thus the literally unrestricted-sheaf reading of subject~21 is false, even for an affine henselian pair satisfying its strongest degree-zero hypothesis. The torsion theorem remains the valid replacement.

\label{B:Fujiwara} Let $(R,I)$ be a henselian pair, with $I$ finitely generated, let $\widehat R=\varprojlim R/I^n$, and put $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus V(I)$ and $\widehat U=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat R\setminus V(I\widehat R)$. For every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $U$, pullback induces a quasi-isomorphism \[ R\Gamma(U,\mathcal G)\simeq R\Gamma(\widehat U,\mathcal G|_{\widehat U}). \] This is the Fujiwara--Gabber punctured comparison. It is distinct from comparing an affine scheme with its closed fibre in Theorem~\ref{B:henselian}.

\label{B:specialization} Let $k=\overline{\mathbb F}_5$, $R=k[[t]]$, and let $\mathcal E/R$ be the projective Weierstrass curve with equation \[ y^2z=x^3+t xz^2+z^3. \] It is smooth and proper with geometrically connected fibres. If $\bar\eta$ is a geometric generic point and $0$ the closed point, then \[ \dim_{\mathbb F_5}H^1_{\acute et}(\mathcal E_{\bar\eta},\mathbb F_5)=1, \qquad \dim_{\mathbb F_5}H^1_{\acute et}(\mathcal E_0,\mathbb F_5)=0. \] Thus the specialization homomorphism of full \'etale fundamental groups cannot be an isomorphism. The general valid replacement for a smooth proper family with geometrically connected fibres is surjectivity, with an isomorphism on maximal prime-to-$p$ quotients when the specialization has residue characteristic $p$.

\label{B:p-Euler} In characteristic $5$, the compactly supported Euler characteristic with constant $\mathbb F_5$ coefficients is not determined by the genus alone, even for smooth projective curves. Explicitly, over $\overline{\mathbb F}_5$, \[ E_{\mathrm{ord}}:y^2=x^3-x, \qquad E_{\mathrm{ss}}:y^2=x^3+1 \] have genus $1$, whereas $\chi(E_{\mathrm{ord}},\mathbb F_5)=0$ and $\chi(E_{\mathrm{ss}},\mathbb F_5)=1$. Thus one cannot answer subject 3 by replacing $\ell\ne p$ by $\ell=p$ in the usual genus-and-Swan formula without additional invariants or hypotheses.

\label{B:subject1} For a scheme $X$, an abelian sheaf $F$ on its small \'etale site, and every $q\ge0$, the canonical change-of-topology map gives \[ H^q_{\acute et}(X,F)\simeq H^q_{\mathrm{fppf}}(X,F_{\mathrm{fppf}}). \] Here $F_{\mathrm{fppf}}$ is the inverse-image sheaf on the big flat site; this is not an assertion about arbitrary flat sheaves. A precise crystalline companion is the following. Let $(A,I,\gamma)$ be a divided-power ring, $A$ noetherian and $p$-adically complete, with $p$ nilpotent in $A/I$. If $Y/A$ is proper smooth, $X=Y_{A/I}$, and $\mathcal E$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent crystal on $X/A$, then it determines a coherent module with integrable connection $(E_Y,\nabla)$ and \[ R\Gamma(\operatorname{Cris}(X/A),\mathcal E) \simeq R\Gamma(Y,E_Y\otimes\Omega^\bullet_{Y/A}). \]

\label{B:subject2} Let $K$ be a local function field of characteristic $p$, and $N/K$ a finite commutative group scheme with Cartier dual $N^D$. With the canonical locally compact topologies, cup product gives perfect Pontryagin pairings \[ H^r_{\mathrm{fppf}}(K,N^D)\times H^{2-r}_{\mathrm{fppf}}(K,N) \longrightarrow\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z. \] Let $C$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over a finite field and $N/C$ finite flat commutative. There are perfect pairings of finite groups \[ H^r_{\mathrm{fppf}}(C,N^D)\times H^{3-r}_{\mathrm{fppf}}(C,N) \longrightarrow\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z. \] For an open curve the second factor is compactly supported flat cohomology, with the topologies specified in the source.

\label{B:subject3} Let $X/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Let $\mathbb F$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, or a local field of residue characteristic $p$, and let $F$ be a constructible \'etale sheaf of finite-dimensional $\mathbb F$-vector spaces. Assume there is a finite irreducible Galois cover $Y\to X$ with $Y$ ordinary and the generic monodromy of the pullback of $F$ pro-$p$. Then \[ \chi(X,F)=(1-g_X)\operatorname{rank}F+ \sum_{x\in X(k)}\bigl(\dim F_x-\operatorname{LT}_x(F_{\bar\eta})\bigr). \] Here $\operatorname{LT}$ is Pink's local term, specified below. Without ordinariness there is no formula obtained merely by using the usual prime-to-$p$ genus term: Corollary~\ref{B:p-Euler} gives two genus-one counterexamples. Independently, a finite \'etale Galois cover $V\to U$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes with $p$-group Galois group satisfies \[ \chi_c(V,\mathbb Q_p)=(\deg V/U)\chi_c(U,\mathbb Q_p). \]

\label{B:subject4} Let $U$ be a connected smooth separated scheme of finite type over a perfect field $k$, and let $\ell$ be invertible in $k$. For a lisse $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$-sheaf $F$ there is a rational Swan zero-cycle class on the boundary, in the inverse limit of the Chow groups of compactification boundaries, such that \[ \chi_c(U_{\bar k},F)=\operatorname{rank}(F)\chi_c(U_{\bar k},\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell) -\deg\operatorname{Sw}(F). \] For a smooth curve its degree is the sum of the usual Swan conductors. In particular a finite \'etale cover $V\to X$ of degree $d$ of smooth proper $k$-schemes satisfies $\chi(V_{\bar k},\mathbb Q_\ell)=d\chi(X_{\bar k},\mathbb Q_\ell)$.

\label{B:subject5} Let $U$ be a smooth connected curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, let $C$ be its smooth projective completion, and let $A/U$ be an abelian scheme. Fix $\ell\ne p$ and a finite-dimensional semisimple $\mathbb Q$-algebra $R$ acting on $A$. Put $V=T_\ell(A)\otimes\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$. After decomposing the split algebra $R\otimes\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$, write \[ V=\bigoplus_\rho W_\rho\otimes M_\rho, \] where $W_\rho$ are its distinct simple modules and $M_\rho$ are lisse multiplicity sheaves. In its representation Grothendieck group, \[ \sum_i(-1)^i[H_c^i(U,V)] =\chi_c(U,\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell)[V_{\bar\eta}] -\sum_{x\in C\setminus U}\sum_\rho\operatorname{Sw}_x(M_\rho)[W_\rho]. \]

\label{B:subject6} For a separated finite-type $X/\mathbb F_q$, a constructible $\mathbb Q_\ell$-sheaf $F$ with $\ell\nmid q$, and geometric Frobenius $\Phi$, \[ \sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(\Phi\mid H_c^i(X_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q},F)) =\sum_{x\in X(\mathbb F_q)}\operatorname{Tr}(\Phi_x\mid F_{\bar x}). \] For a compact complex manifold $M$, a holomorphic $f:M\to M$ with only fixed points satisfying $\det_{\mathbb C}(1-df_x)\ne0$, a holomorphic vector bundle $E$ and a lift $u:f^*E\to E$, \[ \sum_q(-1)^q\operatorname{Tr}(f,u\mid H^q(M,E)) =\sum_{f(x)=x}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(u_x)}{\det_{\mathbb C}(1-df_x)}. \]

\label{B:subject7} Let $B$ be the spectrum of the ring of integers of a number field and let $f:X\to B$ be separated of finite type. Let $\mathbb Z_X^c$ denote Bloch's dualizing cycle complex. For a torsion \'etale sheaf $F$ on $X$ there is a natural duality \[ R\operatorname{Hom}_X(F,\mathbb Z_X^c) \simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(R\Gamma_c(X,F),\mathbb Z)[-1]. \] For constructible $F$ it induces perfect finite pairings \[ \operatorname{Ext}^{2-i}_X(F,\mathbb Z_X^c)\times H_c^i(X,F) \longrightarrow\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z. \] At real places compact support is understood with the source's Tate modification.

\label{B:subject8} Let $M$ be a complex manifold. Holomorphic finite-rank vector bundles with integrable connection are equivalent to finite-dimensional complex local systems, compatibly with tensor products, duals and internal Hom. If $M$ is compact of complex dimension $d$, the associated de Rham groups have perfect pairings \[ H^i_{\mathrm{dR}}(M,E)\times H^{2d-i}_{\mathrm{dR}}(M,E^\vee) \longrightarrow\mathbb C. \] For a smooth scheme in characteristic zero an integrable connection is the same as a left module structure over the sheaf of differential operators on the underlying vector bundle. In the divided-power characteristic-$p$ situation of subject~1, the crystal--connection correspondence additionally requires topological quasi-nilpotence.

\label{B:subject9} Let $X$ be a complex analytic space, countable at infinity and of bounded dimension. There is a dualizing complex $K_X$ and trace such that, for a coherent sheaf $F$, the separated quotients of \[ H^p(X,F)\quad\hbox{and}\quad\operatorname{Ext}^{-p}_c(X;F,K_X) \] are perfect strong topological duals in the canonical quotient-Fr\'echet and quotient-DFS topologies. Similarly $H_c^p(X,F)$ is dual to $\operatorname{Ext}^{-p}(X;F,K_X)$ after separation. When $X$ is compact, these are the usual finite-dimensional perfect pairings.

\label{B:subject10} For a quasi-projective scheme $X$ over a field, there is a natural transformation $\tau_X:G_0(X)\to\mathrm{CH}_*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$, covariant for proper morphisms, satisfying \[ \tau_X(E\otimes F)=\operatorname{ch}(E)\cap\tau_X(F), \qquad \tau_X(\mathcal O_X)=\operatorname{td}(T_X)\cap[X] \] when respectively $E$ is a vector bundle and $X$ is smooth. More generally, for a projective local-complete-intersection morphism $f:X\to Y$ of constant virtual relative dimension, where $Y$ is quasi-compact with an ample line bundle, SGA~6 gives \[ \operatorname{ch}(f_!x)=f_{\mathrm{gr},*} \bigl(\operatorname{ch}(x)\operatorname{td}(T_f)\bigr) \] in the rational associated graded of $K$-theory, for perfect-complex classes $x$. For complex analytic spaces there is a proper-covariant transformation from coherent $G_0$ to topological $K$-homology, agreeing with the usual bundle class under Poincar\'e identification on a complex manifold.

\label{B:subject11} Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring, $K$ its fraction field, and $A/K$ an abelian variety. The functor on smooth $R$-schemes \[ T\longmapsto\operatorname{Hom}_K(T_K,A) \] is represented by a smooth separated group scheme $\mathcal A/R$ of finite type. Its generic fibre is $A$ and its representing property characterizes it up to unique isomorphism.

\label{B:subject12} Let $S$ be a connected Dedekind scheme, $K$ its function field and $A/K$ an abelian variety. There is a smooth separated finite-type $S$-group scheme $\mathcal A$ with generic fibre $A$, satisfying \[ \operatorname{Hom}_S(T,\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(T_K,A) \] for every smooth $S$-scheme $T$. On an open set on which $A$ extends to an abelian scheme, that abelian scheme is its N\'eron model.

\label{B:subject13} Let $R$ be a henselian discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $t$, and assume $\widehat K/K$ is separable if the fraction field $K$ has positive characteristic. For a finite-type $R$-scheme $X$ there is a linear function $\beta(n)=an+b$ such that any point modulo $t^{\beta(n)}$ has the same reduction modulo $t^n$ as some point of $X(R)$. In particular \[ X(R)\ne\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X(R/t^n)\ne\varnothing\text{ for every }n. \] For an excellent henselian noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$, every finite system of polynomial equations over $R$ with a solution in $\widehat R$ has solutions in $R$ congruent to it modulo any prescribed $\mathfrak m^n$.

\label{B:strong-approximation} For a noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$, the following three conditions are equivalent: $R$ is excellent and henselian; $R$ has the approximation property; and $R$ has the strong approximation property. Here approximation means that every solution in $\widehat R$ of a finite polynomial system over $R$ can be approximated to every finite order by a solution in $R$. Strong approximation means that, for each $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\in R[Y_1,\ldots,Y_N]^r$, there is a function $\beta:\mathbb N_{>0}\to\mathbb N_{>0}$ such that \[ f(a)\in(\mathfrak m^{\beta(n)})^r \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \exists b\in R^N:\ f(b)=0,\quad b-a\in(\mathfrak m^n)^N. \] In particular every complete noetherian local ring has strong approximation. The function need not admit a linear bound, even for $R=\mathbb Q[[s,t]]$.

\label{B:nonlinear-Artin} In $R=\mathbb Q[[s,t]]$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=(s,t)$, put $f(U,V,W)=U^2-V^2W$. For every integer $m\ge5$, set \[ \begin{split} u_m&=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}{\binom{1/2}{j}} s^{2m-2-2j}t^{(m-2)j},\\ v_m&=s^{2m-3},\qquad w_m=s^2+t^{m-2}. \end{split} \] Then $\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak m}f(u_m,v_m,w_m)=m^2-4$, but no exact zero of $f$ is congruent to $(u_m,v_m,w_m)$ modulo $\mathfrak m^{2m-2}$. Hence every function $\beta$ in Theorem~\ref{B:strong-approximation} for this $f$ satisfies \[ \beta(2m-2)>m^2-4\qquad(m\ge5), \] so no linear bound exists.

\label{B:subject14} A topos admitting a site with finite limits and with a finite subcover refining every covering has enough points. Also, if $R\rightrightarrows U$ is a smooth groupoid in algebraic spaces, its quotient stack $[U/R]$ is algebraic. Conversely an algebraic stack with a smooth atlas $U$ has the presentation $[U/(U\times_{\mathcal X}U)]$.

\label{B:pointless} Let $B$ be the complete Boolean algebra of regular open subsets of $\mathbb R$, where $U$ is regular open if $U=\operatorname{int}\overline U$. Regard $B$ as a site whose covers of $U$ are families with join $U$. The Grothendieck topos $\operatorname{Sh}(B)$ is nondegenerate and has no geometric point $\operatorname{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(B)$. In particular it has no set-valued fibre functor that preserves finite limits and all colimits.

\label{B:Boolean-localization} For every Grothendieck topos $\mathcal E$, there are a complete Boolean algebra $B$ and a surjective geometric morphism \[ p:\operatorname{Sh}(B)\longrightarrow\mathcal E. \] Equivalently, $p^*:\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Sh}(B)$ preserves finite limits and all colimits and is conservative. It is comonadic, so $\mathcal E$ is recovered as the category of coalgebras for its induced comonad. This gives a universal Boolean-valued replacement for ordinary fibre functors even when $\mathcal E$ has no points.

\label{B:subject15} For every field $k$ and pointed connected simplicial set $T$, there is a schematization $(T\otimes k)^{\mathrm{sch}}$, characterized by the universal map from $T$ to a pointed schematic homotopy type. Its fundamental group is the affine proalgebraic completion of $\pi_1(T)$; for simply connected finite-type $T$ in characteristic zero its higher homotopy groups are the additive group schemes of $\pi_i(T)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}k$. Separately, for a henselian pair $(A,I)$ and a proper $X/A$, the closed fibre $Z=X_{A/I}$ has the same profinite \'etale homotopy type as $X$.

\label{B:Lie-comparison-counterexample} There is a pointed simplicial affine scheme \(X_\bullet\) over \(k=\mathbf F_2\) such that \[ X_0=X_1=\operatorname{Spec}k, \qquad X_n\simeq\mathbf A_k^{\,2\binom n2}, \] all simplicial structure maps are pointed polynomial maps, and \(X_\bullet(R)\) is Kan for every commutative \(k\)-algebra \(R\), but \[ \pi_2\bigl(X_\bullet(k)\bigr)\simeq\mathbf Z/4\mathbf Z, \qquad H_2\bigl(N\operatorname{Lie}X_\bullet\bigr) \simeq(\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z)^2. \] Here \(N\) denotes the normalized chain complex. In particular, the left group admits no \(k\)-module structure, and the comparison cannot hold even as an isomorphism of abelian groups.

\label{B:Lie-comparison-integral-counterexample} There is a pointed simplicial affine scheme \(Y_\bullet\) over \(\mathbf Z\) with \[ Y_0=Y_1=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z, \qquad Y_n\simeq\mathbf A_{\mathbf Z}^{\,2\binom n2+\binom n3}, \] polynomial structure maps, and a Kan simplicial set \(Y_\bullet(R)\) for every commutative ring \(R\), such that \[ \pi_2\bigl(Y_\bullet(\mathbf Z)\bigr)\simeq\mathbf Z, \qquad H_2\bigl(N\operatorname{Lie}Y_\bullet\bigr) \simeq\mathbf Z\oplus\mathbf Z/2\mathbf Z. \] Thus restricting the displayed comparison of \S118 to \(k=\mathbf Z\) does not repair its stated smooth Kan sufficient conditions.

\label{B:integral-affinization} Let $T$ be a pointed simply connected space with every $\pi_i(T)$, $i\ge2$, finitely generated. Work in hypercomplete fpqc stacks on affine schemes over $\mathbf Z$. Let affine stacks mean the full subcategory generated by the $K(\mathbf G_a,n)$ under small homotopy limits, and put \[ F_T=(T\otimes\mathbf Z)^{\mathrm{uni}} =\mathbf R\operatorname{Spec}C^*(T,\mathbf Z),\qquad \mathbb H=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbf Z). \] Here $C^*$ is the cosimplicial commutative cochain ring, and $\operatorname{Int}(\mathbf Z)=\{P\in\mathbf Q[x]:P(\mathbf Z)\subset\mathbf Z\}$, with the additive Hopf structure. Then $F_T$ is universal for maps from $T$ to integer-valued points of affine stacks, and \[ \pi_i(F_T)\simeq\pi_i(T)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbb H\quad(i\ge2) \] as fpqc abelian sheaves; these sheaves have natural $\mathbb H$-module structures. The unit $u_T:T\to F_T(\mathbf Z)$ has a natural retraction. The induced map of mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}(T,S)\to\operatorname{Map}(F_T,F_S)$ also has a retraction for every $S$ in this class, and $F_T\simeq F_S$ if and only if $T\simeq S$. At the induced basepoint, \[ \pi_i(F_T(\mathbf Z))\simeq \pi_i(T)\oplus\prod_{p\text{ prime}}\widehat{\pi_{i+1}(T)}_p \qquad(i\ge1). \] The homotopy sheaves need not be $\mathcal O$-modules, and the unit need not be a weak equivalence. These assertions concern this specified integral affine-stack construction, without identifying it with the unspecified infinitesimal enrichment in the 1964 sheet.

\label{B:unipotent-homotopy} Let $k$ be a field. A higher stack here is a sheaf of spaces for the fpqc topology on affine $k$-schemes. An affine stack is $\operatorname{Spec}B$, where $B$ belongs to the homotopy theory of cosimplicial commutative $k$-algebras. For a pointed higher stack $(X,x)$ such that $k\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$, put \[ \mathbf U(X)=\operatorname{Spec}R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X),\qquad \pi_i^{\mathrm U}(X,x)=\pi_i(\mathbf U(X),x)\quad(i\ge1). \] The derived algebra structure, including its cosimplicial commutative operations, is part of this definition. Then the following hold. \begin{enumerate} \item The map $X\to\mathbf U(X)$ is universal for maps to affine stacks. The stack $\mathbf U(X)$ is connected and hypercomplete, and its $\pi_i^{\mathrm U}$ are represented by unipotent affine group schemes, commutative for $i\ge2$. Here unipotent means that every nonzero finite-dimensional representation has a nonzero invariant vector. Finite type of these group schemes is not required. \item If $X$ is a scheme of finite type over $k$ and $x\in X(k)$, then $\pi_1^{\mathrm U}(X,x)$ is naturally the Tannaka group of the category of unipotent vector bundles on $X$, with fibre functor $x^*$. Here a unipotent vector bundle has a finite filtration by subbundles whose successive quotients are trivial line bundles. This is the unipotent Nori fundamental group in this specified sense. \item For every integer $r\ge1$, \[ H^j(X,\mathcal O_X)=0\ (1\le j\le r) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \pi_j^{\mathrm U}(X,x)=1\ (1\le j\le r). \] Under these equivalent conditions there are natural maps \[ H^{r+1}(X,\mathcal O_X) \simeq\operatorname{Hom}(\pi_{r+1}^{\mathrm U}(X,x),\mathbf G_a), \qquad \operatorname{Ext}^1(\pi_{r+1}^{\mathrm U}(X,x),\mathbf G_a) \hookrightarrow H^{r+2}(X,\mathcal O_X). \] The extension group is for commutative fpqc group sheaves; the restriction $r\ge1$ ensures that its first argument is commutative. \item If $X$ is a proper $k$-scheme and $k$ has characteristic $p>0$, every $\pi_i^{\mathrm U}(X,x)$ is profinite. If moreover $k$ is algebraically closed, the comparison induced by $\mathbf F_p\to\mathcal O_X$ identifies its maximal pro-\'etale quotient with the affine group scheme associated to the pro-$p$-finite group \[ \pi_i\bigl(\operatorname{Et}(X)^{\wedge}_p,x\bigr). \] Here $\operatorname{Et}(X)^{\wedge}_p$ is the pro-$p$-finite completion of the entire \'etale homotopy type. The displayed group retains its profinite topology. Still assuming $k$ algebraically closed, if Frobenius acts bijectively on every $H^j(X,\mathcal O_X)$, these comparison maps are themselves isomorphisms. \end{enumerate} These conclusions concern a specified theory of schemes and higher stacks. They make no identification with the unspecified infinitesimal enrichment of the 1964 thesis sheet.

\label{B:formal-homotopy} Let $k$ be a field, let $n\geq2$, and let $X$ be a pointed higher stack for the fpqc topology on affine $k$-schemes. Use the affine-stack construction \[ \mathbf U(X)=\operatorname{Spec}R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O), \qquad G=\pi_n^{\mathrm U}(X)=\pi_n(\mathbf U(X)), \] where $R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O)$ retains its cosimplicial commutative algebra structure, in the category used in Theorem~\ref{B:unipotent-homotopy}. Suppose that \[ \begin{gathered} H^0(X,\mathcal O)=k,\qquad H^i(X,\mathcal O)=0\quad(0<i<n),\\ g=\dim_k H^n(X,\mathcal O)<\infty, \qquad H^{n+1}(X,\mathcal O)=0. \end{gathered} \] Then $G$ is a commutative affine unipotent group scheme and its dual $G^\vee$ is a commutative formal Lie group of dimension $g$. Here the dual is defined by the linearly compact topological Hopf algebra $\mathcal O(G)^*$, with the topology dual to the finite-dimensional subcoalgebras of $\mathcal O(G)$; the conclusion includes an isomorphism of its underlying topological algebra with $k[[t_1,\ldots,t_g]]$. If, in addition, $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic $p>0$ and $X$ is a proper $k$-scheme with a chosen $k$-point, let $\operatorname{Art}_k$ be the category of local Artinian $k$-algebras with specified residue identification $A/\mathfrak m_A=k$. The covariant functor $\Phi_X^n:\operatorname{Art}_k\to\mathrm{Ab}$ is defined by \[ \Phi_X^n(A)=\ker\!\left( H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathbf G_m) \longrightarrow H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\mathbf G_m)\right) \qquad(A\in\operatorname{Art}_k) \] and is represented by the formal Lie group $G^\vee$. In particular, \[ \Phi_X^n\simeq (\pi_n^{\mathrm U}(X))^\vee, \qquad \mathbf M(\Phi_X^n) \simeq \varprojlim_r H^n_{\mathrm{Zar}}(X,W_r), \] where $W_r$ denotes the length-$r$ $p$-typical Witt-vector group and $\mathbf M$ is the formal-group Dieudonn\'e functor in the convention specified below. Smoothness, projectivity, ordinarity and finite formal-group height are not needed for this comparison.

\label{B:subject16} The blanket assertion that full \'etale fundamental groups are invariant in smooth proper curve families is false, even for the explicit genus-one family of Proposition~\ref{B:specialization}. For such families over a trait of residue characteristic $p$, specialization is surjective and induces an isomorphism on maximal prime-to-$p$ quotients. At the homotopy level, after completion away from the residue characteristics, the geometric fibres of a smooth proper morphism of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes have equivalent \'etale homotopy types under specialization.

\label{B:nori-finite-flat} Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $X/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve, and fix $x\in X(k)$. There is a profinite affine $k$-group scheme $\pi^{\mathrm N}(X,x)$ such that, for every finite $k$-group scheme $G$, homomorphisms \[ \pi^{\mathrm N}(X,x)\longrightarrow G \] classify isomorphism classes of pointed fppf $G$-torsors $(P,p)$ on $(X,x)$, with the structure group $G$ fixed. Restricting this classification to finite \'etale $G$ recovers the usual pointed finite \'etale torsors, so the maximal pro-\'etale quotient is the constant pro-group scheme associated with $\pi_1^{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,x)$.

\label{B:nori-base-change-counterexample} Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_2$, choose $\alpha\in\mathbf F_4\subset k$ with $\alpha^2+\alpha+1=0$, and let $X/k$ be the smooth projective model of \[ y^2+x(x+1)y=x(x+1)(x^3+\alpha x+\alpha). \] Choose any $x_0\in X(k)$ and put $K=\overline{k(t)}$. Then $X$ is an ordinary curve of genus $2$, but the canonical map \[ \pi^{\mathrm N}(X_K,x_0)\longrightarrow \pi^{\mathrm N}(X,x_0)\times_k K \] is not an isomorphism.

\label{B:Picard-general} Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper flat finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces. Assume that $\mathcal O_T\to f_{T*}\mathcal O_{X_T}$ is an isomorphism for every scheme $T\to S$. Then the fppf sheaf $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S}$ is an algebraic space, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation over $S$. It is separated if all geometric fibres of $f$ are integral, and smooth if $f$ has relative dimension at most one. No noetherian or one-dimensional hypothesis on the base is required.

\label{B:subject17} Let $R$ be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring with perfect residue field, and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a proper flat regular model of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve. Write the special fibre as $\sum_jm_jC_j$, and put $\delta=\gcd_jm_j$. Then \[ \delta=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{Pic}^0_{X/R}\text{ is representable by a scheme} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{Pic}^0_{X/R}\text{ is separated}. \] Moreover the appropriate separated quotient of the closure of the generic Picard identity component is the N\'eron model of the generic Jacobian.

\label{B:Picard-double-fibre} Let $R=\mathbb C[[t]]$, $R'=\mathbb C[[s]]$ with $t=s^2$, and let $E/\mathbb C$ be the elliptic curve $y^2=x^3-x$, with origin $O$ and two-torsion point $T=(0,0)$. The involution \[ (P,s)\longmapsto(P+T,-s) \] on $Y=E\times\operatorname{Spec}R'$ has a scheme quotient $X=Y/C_2$. The morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is proper, flat and finitely presented, its total space is regular, and its generic fibre is a smooth geometrically connected genus-one curve. Nevertheless $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{X/R}$ is not separated and is not representable by a scheme. The full Picard functor is represented by an algebraic space.

\label{B:subject18} For any fpqc covering $\{S_i\to S\}$, every descent datum on schemes affine over $S_i$ is effective, with no noetherian assumption. In particular this applies over an Artinian base. If a finite locally free group scheme $G/S$ acts freely on an $S$-scheme $X$, the fppf quotient is an algebraic space; when that quotient is represented by a scheme, the descended $G$-torsor and its affine descent data are effective.

\label{B:descent-counterexample} Let $k=\mathbb Q$, $L=\mathbb Q(i)$, and let $X/L$ be the affine line with doubled origin: glue two copies $U_+$ and $U_-$ of $\operatorname{Spec}L[t]$ by the identity on $D(t)$. The involution that conjugates $i$, fixes $t$, and interchanges the two charts gives a descent datum for the finite \'etale cover $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. This datum is not effective in schemes, although $X$ is smooth and of finite type over $L$ and the base $k$ is Artinian. Its quotient is an algebraic space that is not a scheme.

\label{B:descent-criterion} Let $L/k$ be a finite Galois extension and let an $L$-scheme $X$ carry a semilinear action of $G=\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)$. Its descent datum is effective in schemes if and only if $X$ has an open covering by $G$-stable affine subschemes.

\label{B:subject19} For a projective variety $X$ over an algebraically closed field, let $N^k(X)$ be the space of numerical codimension-$k$ classes. The pliant cone $\operatorname{PL}^k(X)$, generated and closed by products of Schur classes of globally generated vector bundles, is full dimensional and salient; ample complete intersections lie in its interior. These cones are stable under pullback, lie in the pseudoeffective cones and are stable under products. The pseudoeffective cone of $k$-cycles is full dimensional and salient, and degree against an ample class extends to a norm on the numerical cycle space.

\label{B:subject20} Let $G$ be a split semisimple simply connected algebraic group over a perfect field, $B$ a Borel subgroup, and $\lambda$ a dominant weight. With the convention that dominant weights define globally generated line bundles on $G/B$, \[ H^q(G/B,\mathcal L_\lambda)=0\qquad(q>0). \] The assertion holds in every characteristic.

\label{B:subject21} For a quasi-compact quasi-separated closed pair, degree-zero comparison for every \'etale sheaf of sets is equivalent to geometric henselianity. In the affine case it implies comparison in every degree for every torsion abelian \'etale sheaf; the same conclusion holds in the proper situation of Theorem~\ref{B:henselian-general}, and for every separated finite-type scheme over a henselian discrete valuation ring by Theorem~\ref{C:henselian-trait-comparison}. If $Z$ is affine and $X$ is quasi-separated, Proposition~\ref{C:henselian-affine-closed-fibre} forces $X$ to be affine and gives the same conclusion. Theorem~\ref{C:henselian-noetherian-pair-comparison} proves the torsion comparison for every separated finite-type scheme over any noetherian henselian ring pair $(A,I)$ with $Z=X\times_A A/I$, assuming only that every closed point of $X$ lies in $Z$. Corollary~\ref{C:henselian-noetherian-closedpoint-criterion} proves that, in this class, the closed-point condition is equivalent to universal degree-zero comparison. No flatness, locality, catenarity, excellence or properness of $X$ is required. Theorem~\ref{C:henselian-horizontal-proper} identifies the proper horizontal components; Theorem~\ref{B:henselian-local-flat-proper} remains a separate proof for flat positive-dimensional local bases. Completeness and henselization give the two affine cases named on scan~4. Completion of a punctured henselian pair with finitely generated ideal gives a second, distinct comparison. The affine and punctured statements extend to torsion sheaves of spaces, and consequently to the associated profinite \'etale homotopy types. The assertion with arbitrary abelian coefficients is false even for the constant integer sheaf on an affine henselian pair, by Proposition~\ref{B:constant-integer-rigidity}; Proposition~\ref{B:nontorsion-rigidity} supplies a separate coherent-sheaf example; the torsion implication for arbitrary closed pairs is also false: Theorem~\ref{C:subject21-torsion-counterexample} constructs a qcqs nonseparated nonnoetherian pair with universal degree-zero comparison but failure of degree-one comparison for every constant $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, $n>1$. It realizes the supported-degree-two obstruction of Proposition~\ref{B:H1-gate} and the cyclic-torsor failure characterized by Proposition~\ref{C:torsion-degree-two-reduction}.

\label{B:subject22} Let $k$ be a field and $\mathcal C$ a rigid abelian $k$-linear symmetric tensor category with $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$. If there is an exact faithful $k$-linear symmetric tensor functor $\omega:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Vec}_k$, then \[ G=\operatorname{Aut}^{\otimes}(\omega) \] is an affine group scheme and $\mathcal C\simeq\operatorname{Rep}_k(G)$. Its other fibre functors over a $k$-algebra are classified by $G$-torsors. If such a fibre functor exists only after a field extension, the stack of fibre functors is an affine gerbe and its representation category recovers $\mathcal C$.

\label{B:super} If $\operatorname{char}k\ne2$, finite-dimensional super vector spaces with the Koszul symmetry form a rigid abelian symmetric tensor category with endomorphism ring $k$ of the unit, but admit no faithful symmetric tensor functor to ordinary vector spaces. Thus the sign and fibre-functor hypotheses cannot be removed from subject~22.

\label{B:subject23} For schemes of finite type over a field, ordinary Chow homology admits proper pushforward and flat pullback. If $Y$ is smooth quasi-projective of pure dimension $e$, $X$ is quasi-projective and pure of dimension $d$, and $f:X\to Y$ is any morphism, there is an integral pullback on classes \[ f^*: \mathrm{CH}^r(Y)\longrightarrow\mathrm{CH}_{d-r}(X), \qquad a\longmapsto f^*a\cap[X]. \] There is no smoothness assumption on $X$. For a separated regular noetherian scheme $Y$ of finite Krull dimension, rational Chow groups with supports have a canonical intersection product, agreeing with the Serre Tor formula when cycles meet properly. In particular $\mathrm{CH}^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ is a graded commutative ring.

\label{B:regular-pullback} Let $Y$ be a separated regular noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension. Give it the dimension function $\delta_Y(y)=-\operatorname{codim}_Y(y)$, component by component, and give finite-type $Y$-schemes the induced dimension function. There is a canonical graded ring injection \[ \mathrm{CH}^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}, \qquad \alpha\longmapsto\widetilde\alpha, \] into operational Chow cohomology, satisfying $\widetilde\alpha\cap[Y]=\alpha$. Consequently every morphism $f:X\to Y$ of finite type, with no regularity assumption on $X$, has canonical operations \[ f^*\widetilde\alpha\cap-: \mathrm{CH}_j(X)_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}_{j-p}(X)_{\mathbb Q} \quad(\alpha\in\mathrm{CH}^p(Y)_{\mathbb Q}). \] They commute with proper pushforward, flat pullback and refined Cartier-divisor intersection, and are functorial under further pullback as operational classes. If $X$ is pure of dimension $d$ for the chosen dimension function, evaluating on $[X]$ gives a rational class in $\mathrm{CH}_{d-p}(X)$. Thus the regular-target assertion has an arbitrary-source rational form, including the ample-line-bundle setting of the manuscript.

\label{B:subject24} Numerically trivial one-cycles on a smooth projective connected threefold need not be $\tau$-trivial. Numerical and rational-coefficient homological equivalence do agree for codimension-two cycles on every smooth projective fourfold in characteristic zero, and for abelian fourfolds in positive characteristic for every permitted $\ell$, using the 2026 Tate theorem stated in Theorem~\ref{B:abelian}.

\label{B:subject25} The product of two algebraically trivial cycles need not be rationally trivial, and an Albanese-trivial zero-cycle on a surface need not be rationally trivial. Both failures occur for the single explicit surface and cycles in Theorem~\ref{B:square}; the zero-cycle has infinite order. On a product of elliptic curves, the Albanese kernel is generated by the exterior products of degree-zero divisors.

\label{B:subject26} Let $S$ be a scheme, $X\to S$ a smooth projective curve with geometrically connected fibres, and $D\subset X$ a relative effective Cartier divisor finite and faithfully flat over $S$. Put $D_n=V(\mathcal I_D^{n+1})$, and let $J_n$ be the relative Picard sheaf of the pinching $X\amalg_{D_n}S$, equivalently line bundles on $X$ trivialized along $D_n$. Let $J=\varprojlim_nJ_n$. The diagonal ideal supplies an Abel map $a:X\setminus D\to J$, and for every smooth commutative $S$-group scheme $G$, \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{S\text{-}\mathrm{grp}}(J,G) \xrightarrow{\ \circ a\ }\operatorname{Hom}_S(X\setminus D,G) \] is bijective. There is an exact sequence of fpqc sheaves \[ 1\longrightarrow\mathbb G_{m,S} \longrightarrow (D_n/S)_*\mathbb G_{m,D_n} \longrightarrow J_n\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S} \longrightarrow1. \]

\label{B:subject27} For a noetherian scheme $X$ and a quasi-coherent sheaf $F$, the Parshin--Beilinson ad\`ele sheaves over flags give a functorial flasque resolution \[ 0\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow\mathcal A_X^0(F) \longrightarrow\mathcal A_X^1(F)\longrightarrow\cdots. \] Its global-sections complex computes $R\Gamma(X,F)$. For a noetherian ring $A$, a formal curve $\mathfrak X=\operatorname{Spf}B$ with $B\simeq A[[t]]$, and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/t]$, define the local Jacobian as the Zariski group sheaf with \[ \mathcal J(R)=\bigl(R[[t]][t^{-1}]\bigr)^\times \qquad(R\text{ an }A\text{-algebra}). \] There is an Abel map $a:U\to\mathcal J_{\mathrm{omb}}$ to its formal shadow such that, for every smooth separated commutative $A$-group scheme $G$, \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{A\text{-}\mathrm{grp}}(\mathcal J,G) \xrightarrow{\ h\mapsto h_{\mathrm{omb}}\circ a\ }G(U) \quad\text{is bijective}. \]

\label{B:subject28} For finite-type schemes over $\mathbb Z$ there are the triangulated categories of rational Beilinson motives $\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm B}(X)$ and their constructible subcategories. For separated finite-type morphisms the six operations preserve constructibility. If $a:X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$ is separated of finite type, then $a^!\mathbf1$ is dualizing on constructible motives: with \[ D_X(M)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(M,a^!\mathbf1) \] the canonical map $M\to D_XD_XM$ is an isomorphism, and duality exchanges the expected pairs of six operations.

\label{B:PM1} Every generically reduced noetherian quasi-excellent scheme $X$ over $\mathbb Q$ admits a finite sequence of blowups along regular centres, all disjoint from the inverse image of $X_{\mathrm{reg}}$, whose final scheme is regular. The sequence can be chosen functorially for regular morphisms, omitting empty blowups after base change. For a noetherian quasi-excellent scheme $X$, a nowhere dense closed subset $Z$, and a prime $\ell$ invertible on $X$, there is a finite family $\{X_i\to X\}$ covering in the $\ell'$-alteration topology such that each $X_i$ is regular and integral and the inverse image of $Z$ is the support of a strict normal-crossings divisor. This latter assertion does not assert a birational resolution in positive characteristic.

\label{B:PM2} Let $n\geq1$ be invertible on a noetherian regular scheme $X$, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed regular subscheme of pure codimension $c$. With $\Lambda=\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$, the cycle-class Gysin map is an isomorphism \[ \Lambda_Z(-c)[-2c]\xrightarrow{\sim}i^!\Lambda_X. \] Consequently $R^qi^!\Lambda_X=0$ for $q\ne2c$, and $R^{2c}i^!\Lambda_X=\Lambda_Z(-c)$.

\label{B:PM3} Let $f:Y\to X$ be a regular morphism of locally noetherian $\mathbb Z[1/n]$-schemes, let $g:X'\to X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and form $Y'=Y\times_XX'$ with projections $g':Y'\to Y$ and $f':Y'\to X'$. For every $K\in D^+(X'_{\acute et},\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)$ the canonical map \[ f^*Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg'_*f'^*K \] is an isomorphism. In particular this applies to the completion map of an excellent noetherian local ring.

\label{B:PM4} Let $X$ be an excellent noetherian $\mathbb Z[1/n]$-scheme with a dimension function $\delta$, and put $\Lambda=\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$. There is a potential dualizing complex $K_{X,\delta}$, uniquely determined together with its compatible local normalizations. It belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\acute et},\Lambda)$, and \[ D_X(M)=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(M,K_{X,\delta}) \] preserves $D^b_c(X_{\acute et},\Lambda)$. For every $M$ in that category, $M\to D_XD_X(M)$ is an isomorphism. If $X$ has finite Krull dimension, $K_{X,\delta}$ has finite quasi-injective dimension and is a dualizing complex in the sense of SGA~5.

\label{B:PM5} Let $X$ be noetherian and quasi-excellent, let $f:Y\to X$ be of finite type, and let $n$ be invertible on $X$. For a constructible $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$-sheaf $F$ on $Y_{\acute et}$, every $R^qf_*F$ is constructible and these sheaves vanish for all sufficiently large $q$. Thus $Rf_*$ preserves bounded constructible complexes. Without invertibility, even finiteness of $H^1$ over an algebraically closed field can fail.

\label{B:PM6} Let $X$ be a quasi-excellent scheme equipped with a dimension function $\delta_X$, let $n$ be invertible on $X$, let $f:Y\to X$ be affine of finite type, and let $F$ be a constructible $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$-sheaf on $Y$. Put \[ \delta_Y(y)=\delta_X(f(y))+operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(y))}\kappa(y), \qquad \delta_X(G)=\sup_{G_{\bar x}\ne0}\delta_X(x). \] Then $\delta_X(R^qf_*F)\leq\delta_Y(F)-q$. In particular, for an affine $d$-dimensional scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed field, cohomology with constructible prime-to-characteristic torsion coefficients vanishes above degree $d$.

\label{B:PM7} For a proper holomorphic map $f:X\to S$ of complex spaces and a coherent analytic sheaf $F$ on $X$, every $R^qf_*F$ is coherent. In particular $H^q(X,F)$ is finite dimensional when $X$ is compact. This does not, without further hypotheses, say that $R^qf_*F$ is locally free or that arbitrary base change commutes with it.

\label{B:PM8} Let $K$ be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field with a nontrivial valuation, and let $A$ be a classical $K$-affinoid algebra of dimension $d$. For every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $(\operatorname{Spec}A)_{\acute et}$, \[ H^i(\operatorname{Spec}A,F)=0\quad(i>d+1). \] If $F$ is $\ell$-primary and $\ell$ is different from the residue characteristic of $K$, the stronger bound is $i>d$.

\label{B:PM9} Let $(X,Y)$ be a Hausdorff polyhedral pair, meaning a pair homeomorphic to a locally finite simplicial complex and a subcomplex, with $X$ second countable. Let $n\geq1$. Suppose every $y\in Y$ has a fundamental system of neighbourhoods $U$ for which $(U,U\setminus Y)$ is $(n-1)$-connected. Then $(X,X\setminus Y)$ is $(n-1)$-connected. The implication therefore applies to second-countable finite-dimensional complex analytic spaces and closed analytic subspaces whenever the stated local depth bound holds.

\label{B:local-Hurewicz} There is a finite polyhedral pair $(X,Y)$, with $Y$ a single point $v$, such that \[ \mathcal H^i_Y(\mathbb Z_X)=0\quad(i<4),\qquad \pi_2^Y(X,v)=0,\qquad \pi_3^Y(X,v)=\mathbb Z/2. \] It refutes SGA~2, Expos\'e XIII, \S6, Conjecture A, which is stated for topological locally triangulable pairs and includes the local fundamental-group condition. For an arbitrary nonempty connected finite polyhedron $L$, let $X=cL$ be its cone and $Y=\{v\}$ its vertex. For every $n\geq3$, the exact replacement is \[ \operatorname{prof\,hpt}_{Y}(X)\geq n \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{cases} \pi_1(L)=0,\\ \widetilde H^j(L,\mathbb Z)=0& (j<n-1),\\ H^{n-1}(L,\mathbb Z)\text{ is torsion-free}. \end{cases} \] The last condition is equivalently torsion-freeness of $\mathcal H^n_Y(\mathbb Z_X)_v$.

\label{C:piecewise-graph-category} A piecewise regular map has constructible graph. Conversely, in characteristic zero every map with constructible graph is piecewise regular. In arbitrary characteristic, a constructible graph whose projection to the source is bijective on all scheme points and induces isomorphisms on their residue fields is piecewise isomorphic over the source, and hence defines a piecewise regular map. Thus the last graph convention, interpreted on finite-type reduced schemes and finite stratifications, gives $\mathcal P_k$.
\label{C:piecewise-group-fullness} Every piecewise regular homomorphism $f:G(k)\to H(k)$ between algebraic $k$-groups is induced by a unique homomorphism of algebraic groups.

\label{C:piecewise-group-algebraization} The functor from algebraic $k$-groups to group objects in $\mathcal P_k$ is an equivalence of categories. In particular, if $\operatorname{char}k=0$, it is an equivalence with group objects in $\mathcal C_k$.

\label{C:absolute-flat-piecewise} Let $k$ be algebraically closed, and let $X,Y$ be separated reduced finite-type $k$-schemes. There are natural bijections \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P_k}(X,Y) \simeq \operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sch}_k}(T(X),Y) \simeq \operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Abs}_k}(T(X),T(Y)). \] Consequently $T$ gives a fully faithful realization of $\mathcal P_k$ as the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Abs}_k$ with objects $T(X)$ arising from separated finite-type reduced schemes (and their finite stratifications). Its categorical product is \[ T(X)\mathbin{\times_{\operatorname{Abs}_k}}T(Y) \simeq T(X\times_kY) \simeq T\bigl(T(X)\times_kT(Y)\bigr). \] The product occurring inside the last $T$ is the ordinary scheme product. It need not itself be absolutely flat.

\label{C:absolute-flat-group-algebraization} With the internal product just specified, group objects in the full subcategory formed by the $T(X)$ for separated finite-type reduced $k$-schemes are equivalent to algebraic $k$-groups. In characteristic zero this also realizes group objects with arbitrary constructible graphs.

\label{B:finite-Greenberg-piecewise} Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $R_m$-scheme, not necessarily reduced. Its finite Greenberg realization $\operatorname{Gr}_m(X)$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme characterized by \[ \operatorname{Gr}_m(X)(A)=X(R_m\otimes_k A) \] for every $k$-algebra $A$. Define the finite-partition presheaf by \[ N_m(X)(Y)=\varinjlim_P\prod_{S\in P} X\bigl(R_m\otimes_k\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)\bigr). \] There are natural bijections \[ \begin{aligned} N_m(X)(Y) &\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_k\bigl(T(Y),\operatorname{Gr}_m(X)\bigr)\\ &\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Abs}_k} \bigl(T(Y),T(\operatorname{Gr}_m(X))\bigr). \end{aligned} \] In particular this is a realization of the finite-partition construction in the absolutely flat category, using its internal products. The Greenberg functor preserves products and group objects.

\label{B:uniform-partition-obstruction} Put $R=k[[t]]$, $A=k[x]$, and let $P$ range over the same finite reduced affine locally closed partitions of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. The natural homomorphism \[ D:=\varinjlim_P A_P[[t]]\longrightarrow T(A)[[t]] \] is injective but not surjective. Nevertheless, for every $m\geq1$, \[ D/t^mD\simeq T(A)[t]/(t^m),\qquad \widehat D^{\,(t)}\simeq T(A)[[t]]. \] In particular $D$ is a proper dense subring of its $t$-adic completion, and \[ \varinjlim_P\varprojlim_m A_P[t]/(t^m) \;\longrightarrow\; \varprojlim_m\varinjlim_P A_P[t]/(t^m) \] is not surjective. This is already the additive-group construction for $\mathbb G_{a,R}$; it is not caused by singularities or non-affineness.

\label{B:finite-cover-partition-obstruction} Let $k$ be algebraically closed. On the category of reduced affine finite-type $k$-schemes, equip fibre products with their reduced scheme structures and take finite surjective morphisms as covers. For $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ define the presheaves of additive abelian groups \[ D(Y)=\varinjlim_P B_P[[t]],\qquad E(Y)=T(B)[[t]], \] where $P$ runs over finite affine locally closed reduced partitions of $Y$. The induced morphism of associated \emph{sheaves of abelian groups} \[ D^\#\longrightarrow E^\# \] is not an epimorphism. The same is true for the associated sheaves of sets. In particular the series $z$ of Proposition~\ref{B:uniform-partition-obstruction} has no local lift from $D^\#$ on this specified site. No conclusion about categorical epimorphisms of sheaves of rings is asserted.

\label{B:complete-Greenberg-points} Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with perfect residue field $k$ and uniformizer $\pi$. In equal characteristic fix an isomorphism $R\simeq k[[t]]$ carrying $\pi$ to $t$. In mixed characteristic use the canonical Cohen inclusion $W(k)\hookrightarrow R$. Put $R_n=R/(\pi^n)$ and let $\mathcal R_n$ be its finite Greenberg ring scheme over $k$. For a $k$-algebra $A$, assume that $A$ is perfect in mixed characteristic, and define \[ S(A)=\varprojlim_n\mathcal R_n(A). \] For every $R$-scheme $X$, without a finite-type or separatedness assumption, the scheme \[ \operatorname{Gr}_R(X)= \varprojlim_n\operatorname{Gr}_{R_n}(X\times_R R_n) \] exists. There are natural bijections \[ \operatorname{Gr}_R(X)(A) \simeq\varprojlim_n X\bigl(\mathcal R_n(A)\bigr) \simeq X\bigl(S(A)\bigr), \] where all points on the right are morphisms over $R$. Here \[ S(A)\simeq \begin{cases} A[[t]],&R\simeq k[[t]],\\ R\otimes_{W(k)}W(A),&\operatorname{char}R=0,\ \operatorname{char}k>0. \end{cases} \] The construction preserves products and group objects. It is generally not of finite type: for $X=\mathbb A^1_R$ its underlying scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}k[x_0,x_1,\ldots]$.

\label{B:Witt-localization-witness} Use standard $p$-typical Witt coordinates and write $[f]=(f,0,0,\ldots)$. For every commutative ring $A$, every $f\in A$, every $N\geq0$, and every $w=(w_i)_{i\geq0}\in W(A)$, one has \[ ([f]^Nw)_i=f^{Np^i}w_i. \tag{\(*\)} \] Consequently, for $A=\mathbb F_p[f]$, with $f$ an indeterminate, the canonical map \[ W(A)_{[f]}\longrightarrow W(A_f) \] is injective and is not surjective. An explicit element outside its image has coordinates $v_i=f^{-ip^i}$. The same conclusions and witness hold for the perfect domain $A=\mathbb F_p[f^{1/p^r}:r\geq0]$. In contrast, the vector with coordinates $w_i=f^{-i}$ does lie in $W(A)_{[f]}$. Thus this particular illustrative vector in \cite[Remark~18.3]{BBertapelleGonzalezAviles2022} must be replaced when using the standard-coordinate convention explicitly fixed in that source, Section~2.3, pp.~8--9. The localization inequality and the corrected Greenberg theorem remain valid.

\label{B:perfect-Greenberg-cohomology} Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, uniformizer $\pi$, and perfect residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Equal and mixed characteristic are both allowed. Fix a coefficient map $W(k)\to R$. For a finite product $L$ of perfect field extensions of $k$, put \[ R(L)=\varprojlim_n \bigl(W_n(L)\otimes_{W_n(k)}R/\mathfrak m_R^n\bigr), \qquad K(L)=R(L)[1/\pi]. \] For $R=k[[t]]$ with its specified coefficient field, these are $L[[t]]$ and $L((t))$. For $L$ a field, $R(L)$ is a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field $L$. Let $S_{\mathrm{pa}}$ be the étale site on finite products of perfect field extensions of $k$, $S_{\mathrm{pf}}$ the pro-fppf site on quasi-compact quasi-separated perfect $k$-schemes, and $S_{\mathrm{ir}}$ the pro-étale site on ind-rational $k$-algebras. Here rational algebras are finite products of perfections of finitely generated field extensions, and ind-rational algebras are filtered unions of rational subalgebras. In the pro-fppf site, coverings are finite jointly surjective families flat of profinite presentation in the perfect sense. The inclusions induce premorphisms \[ h:S_{\mathrm{pf}}\to S_{\mathrm{pa}},\qquad \widetilde h:S_{\mathrm{pf}}\to S_{\mathrm{ir}},\qquad \mathsf a=R\widetilde h_*Lh^*: D(S_{\mathrm{pa}},\mathbf{Ab})\to D(S_{\mathrm{ir}},\mathbf{Ab}). \] These premorphisms are not assumed to have exact inverse image on arbitrary sheaves of sets. \begin{enumerate} \item Let $\mathcal P'_{\mathrm{fc}}$ consist of commutative proalgebraic groups representable as extensions of perfections of abelian varieties by perfect affine groups, with finite étale component group. Restriction to $S_{\mathrm{pa}}$ is fully faithful on this category, and its derived counit is an isomorphism: \[ Lh^*(P|_{S_{\mathrm{pa}}})\simeq P \quad\text{in }D(S_{\mathrm{pf}},\mathbf{Ab}). \] \item The functors $R(-),K(-)$ induce premorphisms $\pi_R:R_{\mathrm{fppf}}\to S_{\mathrm{pa}}$ and $\pi_K:K_{\mathrm{fppf}}\to S_{\mathrm{pa}}$. Define \[ \mathcal R_R(F)=\mathsf aR\pi_{R,*}F,\qquad \mathcal R_K(F)=\mathsf aR\pi_{K,*}F,\qquad \mathcal R_x(F)= \operatorname{fib}\bigl(\mathcal R_R(F)\to\mathcal R_K(F|_K)\bigr). \] They give a functorial localization triangle. Call $Q\in D(S_{\mathrm{pa}},\mathbf{Ab})$ $h$-acyclic if its unit $Q\to Rh_*Lh^*Q$ is an isomorphism. If $R\pi_{R,*}F$ is $h$-acyclic, then \[ R\Gamma(L_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\mathcal R_R(F)) \simeq R\Gamma(R(L)_{\mathrm{fppf}},F). \] The analogous assertion holds over $K$. If both unit conditions hold for $F$ and $F|_K$, the analogous comparison holds with support on the closed fibre. Under this unit hypothesis, if both $F$ and $\mathcal R_R(F)$ are bounded below, there is the spectral sequence \[ E_2^{ij}= H^i(L_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\mathcal H^j\mathcal R_R(F)) \Longrightarrow H^{i+j}(R(L)_{\mathrm{fppf}},F). \] For algebraically closed $L$, this reduces to $\mathcal H^q\mathcal R_R(F)(L)=H^q(R(L)_{\mathrm{fppf}},F)$. \item If $G/R$ is a smooth commutative group scheme of finite type, write $G_n=G\times_RR/\mathfrak m_R^n$ and \[ \mathbf G=\varprojlim_n \bigl(\operatorname{Gr}_{R/\mathfrak m_R^n}(G_n)\bigr)^{\mathrm{perf}}. \] Then $\mathbf G\in\mathcal P'_{\mathrm{fc}}$ and \[ 0\longrightarrow U_G\longrightarrow\mathbf G \longrightarrow G_k^{\mathrm{perf}}\longrightarrow0 \] is exact, with $U_G$ connected pro-unipotent. Consequently $\pi_0(\mathbf G)=\pi_0(G_k)$, and $\mathcal R_R(G)\simeq\mathbf G[0]$. The unit condition in the preceding clause holds. \item If $N/R$ is finite flat and commutative, then $\mathcal H^0\mathcal R_R(N)$ is finite étale and agrees with $\mathcal H^0\mathcal R_K(N_K)$, $\mathcal H^1\mathcal R_R(N)$ is connected pro-unipotent, and $\mathcal H^q\mathcal R_R(N)=0$ for $q\geq2$. The object $R\pi_{R,*}N$ is $h$-acyclic. \end{enumerate}

\label{C:explog} For an associative unital $\mathbb Q$-algebra $R$, exponential and logarithm give inverse bijections between nilpotent elements $x\in R$ and unipotent elements $1+y\in R$, where $y$ is nilpotent. For a $K$-module $M$ they also give inverse bijections between locally nilpotent $u\in\operatorname{End}_K(M)$ and automorphisms $U\in\operatorname{Aut}_K(M)$ for which $U-1$ is locally nilpotent. The formulas are interpreted vector by vector in the latter case. They commute with every intertwining $K$-linear map.

\label{C:unipotent} Exponential induces a bijection \[ \{D\in\operatorname{Der}_K(A):D\text{ is nilpotent}\} \longrightarrow \{U\in\operatorname{Aut}_{K\text{-alg}}(A):U-1\text{ is nilpotent}\}. \] It preserves the nilpotency index. The same statement holds with both occurrences of ``nilpotent'' replaced by ``locally nilpotent.''

\label{C:filtered} Let $I\subset A$ satisfy $I^q=0$, with $q\geq1$, and put $I^0=A$. Define \begin{align*} \mathfrak g_I&=\{D\in\operatorname{Der}_K(A):D(I^k)\subset I^{k+1}\text{ for all }k\geq0\},\\ G_I&=\{U\in\operatorname{Aut}_{K\text{-alg}}(A):(U-1)(I^k)\subset I^{k+1}\text{ for all }k\geq0\}. \end{align*} Then $G_I$ is exactly the group of $K$-algebra automorphisms preserving $I$ and inducing the identity on $\operatorname{gr}_I(A)$, and \[ \exp:\mathfrak g_I\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }G_I, \qquad \log:G_I\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathfrak g_I \] are inverse bijections. Both defining series terminate before degree $q$. This supplies a valid replacement for the last corollary of cote~68, scan~046, using the deleted condition on scan~045.

\label{C:differential} For $U\in\operatorname{Aut}_{K\text{-alg}}(A)$ put $J_U=(U(a)-a:a\in A)\subset A$. For every integer $n\geq0$, $U$ is a differential operator of order at most $n$ if and only if $J_U^{n+1}=0$. In particular the differential automorphisms are exactly the automorphisms inducing the identity modulo some nilpotent ideal. Among them, exactly those with $U-1$ globally nilpotent are exponentials of nilpotent derivations.

\label{C:conormal} Suppose $J=J_U$ and $J^q=0$. The ideal $J$ is $U$-stable, and the induced map $U_1$ on $J/J^2$ is linear over $B=A/J$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $U$ is the exponential of a globally nilpotent $K$-derivation; \item $U-1$ is globally nilpotent; \item $U_1-1$ is globally nilpotent on $J/J^2$. \end{enumerate} If $(U_1-1)^r=0$, then \[ (U-1)^{\,q+(r-1)q(q-1)/2}=0. \] Thus the other differential automorphisms are exactly those whose conormal action has no uniform unipotence exponent. This includes conormal actions that are locally unipotent with unbounded exponents.

\label{C:squarezero} Let $B$ be a commutative $K$-algebra, $M$ any $B$-module, and $A=B\oplus M$ with multiplication $(b,m)(c,n)=(bc,bn+cm)$. Every $K$-algebra automorphism of $A$ inducing the identity on $B=A/M$ is uniquely \[ U_{d,\sigma}(b,m)=(b,d(b)+\sigma(m)), \quad d\in\operatorname{Der}_K(B,M),\quad\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_B(M). \] Composition is $(d,\sigma)(e,\tau)=(d+\sigma e,\sigma\tau)$. All these automorphisms have differential order at most one. They are exponentials of globally nilpotent derivations precisely when $\sigma-1$ is globally nilpotent.

\label{C:counterexamples} On $A=\mathbb Q[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$, the automorphism $U(\varepsilon)=2\varepsilon$ is differential of order one but is not an exponential of a nilpotent derivation; it acts as multiplication by $2$ on $J_U/J_U^2$. On $A'=\mathbb Q[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^3)$, the derivation $D=\varepsilon\,d/d\varepsilon$ has $D(A')\subset I=(\varepsilon)$ but is not locally nilpotent. Thus identity on $A/I$ does not imply identity on $\operatorname{gr}_I(A)$, and merely requiring $D(A)\subset I$ does not make the exponential finite. The correct replacements are Theorems~\ref{C:filtered}, \ref{C:differential}, and \ref{C:conormal}.

\label{C:intertwine} Let $M,N$ be arbitrary $K$-modules, $u\in\operatorname{End}_K(M)$ and $v\in\operatorname{End}_K(N)$ locally nilpotent, and $f\in\operatorname{Hom}_K(M,N)$. Then \[ f\exp(u)=\exp(v)f\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad fu=vf. \] The equivalence also identifies intertwining at time $1$ with intertwining for every parameter over every commutative $K$-algebra, and with intertwining of the formal additive group actions.

\label{C:module-actions} For any $K$-module $M$, let $\mathcal M(R)=M\otimes_K R$ and $\widehat{\mathbb G}_a(R)=\operatorname{Nil}(R)$. Natural $R$-linear additive-group actions on $\mathcal M$ satisfy \begin{align*} \operatorname{End}_K(M)&\simeq \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{grp}}(\widehat{\mathbb G}_a,\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal M)),\\ \operatorname{LNil}(\operatorname{End}_K(M))&\simeq \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{grp}}(\mathbb G_a,\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal M)), \end{align*} by $u\mapsto[\lambda\mapsto\exp(\lambda u_R)]$. Here $\operatorname{LNil}$ means locally nilpotent endomorphisms. Restricting the second map to globally nilpotent endomorphisms is bijective exactly when every locally nilpotent endomorphism of $M$ is globally nilpotent. Finite generation of $M$ is sufficient, but is not necessary.

\label{C:functor-criterion} For an arbitrary $\mathcal O$-module functor: \begin{enumerate} \item The map $u\mapsto\bar e_u$ from $E$ to formal additive-group actions has fibers exactly the additive cosets of $\ker\delta$. A formal action $\rho$ belongs to its image if and only if all three following tests hold: each $\rho_R(\lambda)$ is unipotent for nilpotent $\lambda$; its finite logarithm is $R$-linear in the parameter $\lambda\in\operatorname{Nil}(R)$; and the resulting morphism $\ell_\rho\in H$ has zero class in $\operatorname{coker}\delta$. In particular the formal exponential map is bijective if and only if $\ker\delta=0$ and these three tests hold for every formal action. \item The map from globally nilpotent elements of $E$ to ordinary additive-group actions is always injective. Its image consists exactly of those actions for which there is one integer $r$ with $(\rho_R(\lambda)-1)^r=0$ for all $R,\lambda$, and whose logarithms satisfy \[ \log\rho_R(a\lambda)=a\log\rho_R(\lambda) \quad(a,\lambda\in R). \] It is bijective exactly when every ordinary action passes these two tests. \end{enumerate} These criteria distinguish failure of uniqueness, failure of unipotence, failure of scalar linearity, and failure to divide the formal parameter. They apply without representability, exactness, or finiteness assumptions on $\mathcal M$.

\label{C:functor-counterexamples} Both maps asked about on cote~68, scan~044, fail to be bijective for general module functors. The manuscript poses a question here, not an assertion of bijectivity. \begin{enumerate} \item For $K=\mathbb Q$ and $\mathcal M(R)=R_{\mathrm{red}}$, the distinct endomorphisms $0,1\in E$ have the same formal exponential. \item For $K=\mathbb Q$ and $\mathcal M(R)=R\oplus\Omega_{R/\mathbb Q}$, the formula \[ \rho_R(\lambda)(a,\omega)=(a,\omega+a\,d\lambda) \] defines an ordinary additive-group action, with $(\rho_R(\lambda)-1)^2=0$ for every $R,\lambda$. Neither it nor its restriction to the formal additive group is an exponential of the required form. \end{enumerate}

\label{C:functor-basechange} Let $\mathcal M$ be an arbitrary $\mathcal O$-module functor over the commutative $\mathbb Q$-algebra $K$. \begin{enumerate} \item Suppose that for every $K$-algebra $R$ and every $n\geq1$, the canonical map \[ \mathcal M(R)\otimes_R R[t]/(t^{n+1}) \longrightarrow\mathcal M(R[t]/(t^{n+1})) \] is an isomorphism. Then $u\mapsto\bar e_u$ is bijective. \item Suppose instead that for every $R$, the canonical map \[ \mathcal M(R)\otimes_R R[t]\longrightarrow\mathcal M(R[t]) \] is an isomorphism. Then ordinary additive-group actions correspond exactly to natural endomorphisms $u$ for which each $u_R$ is elementwise locally nilpotent. The map from the globally nilpotent elements of $E$ is therefore bijective exactly when all these natural locally nilpotent endomorphisms are globally nilpotent in $E$. \end{enumerate} The first hypothesis holds for \[ \mathcal M(R)=\operatorname{Hom}_R(P\otimes_KR,Q\otimes_KR) \] with arbitrary $K$-modules $P,Q$, without finite generation or projectivity, and for arbitrary product functors $\mathcal M(R)=\prod_{j\in J}R$. Both hypotheses hold for every tensor-product functor $M\otimes_KR$. For the internal Hom functor the second hypothesis also holds when $P$ is finitely generated.

\label{C:functor-separate-obstructions} The distinct tests in Theorem~\ref{C:functor-criterion} cannot in general be omitted. \begin{enumerate} \item There is a natural formal additive-group action whose value at a square-zero scalar is not even locally unipotent. \item There is a natural formal action which is uniformly unipotent of exponent two and whose logarithm is $R$-linear in its nilpotent scalar parameter, but which is not a formal exponential because its logarithm has nonzero class in $\operatorname{coker}\delta$. \end{enumerate}

\label{C:sheaf-globalization} Let $X$ be a scheme over $\mathbb Q$, and let $D$ be a derivation of the sheaf $\mathcal O_X$. Suppose each point has an open neighborhood $V$ and an integer $r$ such that $D^r=0$ as an endomorphism of $\mathcal O_X|_V$. The local finite exponentials glue to an automorphism $E_D$ of $X$ inducing the identity on $X_{\mathrm{red}}$. If $X\to S$ is a morphism and $D$ is an $S$-derivation, this is an $S$-automorphism. If $D,D'$ satisfy this hypothesis and commute, then $D+D'$ satisfies it and \[ E_0=\operatorname{id}_X,\qquad E_{D+D'}=E_D\circ E_{D'}. \] Thus the plus sign between automorphisms in the transcription of scan~044 must be composition. Elementwise local nilpotence on the ring of one affine open is a weaker hypothesis and does not imply identity on its reduction.

\label{C:majorization} For nonnegative finitely supported functions on a set, the maximum scalar product over rearrangements is $R(f,g)$. It is attained exactly when all positive level sets of the two functions are mutually nested. Moreover $f'\preceq f$ is equivalent to $R(f',h)\leq R(f,h)$ for every nonnegative finitely supported $h$, and to this inequality only for indicator functions of finite subsets. On a finite universe the set $\{f':f'\preceq f\}$ is the convex hull of the functions lying coordinatewise below a permutation of $f$.

\label{C:pretasse-cones} For the preceding system, every pair $(f,g)\in S^2$ is pr\'etass\'e. In particular the two-factor peak inequality \[ f'\preceq f,\quad g'\preceq g \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \|f'*g'\|_\infty\leq\|f*g\|_\infty \] holds. This does not imply the corresponding inequality for three factors, or two-factor majorization.

\label{C:K-counterexample} Axioms a)--d) of cote~68, scan~017, do not imply Condition~K of scan~021. This remains false when $\rho$ is surjective, its kernel is exactly the specified copy of $G[2]$, every chain is nonempty, every chain contains $G$, every singleton occurs, and every cardinality from $1$ to $|G|$ occurs.

\label{C:K-repair} Assume the system axioms and that $S$ contains an indicator of every possible finite cardinality. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item every pair of generating indicators, from any two labelled chains, is tass\'e; \item every pair in $S^2$ is tass\'e; \item for every $n\geq2$, $f_i\in S$ and $f_i'\preceq f_i$ imply $f_1'*\cdots*f_n'\preceq f_1*\cdots*f_n$; \item Condition~K: for the same data, $\|f_1'*\cdots*f_n'\|_\infty\leq\|f_1*\cdots*f_n\|_\infty$. \end{enumerate} The cardinality assumption is needed only for (4)$\Rightarrow$(2); (1)$\Leftrightarrow$(2)$\Leftrightarrow$(3)$\Rightarrow$(4) holds without it. Thus a)--d) provide compatibility of the proposed extremizers, while extremality of generator pairs is an additional mathematical condition.

\label{C:group-classification} Suppose $G[2]$ means the full set of elements whose square is $e$, and the displayed $i:G[2]\simeq\ker\rho$ is a group isomorphism. With finite subsets and empty families allowed, a nonzero system satisfying all the displayed data and all lettered axioms exists if and only if the elements of $G[2]$ commute pairwise. Surjectivity of $\rho$ does not change this answer. For finite groups satisfying this condition, all fibers can also be required nonempty. If instead $G[2]$ is interpreted as a specified subgroup $H\leq G$ of exponent two, every ambient group $G$ admits such a system with $\ker\rho\simeq H$. This includes the choice $H=\{e\}$ for every group. In either interpretation, the requirement that $i$ map \emph{onto} $\ker\rho$ is not forced by the chain, reflection, convolution, alignment, and kernel-covariance axioms, even with full finite cardinality coverage and $i$ still injective into the kernel.

\label{C:integer-system} For $G=\mathbb Z$, a nonempty system representing every finite cardinality is obtained with $\widetilde G=\mathbb Z$, $\rho=1$, and $\mathcal A(k)$ consisting of all finite integer intervals whose midpoint is $k/2$. Its kernel is $0=G[2]$. The same chain, reflection, and convolution construction descends to cyclic groups of even order $N$ with indexing group $\mathbb Z/(2N)$, $\rho(k)=k\pmod N$, and $i(N/2)=N$, after including the whole group in every chain.

\label{C:C3-coverage-obstruction} Let $G=\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z$ and retain the printed exact-kernel condition $\ker\rho=G[2]=0$. Any system satisfying the chain and convolution axioms has no two-element generating set in any family. Consequently it cannot have full cardinality coverage. Surjectivity of $\rho$ and the remaining printed axioms do not remove this obstruction.

\label{C:symmetry} Neither pr\'etass\'e nor tass\'e is a symmetric relation on arbitrary groups. Both are symmetric on abelian groups. On every group their universally valid reversal is \[ (f,g)\text{ has the property} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (\check g,\check f)\text{ has the property}. \] For the pr\'etass\'e property, symmetry also holds whenever each function is invariant under inversion followed by some left translation.

\label{C:graded-determinant-sign} Let $S$ be any scheme. Let $\operatorname{Pic}^{\mathbb Z}(S)$ be the groupoid whose objects are pairs $(L,a)$, with $L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_S$-module and $a:S\to\mathbb Z$ locally constant, and whose arrows are degree-preserving $\mathcal O_S$-linear isomorphisms. Set \[ (L,a)\otimes(M,b)=(L\otimes M,a+b),\qquad \symbf{1}=(\mathcal O_S,0). \] With the ordinary tensor associator and unit maps, the formula \[ c_{(L,a),(M,b)}(l\otimes m)=(-1)^{ab}m\otimes l \] defines a symmetric monoidal Picard groupoid. The functor \[ E\longmapsto\operatorname{Det}(E) =(\textstyle\bigwedge^{\operatorname{rk}E}E,\operatorname{rk}E) \] on finite locally free modules and their isomorphisms, equipped with the exterior-product maps for direct sums, respects this symmetry. It respects all finite block permutations and, on finite free modules, the change-of-complement condition of scan~056. The replacement $(-1)^{a+b}$ printed in the commutativity formula of Knudsen--Mumford, p.~20, fails these unit and exterior-product requirements already over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Q$.

\label{C:determinant-ordinary-basechange} The assumptions ``$p:X\to Y$ proper of finite Tor dimension, $Y$ noetherian, $F$ perfect on $X$, and $g:Y'\to Y$ a morphism of noetherian schemes'' do not imply the ordinary-fibre-product comparison displayed on p.~46 of \cite{ROOT_KnudsenMumford1976}. With $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ and projections $g':X'\to X$, $p':X'\to Y'$, the two graded lines \[ \operatorname{Det}(Lg^*Rp_*F) \quad\hbox{and}\quad \operatorname{Det}(Rp'_*Lg'^*F) \] need not even have the same degree.

\label{C:determinant-basechange-repair} Let $R\to S$ and $R\to A$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, and put $B=A\otimes_R S$. For a perfect $S$-complex $F$, consider the classical comparison in $D(A)$ \[ \beta_F:A\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F \longrightarrow B\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}F, \] where the target is restricted along $A\to B$. Then $\beta_F$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every perfect $S$-complex $F$ if and only if $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(A,S)=0$ for all $i>0$. More generally, let $p:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes, let $g:Y'\to Y$ be any morphism, and form $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $g'$ and $p'$. Suppose that $X$ and $Y'$ are Tor independent over $Y$: on affine charts over an affine open of $Y$, all higher Tor modules of their two coordinate algebras vanish. For every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the canonical map \[ Lg^*Rp_*E\longrightarrow Rp'_*Lg'^*E \] is an isomorphism. If $Rp_*E$ is perfect, this gives an isomorphism of their graded determinants as well. In particular, flatness of either $p$ or $g$ supplies the Tor-independence hypothesis. When $p$ is proper of finite Tor dimension, $Y$ is noetherian and $E$ is perfect, $Rp_*E$ is perfect, so this is a corrected version of the printed determinant comparison.
